ResponsesInList.Title: Re: which type of file course  content should be uploaded so that the course content cannot be downloaded by any students

ResponsesInList.Title: Copying an assessment
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm using Moodle 3.66 I've created an assessment (multichoice quiz) within a course. I want to copy this and then use it as a template (keeping the answer options and question text but just changing the graphic, and correct answer). I can copy the assessment or backup and restore it fine. However, when I amend the questions, it changes them in the original copy of the questions as well. I guess this is probably because the questions are being saved in a question bank, and it might be something to do with saving into another category? Not sure. Can anyone help?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copying an assessment
ResponsesInList.Text: Spot on - that's exactly why. However, where is your question bank? That should only happen if both quizzes can 'see' the same question bank. If you restore it to a different course that shouldn't happen.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copying an assessment
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Howard. Unfortunately I need to copy it to the same course. I'm basically trying to create a template with 16 questions that have the same format: same multichoice options (11 options) There will be three assessments using this same template.

ResponsesInList.Title: Copying an assessment
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to go into the original quiz you're attempting to duplicate -- open up each question, change the location of the Question from the course-level question bank to the quiz-level question bank. Then, when you duplicate the quiz, the questions in the copy will be unique to the copy. My team spent a year doing this to all the quizzes on our site when teachers wanted to make copies of their quizzes in order to make the copies more rigorous that the original versions. This Google doc outlines the steps we went through to do this: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uyU2K15wI7scew6lzmevkj0zBUFvgl8k_9OUr6uG6tc/edit?usp=sharing

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copying an assessment

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle install on Centos7
ResponsesInList.Text: Where do you host ?  and what type of hosting is it?  Shared?  VPS? Look for docs provided by your hosting on how to install Moodle.  Sometimes those are available to customers only. I run 2 servers on CentOS 7.   The directions one sees for Ubuntu are similar only web service user (www-data in Ubuntu ... apache in CentOS 7).  Since newer versions of Ubuntu server are supposed to be "linux standards base" (CentOS 7 is also) locations of directories should also be the same. Document root is /var/www/html/ (moodle code goes in there) Apache user's 'home directory' is /var/www/ and manually creating a 'moodledata' directory in that location and setting ownerships/permissions to owner 'apache'  group 'apache' +  Read/Write/Execute to /var/www/moodledata to 'anything contained therein will suffice for install. Where things differ .. CentOS 7 probably has seLinux installed by default and it would interfere with Moodle installation.  Set seLinux to 'permissive' and no issues. Don't use cPanel myself ... while it might the easier tool to use for things like creating a DB for Moodle via PHPMyAdmin ... it's also less efficient than terminal (ssh) access to the server. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: uploading student assignment to group
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there a way to upload groups and groupings assignments to a class with students already populated? Often, I create the groups in a spreadsheet with a column of student names/emails, and a second column for groups. Then, I usually goto moodle, and manually create the group name, then manually assign the individuals to it. I figured there must be a better way to do this, where a .csv file could be uploaded (or it could be downloaded with student names, populated with group names, then uploaded). I'm aware that you can upload the students when creating the class, and at that time, you can also upload groups. But what I'm talking about is when you have a class that has started, and and you want to add/change group while that class is still going (and already populated with students).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: uploading student assignment to group
ResponsesInList.Text: Upload_users is quite flexible. You can use it to upload more users and even modify existing ones in running courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: uploading student assignment to group
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the response, Howard! For groups, I'm anxious to know if uploading a user file with names matching existing students with a new group name will override existing group designations. Moodle allows the existence of multiple grouping schemes. So, could I cut a three schemes of groups, make separate csv files, then upload them in sequence, then each of the students will be assigned three different groups? I'm less concerned about the groupings, since grouping groups in to groupings is not a large number of steps. Finally, there is the issue of having a student on my system that appears in multiple classes. If this is done at the user lever (site administration level), how does moodle know to add the group designations to the person in a particular class (but not some other class)?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: uploading student assignment to group
ResponsesInList.Text: What will happen is whatever you ask it to do last. It will update according to the data in the latest CSV file - whatever that is. If you're still unsure you need to go and test it with your exact scenario and satisfy yourself. The second question - Moodle doesn't have anything called 'classes' so I don't know what you mean.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: uploading student assignment to group
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry , by "classes", I mean a course. What I'm unsure about is to see how moodle stores the group that students are in, since an individual is in multiple groups. examples ( https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Upload_users ) show a Group heading as a single field - not sure how moodle would store multiple groups and groupings, so I'm not sure how to create an upload file that would account for that. Perhaps if there is some sort of Download_users function, we could recover the .csv structure that would be used for a bulk update.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: uploading student assignment to group
ResponsesInList.Text: The docs howard linked are quite useful in showing the step by step on how to set up the csv to upload, but the basic structure is: username, course1, group1 to add a student into two different groups in the same sheet, you'd have to do username, course1, group1, course2, group2 (where course1 and course 2 would be the same course shortname). If a student is already in a group before you do any uploads, "group red" for example, then when you upload a csv to add them into "group blue", the student will then end up in both red and blue groups. CSV uploads for adding students into groups wont undo' anything existing groups if that is what you are worried about. CSV uploads cannot remove students from groups, it only adds them into new ones (if the group doesnt exist, it will then also create the group for you which is hepful.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: uploading student assignment to group
ResponsesInList.Text: When adding a student into group, you must always also indicate which class, so that is how moodle will know: username, course1, group1 ties that course, group and student together, for another group for a different course within the same csv sheet, adding on 2 now columns (course2, group2) would ensure only that group2 is made in that course and not in course1

If you cannot do that, ask the server tech to do it. Dunno why anyone do so, but a person at the true server tech level could have a re-write rule which would distort/change what moodle sees.   That's done inbetween the network layer and the beginning of the application layer - before Moodle sees it. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Debby, If a field is not being used by any user's profile, you can customize the field via Language customization and rename them to anything you want. For Assignment, the employee would return from the actual course, enroll in the tracking course and upload an electronic copy of the certificate to the assignment. You could either have it automatically assign completion upon upload or require a manual grade be assigned (someone verifies it is a legitimate certificate and issues credit). The second is what I would do but I'm a suspicious, untrusting so-and-so. For Face to face, if you don't have it installed, you would have to install it, since it is a plugin. This option would be entirely manual--the employee would turn in the certificate and you would enroll them in the course, add a session for those course dates and register the employee, then take attendance. Of course, if you keep track of the external training opportunities, you could set up sessions for all the available dates and have the employee enroll and register in your course area and then give credit when they return. You could upload the certificates to the course (maybe using database) to keep copies of the certificate and just hide them from students (unless you wanted to leave them visible to each student, which would be easy to set up when you upload the doc...though...maybe not in database). That's a lot of ifs. I used to do the second option (face to face) and we just kept the certificate in their training file. It worked. I would have preferred the first option, but I was over ruled...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cron script contiually failing -- for years!
ResponsesInList.Text: Definitely contact your Moodle Partner if cron tasks are failing. Cron is essential for the health of the entire website, not just forum emails. Have you tried going to Site Administration > Server > Tasks > Scheduled tasks > Forum mailings and maintenance jobs to see the last time this specific task has run? You'll be able to see some statistics there, whether or not this task is disabled, and so on. This task runs every minute by default. You can also check Site administration > Server > Email > Outgoing mail configuration to verify your outgoing email is set up correctly. Email is a tricky thing. It seems like it should be simple yet is a real pain to ensure you reach your users' inboxes (especially if you send out a lot, the chances of being flagged as spam increase dramatically). It might not be Moodle's fault. If email is critical for your website, you might consider going with a dedicated email service.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cron script contiually failing -- for years!

We've also released some of the tools we use as open-source plugins - see: https://moodle.org/plugins/tool_heartbeat https://moodle.org/plugins/tool_lockstats We do occaisionally see issues with certain Moodle plugins causing cron failures, but there are also a lot of improvements to the cron processes in newer versions of Moodle - it would be interesting to hear what version of Moodle you are using and what parts of cron are failing.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to add public forum to Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: While it's impressive that Moodle uses it's own forum module for Community forums and it might be based on the same forum module one finds in stock Moodle, it is, however, a 'special' dedicated implemenation with additional config/protections one doesn't have with a stock Moodle. Check the full header of a message from this forum compared to a message from one of your own moodle's forums to get an idea. IF one sets up a site wide forum in a Moodle and force subscribes all users on the system, one will have to use a robust SMTP relay.  And, just one message could bog down your Moodle ... factors depending. IF, however, one wants only to communicate with all members of a moodle site, that can be accomplished by using something that's really outside of Moodle. Consider a Google Group!!! Briefly ... https://groups.google.com/forum/?nomobile=true#!creategroup Must have a google account to set up. And it will mean some admin ... don't think that can be avoided. Visible The group's name, email address, and description will be visible and searchable to the selected users. This setting can be overridden in search. To restrict group visibility in the Groups UI and search, ensure the View topics setting is at least as restrictive as the Group visibility setting. View Topics These users can view and search for topics in this group. If users experience trouble, check your group visibility settings. Post These users can post messages to this group. Join Invite ... from users in course list https://policies.google.com/?hl=en https://policies.google.com/terms?hl=en https://policies.google.com/privacy?hl=en https://policies.google.com/faq?hl=en There is an open sourced application called 'MailMan' but it would require manual set up of list and some admin. It also might need an SMTP relay. https://www.list.org/ You'd probably need to create your own policy/TOS/ etc. with Mailman.  It's especially good for one way ... admin of the Moodle -> all members of the moodle.  In this day and age of spammers everwhere using everything ... wouldn't be a bad idea to run as separate server - VM 's are fairly cheap ... but here again ... an SMTP relay. My 2 cents.  As a former mail server(s) and mailman admin for a K12 private IP'd Regional Network consisting of 38 districts - large and small (it's why I have thinning gray hair!), 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to add public forum to Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Think (really know) there's a misunderstanding ... the 'gloom and doom' is in a moodle site forum on the front page where all users are forced subscribed to that forum.  Normally, that forum isn't graded ... no expectation past Moodle admin user informing all users of a scheduled maintenance or some sort of system thang affecting all users ... in all courses.  And you've not mentioned how many users on your Moodle, have you?  or did I miss that! True story ... a 2.7.x with a hidden site forum - all users forced subscribed to it.  Former admin of the Moodle had tested it, saw the problem and hid the forum.  That admin left the corp.  New admin exploring decided to give it a shot ... 20,000 users. Needless to say the Moodle slowed to a creepy crawl.  Corp did have a hidden SMTP server set up but not with all of what's needed now ... SPF, DKIM, etc. for the Moodle server.  Messages to a majority of those 20,000 users were being rejected ... Moodle server was getting bounces and the SMTP server throttling messages as well ... delaying receiving messages from the Moodle ... which meant qued up mail ... next run at it when cron job ran.    Thank goodness had a Postfix on that server that acted as a shim between the Moodle and the SMTP server ... took 2 hours of monitoring ... waiting for que to fill up .. removing those outgoing messages before they were sent.  Deleting rejection notices coming back until things finally settled down ... mail wise.  That was the last time new Admin tried to use a forum ... of any kind. :| (gun shy at that point - and all I did was to 'wag a virtual finger' ... nicely, I might add!) Now a moodle forum in course (fewer users) and used for graded discussions ... 'sharing' attachements, etc. ... that's a different story.   By all means use ... just get an SMTP server set up. Suggestion to use Google Group not an all/in every case solution ... but something that fits site forum where all users forced subscribed - would have fewer issues. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: How to hide a menu item - Help please
ResponsesInList.Text: Part of managing users is both creating accounts and assigning roles to those accounts. If you don't want managers to assign System roles to uses, remove their ability to do this by going to Site Admin - Users - Permissions - Define Role - then click Edit for the Manager role. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting number of participants from mysql
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle uses a relational database to keep its data, so this is why you don't see the number of participants, and many other things of interest, in a single table. It's all there, and you can get to anything you want by writing custom SQL . Explore some SQL queries that have already been contributed: List of SQL Contributed reports . Learning which tables do what can take some learning.  I think most Moodles have around 400 tables

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting number of participants from mysql
ResponsesInList.Text: Begin small, then work your way up. This code, which you pointed me to in the contributed reports, works for me: SELECT c.fullname, COUNT(ue.id) AS Enroled FROM mdl_course AS c JOIN mdl_enrol AS en ON en.courseid = c.id JOIN mdl_user_enrolments AS ue ON ue.enrolid = en.id GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY c.fullname

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Block or report: Show participant NOT logged in a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Others will correct me if I am wrong. A user who logs in is a "system" level event. They log into the system. Then, they can navigate to their course. Moodle also logs the event that they clicked on a course. The Moodle logs will also record a "log out" but this again is a system-level action. Some students can jump from course to course, and they may never log out! Sure, after a time period (set by your administrator) the system will log them out (I am not sure if this event is captured.)  I seldom log out of my Moodle, I just leave it. So, if you were to physically watch a student, let's assume in a computer lab, for example, you might observe them logging into moodle, then navigate to their course, then, they stand up and walk away. As you watch them, you are wondering "Are they done?" Then, 3 minutes later they return, sit down, open and read their book as they look at their computer screen. Would you want to sa they are logged in? Or idle? Then they get up again, walk away. You assume that they will return, but they don't. At what time do you want to consider them logged out? If all of this happened within 5 minutes, they would show in the Online user's block as logged in. You can watch Moodle's "live logs" reports and see exactly what is going on. In one browser, log in as a student while in a different browser product, you are logged in as the administrator. You will be able to see how Moodle's live logs show these events. If you want more than this "live logs" report, you could always write SQL . If you do happen to go to Participants and sort by last access, this statistic is really the last time that they clicked on something.  But be careful interpreting this as student course (study) activity. A student can click on a Moodle administrative link, for example.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Advanced text editing tool
ResponsesInList.Text: I am using Moodle 3.8, installed using the automated package, on a MacBook Pro. I wanted to share that I have resolved the issues related to adding font color and background color choices. That said, I wanted to share some hiccups that I had along the way. 1. I downloaded and installed the plugins entitled, "atto_morefontcolors" and "atto_morebackgroundcolors". They involve a manual install, as they aren't rated for Moodle 3.8 but once installed they are working fine. 2. To add additional colors to the palette of colour choices, scroll down using the path: "Site administration/Plugins/Plugins overview" until you reach the section entitled: Atto HTML editor/Atto plugins (quite a looonng way down in the list) 3. Find the two plugins. For either plugin, click on the "Settings" button. As a result, you are shown a list of default hexadecimal colour codes (4 colours per line, 4 lines). Click inside the box containing the default codes and simply enter any additional hexadecimal codes that you wish to use. Don't forget to scroll down to SAVE your changes. Note: you have to do this for BOTH plugins. I does not autopopulate all similar plugins involving colour. Even after doing this, I was still getting the default 5 colour palette when I clicked on the corresponding buttons on the ATTO editor toolbar. There is an additional step that you must do in order to activate the two plugins. Scrolling further down, you will find a section entitled, Toolbar config (editor_atto|toolbar). There will be a list of parameters related to the toolbar buttons. 1. Find the parameter called "Color". 2. Replace the default names under the category with "Color = morefontcolors, morebackgroundcolors" (No spaces in the new names and separate each plugin name with a "," and a single space) 3. Scroll down and click "Save Changes" Until you do this second step, you will not see your new color choices when you click on the corresponding buttons on the Atto toolbar. If one of your new colors is missing (the space will be blank), simply review your entered hexadecimal codes - you have likely either entered 5 instead of 6 numbers/letters or incorrectly entered the hexadecimal code). Once you fix that, you should see your full range of new colours in the colour palette. Please let me know if this is helpful.

My inclination is to suggest loading MySQL 5.7 (which is part of the distro) instead. There is loads of online support. Centos is a lot more conservative than Ubuntu and you are going to have to semi-manually install a lot more software to get the versions you need. Although, it's still not difficult and there's heaps of documentation. And there's Ken There's nothing wrong with Debian - Ubuntu is based on it. The problem it has is that Ubuntu exists. You ask ten different Linux professionals what setup they prefer and you'll get ten different answers. You won't go wrong with Ubuntu or Centos. Just don't go off the rails with something weird that almost nobody uses. If you don't listen to anything else I say - listen to this. Put aside an afternoon and learn the command line basics. There are lots of tutorials. Pay particular attention to file permissions and ownership (which you definitely need to know anyway). It's time very well spent. Plesk (and the like) is for wimps - you're actually making it harder for yourself.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: recommended Unix for Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: Howard Miller wrote: > None of which are Unix... to be pedantic. Very true. To call something UNIX it had to go through a certification process by whoever owned the UNIX TM - costing hundreds of thousand dollars. Linus didn't have that money. Instead the community conned the phrace "Linux is Unix-like" (watch the case). That was in the 90's. Today, the Unixes call themselves "Linux-like". That's how the Wheel of Luck grinds.

From there each button would link to an embedded video for the student to watch, each video would have its own button, and video quantity would range from 3 up to 9.  There would be no "coursework (assignments)" or any sort of thing to 'grade' persay.  What we do need is the ability for the instructor to mark a set of goals met during discussions with the student (an average of 5 per course) if all goals are met, then they have satisfied the course requirements and can either be auto enrolled in the next course, or manually.  The instructor would have sole discretion of whether or not the requirements have been satisfied and would need a way to mark yes or no and also a way to provide feedback. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best Way To Setup a Course for...
ResponsesInList.Text: Competencies are a separate framework that does not relate to the gradebook. Grades and competencies are two different systems for judging a students comprehension. https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Competencies https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Learning_plans Kind Regards

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best Way To Setup a Course for...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best Way To Setup a Course for...
ResponsesInList.Text: You cannot turn off the gradebook. The competencies and learning plan objects functionality is not as robust or have the functionality that you might need. 1. Consider if a competency reflects a version of a course, and you do frequent revisions to content, does the revision need to correspond to the competency. 2. Consider how you will use these objects. There is no end date on either object. 3. You can hide both of these objects, but it does not remove it from the Student's view if competencies have been awarded. 4. Build a small test competency framework and Learning Plan template, before you setup large structures. Kind Regards

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best Way To Setup a Course for...
ResponsesInList.Text: Competency completions are not one of the options for course completion or course restrictions. Course completion options are triggered by activity completions or passing grade conditions. Course restrictions are also triggered by other activity completions or passing grade conditions. So even for the course that I did not want to have a quiz, I had to create a one question quiz, valued at 100 points. Yes/No or True/False to trigger an activity completion to award the competency. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: Re: Generate custom URL
ResponsesInList.Text: The "?" marks are being used as "query code." It's a URL/Internet thing, and my guess is intentional. What you might need to figure out is how your server can be configured to understand these "query codes." Many years ago, I used query codes in my custom designed Flash Video player. In the URL, these query codes would be interpreted by my Actionscript and then pick the correct video to play. It was an interesting solution, and worked. But then, when all browsers could play mp4 files directly, I aborted my custom video player. Adobe's ActionSript had a way to parse these more complex URLs. I am not a java programmer, but my guess is that there are ways to parse URLs that contain query codes. Maybe someone else will know. But Howard is correct, this has more to do with things on your server-side than with Moodle. For example, if you use something like https://mydomain.com/home.html?xxx , I think your browser ignores the xxx. It is up to your server and web page to interpret the xxx and do something with it. I might be way off on all of this, so consider my comments as just some ideas.  Put "using url variables" into a Google search. Nope, don't change core code, as Howard suggests.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How are courses auto-restored, on a schedule?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Blair F., The Sandbox you found IS the one you want. After install, in it's settings you provide a path where your store your course backups, usually a folder named, sandbox, in your moodledata folder. Then in, Scheduled Tasks, you setup how often you want the course to be restored. This is the exact way I do a weekly restore of all the MooTyper sample courses at http://m3x.drachels.com/ . The only downside as far as I am concerned, is the courses are NOT restored in alphabetical order. One other downside is that when you want to make a change to a course that you want to keep, you must remember to make a new backup file and replace the old version with the new one.

ResponsesInList.Text: I'll wade in with my typical cynicism.... having a video of all your students seems like a load of hassle and bandwidth for next to no benefit ( IMO ). I would consider ways to reduce that rather than increase it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Coronavirus - Video / class conferencing options we should consider
ResponsesInList.Text: I'll second Howard's "don't use video" because the load is really big on people who are at the end of the bandwidth pipe. Zoom is a good choice, but only use video when you need it, which is quite definitely not all the time. Otherwise, the computer audio function is much less bandwidth and gives really good sound (assuming the computer is relatively recent). A trick to audio with laptops is to tilt the screen back to prevent feedback echo: a bit more than 90 degrees works fine. Also, having spent more than half an hour trying to figure out how to get computer audio to work for one of my people, it's really worth a 1-minute recorded tutorial on how to make audio work. As for wanting to see faces, use a round robin approach: Ask Daisuke a question and have him turn on his video while talking; next to Abraham, Daisuke turns his off and Abraham turns his on. And so on. This keeps the bandwidth at a reasonable level.

ResponsesInList.Title: Scalable SCORM Package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello MOODLE community. I am having an issue with adding Scalable SCORM packages in MOODLE 3.2. When I add the package, everything seems to work correctly, except the edge of the package goes outside of the window (it seems to cut off about 10% of the right side of the interaction). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scalable SCORM Package
ResponsesInList.Text: How are you opening the package outside of Moodle? Are you previewing it with the authoring software? If so, that has no relationship to how it displays in Moodle. Look at your package settings for page size in your authoring software. Look at the screen display settings in Moodle.  If your package displays at a different ratio than it was built, it could cause problems. Are you opening it in a new window or in the same window? What authoring software do you use? Are you also using Chrome for Moodle? When you say 'Scaleable SCORM packages' what does that mean? Do you mean they were designed to be responsive? or something else? Windows generally do scale, unless there is something preventing it...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scalable SCORM Package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Melanie, thank you for your quick response. I am previewing it in Chrome which displays it correctly. I have MOODLE set to display in a new window. I am using Adobe Captivate 7. It does not seem to matter which browser I open MOODLE with, they are all having the same problem ( IE , Edge, Chrome). What I mean by Scaleable is that the package will resize to fit in the window no matter what size the browser window is (not necessarily meaning that the package is being responsive - i.e. reformatting anything within the package other than the size of the entire package, including the player). I appreciate your help. Let me know if you need any other details. thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scalable SCORM Package
ResponsesInList.Text: Previews have very little to do with how they actually run, unfortunately. I've run into that many times, myself. Captivate 7 is probably the issue. I'm guessing you're not using Windows 10, since versions prior to 9 (?) don't work past 8. Older versions of Captivate had issues with all sorts of things, it would not surprise me if scaling was one of them. Check your Moodle SCORM Appearance settings--you can set the window size there and, considering your problems, probably should. What is your page size? The place I used to work had a lot of old equipment--their monitors couldn't handle packages bigger than 800 X 600--if I built them bigger than that, I (and all users) had trouble.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle docs/Importing glossary entries in XML format
ResponsesInList.Text: I am using Moodle 3.8.1, on a Macintosh laptop, my home computer and playing/exploring the different features of Moodle.  I am preparing to teach a university course and they encourage faculty to use Moodle for course delivery.  This is not my first time with Moodle, but I am strictly a public user, with little to no programming/HTML5/system knowledge. I was trying to import glossary entries from a previous course that I developed for this university.  In the university version, I easily found the method for exporting the entries as an XML file.  I was then intending to import the entries into my home version.  However, when I attempted to find a method to do so, I was stymied.  Consequently, I accessed the Moodle 3.8 documentation - specifically the article entitled "Importing glossary entries" Unless I am wrong, the documentation needs to be updated. 1.  I did not need to change roles to "Editing Teacher" as told to do, remaining as the "Administrator" seems to allow me to do the same thing. 2.  Secondly, I did not need to go to Administration > Glossary administration > Import entries and could not, indeed, find a way to do so (Although I was able to display the Administration block on my home installation). INSTEAD, I followed this procedure and successfully added the entries from my previous course. 1.  Remaining in the "Administrator" role, I clicked on the glossary that I had created on my home installation (It is listed as the main glossary in the settings, not a secondary glossary) 2.  I clicked on the wheel with the spokes (not sure what it is called) on the RH side of the glossary block, above the text giving you the option of a "printer-friendly version". 3.  Examining the resulting list, there is an option to "Import entries" 4.  When the new import window opened up, I browsed for the XML file that I had previously created, selected it, and clicked "Submit". In a few seconds, the entries were there in the glossary created in my home installation, complete with the linked content and pictures.

ResponsesInList.Text: The mdl_user contains | id | auth | confirmed | policyagreed | deleted | suspended | mnethostid | username | password | idnumber | firstname | lastname | email | emailstop | icq | skype | yahoo | aim | msn | phone1 | phone2 | institution | department | address | city | country | lang | calendartype | theme | timezone | firstaccess | lastaccess | lastlogin | currentlogin | lastip | secret | picture | url | description | descriptionformat | mailformat | maildigest | maildisplay | autosubscribe | trackforums | timecreated | timemodified | trustbitmask | imagealt | lastnamephonetic | firstnamephonetic | middlename | alternatename | I guess, I have to look at "timecreated". ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sorting users based on registeration time
ResponsesInList.Text: Times are internal UNIX times and need to be converted. Searching Google for help will show you how.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sorting users based on registeration time
ResponsesInList.Text: You can simply use SQL fetch by order by using timecreated column. SELECT * FROM `mdl_user` ORDER by timecreated

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sorting users based on registeration time
ResponsesInList.Text: or even... SELECT *, FROM_UNIXTIME(timecreated) FROM `mdl_user` WHERE deleted=0 ORDER by timecreated It occurs to me that they will be in the database table (ordered by id) in the created order anyway. Not that it matters especially.

"If this setting is enabled, users on the site can view all other users when selecting someone to message..." Given these explanations, I would expect that a simple student user (which seems to qualify as a member of the set "users") would be able to go to the Messages page, search for any user on the site (members of the set "list of all users"), and see the list of users who match their search term, even if they are not in a course with them. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple (not all) courses shown on one page
ResponsesInList.Text: As an idea, why not give students a brief description of each course, let them pick which one they want, and then either you or an administrator adds them to the course? Once they are added, they see the course among their other courses. It appears that you are using the word "session" to map to what you might already call these. ResponsesInList.Title: Certificate program - recommendations
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm wondering if you can provide suggestions, tips, tools/plugins to use in order to make our process more efficient. Most of our courses belong to a Certificate program and some are standalone courses (i.e., students can take a course but not necessarily want to obtain a Certificate). Our Certificate programs include a core course and a few elective courses - and each course has been assigned credit hours by various accreditation bodies. A student who wants to obtain a Certificate needs to complete certain number of credit hours so they take a core course then take 2 or more electives (depending on how many credit hours is required in the Certificate). I'm sure this process sounds familiar/is similar to most of your schools and organizations. Here is our current process for most of our course offerings: Students register to our courses (we use a different application for registration) We export the registrant list (csv file) from that application In our Moodle site, we enroll students to the course via bulk import (using the csv file) We check each student's course progress (some components of the course we use Restrictions feature - e.g., student needs to achieve at least 80% in a quiz to move on to next module - and some learning activities we check manually) Once the course offering ends, we send out letters of completion to those who have completed the course requirements If a student wants to obtain a Certificate, they have to keep track of courses that they have completed and which courses they still have to register for and complete in order to meet the credit hours required for the Certificate. Note that we do offer some self-directed courses and have made use of Moodle's self-registration feature, Certificate plugin, and Badge. Our ideal process is to help students with #6 so that they don't have to keep track of the courses they have taken in order to obtain a Certificate. We currently have our courses organized in Course Categories - but not sure if we should be using cohorts instead (or other features, tools or plugins that you can think of) Looking forward to your replies! Our Moodle site version is 3.7.1

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: never run Cron job
ResponsesInList.Text: The OP sharing all this info providing proof that cron is running and did nothing to set it up indicates hosting provider and Softac are finally getting it right . That's good for folks who are not IT, don't wanna be IT, just want to use a Moodle. However, some cautionary comments: 1. OP is running 3.7.2 of Moodle.   Already a couple of point releases behind: https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Releases#Moodle_3.7 The real acid test will be when OP decides to upgrade the moodle to the 3.8.x series or when released (soon) 3.9.0. If Softac where you host, offers an 'upgrade' button, do a site Environment check first in Moodle to see what is required for 3.9.0 or whatever the highest version shows in the environment check. 2. Advise make sure you have a site backup and know how to restore before using Softac upgrade button. BTW , another poster in these forums shared how Softac installed the data directory for moodle in a hidden directory of the code ... a 'hide'.  Users will not find that in Moodle docs anywhere and only provider would know.  IF a Softac upgrade button doesn't do things right, site could be rendered useless ... no data directory ... unless OPT knows of that quirk and what to do about it. One of the common post seen in this community is where to host a Moodle ... ie, with what provider.   So if OP wouldn't mind sharing with what provider they are hosted?   OVH? Other? 'SoS', Ken

So again ... where ... with what provider ... do you host? 'SoS', Ken

MariaDB is coming into its own now and think one should consider MariaDB to be a successful fork of MySQL - similar, but may not be 100% alike. ResponsesInList.Title: Finding the default role
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi I want to be sure that everybody that registers on our website is in "student" role. I will then want to promote some of them to teacher and others. How can I check the default role?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Finding the default role
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mahmood, When a user logged in to the system, the default role selected to "Authenticated users". You can check that form Dashboard > Site administration > Users > Permissions > User policies > Default role for all users. After that, when you assign a user to a particular course then he/she gets the role of a student (by default). You can set them to teachers or non-editing teachers or anything else. You can check the capabilities of individual roles from Dashboard > Site administration > Users > Permissions > Capability overview. Thanks and regards, Sandipa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Finding the default role
ResponsesInList.Text: However... don't let this tempt you to *change* the default role for all users. That is almost certainly not what you intend. Moodle, fundamentally, does not have a concept of a user being a 'student' or being a 'teacher' *site wide*. They are given these roles within Courses. This is so a user can be a teacher in one course and a student in another (for example). By default, you are not even able to assign the teacher and student roles outside of a course. While you can change this, it falls into "only do this if you know what you are doing"

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Finding the default role
ResponsesInList.Text: The authenticated user role is *very* limited. Users certainly can't search for or see the details of other users. Not with default settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with file upload/download
ResponsesInList.Text: After a few days of trying, reading other people's problems and solutions, and reading the documentation again and again, I found a solution which I'm going to share to help whoever wants to complete the Blocks-Advanced tutorial and display a download url for users. - As suggested by the documentation, I used a filemanager (named 'attachments') instead of a filepicker (which was named 'filename') - A first error in the tutorial is that $displaytext is stored as associative array, containing the keys 'text' and 'format'. So, the insert on the DB won't work unless fixing this error. I made it work with these simple lines, inside the if(... get_data() ...) in view.php $fromform->format = $fromform->displaytext['format']; $fromform->displaytext = $fromform->displaytext['text']; - I added the following lines in view.php, inside the if (... get_data() ..): $draftitemid = file_get_submitted_draft_itemid('attachments'); file_prepare_draft_area($draftitemid, $ context ->id, 'block_simplehtml', 'attachment', $draftitemid, array('subdirs' => true)); file_save_draft_area_files($draftitemid, $context->id, 'block_simplehtml', 'attachment', $draftitemid, array('subdirs' => true)); $fromform->attachments = $draftitemid; - Also in view.php, inside the final else (the one covering first visualization / form not validated cases), I added the following lines, so that when editing a page previously created the attachments are shown into the file manager: $draftitemid = $simplehtmlpage->attachments; file_prepare_draft_area($draftitemid, $context->id, 'block_simplehtml', 'attachment', $draftitemid, array('subdirs' => true)); $simplehtmlpage->attachments = $draftitemid; - lib.php needs to contain the function block_simplehtml_pluginfile(...), whose template can be found in the documentation - In lib.php, I created the following functions: 1) itemid_to_files_info($itemid) which accepts the $itemid as parameter (can be called in the display function using $simplehtmlpage->attachments) and returns the sql records whose itemid matches the parameter, in the {files} table 2) get_files_urls($itemid) which accepts the same $itemid as the first function, and returns an array of download urls, one for each file which has been uploaded and returned by the first function. It uses the following code: foreach($files as $file) { $url = moodle_url::make_pluginfile_url( $file->contextid, $file->component, $file->filearea, $itemid, $file->filepath, $file->filename, false) ; array_push($urls, $url); } Where $files is the array of records returned by the first function (something like $DB->get_records_sql(..)) - Given the array of download URLs, they can be displayed in HTML Everything should work now. For the sake of clarity, I'm sharing my full lib.php and view.php files: - View.php: https://pastebin.com/dGDBakn5 - Lib.php: https://pastebin.com/VqKXPhw5

ResponsesInList.Title: Sharing uploaded files.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Is there any way to share the files that have been uploaded in the private file manager. I am looking for a place to upload the files on moodle website and share that to other users.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sharing uploaded files.
ResponsesInList.Text: For locally (on server ), check into File System Repo. https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Repositories Have a system with two instances of Moodle ... a dev and a prod.  Use File system repo to point to a 'neurtal unirepo' folder which resides in directory that knows about already.   Both Moodles can see the unirepo.  Backups of developed courses from dev and be place in unirepo and on prod server those backups can be restored as courses. There is also things like Google Drive, Dropbox, etc. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sharing uploaded files.
ResponsesInList.Text: The most intuitive place is the https://docs.moodle.org/en/File_system_repository Ken has mentioned. But you need to (S) FTP your files to the server. The others can link to or copy them without (S)FTP. The low-tech solution is to place them in a "Course preparation" course where those people have access. Otherwise there are hundreds of external (to Moodle) solutions which can be reached by Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Bulk uploading files on behalf of students
ResponsesInList.Text: Does anyone know if there is a way or plugin that would allow for student submissions to be uploaded in bulk to a course/assignment the student is enrolled into? I've seen a similar unanswered question here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=377334 We are trying to make a system where a number of faculty will do blind grading, so we can assess the quality of learning in aggregated areas; such as Honors courses or 200 level English. In our case we have a collection of Word/PDF voluntary submissions from students across several sections /teachers that were collected through SurveyGizmo. From SurveyGizmo we download a spreadsheet of the info provided by the student and a zipped file of their collective submitted documents. What we want to be able to do, is a bulk student enrollment upload and also have their submitted files attached to the course/assignment. We already have a less than ideal way that we create the upload/enrollment/ grouping CSV file; but I can't seem to find any way or anyone that knows how to also automate the uploading of the students work to the course/assignment. So far the best method we have come up with is to "log in as" to each student account and then navigate to the assignment and upload the file. This process is unsustainable as we are starting to do more and more of these assessments. We are on Moodle version 3.7.2.  Does such a plugin exist? ...or any other ideas?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Old course no longer working, what has changed? Flash?
ResponsesInList.Text: You're not really using Moodle to create content. All these things are external to Moodle and then you're just using Moodle to deliver them. Anyway, you're more than likely correct. For all reasonable purposes, Flash is now a dead technology. Again, this is nothing whatever to do with Moodle. The SCORM package is played by software in the user's browser. Up to date browsers do not include Flash. There are ways round about this using content builders that generate pure HTML5. ResponsesInList.Title: Enabling teachers to assign other teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: Using Moodle 3.7.3 I have not been able to find the means of allowing teachers to add other teachers to a course without being able to add students to the teacher role. The route is: Click on Administration > Site administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles . Click the Allow role assignments tab. Click the checkbox where the teacher row and column intersect. Click the "Save changes" button. Then, in course "enrol" users, filter users and select (the dropdown allows the selection of any user). The assigned role can then be set to teacher, even if the dropdown selection was for a student. Is there a way of removing students from the dropdown selection or pre-select the group filtering from to remove those with a student role? There must be something wrong in the roles and permissions because I would think this an obvious setting you would want to stop teachers adding student in error as teachers to courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enabling teachers to assign other teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Diane, there's nothing wrong with your roles and permissions. It's just that Moodle doesn't have a concept of a student person or a teacher person, just roles you assign in a particular context . It's something we've wrestled with and our solution was a programmatic one - i.e. we have a plugin that watches for role assignment events, and then checks if they're a student. If a student has been given a teaching role, we ping an email off to the offending teacher, and copy in the DPO. It's pretty effective at getting them to undo their mistake. Essentially we're trying to educate our teachers not to do it. I guess, if you're absolutely confident that assigning a student a teaching role is always wrong, the same program could unassign the role. I'm planning on doing a presentation at the MOOTIEUK in Dublin on this so I'll have something more I can share when I get down to preparing the presentation. Mark

ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you Mark, this is really helpfully explained. The plugin would be extremely useful as the current alternative used is to remove the ability to assign roles for courses from teachers/owners. It is a fairly recent issue with the concerns around GDPR . Look forward to seeing more, good luck with your presentation.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enabling teachers to assign other teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: That's exactly the way it's meant to work. A user can be a teacher in one course and a student in another. To put it another way, how does Moodle "know" who is a teacher and who is a student?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enabling teachers to assign other teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, but wouldn't this also be something you would need control over in Role Overrides? Maybe a two tier column "allow assign teacher role" but "restrict to these existing roles". I guess this one is less on roles and permissions than on a simple way to remove/filter out those with the existing student role from the dropdown (when enrolling from participants) for those with the teacher role (but still available to other roles, such as admin, to do exactly as you say). Mark's plugin sounds like an ideal way of addressing this however, giving teachers freedom but allowing an admin to maintain control.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enabling teachers to assign other teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: Roles are defined within courses - NOT sitewide. So, as far as Moodle is concerned, it doesn't know if a user is a student or a teacher. If they are enrolled as a teacher in 'Course A' and then a student in 'Course B' then which are they? Roles are not assigned site-wide.

When one deletes an item from course or courses themselves, backups (.mbz files) are made of them and held in the virtual recyclebin (meta data in mdl_files).  They stay until cron job runs the task that changes the status references in DB and moves files finally to moodledata/trashdir. If in a crunch for space, one can manually remove all contents of moodledata/trashdir/ without ill affects on moodle. When a task in cron job builds up ... lots to do ... and with 4 Gig memory (underpowered for Moodle I might add) bet that 100% of CPU was really your DB server and clean ups etc. related to a cron job/task. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Restrict access until assignment submitted (before grade)
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle 3.5.6: I have a couple of conflicting requirements that are making some course design difficult for me. My course has about a dozen sections , each with a couple of assignments. I want to enable course completion for each assignment, and set it up so that the users pass the course when they get a passing grade in every assignment, which is easy enough. I also want to prevent users seeing the next course section until they have submitted their work for the previous section. I don't want the users to have to wait around until their work is graded before the next section unlocks, though - only once they submit work. Unfortunately these requirements conflict - as far as I can tell, there's no way to unlock activities when a user submits work to an assignment, only when the assignment is counted as completed. I can count the assignments as complete when work is submitted to it, but then course completion is messed up - users will pass the course regardless of their grades. ----- I hit on one possible solution - have the assignments set to complete when the user receives a passing grade, but also include a label resource under the assignments with the name "Tick this box when you have submitted your work to the assignments above to unlock the next course section" which unlocks the next course section. The only drawback to this is that it's explicitly obvious what's going on, and a user might go through the course ticking the boxes and unlock the entire course early. ----- The ideal would be a "restrict access until assignment X submitted" control - is anyone aware of such a control?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrict access until assignment submitted (before grade)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, That's a tough one. A variation on your idea would be to set that the assignments are complete when the file is submitted. Restrict access to the next section based on completion of the previous assignment At the bottom of the course page create a label and set it to manual completion. This label says something like "Tick here to confirm you have completed the course. Restrict access to this label as follows: 'Grade for assignment 1 is 40' AND 'grade for assignment 2' is 40 AND 'grade for Assignment 3' ... etc. Go to your course completion settings and set it that every activity is marked as complete for the course to be complete. Not perfect but it helps you restrict the access to the various sections and students cannot tick their way to marking themselves as complete. The only way they can tick that final box is by getting a passing grade in everything. Another method that would be more automated could be to use the 're-engagement plugin'. A caveat - I have used the re-engagement activity in the past but never in this way. With this method, forget about the final label set up the completion criteria as above. create your Re-engagement activity. Restrict access based on the grades (like the label above) Under completion settings, set the re-engagement time as 5 mins. Go to your course completion settings and set it that every activity is marked as complete for the course to be complete. Catherine

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrict access until assignment submitted (before grade)
ResponsesInList.Text: That's excellent, Catherine - I like that first solution a lot.

ResponsesInList.Title: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm rather new to Moodle, and only recently I started administering tests created as Moodle quizzes. I'm encountering a few issues, and I will post them in different threads so that they can be addressed independently. Let me add that Moodle is administered by my university's IT services, and I have no control over the installation (I may be able to request some modification/plugin installation, but I'm not sure of the answer). I also can't fine any information on the Moodle version. First issue I have is with the calculated multiple choice question type, which is the main question type I use. It is indeed very powerful. However, one big issue I'm encountering is the possibility (not that remote) that for a given set of random parameters, two calculated answers give the same value (or two values that look the same once rounded to the requested number of significant digits/decimal places). Of course this can be avoided by a (very) careful choice of formulas in the answers and parameters space, or by manually checking the answers corresponding to each random set of parameter. Both approaches are very time consuming and tiresome. On the other hand, it would seem easy to program Moodle so that to check for duplicated values in the answer resulting from a given random set of parameters, and discard it (or display a warning) if that's the case. Am I missing something? Does this functionality exists? If not, can it be implemented? Thanks Giacomo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: (Your IT services should be able to tell you the version of Moodle that you are using.) As a reference, I gave this presentation at a couple of MoodleMoots this year. MoodleMoot2019 (Global and Mountain), "Using Calculated Multichoice Questions" When you have Calculated Multiple Choice create the datasets, you should always look them over for duplicates. If you see a duplicate, you can manually change one of the input variable values and Moodle will then use the new value. As far as I know, there are no "automatic" checks. And there could be situations where you would want duplicates, perhaps because one set of input values are really desired to appear more frequently.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, thanks for your answer, and for the link to the presentation, which is very useful. Given that you confirm that there is no automatic check, I guess I should move to the tracker and submit a feature request there. Manually checking 100 datasets for each question I create (and I create 30 for each test) is not very practical, and extremely time consuming. Automatic checks, on the other hand, are what computers are good at...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Okay, I better understand your situation. I can give, perhaps, a simpler example. Assume that the question is "What is the area of this rectangle?" The correct equation is length x width. The incorrect equation is length + width. However, if length and width both equal 2, both of these equations produce the same result. So you want Moodle to "flag" you when two equations produce the same result, given some randomly generated input values. Well, interesting request. My guess is that you don't want Moodle to fix the problem. This would be up to the teacher. But you do want Moodle to show you ("flag") that your equations have produced two (or more) identical answers. Actually, I understand what you mean. I think that I was once caught by this kind of situation. So, I have learned to scan the answers and manually look for these problems. Maybe Tim Hunt is watching this conversation. He's the Moodle Quiz Engine guru, and a good guy. I wonder if he would think that flagging these situations, maybe with a red color, is easy to program. Sure, you can create a Tracker item for this (after searching to see if it already exists.) This is a good way to get your idea noticed. In my own case, I typically create questions with less than 25 or so "sets" of answers, so a manual scan is not that hard. And I wonder if Moodle did flag the dataset with duplicates, maybe with a red color, if it would really save much time since you would still need to look at the results? But sure, color or some other kind of mark (since color by itself might not meet " accessibility " guideline for colorblind folks) might be handy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Yep, you got it right, and your example is simpler than mine. Two comments: 1) I don't know if I completely agree that Moodle shouldn't correct the answers (where "correct" here means simply generate a new random set). One possibility: add a checkbox on the dataset generation page that says "avoid duplicated values". If that's checked, for every new dataset generated, Moodle checks if it results in duplicated answers. If it does, the dataset is discarded and a new one is generated. personally, I would use it all the time. 2) Even if one decides to not let Moodle "autocorrect" the dataset, there are plenty of ways of highlighting the problem in a way that is noticeable without scanning the datasets. For example, when new datasets are generated, if there are problematic ones a pop-up a window could appear pointing to their number

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Maybe so, but for #1, how does Moodle know that the instructor did not intend to have two correct answers? And the issue is with the person who created the questions. There could be situations where Moodle will not find a good dataset, and how many tries should Moodle attempt? For #2, Moodle is generating random values correctly. The error is with the equations. I am not saying that this can't be done. But I am wondering about the logic that a programmer would have to go through. If you make a feature request, try to provide a flowchart of the logic.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Rick, I guess you know by now that I like debate, but this time I don't really understand your objections. 1) not sure what having "two correct answers" has to do with "having duplicated answers", which is what I am talking about. And Moodle will know the intentions of the instructor, because he/she would have checked the "avoid duplicated values" option I'm proposing. Besides, if you think about it, there is really no real-life case in which you may want duplicated answers in a multiple choice calculated questions (if you can find one, please let me know). Also I ond't understand what you mena by "the issues is with the person who created the questions". If the issue is not wanting to spend an hours performing a mechanical check that a computer can do in a fraction of a second, well, I wouldn't call it an issue. If the issue is having chosen equations that can yield duplicated values for some combinations of the input parameters, believe me: avoiding this situation for a moderately complex physics exercise with parameters varying in a reasonable range is not a trivial mathematical problem. 2) I never said Moodle was in error. Nor I think it is correct to say that the equations are not correct. In fact, I don't think there is an error anywhere here. But there is something that can be done in an easier, faster and more reliable way, which is generating datasets that do not result in duplicated answers. Moodle's job is not (only) generating random numbers (one line of code in any common programming language is good enough at that), but it is (in this context ) to help create and administer viable and formally correct quizzes. Any task related with this activity that can be performed by a computer is in principle in Moodle's scope, and the one I'm proposing is one of these (and an easy one, even). As for the logic, the details can be discussed, but a baseline is pretty trivial. If the option to avoid duplicate answers is checked: A) set a counter C = 1 B) generate a set of parameters S C) Check if S results in visually identical answers (once rounded as requested) D) if is does not, S is good ad gets added to the dataset E) if it does not: F) if C is smaller than a given threshold (say 100), go to B) G) if C is equal to the threshold, display a message ("Unable to find an unambiguous set of parameters in 100 trials. Please check your answers and/or adjust the parameters range") and abort the operation. No black magic... and I bet that for a reasonably designed questions E) will happen a few times, but G) very, very rarely,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Giacomo, you are correct about #1. I wasn't making sense. No, Moodle isn't in error. We are brainstorming a better approach. Relative to the logic, maybe so. Maybe the message can show itself, but then we (the creator) will have to scan the 100 trials and see what is going on. There might be a clue about why we are getting duplicates. It should probably be left up to us what we want to do. We could, for example, delete all (as we can right now), or delete the last 10, and just regenerate 10. Alternatively, if we did let Moodle regenerate all, and if we didn't give Moodle enough flexibility, Moodle might be in some kind of infinite loop. I am not sure if we are debating this, rather just discussing a variety of methods and logic about your idea. 😀

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, I'm not a native speaker and maybe my use of the word "debate" is a bit off-target. "Discuss" sounds goo to me As for the logic, let me explain better. My (basic) proposal: - you ask Moodle to add N sets of parameters - for each one of them Moodle goes through the decision process outlined in my previous message. So 100, or whatever, in that case has nothing to do with N, it is just how many timea you want Moodle to keep trying, to see if you are lucky and find a set that works (in the sense of not giving duplicates). It is your "timeout" to avoid infinite loops. The higher that number, the lower that chances of a fail. - in the event of success, Moodle adds a set of parameters and repeats the procedure with the next set. - in case of failure, it shows the error message and stops wherever it is. - or, it stops when it has generated N sets. I'm fairly confident that only two things will happen in rel life: - the instructor mad a mistake in writing the equations, and two of them, although apparently different, always yield the same result: in this case the error comes up already when Moodle tries to generate the first set. - the equations/paramters range are such that the equations, although not identical, can sometime produce the same result. The above procedure should just be able, with very, very high degree of success, to reject the "accidental duplicates" and just go on. So, in practice, I expect that the instructur gets an error immediately, or never. However, the procedure should be robust in any case. It's true that I can think about ways of constructing (quite artificial) cases in which the duplicates happen not 100%, of the times, but often enough that Moodle may be successful in generating a few datasets and then fail later on. The procedure is however robust also in these cases: Moodle will save the sets it was able to generate before incurring into the error.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic check for duplicated questions
ResponsesInList.Text: I think that you are to the point where it is now worth it to create a Feature Request in the Moodle Tracker system. With the calculated multiple-choice question, the Moodle developers chose to create x number of datasets as a last step in the process and then left the burden of reviewing the dataset to the instructor.  At times, I have wondered why Moodle doesn't create the variable values "on the fly?"  Why specific datasets.  However, as I continue to use this question type, I have come to appreciate why the specific datasets are created... so that you are not caught with any surprises.  So I like the current method. As I have mentioned, I have been caught with the exact problem that you describe, so when I review my datasets and answers, I look for duplicate answers, and immediately fix them by typing in new values. Having some form of automatic check could be useful.  I am not the developer, so I am not sure how easy or hard some of this programming can be.  But I think that we have identified some techniques. Moodle is the only major LMS with calculated multichoice questions, a very powerful question type.

ResponsesInList.Title: Historical record of tests
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm faced with an "organizational" issue related to keeping an historical record of the quizzes I administer. I would like to: - completely "freeze" a test after it is closed (including any possible error I may have done in preparing it), just as a record. - keep track of which questions have been used in which quiz (this could be a functionality to be implemented regardless of the particular discussion here, with is broader) - be able to amend questions with errors/imprecisions (150 students taking a test are a rather good beta-testing team... and WILL find something that you overlooked) an reuse them in the future Currently, Moodle seems to have a mixed philosophy in this respect: it doesn't allow you to change which questions are in the quiz after it has been taken, but it does allow you to change the text, parameters and values of the questions themselves, which is kind of odd. When you look at a test, you have no guarantee that it is as it was given to the students, although you are guarantee that at least it has the same number of questions After thinking a bit about this, I came out with the following "manual" procedure: - I put all my questions in the "default" category - when I prepare a test, I create a question category with a name identifying the test. Then I make a copy of the questions I want to use and put them in that category. Those are not to be modified ever again. - if during the test a problem with a question arises, I go back to the question in the default category and correct it, ready to be used in a future test. It looks like this could work, but there are at least a couple of issues: - I can't use categories to classify questions. Maybe that's not too bad, since tags can probably serve the purpose just as well. - the amount of questions in the bank will grow substantially over time. I wonder if this could lead to performance issues further down the line. Is there a better way of doing this? Comments? Idea? Giacomo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Historical record of tests
ResponsesInList.Text: 1) You can "lock" a quiz in the grade book. 2) Not sure what you mean. The quiz always shows which questions it used. 3) Yes, you can do this. Just fix the question. If it is used again, the fixed question will be used. 4) Correct, you cannot remove or add questions once someone has taken a quiz. This seems logical. Yes, you can fix some kinds of quiz question errors, even while students are taking the quiz. You can also "regrade" these quizzes that have fixed questions. No other LMS is as powerful as Moodle relative to these features. 5) Organizing questions in the question bank takes some time to master. Moodle is the only major LMS that provides a powerful "question bank" database . 6) I am not sure that I would use your technique when I prepare my tests, but you can do what you are doing. I just don't know if it is really the best method. 7) See my response #4.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Historical record of tests
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, thanks gain for engagin with me. See my answers to some of yours: 1) If I understand this correctly, I can lock the votes, but if I change the text or values of the questions comprising the quiz, I will have lost what the students had originally been presented with. SO this doesn't really address what I'm concerned with here. 2) they do. But If I want to pick from my question bank questions that have not been used in, say, the past three quizzes, I have to go check them one by one. Instead, this information could be summarized in a more convenient way. I can think of several ways of implementing this. One could be for each question in the question bank to have an icon linked to a popup with the list of quizzes that use the question; another possibility is to provide a standalone table with questions on the rows, quizzes on the columns, and checkmarks to indicate if a question has been used in a quiz. 3) Again, if I do it this way, I will loose the information that the students, for that particular quiz, were presented with an incorrect question. I think I need to make a copy to keep that record. 4) I'm not sure that is all that logical to allow for modifying the questions, but not to add/remove questions. They don't seem fundamentally different actions to me: you are changing the quiz. Anyway, it is probably just a philosophical debate. Giacomo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Historical record of tests
ResponsesInList.Text: 1) Okay, you seem to want to make some changes but not fix the student's grade with the fixed question. You want to show the student the incorrect question and answer, but provide the student credit? Your request might be getting into the advantages and disadvantages of centralized versus decentralized content. I have used both methods for questions and quizzes (i.e., Blackboard versus Moodle). Yep, both different. However, I prefer Moodle's approach where I make a question improvement and it is immediately used throughout my quizzes.  Otherwise, managing "changes" becomes a major headache (maybe as you are describing.)  (I am one who has no problem fixing an electronic syllabus and not worrying about the many changes that I made throughout the course, or year.  As another example, if I had a digital textbook, I would want any errors immediately fixed instead of waiting for a new edition to contain the fixes.)  I am not saying there is a right or wrong way, I am just suggesting two different perspectives. So, in your case, if you freeze the quiz, how do you want to give the student credit? (Incidentally, my suggestion about locking the quiz does not address your need, sorry.) 2)  It appears that you are picking questions manually as opposed to letting Moodle randomly pick questions.  If so, you might need to write a custom SQL query for what you seek.  I am not the expert, but I don't think Moodle has any tool (yet) that allows one to ask "Tell me how many times the questions in this quiz category have been used?"  But this is the beginning of your custom SQL. 3) Perhaps.  When you "regrade" in Moodle, Moodle does a great job showing which students were presented with the corrected question. It shows their previous score, and the new score, quite clearly  Also,  when regrading, the instructor can decide which specific student quizzes get re-graded.  In my case, if the student's score goes up, I let this happen.  If it would go down, I don't let this happen, giving the student the benefit of my error. (If you have used other LMSs, Moodle's ability to regrade will come to you as a great surprise.  No other major LMS has Moodle's powerful re-grading feature.  Give it a try!) 4) I can't say that I agree with you.  If you add or remove a question, it is a different quiz.  If you fix an answer, it is just a fixed question.  In my case, I prefer to fix the question, regrade, and be done with it.  From this point forward, the fixed question will always be correct.  Incidentally, when I fix questions, I typically make a post letting students know what I have done.  Yep, they see that I am a human who makes mistakes.  But they also see that I am a human who corrects mistakes. Relative to this #4, there has been a time or two where I did make a mistake and wanted to add or remove a question.  What I did in these situations is to create a new quiz, use groups, and make it so that students who have not taken the quiz yet will see the new corrected quiz.  Yep, another Moodle technique, one that takes a little practice.  The instructor can even use this technique to some advantage, perhaps having 4 different quizzes and putting students into 4 different groups.  I probably have some folks already confused. All of my comments are not meant to be critical or anything like that.  I am just trying to participate in some of your ideas.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: student removed themselves??? Moodle 3.7
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Billy, Usually yes. I have had students unenrol themselves from courses in the past, and no problem when I re-enrol them into the course, bingo all their data is back. However, it can be that if you have cleared out caches, upgraded or performed some other sort of maintenance on your system, that the student becomes detached as it were from their course data. I tell students that they should not unenrol from courses without first asking the course tutor. In other more extreme cases, I have disabled the possibility for students to remove themselves meaning that the course tutor is the only person below admin who can perform that function. So if a student has removed themselves completely from Moodle, you might try to manually re-enrol them into Moodle, but without sending out any new login details, you set the "Send login information" to off when you do this. You will need to follow the format that you used previously precisely, and hope that Moodle still has the data cached. Unfortunately I do not know of any backdoor ways to reinstate users who have removed themselves. I hope that this helps you and good luck, please let us know if you succeed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to Change Maintenance text to own text?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, To change the maintenance mode text please go to Site administration > Language > Language customisation > Click on the "Open language pack for editing" button after choosing your language > Click on the "Continue" button when fully loaded your language pack > Select "admin.php" from "Show strings of these components" > Add the text "sitemaintenance" into "String identifier" field then click on the "Show strings" button > Then add your text into "Local customisation" field of the sitemaintenance String > When all done click on the "Save changes to the language pack" button. Thanks & Regards, Moumita

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: scheduled tasks & cron fail due to problem with "Background processing for gradebook"
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to check ... is your cron job running as the web service user? And ... ran into this once ... there is a lock directory in moodledata ... if cron job run as root user (was on a Linux box) and a task/job related to locks was created by that user, a later run of cron would throw some errors such as you've seen/shown here.  Files in moodledata/lock/ had ownerships by root user and web service user had issues. The lock directory is re-created automagically on cron job/task runs. So I manually removed the *contents* of the lock directory in moodledata and then manually ran cron as the web service user.   No issues.  And, strangely, never saw that error again on that system! 'SoS', Ken
