Any ideas? Many thanks, Jack

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Putting theme in "themes" folder doesn't do anything
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hey Jack, when installing Plugins / Themes on a file level, always check to adjust file permissions so the webserver-user (under Linux usually www-data) can read the files. In doubt just check the permissions on the parent directory and apply them to the new folder. Don't forget to do this recursively (replace everything within angle-brackets, including the brackets themselves): 
```text
sudo chown -R <user>:<group> <path/to/moodle>/theme/<ThemeFolder>
```
 
```text
sudo chmod -R <XXX> <path/to/moodle>/theme/<ThemeFolder>
```
 <XXX> is the permissions mask (e.g. 755), I hope the rest is self-explanatory, but don't hesitate to ask if you got questions. If you're not hosting on Linux, I'm all out of advice, since I got no clue as to what peculiarities might lurk on Windows servers. Greetings

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Putting theme in "themes" folder doesn't do anything
ResponsesInList.Text: Make sure.... - You have unzipped a folder, not the files. You don't say what theme it is but some plugins unzip with an incorrect name (e.g. moodle-theme_mytheme). You would need to rename that (moodle-theme_mytheme => mytheme). If you're stuck, tell us what the theme is. - Make sure the directory and all the files are readable by everyone. On Linux/Unix that would probably be 0755. But first! Switch on Debugging . Hopefully if something goes wrong you'll get a useful error message.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is it legal to embed Youtube video into H5P with interactions?
ResponsesInList.Text: In the US, there are caveats to fair use that make some exceptions for educational use. If you're not making money on it and it is being used for education...etc etc, it can (not necessarily is) be okay. I don't know about other places.  Of course, if it is one piece of a larger course you are charging for, the making money might get thorny. Other considerations: if you take the video and modify it to be something else, sometimes that falls under the umbrella of derivative works and may cover you. Or it may get you in trouble. Make sure you are attributing the original owner (be careful of youtube--I was asked to put a video in training that I found at least 10 different version of on youtube...eventually I found out the owner was a TV station...none of the youtube versions I saw were posted by them. I contacted them and got permission .) Some videos have enough information about the poster that you can reach out and get permission. I'd like to think most people aren't jerks. But reading comments on youtube (and news sites and all over the darned internet) makes me think this might be a bit optimistic. ResponsesInList.Title: SQL Server and query parameterization
ResponsesInList.Text:
Are there any other users who have Moodle running with SQL Server ? Very recently we've noticed our SQL Server 2014 database has been running out of memory. In trying to track down the problem we've noticed that the queries that Moodle executes aren't parameterized, and instead run as ad-hoc queries with parameter values
baked into the query text. Which we're not certain that this is the cause of our memory problems it seems reasonable that it's at least a contributing factor. Digging into the database code , there's a helpful comment that -- according to somebody from microsoft -- PHP's sqlsrv drivers don't
support parameterisation and so there's a hack in place to emulate this instead. This comment is 8 years old, and the concern it mentions with SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY() doesn't appear to be valid anymore as scope_identity is used elsewhere in the class, so we developed a patch for our test instance that binds the parameters properly into sqlsrv_query. Our initial tests indicate that this works, although we're reluctant to push it onto our production servers to see if it solves our memory issues for fear that we might accidentally mangle our data. Wrapping up, I have two questions: Are there any other Moodle users using SQL Server 2014 who've encountered this issue, and how did you fix it? Does anyone with a more intimate knowledge of the sqlsrv database class know if the comment re: parameters not working in sqlsrv is still relevant? If our patch does fix the problem, or at least improves the situation for sqlsrv users, I'm more than happy to submit a pull request. Additional data to prove I've read the stickied post: Moodle 3.7.2+ No error messages to speak of; Moodle simply doesn't connect to the db when it falls over SQL Server 2014 (12.0.5223.6) PHP-FPM (7.3.14-5) msodbcsql17 (17.5.1.1-1) Debian stretch (4.9.0-12-amd64)

ResponsesInList.Title: Disabling Notation Tex
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello! I am an administrator of a common moodle for several schools. Last week, I disabled "Notation Tex", only enabling "Mathjax" in order for the formulas to be displayed in the mobile app. Since this moment, moodle is very slow. We are not sure wether it is because of this parameter change. Has anyone ever disabled "Notation Tex"? Did it cause slowliness for you? And also, does anyone know the difference between Notation Tex and Mathjax and has a recommandation about witch filters should be activated? (I tried to understand the documentation but can't realy understand the difference: both seem to parse formulas written in tex and generate the correct image?) Kind regards, Fanny

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling Notation Tex
ResponsesInList.Text: I think the MathJax filter will be a bit slower than the TeX Notation filter. It looks like TeX Notation generates an image which can be cached by the browser but also by the web server .  With MathJax the browser additionally downloads JavaScript and some dependencies – also cached by the browser – and then converts the T E X source on the fly into HTML elements. In my tests course pages with a few formulas were about 25% slower to load with MathJax but it wasn't really noticeable, an increase from about 0.9s to 1.2s. You could try using any developer tools in your browser (e.g. Network Monitor in Firefox ) to see how long the pages take to load with the different filters enabled, and see if there are any large or slow dependencies MathJax is loading. Does this issue affect all pages or only pages with formulas? If it's only pages with formulas you could post the source here to see if the problem can be reproduced.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling Notation Tex
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you very much for answering! The whole service has become slower, not only the loading of pages with formulas. Unfortunatly changing now the activation of those filters don't improve the loading of pages. Another thing that we witnessed is an increasement of several gigas of the database . Again, we are absolutely not certain where it comes from and we are investigating the tex filters because we think it is the last operation we made before it became slow. Thanks again, it is very hepfull to understand how those filters work. Fanny

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Your browser offers limited or no support for WebRTC technologies yet, and cannot be used with this plugin.
ResponsesInList.Text: The reason for this is that you need an HTTPS connection to the server with most browser varieties for RecordRTC to be granted access to the mic and webcam. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Your browser offers limited or no support for WebRTC technologies yet, and cannot be used with this plugin.
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes its a bit of a hassle alright. You will need to generate a self signed certificate and then tell your teacher PC's web server to use it. When your student clients connect they will see an ugly message that the site they are accessing is insecure, and have to ignore the message and continue. Its not ideal. I might be possible to relax the browser imposed conditions. I am not sure about that. See here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34197653/getusermedia-in-chrome-47-without-using-https All around the best situation is to set up Moodle on a server with a public IP address and a DNS name and an SSL certificate. The one cunning work-around I can think of is: a) register a domain eg supermoodle.net b) register a wildcard SSL for that domain. You will probably need a public server somewhere to do this. c) set the dns for subdomain(eg teacherpc.supermoodle.net ) that you plan to use, to point to the local IP address of the teacher PC(eg 192.168.1.15) e) install the SSL certificate on your teacherpc web server I think this would work but its not super easy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suddenly none of my students can login
ResponsesInList.Text: Edit the config.php file with nano or TextEdit and add the following line: $CFG->enrol_plugins_enabled='manual,guest,self,cohort'; just after the following config line: $CFG->admin = 'admin'; Save file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suddenly none of my students can login
ResponsesInList.Text: Hmmmm ... seems admin of a Moodle is becoming more difficult! ;) In version 3.8.x, an admin user can review what changes have been made to the site by visiting  Site administration -> Reports -> Config changes or directly via browser:  https://site/report/configlog/ and a very handy, cli script in moodlecode/admin/cli/ is cfg.php Running from that directory: php cfg.php will show all settings. I use it now to redirect output to a text file like so: php cfg.php > settings.txt which will save to site/admin/cli/settings.txt One could then view that via browser by using URL line in browser: https://site/admin/cli/settings.txt and save it locally as a text file for later reviewing/archiving. All the settings there can be set by taking the first column info like 'enrol_plugins_enabled' and the values into a config.php file line: $CFG->enrol_plugins_enabled='manual,self'; as an example would restrict user enrollment to only manual and self. The trick is figuring out what values/settings to use. Nice thing about editing config.php, if one changes a config line added, it's easily reversable by commenting it out (// in front of the line) or changing the values as in above example one could add back 'guest'. No restart of services etc. required ... the next click in anything moodle the change is immediately in affect. Does kinda illustrate, however, that ssh access to moodle code to be able to edit config.php is becoming more and more a necessity/requirement to admin a moodle if running/admin a moodle of your own. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Courses with multiple sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Abdou, I don't know of a way to update multiple existing courses at once, but groups or upload courses might help if they fit your use case: Are the three sections for the same course content? By that I mean - Are you adding the same file to three different courses in Moodle? If so, are the three courses the same - are they copies of each other? If so, it might be easier/efficient to use three groups of learners in one course. The groups could be Section 1, Section 2, and Section 3. Then you add the file once and all three groups have access to it (while unaware that there are two other groups). If you do need three separate courses and the courses will not need to be updated after being created, you can create one course and use it as a template to create the others with Moodle's Upload Courses feature ( https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Upload_courses ). David

Ideally would've wanted to enroll a user to multiple courses at once through the whole category, rather than to each individual course. I am using Moodle 3.6 Anyone any clues PLEASE?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Category enrolment not marking course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: That is because in your scenario, Student is inherited, not assigned and you don't get grades with inherited roles. I would recommend cohorts (you could do this at the category level if you like) and then enroll the cohort. If you look at grades, the student shouldn't even show up on the list. I haven't tested this is 3.6 because I'm super happy category roles don't include student by default. I just never turned it on.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Category enrolment not marking course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Many thanks Melanie! I have to try that and see how to create the cohort and then the enrolling. This brought me some further question if you know. Do you know if it works both ways in the same time? I mean, for example... If Melanie and Alex are in cohort 1 and cohort 1 is enrolled to category 1, they can access all the 10 courses within category 1. But if we have John that is not part of cohort 1, can Bob still be enrolled separately to have access only to course 5 from category 1?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Category enrolment not marking course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Enrollments by category will not ever work satisfactory. Enrollment works for courses only. Category enrollment allows access but not actual activity or credit. This has been the case for the whole 15 years I've been working with Moodle. There are plenty of people around who have been around longer and will likely say the same thing. If I were assigned to Cohort 1, each course in Category 1 would need to have Cohort 1 assigned to it. If Bob is assigned to cohort 1 three weeks from now, he would automatically be assigned to all 10 courses because each course knows to enroll everyone in cohort 1. Or, if you only want Bob to attend one of those courses, you can have manual (or self) enrollment set to allow that. If you enroll me by cohort, I cannot unenroll. If you enroll me manually, I cannot unenroll. If I self enroll, I can unenroll. As for cohort enrollment, you can always have multiple cohorts which can include the same people. Cohort 1 could be everyone who needs 10 courses from Category 1. Cohort A could be everyone who needs course 1 and course 5 from Category 1. And Cohort 1a could be people who need course 5 from Category 1 and Course 3 from Category 2. And I could be assigned to Cohort 1 and 1a. Removing someone from a cohort will remove their enrollment from all the relevant courses. No, you can't limit viewing of categories by cohort (or by anything, really) but if you set it to show the dashboard , if someone is in a cohort which enrolls them in 10 courses, those 10 courses will show on their dashboard.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Category enrolment not marking course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: You could prevent course categories from displaying on Site Home and put links to categories there instead with restrictions to profile fields or maybe cohorts (if the cohorts were site level, not category level). This wouldn't block the categories from being seen (bread crumbs might still have them, depending on settings) but it would limit availability.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrading to https - Lost all internal links
ResponsesInList.Text: When I checked your site, it showed using LetsEncrypt for certs.  In their recommendations, once cert files are acquired and site is responding, they recommend setting up a redirect so that any request ... http:// or https:// headed to your site is automagically changed to https://. That's an extremely good idea these days considering more and more attacks via web are on the rise.  Many site providers now offer a CDN (CloudFlare) which is both for caching and for protection.  Many strongly suggest setting up a WAF (web application firewall) like mod_security that sits in front of any web based application ... WordPress, Joomla, and even Moodles could use the 'extra protection'. Would strongly suggest *NOT* using option https for login only ... make your site 100% https and be done with it. The httpsreplace tool I think was designed for moodle sites that had originally been set up using http:// ... there fore all *internal* links inside of Moodle would use the CFG variable for the site (http://youresite/ to build/concactate ALL internal links.   The search then, if site was functioning as http://site/ should have been search for 'http://yoursite/' ... note the protocol in front and the 'trailing slash'.   Replace with 'https://yoursite/' ... again ... note the protocol in front and the 'trailing slash'. And a caution ... before your next attempt, make sure you have an SQL dump - date/time stamp the sql dump file names if site is functioning as http://.  You could in-advertently have a messed up sql dump and restoring it could complicate the issue.   Such that your ONLY alternative is to use a true text editor ... NOT Word or other like it ... but a *true* text editor (like nano on CentOS) to search for all links 'http://site/' and replace with 'https://site/' ... then use that raw edited sql file to import into a new DB for the moodle. My $100.00 tip! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Course enrollment maximum date - not beyond Dec 31 2020
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, We just realized our course enrollment date maxes out at Dec 31, 2020. How would we go about updating this? Version: Moodle 2.5+ (Build: 20130524) Thank you Jordan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course enrollment maximum date - not beyond Dec 31 2020
ResponsesInList.Text: I suspect your underlying problem is: Version: Moodle 2.5+ (Build: 20130524) If you have access to your Moodle server , then you may be able to fix it (and I am doing this from memory) in the Moodle > admin > settings directory there is a file called "server.php". I think the setting you're looking for is in there, you can edit it and that should relieve your immediate problem, BUT, it may be another file altogether, so you may have to go looking for it. IF you don't have access to editing on your server, then the other option is to update. The other problem you have is that you do not have an upgrade policy. Seriously? That is such a no-no. I suggest that you set up a test Moodle using v2.5+, if you can still get it. Backup your database and use the backup to populate your new test Moodle. Download a v2.7+ then install, test to make sure it's all working. Then repeat using v2.9+, then with v3.1+ then v3.3+ then the latest v3.5 then to v3.7 latest. Once you have a modern Moodle setup and working, either replace the source code, moodledata directory and database with the updated one or redirect to the update site as your production Moodle. If you're using custom or additional plugins, look for replacements or updates or even similar plugins for those you use and update those as you go. You will not be able to go from v2.5+ to 3.8.x in one step without risking severe damage to your database. You also should be talking to the powers-that-be to make sure your site is updated once per year, during the longest break in your year not to the latest, but the one before the latest, version. This won't guarantee smooth sailing all the time, but you have a much better opportunity of vastly reduced problems when updating if you keep your Moodle relatively positioned to the latest version.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum messages not send. Fixed !
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Ken. Problem fixed ! Checking the Scheduled task Logs and running manually the cron , I could see that the cron stopped at Site Register (core\task\registration_cron_task) and after disable it, stopped at Refresh RSS feeds task (\block_rss_client\task\refreshfeeds) . - So, I executed the cron manually again after disabling the two tasks with problems , and all the process ran successfully!. - I enabled the core\task\registration_cron_task ran the cron, and checked everything runs ok. - And I finally enabled the other task \block_rss_client\task\refreshfeeds and everything started to work normally. So the problem was with some tasks not running properly. Thanks a million Ken and everyone with the help provided. Good day !.

ResponsesInList.Title: 2 related courses. One mandatory for all and the second only for some
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, we need to configure two courses that have these characteristics: 1st course Required for two groups Group A - Doctors Group B - Nurses and other carers 2nd course Required for two groups Group B - Nurses and other carers Group C - Doctors who have a specific specialty. It would be a part of group A of 1st course and defined by the user himself, based on his specialization (this data is absent in the user profile in Moodle). We would like to create a relationship between the two courses and above all, at the end of the 1st course, to define with a few questions to the user, who from Group A will have to participate in the 2nd course. We thought of doing this: At the end of the 1st course, members of group A must complete a questionnaire with the lesson activity and based on the answer they will be directed to the respective page which will show: a- If they fall into the category that the second course must do, they will have the link to enroll in 2nd Course in the Doctors group. b- If they do not fall into the category that the second must do, they will have finished their course. In the 2nd course the first activity will be Group choice where the user will choose whether to belong to the Doctors or Nurses and other carers group. We chose this solution because we can manually enroll all users in the 1st course on the basis of the profile, but in the 2nd course we need an information that only the user has, to decide whether he must do the 2nd course as well, we cannot define it. Anyone have other ideas?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2 related courses. One mandatory for all and the second only for some
ResponsesInList.Text: Ray's suggestion may work, although two enrollment keys for one course, I've never tried it, my requirements are just not that explicit. However, I would think of using course meta links before anything else. Essentially, if I'm reading this right, you have 2 courses and three groups, 2 for nurses and carers and for specialist doctors, 1 course for other doctors. Set up courses as parents with all information, assignments and everything, but no enrollments, identifying each course as a metacourse. Set up three courses as child courses, with enrollments only in the groups determined by the requirements so that Child Course A contains Nurses and Carers, Child Course B contains Doctors who are not specialists Child Course C contains only Specialist Doctors 1. Child Courses A, B and C all connected to Course 1. 2. Child Courses A and C connected to Course 2. The above link has more detail on how this actually works. Just if you're using self enrollments, then make sure you label and title the course that they are supposed to enroll in properly so there is no confusion, but I am sure you can work it out. There are other considerations, of course, like Teacher, grading methodologies, assignment assessments and so on that might make this structure too unwieldy, for one Teacher, in which case you might just use keys or Groups maybe, but you might want to look at it and see if it can be applied elsewhere.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: Re: 2 related courses. One mandatory for all and the second only for some
ResponsesInList.Text:
So, the Group A users needs to figure out whether or not they belong in Group C, by answering some questions. If I understand correctly, right now, the path to Course 2 for Group C members is: 1. Fill out the questionnaire at the end of Course 1 2. At the end of the questionnaire: copy the enrollment key and click the link to Course 2 3. Paste the enrollment key 4. Click the enroll button, and begin using the course They need to do #1, since you do not know it, and they need to answer specific questions for figure it out themselves. If you need to direct them to a new course, then they need to click a link at some point (part of #2). Even the Group B people need to navigate to the new course by finding it in their list of courses, or clicking a link that you put in Course 1. That means that #1 and #2 are mostly unavoidable . So the question is: can you get rid of 3 & 4 somehow , so that Group C people only need to click a link at the end of the questionnaire? That is basically the experience that Group B people have (just clicking a link to go to their course). If I am correct up to this point, then I would personally stop and consider: are steps 3 & 4 really that burdensome? Of course, I support end-users with similar tasks, and some people will somehow have problems with those steps, so I understand. The question is: is that support more or less work than maintaining a different solution? Another question is: what is the point of using the enrollment key? I am mostly asking that for my own purposes, to make a point: you do not want the course to be open to just anyone (self enrollment) who can see the normal course link in the sitewide list of courses. So, Group C needs to be able to let themselves into the course, but you do not want to leave the door open for everyone. Can you automatically mark them at the end of the questionnaire, or is it just easier to give them a key (tell them a simple passphrase)? Can you give them a specially generated link, or can the questionnaire automatically enroll them in the course somehow? Something like that would then prevent them from needing to copy and paste the enrollment key. I tried thinking of some other options, like perhaps some usage of the "Course completed enrolment" plugin, or maybe some scheme of an " LTI External tool" pointing at a "Publish as LTI tool" instance (not even sure if this is possible, since it would be using parts of the same Moodle site as a consumer and provider). There may be other enrollment plugins that could achieve this, but now you (administrator) need to keep track of a third-party plugin. Those just felt like they added an unreasonable amount of complexity, or would create other ways that the students could get confused. https://moodle.org/plugins/enrol_coursecompleted I guess the only real change would be: do you want to manually enroll
Group C people in the course? Is it just one cohort of people at a time?
Could they do the questionnaire in a Google Form, you download the results one time, and do a manual enrollment for Group C based on
those results? That means they need to wait for you to put them in
Course 2, which is a tradeoff. If you have rolling enrollments (people
coming into the course throughout the year), then this solution would
probably be too much work for you. My conclusion: if you map out the exact steps for Group C people, and compare them to the Group B people, then you can figure out what part of the process is more complicated, and whether or not it is practical to simplify it. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error in Moodle 3.8 when inserting new user
ResponsesInList.Text:
When you configured your database server did you follow the my.ini recommendation as per here: https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/MySQL Add the following settings to the configuration file: 
```text
[client]
default-character-set = utf8mb4

[mysqld]
innodb_file_format = Barracuda
innodb_file_per_table = 1
innodb_large_prefix = 1

character-set-server = utf8mb4
collation-server = utf8mb4_unicode_ci
skip-character-set-client-handshake

[
mysql
]
default-character-set = utf8mb4
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How best to post issues in tracker.moodle.org
ResponsesInList.Text: Separate issues should be posted as separate issues. Make sure you explain *in detail* (step by step) how to reproduce your reported problem. A bug is something that produces incorrect or unexpected behaviour. Otherwise, it's a feature suggestion. If it's a grey area then just pick one. It can be changed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How best to post issues in tracker.moodle.org
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for this. Fun fact for future reference: There's a limit of 1 issue post per hour, so don't do like me and write all of your issues and do all of your research and plan on inputting all of them at once.

ResponsesInList.Text: There is? While I enjoy a good bug, I've never managed to find them at that sort of rate. I'm not sure if this is the case this time but some things in the bug tracker are 'reputation' related. Once it becomes clear that you are not a spammer it might improve.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How best to post issues in tracker.moodle.org
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't know if that's the best structure of a report in Moodle Tracker , but that's what I do when I report a bug: 1) Repro steps - detailed steps with information about the process that the user needs to follow in order to produce the bug. 2) Expected results - What should be the right behaviour of the system, in my opinion. Should be be a brief and clear text as possible. 3) Actual results - What is the actual and wrong behaviour of the system, in my opinion. Should be be a brief and clear text as possible. 4) Description/Problem - A detailed explanation about the nature of the problem, what should be done and etc. For example: MDL-66174 ("Annotate PDF - The width of the stamps menu is too big")

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How best to post issues in tracker.moodle.org
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh, and of course it always helps to attach a relevant screenshot or screenshots, and sometimes even a video that demonstrates the issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copy courses and / or course activities
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Stefan, Have you seen the option of Upload courses ( Moodle docs : https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Upload_courses ), where you can basically use a CSV file to create courses from templates? You'd have to create a csv with the following required fields: 
```text
fullname, shortname, category
```
 Additionally, you can add templatecourse (shortname of course functioning as a template) to your CSV so all duplicates created from each template will be filled with corresponding course content. The only thing you can't do with the Upload courses CSV file, is creating new categories. This is something you'd have to do manually. Following this approach, you don't have to go through backup-restore manually for each course. Instead, it's a matter of making sure the CSV file contains the correct references. Also, using this approach, you don't have to worry about incidentally including enrolled user data in the course backup. To conclude: Do not include an Announcements forum in your templates. Also, remove any blocks from the template courses, that are created as default for the course. Doing this should prevent having duplicates of these in all copies.

Then click the link for, Copy to Sharing Cart. Go to the course where you want to copy to. Make sure you have a Sharing Cart block there, and you will see the contents you have added. Click the, Copy to course, toolbutton. Pick where you want the contents to go.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Uploading of photos
ResponsesInList.Text: Please do not provide too much in the way of detail, exactly what is going wrong, what error messages you might be getting, anything like that. Chances are though that you are running into upload limits. There are three upload limits for Moodle. One is set by the Server itself. Usually this is the least problematic but you may want to look at the httpd.conf file for a Linux server or the win.ini file for a Windows server, and no idea what it is in a Mac server, if anyone still uses one. Check to see of there are any limits on uploaded file sizes and change them if needed. On a hosted Moodle this should not be an issue at all, but you may want to ask. The second part is the php.ini file. Open it for editing these settings, make sure that the limits you have set are large enough to accomodate the files you want uploaded. For example: Php setting. max_execution_time = 600 post_max_size = 1000M upload_max_filesize = 1000M should give you plenty of size limits for your uploads, 1gb of size actually. Lastly, for inside the Moodle, go to Site Admin > Security > Site Security Settings and check that the uploaded file size settings have been changed to reflect the php.ini settings if you have changed them. If not, go to the server root directory and do a search for php.ini files across the entire server, you might be surprised at what you find.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Not in edit settings, but you can do it by adding custom CSS in your theme configuration. ResponsesInList.Text: Justin and Howard have provided good responses, which I agree with. Keep in mind that Moodle has the ability to duplicate resources and activities , so consider creating some "templates" for these, with all appropriate settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Importing a blackboard course into Moodle (Very Urgent  - pls help)
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with Howard, rebuilding is the better solution. I did this some 9 years ago now whilst working in a college. We migrated a modest Blackboard installation into Moodle, it was over 50 courses. What we found was that most of the courses were resource heavy (I.e documents) so we were able to drag and drop these into new Moodle courses. For everything else we just copied and pasted. It took a couple of weeks with just 2 of us working on it alongside the day job. Moodle courses and Blackboard courses are complete opposites in terms of look, feel, layout and to be honest, your courses will be all the better for it. Even if there was a magic bullet to pull everything in from Bb, you would probably spend longer refactoring everything and making it look right. Plus you get to prune the course and drop outdated content. I hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't switch user account from manual to LDAP
ResponsesInList.Text: Are the LDAP username same formats as Manual users? like bob.jones or email addresses bob.jones@somenet.net? In set up of LDAP there are field mappings which also has an option for checking ... once upon every login, etc.  As well as 'locked'.   Have you looked at those settings? Since there is only 3-4 consider editing mdl_user table directly IF this isn't an annual type 'swing' ... ie, you won't be doing this manual -> LDAP thang in future. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't switch user account from manual to LDAP
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you tried to use a csv bulk upload to overwrite it? It seems like I remember something like that happening occasionally in 2.5 a long time ago but don't remember the solution...are you changing the username in the same account edit as the authentication change? If so...that won't work. You have to change the username, save, edit again and then apply the authentication change and save. That might be what I'm remembering... to do the bulk upload, download all the accounts you need. If the download includes the auth column (it might not), change it from manual to ldap. If it doesn't, add a column at the beginning of the spreadsheet and put auth in A1 and ldap (all lowercase) in for all the students that need the change. Make sure the usernames are consistent with the names in the active directory. Then upload the file, making sure to enable changes and to update usernames. I would second Ken's suggestion to verify the username is consistent with what is in your active directory and to check the mapped/locked fields.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't switch user account from manual to LDAP
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, I think this is the bug you are describing. https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-66071 If can update your site to a more recent version of 3.7 that should resolve it. In the short run, either update your users with a CSV file or use the workaround described here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=389147#p1568797

I have tried changing the password (even dropping her to a regular user too) but Moodle does not seem to take the password change (certainly no records on the logs of it). When I check the logs as to why, Moodle says the following: "Login failed for user '-----------'. User is suspended (error ID '2')." ----- was put in to hide the user id info. The error code is for suspension... but the user is not suspended at all.  I've even suspended the account, saved and unsuspended it (just in case), still no difference. I've also tried changing the password, but Moodle won't take it even though it saves the profile (Logs show no change in password). I did have one similar case on our old installation but I could change their password and they could login... but it wouldn't allow a password change. Other users, including myself have had no issues logging in. Please help with what has happened and how I might be able to fix this user account. Jayden

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Exisiting User Can't Log In - Moodle Moved Locations
ResponsesInList.Text: This happens when the authentication method for that user is disabled. Go to 'Edit profile' for that user and check 'Choose an authentication method' if (as I'm guessing it isn't) it's not 'manual' go to Site administration > Plugins > Authentication > Manage authentication and make very sure that method is enabled and configured (and working). As an aside, I would strongly recommend having a dedicated accounts for Admins (that is actual Moodle admins) and they should definitely use manual accounts. Don't elevate ordinary users to Admin level. Manager is for that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: what is really in moodledata session folder ?
ResponsesInList.Text: By default PHP stores 'session' information in files. Moodle redirects them to this location. Session information is, strictly speaking, stuff that is loaded to PHP's magic $_SESSION variable. This is all sorts of things. Significantly, the user information that confirms that you are logged in (and lots of other things). If you delete that information everybody gets logged out. You definitely don't need to back it up.

ResponsesInList.Title: Deleting or fixing a broken course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all When we were on version 3.3 a teacher mistakenly added 320,000 topics to a course. This broke access for all students and teachers assigned to this course, both directly and to the dashboard . We quickfixed it with direct links to all the other courses the students were assigned. I have upgraded the platform to 3.7.1 and PHP to 7.2 and had hoped that it would fix the issue but alas. I have tried increasing the memory_limit to 4096MB and this is enough to show me the course in course management. But when I try to open the course I get an HTTP error 500. When I try to delete it I get an empty page with "Deleting". I found a CLI tool to delete courses, this returns the attached error. I have run out of ideas, any suggestions? Regards Mads

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Deleting or fixing a broken course
ResponsesInList.Text: Error has to do with recyclebin. When deleting a course your moodle actually makes a backup of the course and tags that course backup as being in the recyclebin for future deletion from the moodle. Since it has the number of sections it does: Suggest manually removing any folders/files found in moodledata/temp/backup/.  Especially after failed attempt to delete the course. "Error while sending QUERY packet." Packets might be too large for DB. Since cannot view the course ... cannot make a backup of it via GUI ... and probably also from cli (moodlecode/admin/cli/backup.php with course ID option and destination out side of moodledata - (did you try that?), this might require direct manipulation of database ... never a first option ... and should be test on a development copy of site.  Or, at least a copy of the DB for the moodle, first. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Deleting or fixing a broken course
ResponsesInList.Text: Follow up ... 1st - make a backup of your database. Did some experimenting with a 3.7 sandbox site ... Mouse over the link to the problem course to see/get the course ID number. Write that down. make a sql dump of database import the dump to a new database - like moodletest put site in maintenance mode edit config.php file and duplicate the DB name line. comment out original DB name line - // in front edit the duplicated line to point to your moodletest From the mysql client of server : use moodletest select * from mdl_course_sections where course = #; where # is the course ID number you wrote down. In this example, am using 3. The above query will should result in a long listing with column headings of: | id | course | section | name | summary | summaryformat | sequence | visible | availability | timemodified | The maximum number of sections should be 52. To remove sections above 52 delete from mdl_course_sections where (course = 3 and section > 52); Leave your mysql client window open. Open site with browser and attempt to go to the course. Fingers crossed ... you will be able to enter the course and make a backup of it. If successful, you can replicate the actions on the true database for moodle. Re-edit config.php and comment out the moodletest line ... // in front. Remove the // from in front of the original DB name. Anyone else having a different/better Idea as to how to fix, please jump in! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Display of Upcoming events block by lang
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kanji Syuto, This is probably not a block issue, but has to do with the following: Unless you're using the multilang filter option, any user generated text will be displayed in the language used by the user who created it. If the courses have been created in Japanese, the course and activity names will be displayed in Japanese. For the Moodle site to behave in a more multilingual fashion, you'd need to set up and activate the Multilang filter (site administration > plugins > filters > manage filters > multi-language content). After this, you can add custom HTML to show Japanese, English and Mandarin / Cantonese text where you need to, following the instructions found in Moodle Docs : https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Multi-language_content_filter Also, @moderators, a move to General Help forum would make more sense

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Display of Upcoming events block by lang
ResponsesInList.Text: Another possibility is that the string in the English Language pack is either unavailable or may have been customised. Either way, I suggest you do the following to check: Go to Site administration > Languages > Language Packs and click "Update all installed language packs." Next, go to Site administration > Languages > Language customisation and choose English. Open the pack, then select assign.php etc and search for customised strings.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eman You write: "We need to build a test directed according to the student's choice, ie when the student chooses an answer, he will get some random questions from a question bank." ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Questions as Per the Student's Choices
ResponsesInList.Text: Good points made, Kees! If Questionnaire is used, there's the option of conditionally branching questions. On the other hand, Questionnaire doesn't allow pulling random questions from the question bank, as the mod uses its own system for creating and managing questions and question types. If the choices are limited to a predefined set, you could consider creating specific course groups for each choice and then do the following: create a preliminary activity (mod_groupchoice) where students would have to make a choice based on the group selected by the student, they get access to 1 or more Quiz activities (restrict access, restriction set to hidden unless participant qualifies) the Quiz activities pull their questions from the question bank based on your criteria for random questions (tag or category based)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Questions as Per the Student's Choices
ResponsesInList.Text: Maybe you create a quiz with one question (the key question) with each answer being worth different amounts and then several quizzes, each set to restrict visibility and access based on a grade on the first quiz. Add a link on the first quiz in the overall feedback that links to the appropriate quiz. So...Quiz 1, group selection. Quiz 2, random selection of questions from question bank A + only visible if quiz 1 grade = 1. Quiz 3, random selection of questions from question bank B + only visible if quiz 1 grade = 2. Quiz 3, random selection of questions from question bank C + only visible if quiz 1 grade = 3....

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Questions as Per the Student's Choices

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questions as Per the Student's Choices
ResponsesInList.Text: Question 1, yes that's what I mean Question 2, I tried the questionnaire, it doesn't provide question banks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questions as Per the Student's Choices
ResponsesInList.Text: The solutions proposed by Joost and Melanie are close to a possible solution. In both cases you ask one question (or several questions). A score follows that determines which follow-up quiz will be offered to you. 1. You cannot do it in one session via the 'test' activity. No conditional follow-up questions are possible within one test. 2. The 'questionnaire' activity is a good option but it does not extract random questions from a question pool. 3. The ' lesson ' activity is a possibility if you have enough time to work it out glimlach. Setting up a lesson with all kinds of jump conditions is not easy and afterwards it is quite static. 4. Take the test in two rounds. First have a choice made with groupchoice (have a question answered) or generate a score with a short test of one or more questions. That choice or score then determines the subsequent choice. Within the 'test' activity you can also include a link in the final feedback (between 0 and 30%: link 1 | between 30 and 60%: link 2 etc.). Good luck! And if you are flying another route, I would like to hear which it is; I like to learn! Regards, Kees Koopman

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Notify Admin when new course is created
ResponsesInList.Text: You'll want to create an event monitoring rule and subscribe to it

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Notify Admin when new course is created
ResponsesInList.Text: I tried this but it seems like I'm not receiving the notifications (both on the website as well as the email ones). I read somewhere that it has to do with cron.php not being run in the scheduled tasks. But I can't tell which one of the scheduled tasks is the one to use, any clues?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Notify Admin when new course is created
ResponsesInList.Text: As John said above, event monitoring is what you need. This is a two-step process, 1st you need to Create the rule (done in Site Administration > Reports > Event Monitoring); 2nd, any user who wants to receive notifications needs to Subscribe to the rule (done from the User menu > Preferences > Miscellaneous > Event Monitoring). See https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Event_monitoring for more info. Now, if you have the rule created but are not receiving notifications, you might have a problem with cron. Just to clear something up, you said "...has to do with cron.php not being run in the scheduled tasks". Actually, scheduled tasks are run as part of cron's execution. So in short, no cron = no scheduled tasks. The easiest way to check if you have cron problems is to go to Site Admin > Notifications. Moodle will tell you if cron hasn't been run recently or is being run with less than optimal frequency. Finally, email notifications will not work if the site is incapable of sending emails at all. This may be worth checking if everything else seems right. Also, individual message settings may be set to NOT send emails for Event Monitoring (when logged in, click the bell icon at the top of the page and then the cog icon on the notifications panel  .)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CSS Selectors for User Tours
ResponsesInList.Text: As a very simple answer (and thus not 100% accurate) it's generally safer to go by CSS class and not id when specifying a selector. CSS selectors that begin with a # refer to the id attribute in the markup. However, the id may be different depending on the user. On the other hand, classes (usually beginning with a period . ) Are more commonly used to all users. So, I recommend you setup tours that use CSS classes as selectors instead of ids.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't open my Moodle site
ResponsesInList.Text:
The browser requests to your site getting the blank page are still getting a 200 OK response from your web server. However, it looks like Nginx will behave like this if it gets a response from PHP-FPM regardless of whether that response is an error or not . So I'd start by enabling debugging by adding the following lines to config.php : 
```text
@error_reporting(E_ALL | E_STRICT); // NOT FOR PRODUCTION SERVERS!


@ini_set('display_errors', '1');    // NOT FOR PRODUCTION SERVERS!


$CFG->debug = (E_ALL | E_STRICT);   // === DEBUG_DEVELOPER - NOT FOR PRODUCTION SERVERS!


$CFG->debugdisplay = 1;             // NOT FOR PRODUCTION SERVERS!
```
 Don't forget to remove these when the issue is resolved. You might also want to make the display_errors PHP-FPM change in the above linked StackOverflow article, my knowledge of Nginx+PHP-FPM isn't comprehensive enough to describe the steps in full. Did you check the permissions on config.php as Ken suggested? What are they (e.g. ls -l config.php )?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Migration - FULLTEXT error
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, Les ... you are about to dive into DB server admin! While you've given OS/Panel info, what is version of DB server software on old host ?  Ditto on DB server you are migrating to? It also sounds like you are attempting migration (moving to another server) and upgrade in one swoop.  It's generally best to migrate (move) so that new server is running same version of Moodle first, then upgrade.  But that could mean running older versions of PHP and/or MySQL + changes to MySQL config on new server.   So you might be in a double whammy situation. Specifically ... what's the old server's Moodle version?  Know you've mentioned you have more than one version now, but which version are you trying to migrate? Do you have command line access in old server? (ssh) ... maybe an icon in Plesk? Reason ... in moodle code/admin/cli/ there are some command line only scripts that do work with the DB character set, collation, etc.  If one might be able to fix on old host before attempting 'migration' (moving) to new server environment, new server might not complain! Yes, I know ... don't like command line and you've never had to use it ... up to now! :|  Now, however, you have a reason and purpose to do so. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Migration - FULLTEXT error
ResponsesInList.Text: Depending upon answers there might exist a 'plan B' that avoids migration of sites ... How many courses do you have in each Moodle on old? If looking at 'plan B', be sure in the new Moodle's have the same updated plugins installed prior to attempting import of courses. Also, if going the 'plan B' route, try to avoid account conflicts a head of time ... the super user of old sites have not been setup as teachers in old courses. There is also a 'plan C' ... which might be even more involved ... but I'll spare ya for now! (involves installing a localhost ... on your workstation first).  Now that I've mentioned that ... am almost certain a few might jump in here with their suggestions! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recycle bin failing, can I delete mdl_task_adhoc records with large fail delay 86400 ?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not familiar with the exact error you're getting, but if there's an exception thrown when processing an adhoc task that will cause the fail delay doubling (up to a maximum of 24 hours), and crashing the rest of the cron. You'll need to figure out exactly why the error's being thrown. It might be that the thing that's trying to be deleted no longer exists, or there's an actual coding error - perhaps you need to update your plugins. One thing I've done in the past is change the nextruntime and faildelay values to push the things that are broken out of the way, and let the things that will work do their thing. e.g. change the nextruntime to 1st August 2019 (whatever that is in Unixtime). This buys you time to figure out what's going on without holding up other things. ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle send mail via mail server or mail domain ? Is that ok to send email by domain shared hosting without internal mail server ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle send mail
ResponsesInList.Text: Interesting. Currently there is a surge of enquiries related to Moodle e-mails (^1). It is also interesting to watch something as simple as plain e-mail can get so complicated. Anyway, I'll try to put it simple terms: a. Moodle is an e-mail creator (amoung many other things). You can compare it to the part of Thunderbird where you write e-mails. b. Similar to Thunderbird Moodle also needs the help of a SMTP server for its outgoing e-mails. You set it in Site administration > Server > Email > Outgoing mail configuration, SMTP. Now comes the confusing part. Although one talks of "SMTP host " as it being a separate machine, Moodle only needs a _service_, which can handle this job. And that service uses a different port, typically 25 or 587, which are different from the ports Moodle serves, the ports 80 and 437. In other words the "SMTP host" could be the localhost. The condition is that it runs a SMTP service like Exim and Postfix. Now to the second confusion. If the SMTP hosts (smtphosts) field of Moodle is empty, which is the default, it internally assumes localhost! So people are surprised to find Moodle sending e-mails although "no SMTP server is configured". To make matters worse, there are wrong documentation somewhere and wrong advice given here, saying that there is a SMTP server built in to Moodle! Long story short,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Admin users can't open the site

I don't know PostgreSQL but other DBMSes allow you to see queries that are being run. If you can do this when few or no other users are logging in that will reduce the number of queries to be checked. The Apache error logs may be recording an error when the 504 Gateway Timeout occurs so check this. It may help to turn debugging on in Moodle temporarily (but don't leave it on). Using your browser's tools may (e.g. Network Monitor in Firefox ) may give you some clues by showing which particular HTTP request is failing and exactly after how long. E.g. if it fails after 120s then there maybe a 2-minute time-out that's being exceeded somewhere. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error restoring course

Moodle is evolving all the time and, I suspect, the database changes, slightly, between versions, but this can accumulate. Some changes are security related, some are more efficient tables, some introduce a new element, so the code is likely calling APIs that are looking for database elements that are different, or no longer exist or do not exist yet in your database. Seriously suggest you install on your test site something like v3.3 then restore and backup, then v3.5, then restore and backup, then v3.7 to restore. As a general policy, I have always used my test Moodle to do these things first and I have not interrupted my production sites. ResponsesInList.Text: Debugging should show to the moodle screen when using moodle and there is an error. What log file?   Most linuxes have logs in /var/log/ ... your server probably has an apache2 directory and in there whatever log files you've defined in config of apache2. Exception: php-fpm/cgi setup might be set up to create error log files (error_log) in the code directory where the error occurred.  So to find which directory might have one, cd /path/to/code/ then issue find ./ -name error_log That command should show you paths to all error_log files found.  Then you could cat them ... cat ./path/error_log Uploading of files via php could use an operating system tmp directory for uploading and then code moves that tmp file to whatever location ... see if you have files in /tmp/ that begin with 'php'. In php.ini there are 2 settings related ... upload_max_filesize and post_max_size they should be same value (technically that's not correct but ....) Location of moodledata ... I tried to explain that apache user has a 'home' directory and with LSB distro's that's normally /var/www/ Directories located in /var/www/ are accessible to apps but not directly via browser.   Where you put moodledata is kinda up to you because it is still necessary to set ownerships and permissions.  I, personally, find it easier to put moodledata in /var/www as I have just one path to do massive backups. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Hiding participants with specific roles from the participants list of a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, TL;DR - Is it possible to entirely hide participants with specific roles from the participants list of a course? Let's say that I don't want the students in a course to know that an academic staff member (with a specific role)  that is a participant in that course. I know about two relevant settings: Site Administration -> Security -> Site security settings -> "Profile visible roles" setting Site administration -> Users -> Permissions -> Define roles -> "Allow role to view" tab However, it seems that even if both of them are turned off for that role, the student, the students still see the staff member in the participants list, just with the value "No roles" in the "Roles" column. Yeah, I know that makes sense in a way, because even I don't want a specific role to be viewed by the students, the user may have other roles that the student could/should see, so this user is still present in the list. Could someone please shed a light on this issue? Is there a workaround that can be implemented? Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hiding participants with specific roles from the participants list of a course

An example of this would be assigning a user to a Principal, Manager or Helpdesk type role to provide them access without confusing the participants list." See this page... - Other_users Do note that as these users are not actually enrolled in the course you may find that there are some differences in behaviour compared to "real" teachers.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ac-hoc report to display decrypted password
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle doesn't use MD5 for passwords, it uses the default algorithm for PHP's password_hash function which looks like it's currently blowfish. Salts are automatically generated in this case. https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.password-hash.php https://www.php.net/manual/en/password.constants.php These passwords are one-way encrypted, so the intention is that you can't decrypt them. The only way to find out what a password is via a dictionary attack.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to categorise my user?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to categorise my user?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Priya, Why would you want to make different roles for different subject matter teachers? The teacher (editing and non-editing) roles are assigned at course level, not at site level. This means, if you enrol an English teacher in an English course, he/she will have appropriate tools and permissions in that context only. Outside the course, this English teacher is just an authenticated user like the rest of your users. Same goes for your Science, History and Geography teachers. If you want to, you could add all the subject matter teachers in their own cohorts (English Teachers, Geography Teachers, History Teachers, ...). You could consult this Moodle Docs page on how to bulk manage these cohorts and user enrolments, once you decide how to organise things: https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Upload_users The only valid reason I can think of, when you'd want to create custom teacher roles, has more to do with adding levels of permission between non-editing (nothing) and editing (everything) teachers. Beginners may only need access to Assignment and Forum, whereas more advanced teachers will want to also have Workshop, Quiz and Lesson in their set of activities . Hope it helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Clearing the htmlpurifier Cache via the Command Line
ResponsesInList.Text: @Daniel ... no need to ask or expect response via PM in this moodle ... response here for all to see ... others could have better suggestions ... below is my 2 cents! Caution you about 'piggy backing' on someone else's post/problem.   Might seem the same but unless your server setup is on same hosting provider or setup exactly as the other poster in this thread, you could be going off and down a rabbit hole that won't lead to resolution of your problem. Please do as Howard has suggested in this thread ... if you are getting error 500's, find out why. Files in something dynamic (changes constantly) like Moodle isn't easy.   Not only the contents of moodledata/filedir/ but the database (mdl_files table) is involved and through queries of DB is how Moodle finds files. To solve your issue think I'd do a query of DB first to find all moodle course backups in moodledata/filedir/ Something like the following ... you would have to adjust accordingly for your setup/server: mysql -u root -p -e "use moodle;select id,component,userid,filename,filesize,timemodified from mdl_files where filename like '%.mbz';" > allbackups.txt;cat allbackups.txt The text file it outputs to can be used to find backups that are dups and large. Example from real in production site: id    component    userid    filename    filesize    timemodified 162051    backup    2    backup-moodle2-course-21-car002-20130716-2311-nu.mbz    25754656    1374030713 163827    backup    2    backup-moodle2-course-21-car002-20130717-2311-nu.mbz    25754658    1374117115 163866    backup    2    backup-moodle2-course-21-car002-20130718-2311-nu.mbz    25754656    1374203510 164170    backup    2    backup-moodle2-course-21-car002-20130719-2311-nu.mbz    25754656    1374289911 164210    backup    2    backup-moodle2-course-21-car002-20130720-2311-nu.mbz    25754656    1374376309 You can see by example provided this one course has several old backups and are a little over 25+Megs in size. Finding them and removing them from admin interface is difficult ... admin level user doesn't see teachers private files unless you login as them. As per example: Logging into server as that teacher and going to course ID 21 which has a shortcourse name of car002 you will be able to see those .mbz files and delete them. But, that doesn't automatically free up that space ... those backup mbz files are moved to moodledata/trashdir where they remain for 4 days I think, then task in cron job to empty trash kicks in to finally deletes them. OR ... since you need space now for inode limits, one can manually remove all contents of moodledata/trashdir/ The database will catch up with cron jobs and task. Manually removing should never be first resort ... but sounds like you are in a crunch and have no choice at present. When you get this resolved, I'd look into finding more space on an attached device/drive/mountpoint which has inode limits of it's own ... hopefully larger than what you have now. Above depends upon how hosted, with whom, does hoster provide such things, etc.   All of that known only to you at present. Good luck! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Clearing the htmlpurifier Cache via the Command Line
ResponsesInList.Text: Great, Ken. THANKS a lot for quick and detailed reply. (And Sorry! for  my previous PM I sent due to my lack of experience in this forums. I thought it was public). Also sorry for my English as non-native speaker. Let me share my experience as I finally SOLVED the problem, and probably it can be similar maybe to other's arriving to this same forum after googling about the 'inodes'. First I will tell my problem, then I will put in context for other users who can be using also ' quizzes ' on their moodles and finally the (very) simple solution. I'm not a developer. I'm a teacher at Uni and I just use Moodle for my work, so I decided it was fun to create and run a home-made website. Currently, after two years, this website hosts one single course with 1.400 users. My problem was that suddenly I ran out of inodes in my hosting company ('Hostinger', by the way). I reached 101% of my 200.000 inodes permitted. Never heard about those 'inodes' in my whole life. When you use Moodle at Uni you never think about all those other limits Inodes seem to be the meta data every single file or folder needs to be hosted in your website. So, no matter how small they are, as long as they exist, they use one. So, for a website like mine (quite small, with no more than 900 MB used, so, less than I GB) with a Premium service plan I payed it seemed to be quite surprising. So, where did all those inodes come from? The answer is the structure and usage of my website, which is full of Quizzes (dozens of them, with 'randomly selected questions' from database) and 1.400 active users. This seems to create a lot of tiny 'cache' files every day. The reason is related to the kind of quizzes used, as they are created 'randomly' for every single user, the amount of information stored tend to grow very fast. The solution seemed to be just clearing those caches, which is something I discover it's quite easy from inside the Moodle itself, but the problem is that when your inodes are full, you cannot even enter your website! (No PhP can run, so no access is allowed for any user, included administrators). So I was out of my own website and couldn't enter as Admin. Just surf the directories using the File Manager... So: what was the solution in my case? I used File Manager to delete another folder (out of Moodle, just an unused folder with rubbish, it was a secondary moodle folder I installed once in the past but never used again). This folder was stored in the same hosting plan and that helped reducing my inodes below the 100% limit. As long as you get below the limit, you can finally enter as Admin. And when you're in, go to: SITE ADMINISTRATION / DEVELOPMENT / PURGE ALL CACHES something like this: https://www.MYWEBSITE.com/admin/purgecaches.php And purge all of of them: This drastically reduced the amount of inodes used to just 14% of my 200.000 limit. Great! very happy... BUT: About the obvious conclusion ("...always purge the caches of your Moodle site before reaching the 100% limit of your storage plan...') A second conclusion I got about this is as follows: Always keep also folder (unused) with rubbish or files you don't need –In my case, that secondary and unused Moodle site– which you can delete in order to create extra space in case of an Emergency. I know other hosting companies do alert their customers when inodes limit is about to be reached (at 90 or 95%) but that was not my case. So that's why I think having the secondary and unused moodle can be a simple lifeguard! Thanks to all users in the forum. Your help is very valuable!

ResponsesInList.Title: moodle 3.1 versus moodle 3.8 - is it necessary to upgrade ?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am being asked by my host to upgrade my version of moodle, presently using 3.1 to the latest. Theres a charge for this and I wonder if I really have to do this upgrade at all or will I be able to get away with using 3.1 for the forseeable future ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle 3.1 versus moodle 3.8 - is it necessary to upgrade ?
ResponsesInList.Text: There are risks with not upgrading. For me these are... * There will be increasingly less experience of the version you run. * It will not be supported. If you find a bug it won't get fixed. * You will not get security releases. I'm not saying you will get hacked but there will be *known* security vulnerabilities for your version. If they make you susceptible then you have a problem. I would say it isn't good to be in a position where you cannot upgrade your way out of trouble. Moodle is free and open source - you don't *have* to pay someone to upgrade it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Relation between activity completion and course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi to everyone! I'm Alessandro. I'm totally new to Moodle communities but it's two years that I'm using this useful LMS. Don't know if someone already answered. In any case, if I: Create a course; Add activites and correctly set up completion when conditions are met; Correctly set up course completion; Everything works fine and when a user do the required activities , the LMS correctly register overall completion of the entire course. I was wandering. if I delete an activity that was enabled to trigger the course completion, users are going to lose the course completion record if they have already finished it? Thank you in advance! Alessandro

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Relation between activity completion and course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: No. Completion is done by a background task. However, if you need to (for example) add another activity to the course completion rules you will need to delete the completion data. The completion is re-calculated for all users on the next run of the background process (using the new rules) so it's rarely a big deal.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: Re: Relation between activity completion and course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you! So: 1) When course completion is registered within a course for a user, you can change/delete activities without losing completion data for this user. 2) Only by changing course completion rules your're going to "reset" completion user data related to the entire course, only to (possibly) retrieve it at the end of the CRON process. AG

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: Re: Relation between activity completion and course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes to both.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: OnPrem AD with Office 365 functionality
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi James, Having tested this in the past, long story short, I believe for your users to be able to seamlessly access their OneDrive they will need to be authenticated by Oauth2 or OpenID (using Microsoft Integration plugin). ResponsesInList.Title: Running CRON
ResponsesInList.Text: So, I installed Moodle a week ago and all was going well. Whilst doing some further reading I came across an article about CRON and how I should definitely have it running. Ok, I thought let's get that done. Oh boy!!! Details are: Ubuntu 18.04.3 running Apache2 and PHP 7.2 for the Web component on 10.10.0.16 Ubuntu 18.04.3 running MySQL (not sure of version) on 10.10.0.15 I logged into the webserver and entered the following; sudo /user/bin/php7.2 /home/linuxadmin/moodle/moodle/admin/cli/php7.2 cron.php and get the result Could not open input file: /home/linuxadmin/moodle/moodle/admin/cli/php7.2 Ist a permissions thing or have I got the command incorrect? *NB the double moodle is correct, I am new to Linux and unpacked stuff in the wrong place but decided to just run with it

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Running CRON
ResponsesInList.Text:
You need to run the admin/cli/cron.php script so the command you probably want is: 
```text
sudo /user/bin/php7.2 /home/linuxadmin/moodle/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php
```
 (I'm assuming that /user/bin/php7.2 is correct on the server , it's usually /usr/bin/… ). What I'd recommend is running the script as the Apache web user. I think this is www-data on Ubuntu making the command: 
```text
sudo -u www-data /user/bin/php7.2 /home/linuxadmin/moodle/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php
```
 Then when you come to add the command to crontab to run it on a schedule, add it to the Apache user's crontab with: 
```text
crontab -u www-data -e
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Running CRON
ResponsesInList.Text: config-dist.php is the example as you say but if you've got a working site, e.g. you can log into it, then there's definitely an existing config.php . If it's not in /home/linuxadmin/moodle/moodle then this isn't the Moodle source code directory for the site, and /home/linuxadmin/moodle/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php is the wrong location too. So you need to find out where the site's source code directory is located. Log into the site and navigate to Site administration → Server → PHP info and search for $_SERVER['SCRIPT_FILENAME'] . On my test site this appears near the end of the page: which indicates that the Moodle source code directory (where config.php is located) is /var/www/moodle37.leon/moodle and cron.php will be /var/www/moodle37.leon/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Display an element on task completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lucas, You can achieve this by using Activity Completion ( https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Activity_completion ) and Restrict Access ( https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Restrict_access ) Restrict access to a label containing the text etc. you want to show based on completion of the other activity. Catherine

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Display an element on task completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Catherine, I'm an idiot, haha. I realise I've missed a detail in my explanation. I know about the basic interaction with restricted access and activity completion. I'm actually not trying to display an entire element like a file, an activity, but an entity within a label. If I had to give an example, I'd say I'd have a list of objectives inside a label, and everytime an activity is completed, the corresponding list item would turn green or something. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Display an element on task completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lucas, You can fake this by having a number of labels. So let's say you have 2 quizzes that the participants have to do. You want them to see a checklist with two items unticked if they have completed neither. If they have done the first quiz they see a checklist with 1 list item ticked If they have done both, then they see a checklist with 2 items ticked. The first checklist label is visible when participants HAVE NOT completed Quiz 1 AND HAVE NOT completed Quiz 2 The second one is visible when participants HAVE completed Quiz AND HAVE NOT completed Quiz 2 The third one is visible when participants HAVE completed Quiz AND HAVE completed Quiz 2 Participants only see one label at a time, and will assume they are looking at the same one each time.

ResponsesInList.Title: Alternative to downloaded student submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: All, I'm looking to tap into your collective wisdom. I have a lecturer who is managing their submissions through Moodle but would like to "open the files in the browser" as opposed to downloading them onto their desktop. IS there some way that this can be achieved. The files are mixtures of word documents, videos and images. As ever any help would be appreciated Kind regards Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alternative to downloaded student submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mark, For all 'regular' document formats, I'd go with Annotate PDF as feedback type. This would convert the submission to a PDF so it can be annotated without the need to download the thing and manage it offline. For media (audio, video), I'd recommend using the online text submission type, where the student uploads his/her media file through the editor buttons. Big advantage is that it'll play without any issues, and that the lecturer can use all the regular grading and feedback tools in Assignment. For image files, I'd recommend using the Annotate functionality. During the QA testing of Moodle 3.8, I saw it's possible to annotate an uploaded image file much in the same way you'd annotate a 'regular' document. For these features to work, you do need a proper document converter. Also, have you considered allowing the students to create their multimedial portfolio on a tool like Mahara and then ask them to submit a Mahara portfolio in Assignment? If the students are expected to submit 'all sorts at once', this may be the best way to approach.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alternative to downloaded student submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Mark, Joost has given some good information.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course participation report not available to non-editing teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm guessing it's something to do with the 'moodle/site:accessallgroups' capability. The report generates the group select menu regardless of group mode. It does that by calling an API function groups_allgroups_course_menu. This checks that capability to decide how to return the menu. Just quickly glancing at the code, not having that capability and there not being any groups means a null return which generates the error. So, yes, a bug. This code has been around since 2012! Bug report created - MDL-66943

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz workflow notifications
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Brendon, As I'm reading what you're looking for, I can't stop to think you want mod_quiz (Quiz) to behave like mod_assign (Assignment), which has all of the notification bits on board, including a very nifty annotate PDF kind of grading interface, and the possibility to grade the essays using a rubric or marking guide. Set up your Assignment activity to be marked as completed after a submission that was graded by the teacher and set up your course to automatically give out a badge for anyone who has a grade > passing grade for Assignment, and you're nearly set. Finally, set up a certificate to be available (through restrict access) when said grade is equal to or higher than a minimum value and your users should only be able to download the certificate when they have passed the assignment.

ResponsesInList.Text: Update: 1. Student takes the quiz and submits it No issues - this uses core functionality 2. They receive an email notification confirming receipt, and telling them they will get their grade once it has been manually marked Similarly to step 5 below, you can send an email indicating that a quiz in "Coursename" has been submitted, and in the body of the email, explain what the next steps are. The trigger will be Quiz: Quiz attempt submitted 3. The course instructor receives a "grading required" email notification I have found a way to send a notification to the teacher whenever a quiz attempt is submitted.  I have not found a way to differentiate between those quizzes that require manual grading and those that do not.  The teacher has to read the notification and apply their mind to determine if manual grading is required. Login as an administrator Site administration / Users / Define roles Edit teacher Filter - enter email Tick Get a notification message when an attempt is submitted Save changes Site Administration / Plugins Default message outputs Notification of quiz submissions Web and email locked Online and offline ticked for both web and email Save changes 4. The course instructor grades the quiz and save the final result No issues - this uses core functionality 5. The student gets an email notification that their final grade is ready I have found a way to send an email alert.  However, I can only state that "a quiz" in this specific course has been graded - I can't tell them which quiz.  Also, if you grade only some of the questions in a quiz and then complete the review, the email will be sent, even though the grade is incomplete (I think, not tested). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle (own host price) and LMS
ResponsesInList.Text: Don't do it! I have seen a massive number of organisations that started with this requirement, so installed moodle on their own system and then never touched it again... and 3-4 years later (or more!) the moodle site is still running the same version... has never been patched with security updates etc....
