With the numbers you're looking at I'd just suggest using a moodlecloud .com account - upgrades/hosting all sorted for you at a very reasonable price. https://moodlecloud.com/app/en/ moodlecloud.com is supported and managed by the team at Moodle HQ.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle (own host price) and LMS
ResponsesInList.Text: You can't set up moodle and just "leave it" - even for a year. Moodle releases security updates every 2 months. If you manage your own site you MUST implement a process to deploy these every 2 months. If you're interesting in upskilling on this yourself - go for it! - there are a lot of posts here in the forums and lots of documenation in our wiki that shows you how to do this.. but, be aware that it will take you a significant amount of time, and if you decide to move on, then the organisation may get stuck with that site and noone to help them upgrade/maintain it. ResponsesInList.Text: "Assigning this role at this level enrols a user in all courses under the category" No it does not! It gives them that "role" in all the courses under the category. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teacher and Non editing teacher category enrolments causes slow page loading times
ResponsesInList.Text: I hope I don't sound unhelpful, but the best I can do is to explain why I cannot answer your question. By default, you cannot assign the teacher role at Course Category level. However, with 3.6, messaging was apparently changed so only (confirmed) contacts can send you a message. That is, you only see messages from people in your "contacts" (that you asked to confirm you as a contact, or vice versa). This is essentially meant as a privacy improvement - but it also "hides" your old messages. For example, I do not see any messages from my student "X" in Moodle 3.6 now. I then searched for "X", clicked on his name, and now I can see all old messages. However, I will have to wait for X to confirm the contact to be able to directly access the (old) messages we exchanged before the upgrade; I can only see them by "searching for X and clicking on X's name". Try this out and it should work for you - as long as you recall who sent you a message. Alas, I am not able to recall the names of everybody who wrote me a message over the past few days (too many, as I am also the site admin). I also consider this to be somewhere between "bug" (the messages are seemingly "gone", but not actually "deleted") and "feature" (privacy improvement). I wish there were some way for me to access the list of persons who I exchanged messages with before, e.g., Moodle asking me after the upgrade if I wanted to add them as a contact... PS. I now added a bug report ( https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-64317 ) for this, as this makes it more likely Moodle HQ will see and address this issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: How do we get around Activity Completion being reset?
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there a way to get around an Activity resetting everyone's prior completion in a course? If we make a change to a Course we may not want to reset completion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do we get around Activity Completion being reset?
ResponsesInList.Text: You could backup and restore the course with retain the students activity completions. Adjust your content of the course and just reset the quizzes and quiz attempts. IMHO the activity completion reset should allow the instructor/administrator to select individual activities to reset. It should not be all/none.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do we get around Activity Completion being reset?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the reply, Shriley! Just to make sure I understand... I would first, backup the course. Then, I would make any changes I need to in the course. Finally, I would restore the backup, only restoring the quiz attempts. The result would keep my completion?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do we get around Activity Completion being reset?
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. backup the course. During the backup have all checkboxes selected. Activity completion, enrollments....etc. 2. restore the course, with all activity completion, enrollments....etc. and with a new name/short name and ID. They have to be unique. 3. after the restore, Hide the course. 4. make you changes. 5. Reset the Quiz and quiz attempts only (unless you want to keep those. then only new enrolled students will have to complete the quiz) 6. Check that the Activity Report is still reporting activities . 7. Check that the Completion Report is still reporting activities . 8. if the reports are good, unhide the course. I normally, send out a notification to the students, the specific activities and quiz will need to be completed by MM/DD/YYYY. I also, end date the original course and move it to a "retired" course category. Hide the enrollment method, it is less confusing for the students. Good Luck

ResponsesInList.Title: Report on Time in Course
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a group I've developed a course for but a question came up our meeting today I can't answer.  They require the students to have a minimum of four hours of training and are wondering if there is a way to document this.  I know I can go into the logs and pull out information on an individual basis.  But they have lots of students and doing this for each individual person will be difficult and time consuming. Is there a report I'm missing that will give me a report on the length of time members of the group have taken to complete all the requirements in the course?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Report on Time in Course
ResponsesInList.Text: Melanie, this question gets asked a lot. Unfortunately, the answer is "no." Computers don't keep track of time, they can keep track of "clicks," which Moodle does do very well. But someone has to figure out what the student was actually doing between clicks. This is no fault of Moodle, it is just the way computers work. Even without Moodle, how do you know? Do you think that if a student sits in front of an instructor who is speaking, that the student's mind is actually hearing (and learning) everything the instructor says? The best advice is to use an assessment to measure what the student has learned. "Time" is not important, but acquired "knowledge" is. Incidentally, another "competing" LMS keeps track of "activity time," (C) but when one probes into the value one finds completely bogus data. One thing that you can do is to have your students be locked in a room for four hours, doing the training on Moodle, and to not let them out even if they finish the training early, like in 30 minutes. They you can probably claim that they spent 4 hours in "training."

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Report on Time in Course
ResponsesInList.Text: Believe me, I agree with you. But I'm in a "don't confuse me with facts, my mind is made up." type of situation. These people have this idea that the amount of time spent on the class is what's so darn important. I mentioned that when a 4-hour class is scheduled you also take breaks so they don't actually get 4-hours of class in a classroom situation either. I also brought up that students, especially those in the back of the room spend a goodly part of the class texting. They also were concerned that if the classes are done on line there's no interaction between students. I explained that we can have forum questions where students would be required to participant in order to complete the course. There was resistence on this as well until two people in the group mentioned they'd taken college classes online and it worked out well to have forums. I did push the fact that Moodle was in all probability the program that was used and if it works in colleges and universities it should certainly work for them. With the amount of material I've put in the courses I don't think it would be a problem for a student to put in four hours. But my bottom line view is, what's more important, the amount of time spent in the class, or learning the required material?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Report on Time in Course
ResponsesInList.Text: I understand your situation, Melanie, I run into this weird thinking all the time from administrators. In the U.S., the government and their subsidized payments for students came under investigation a few years ago when the government discovered that some schools were "charging" for a 3-hour course when the course contained only 1-hour of instruction. A scam! So the government said that schools would have to prove that a 3-hour course was indeed a 3-hour course, through documenting course contents, assignments, and a review process. But then there was an "OR." This "OR", reluctantly agreed to by the government folks, was that "time" could be used, and that a 3-hour college course should have 120 hours of "time" in it. Of course, it was easy to say that when a student sits in a chair in a room called a class, texting friends, daydreaming, working on assignments in another course, that this was counted as course time. So many administrators wanted to take the easy path; just document "time." I repeat, the government folks were not stupid, they knew that education was not about time, but this alternative was reluctantly still provided to ease the administrative burden of proving a 3-hour course is a 3-hour course. Okay, a lot said, not helpful to your situation (where you seem to have some of these kinds of administrators.) I find it odd that your administrators had resistance to using actual Moodle forum discussion, but seem to be willing to accept any other forms of chit-chatting. Actually, I have been using the Moodle discussion forum tool for 10 years, and in my opinion, it is one of the best ways to stimulate, and document discussion. Ask your administrators to go to any face-to-face instructor and ask them to prove, via documentation, that students "discussed" things in class and that a valid "score" was recored in the grade book. Your last paragraph indicates your understanding. As a side note, just this summer I had one of my online courses certified by "Quality Matters." Yes, I had to "prove" that students had sufficient interaction (for my 3-hour course), which I did. I didn't need to show any thing like this goofy student "time," but I did need to illustrate all the activities that students did, including watching videos, working with Excel models, doing quizzes, etc. Yes, my course passed, but my Quality Matters audit took a lot of "time." About 50 hours. Much more "time" than either most instructors or administrators want to spend reviewing a course. Right? (Incidentally, my course is the only Quality Matters certified course at my big-10 university, somewhat illustrating the interest in this kind of audit.) So, as an idea, maybe you could suggest that your school's courses should be subject to the Quality Matters system. But I suspect that your administrators might say that it would take too much "time" and "money." Alternatively, some schools have resorted to a student survey "How much time did you spend in this course?" The problem, however, is that if you do this for face-to-face courses you might not get what your administrators want. For my Quality Matters certification, I showed a variety of course "assessment" instruments, which helped. Getting back to your administrator's view of forum posts, they would probably say that our posts, and discussion about your needs, has not taken any "time." But the real answer to you initial question is that Moodle does not record "time."  Only clicks.  So your administrators might need to abort their ideas about using any LMS. (Be careful, there is one LMS that lies about Activity Time that your administrator might prefer.)

ResponsesInList.Title: The color of Moodle.org links does not meet WCAG web accessibility standards
ResponsesInList.Text:
This issue concerns colors used in Moodle.org forums and MoodleDocs . Body-text-to-background contrast ratio With a #595959 body text color on a #FFFFFF background color, MoodleDocs 's and Moodle.org 's body-text-to-background contrast ratio is 7:1, at the lower end of WCAG's 7:1 requirement. In comparison,
Google's body-text-to-background contrast ratio ( #3C4043 /#ffffff) is 10.46:1, that of Wikipedia ( #222222 /#ffffff) is 15.9:1 and that of w3.org ( #000000 /#ffffff)
is 21:1 (the maximum possible). Link-to-body-text contrast ratio With a #0070AB color for links which are not underlined and a #595959 text color, MoodleDocs 's and Moodle.org 's link-to-body-text contrast ratio is 1.29:1, which
does not meet WCAG's 3:1 requirement. In comparison, Wikipedia's link-to-body-text contrast ratio ( #0645AD / #222222 ) is 2.32 and that of Google ( #1A73E8 / #3C4043 ) is 2.32. W3.org uses underlined links . Recommendations My recommendations are that the WCAG requirements be met: Although the body-text-to-background contrast ratio just meets WCAG's requirement, Moodle could darken its text a bit. If the text color is maintained at #595959, the links must be underlined or the color changed so that the link-to-body-text contrast ratio reaches 3:1. Moodle should use a link color with sufficient lightness, such as #A3A3FF or #1FB4FF . References W3C WebAIM.org

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The color of Moodle.org links does not meet WCAG web accessibility standards
ResponsesInList.Text: Erm... ok, but not really 'General help'. Please raise a ticket at https://tracker.moodle.org/ against the project 'Moodle community sites'

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The color of Moodle.org links does not meet WCAG web accessibility standards
ResponsesInList.Text: Howard, Thank you for your reply. I just created https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/ MDLSITE-6029 .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The color of Moodle.org links does not meet WCAG web accessibility standards
ResponsesInList.Text: For body-text contrast, Moodle meets WCAG's guidelines. There is no need for change. For link-to-body, yes, Moodle seems to not meet the guidelines. However, there are many WCAG guidelines that Moodle and many websites do not meet, which is probably why they call these WCAG "guidelines." That's the "G" in the acronym. Yes, I know. And yes, I go crazy trying to "conform." Quite honestly, I have never seen anyone make a post saying that they could not see objects in Moodle.org.  And isn't it better to use "Web Content Accessibility Guidelines" instead of WCAG, or at least initially use both? My post is meant to stimulate discussion, not to "break rules" or "argue."

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No user input works after update
ResponsesInList.Text: Not sure I understand this question ... Are you asking if you can get 'lessons and events' from old moodle into a fresh 3.7 install of Moodle? Am gonna guess that means 'courses' from old moodle into a fresh 3.7 install ... is that correct? Can do ... **if** you have full backups (.mbz files) of courses from your 3.4.   Full backups are ones that included users and all their activities /assignment/grades, etc. Unfortunately, if you made course backups,  the .mbz files are located in the sea of files of moodledata/filedir by filenames that are not humanly recognizable.   And if you did not download those .mbz files, finding them would take command line access to server and a lot more work than I imagine you'd care to do! To fix this am gonna suggest this workaround ... First, keep your old code folder ... don't remove it. Download the fresh 3.7 code to your local computer. Un-compress/un-archive it there. On the server, remove the mod and themes directories in the active code. Upload the mod and theme directory from the downloaded archive you have on local machine to the same location of mod/theme you deleted. (don't copy over or try to over write them). The 3.7 mod directory should contain the following files/folders: README.txt    choice        glossary    lti        survey assign        data        imscp        page        upgrade.txt assignment    feedback    index.html    quiz        url book        folder        label        resource    wiki chat        forum lesson scorm workshop The 3.7 theme directory should contain the following files/folders: boost javascript .php        upgrade.txt classic            jquery.php        yui_combo.php font.php        styles.php        yui_image.php image.php        styles_debug.php index.php        switchdevice.php Then, copy ... **that's copy** ... any mod **folder** that is not part of 3.7 core code from your old moodlecode/mod/ directory to the new moodlecode/mod/ directory. I cannot provide a list of those.   You just have to compare. Do the same for theme ... old theme folders to new code/theme/ - even though we know you might have to upgrade the moove theme later. We are trying to get to a place where Moodle will/might upgrade again .... and, of course, you can login. Fingers crossed! If all above fails, contact provider to see if they have a backup of your account and if they could restore it for you .... depending upon how old it is, etc.   That will be your last resort! :\ For future reference ... bookmark or favorite this: Upgrading: https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Upgrading Sometimes there are no 'short cuts'. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Brute force attack? saw them in error log
ResponsesInList.Text: ﻿ Not a brute force attack ... just 'normal' almost script kiddie scan of your server looking for vulnaerable versions of PHPMyAdmin or evidence of a hacked box.   The IP address could be blocked. It is more trouble and harder on processing of apache server to attempt to deal with all those ... they happen frequestnly and from multiple IP addresses. It's more annoying than anything else ... still, on servers where I find an IP address too aggressive with such scanning, I blockhole the IP or a range of IP addresses from same Class C or Class B block as the offend//too aggressive IP. do some checks on 193.112.198.172 - like whois and nmap scans ... etc. If there is doubt your Moodle would ever be access by someome coming from a range of IP addresses that include that specific IP, consider blocking access at the network layer. How to block at network layer with current state of your server (reference most recent posting) is an exercise up to you. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restricting self enrolment to specifi email addresses
ResponsesInList.Text: Altan, Here is the main documentation for self-enrollment, including enrollment keys: https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Self_enrolment Depending on how enrollment information and instructions are communicated to your users, an enrollment key may be sufficient to accomplice your goal of limiting the course to a single audience. The enrollment key is basically a password that a user needs in order to self-enroll into a course. You create the key, so it can be as simple or complex as you want. If you limit the enrollment methods to just self-enrollment (and maybe manual enrollment for special situations) and require the key, then only those people with the key can enroll into the course. Users can always share the key with others who shouldn't have it, of course. But, if there is a defined enrollment period - say one week - then, at the end of that period, you can change the key and not publicize it. The enrolled participants remain in the course, and the original key is no longer useful if anyone shares it. And if there is a gap between the enrollment period and the course start date, you can use that time to examine the participants list and unenroll any non.govt enrollees who may have been given the key by a govt user. I only mention enrollment period as a means to address the possibility of enrollment keys getting passed around to users who shouldn't have them. This likely is not an issue for most situations and you can probably handle the enrollment time period as you normally do. Enrollment keys are great, too, if you use groups in the course. Each group can have its own enrollment key. When a users enrolls using the key for a particular group, he is enrolled into the course and sorted into the correct group.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Partial course completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Whitney, long time I think that you should add some activity completions for other items at key points of the course where you want to see progress on the activity completion report. Adding some automatic completion to simple things like videos, page, links, etc. can give you this with no interruption to course flow. One trick I use is to have a simple Choice activity at the beginning of a course for students to answer some basic question, so that you can get a first interactive activity completion with a time and date on it as a starter. Or make them read the syllabus or accept some course specific terms and conditions, for example, but the goal is to mark that starting point of their work. Another way, especially if you want to improve motivation and completion, is using Badges, again at some strategic points in the course. This is especially useful if the courses are long and take some time to complete, since it can help identify a reachable interim stage in a long course. Randy

ResponsesInList.Text: Does anyone know if this differential access of assignments based on groups gets propagated to the gradebook? Ex: people in group A must do an worth 20 points, while people in group B have no assignments at all. In which case, when generating grade reports for those in group B, you should see no such assignment mentioned at all, because from their perspective it doesn't exist? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Exclude a group from activity
ResponsesInList.Text: That sure would be nice, wouldn't it! But neither grade items nor grade categories are group aware in that way. Now, for grading, if you have two Assignments A and B assigned to different Groups A and B, then the grade for users for the assignments they can't do will be empty. So, if you have set an item or category to "Exclude empty grades", then those are excluded from the math. So you may need to manage those empty grades in some way to make the math come out as you want in your example situation. Further, for visibility, if you have the access restriction set so that the Assignment is visible to all groups in the course, even if they can't do it, then that Assignment will show up greyed out in the Grades view for those other group students, but will of course have no grade and be empty. If you have the access restriction set so that the Assignment is only visible in the course to the Group it is restricted to, then students in other groups will not see any entry in the course nor in their view of the Grades. So that visibility behavior is consistent or what I would expect. However, even though it is not visible, that empty grade does still exist, and doesn't change the math going on due to the empty grade.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to edit past completion dates?
ResponsesInList.Text: How can I alter completion dates/scores for a student's activities , course completion, and issued certificate date/times?  I'm using the Simple Certificate plugin.  Basically I need to alter a student's records to indicate completion several months ago.  I don't see any options to allow an admin user to modify scores/dates/times.  Also, I am using only SCORM activities tracking only "complete/incomplete" (no grades). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to edit past completion dates?
ResponsesInList.Text: I do not advocate doing this, but I have done it in the past for a variety of reasons.  This is VERY dangerous from the data management perspective. You can seriously screw up stuff doing this (I say this because I have). If you do it, BE CAREFUL! Get Adminer (if you don't have it).  Go to the background database .  Find the relevant completion tables (you'll need to look at more than one mdl_course_completions, mdl_course_modules_completion), find the dates you need to change. Change them. I know this sounds pretty simple...but it isn't.  It requires you know the userid, the courseid, the activity id and the UNIX time stamp for the date you want to display for EVERY user and EVERY course and EVERY relevant activity. I repeat, I do not advocate doing this.  But if you have to, it works.  If you do it right.

Ideally we want to have a record of their real completion date. This can be done in a learning plan as a record of prior learning but that does not really do what we want. I agree that messing with the database is risky and not for the naive. Its not an option at an operational level.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course creator doesn't get Teacher role in created courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, We fixed a bug with course creation whereby the default course role was given regardless of whether it should be. Essentially, in order to assign a role, you need two things: 1) The moodle/role:assign capability; and 2) The ability to assign the specified role (Site administration -> Users -> Define role -> Allow role assignments) Unfortunately the default "Course creator" role has neither of these. There are a few other parts to this but they should not normally be fixed by an upgrade script. We do not change either the capability assignments, nor the role configuration of an installed site (normally). I've created MDL-66683 to address this for 3.8. We may need to consider adding this to stables in an upgrade step, but this is unusual for stables. I suspect we should accept such a change in our next minor release and grant the assign to the coursecreator archetype for the current default role only.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I get a 404 error when I try to make my Moodle site visible on the LAN
ResponsesInList.Text: No qualifications to talk Microsoft. Still my two cents believing this is more about networking. (If your instructions from the year 2003 was valid, this should holt too.) As you already stated, your project has three stages: 1. Moodle on 'localhost' 2. Acces in the LAN 3. Opening to the Internet Stage 1 is successful? If a browser running in same (Windows 10) computer accesses Moodle on http://localhost/moodle or http://127.0.0.1/moodle , it is. Check $CFG->wwwroot in moodle/config.php. For stage 2 you change $CFG->wwwroot to ' http://private.ip/moodle' , where private.ip is the IP your Windows 10 machine in the LAN, possibly 192.168.1.117 in your case. If another computer in the same LAN answers to http://private.ip/moodle , you were successful. Strictly speaking, you should now run the https://docs.moodle.org/en/Search_and_replace_tool to replace the old URL with the new one. For stage 3, you need to change $CFG->wwwroot again, this time to ' http://public.ip/moodle , where public.ip is the "proper" IP address you got from your provider, your router might call it the WAN address. You need to configure your router to some kind of IP forwarding from the WAN IP to your Windows 10 LAN IP and NAT routing for the machine to reply to the calling IP. This is the tricky part. If you managed to give your WAN IP a domain name (in the DNS), you have to use that in $CFG->wwwroot to ' http://private.ip/moodle' . Once it works, the replace tool has to run again. That said, there are other alternatives for test runs. MoodleCloud is free up to 50 users. My favourite is the MoodleBox https://moodlebox.net , a SD pre-installed with Moodle latest for Raspberry Pi 3 and 4.

Then you need two things: One is a configuration parameter of the web server, which is called DocumentRoot in Apache ,. It should point to the parent directory of your Moodle code directory, in Debian and derived systems it is /var/www/html. The other one is $CFG->webroot which we were discussing. It must be 'http://domain/moodle'. The future platform: If you planned Raspberry Pi any way, MoodleBox is a turn-key solution.

ResponsesInList.Text: From what directory did you issue the command: php automated_backups.php For any of the moodle cli scripts to work one must be in the moodle code directory. So ... **example** ... if moodle code was in /var/www/html/ cd /var/www/html/ php admin/cli/automated_backups.php Reason ... the CLI scripts reads variables in config.php of Moodle. ** Read the Docs ** : https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Course_backup https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Automated_course_backup From your screen shot of where you storing backups, I'd say none of the course backups have completed successfully.  Backup files in Moodle end with .mbz. Example of a M34 version using autobackups to designated directory outside of apache: /home/backup/m34/courses [root@sos courses]# ls -l *2019* -rw-rw-rw-. 1 root root    2768323 Feb 19  2019 backup-moodle2-course-2-sa-20190219-1555.mbz -rw-rw-rw-. 1 root root    3871679 Feb 19  2019 backup-moodle2-course-3-test-20190219-1553.mbz -rw-rw-rw-. 1 root root   23624714 Feb 19  2019 backup-moodle2-course-4-mshare-20190219-1554.mbz -rw-rw-rw-. 1 root root    1217811 Feb 19  2019 backup-moodle2-course-5-slcentos-20190219-1554.mbz -rw-rw-rw-. 1 root root 1260971342 Feb 19  2019 backup-moodle2-course-6-gte_complete-20190219-1554.mbz Also, this warning ... ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Announcements Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: From my recollection, direct messaging and Forum and announcements and e-mail messaging are not the same. Moodle has different was to handle messages. One is using its internal messaging system, the other relies on the e-mail system to be set up and for cron to be running. This is basically because some processes, and this one we are using here is an example have a timer attached. For that timer to work, there has to be a system that processes the time the message was written, and then compare that to the current time. When the delay has be reached, the mesage is sent and with it is an email notification, which we receive to tell us something has been updated. I may be wrong, but if my memory serves me correctly when I had something similar, internal messages sent fine even when the Cron process wasn't running. However, e-mail and the other forms of messaging didn't, hence my suspicion that it may be your Cron that is not working here. Have you checked it?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Linking Scales
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to have deploy a scale value when you create a competency framework. When multiple scales rating are deployed in competencies the instructor must manually rate the student before the competency can be awarded. The competency value cannot be automated completed for an activity that awards the competency. Please note Scales cannot be changed once they are awarded, they are unforgiving.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teacher Orineted Website
ResponsesInList.Text: It is not odd that people come across other websites and ask "Can Moodle be like this?"  This happens not only with other LMSs (e.g., why can't Moodle be like Blackboard) but also other products like WordPress, Joomla, Facebook, etc.  From my experience, Moodle is the most "open-source" product around, very flexible, and powerful.  It can take on many looks.  It has many plugins.  Etc.  Additionally, if one knows what they are doing, they can make it do all kinds of things by modifying code. But you can't make Moodle be one of these other products.  italki.com appears to be a specialized product with a very specific focus:  Letting "students" pick their preferred language instructor. Getting back to your original questions, which are perfectly fine questions to ask here on moodle.org: "I want each teacher to have a page, with introductions, videos and .... and students, select their own teachers and enroll in their courses." I don't think you can achieve this, where students pick their own teachers.  I think this might take special coding.  Moodle seems to prefer organizing its data around "courses."  And then these courses already have teachers in them. But one could provide each language teacher their own course, and the course could contain teacher introductions, and videos, and whatever that particular teacher wants to include.  Yep, if you have 1000 teachers, Moodle can handle 1000 courses.  Each course could have an enrollment key, which somehow is provided to each student.  Additionally, these 1000 courses could, for example, be put into their own categories by language, such as Spanish, German, etc.  So it might be that the answer to this question is "yes."  But it still would require some administration. I don't know of any plugin that allows students to pick a teacher, then get an enrollment key.  But this probably could be coded.  You might have a "master file" of teachers and enrollment keys.  Or use the Paypal plugin and let students pick any teacher's course. As far as "I want students to be able to rate teachers.  And moodle sort teachers according to their rating or other taxonomies?" Again, this seems to be a specialized plugin.  As an idea, maybe you could have one course be for teacher ratings.  And somehow use an idea like moodle.org's (a forum feature) where students can rate "like."  This might take some brainstorming.  Maybe something like a forum that has a post for every instructor, where students can rate. However, Moodle is not italki.com.  But there might be ways to accomplish what you want to do, either directly (and creatively), or by writing a plugin.  If you plan to charge students by the hour, as xxx does, maybe you would be able to pay a programmer to create the necessary plugins.

I located where the categories are being collapsed in the renderer. You can force the categories to be opened when the page is loaded by changing 
```text
if ($chelper->get_subcat_depth() > 0 && $depth >= $chelper->get_subcat_depth()) {
```
 to 
```text
if (false && $chelper->get_subcat_depth() > 0 && $depth >= $chelper->get_subcat_depth()) {
```
 (Shown below) Original Function Modified You could make this modification directly in the renderer but you can prevent a core edit and make your upgrades easier by overriding the renderer via the theme. If the Moove theme has already overridden this function, then you will have to modify it in the theme to see the changes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle APP: changing colors?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Stefan,
I don't think anyone has created something like this. The "orange" colour is defined as as SASS variable in the app's source code, if you pay for a branded Moodle app this will be overridden with the colour you specify in your version. However, once the app is built, the colour will be used in lots of different CSS rules. I'd suggest you start by running Moodle Desktop and opening the developer tools with Ctrl+Alt+I. From here, you can inspect each orange element to work out which rule is applying the colour, and override it in your custom CSS.

ResponsesInList.Text: Ok I believe I am experiencing the same issue as https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=388894 I found the tracker case for the issue MDL-66569 Turns out they did make a change in how email was handled. The recommendation is to use local MTA relay. So here is what I have done and will continue to test over the next few days. 1. Install Postfix on ubuntu 2. configured it to send to amazon SES ( https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/DeveloperGuide/postfix.html ) 3. cleared out smtp settings in moodle (blanks), my understanding if it is blank moodle (phpmailer) will use system default to send mail So far tests look good. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students not getting email with New Announcement
ResponsesInList.Text: Of course a local mail server like Postfix or Exim gives you the maximum flexibility. Yes, then all the SMTP settings in Moodle are empty. Configuring Postfix to send mail directly, in plain SMTP, is trivial. See https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=390369#p1573674 . It you want to relay them through another mail server, this time SMTP-Auth, is a bit more involved. The tutorial you've linked has it. See also the follow-up in the sub-thread mentioned above. BTW , MDL-66569 is not a bug as Andrew Nicols explains there. It helps to push large number of e-mails to (major) MXes. Still what surprises me is why you should hit it with your 114 students. Is the AWS server particularly sensitive (although the mails originate in their network and authenticated)? (The 2 hour delay could mean that.) If so you might have to do some tuning in Postfix. BTW, why do you relay through them, not let local Postfix send directly to the recipients' MX?

ResponsesInList.Title: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: Good day Version: Moodle 3.6.2+ (Build: 20190301) Currently a teacher can grade submissions on an assignment without a student having submitted anything. Why is this the case? Is there a way to disable this? Ideally I would like this to only be an option if both submission types have been disabled. Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't think so. Albeit a common use-case, grading uploaded work isn't the only use for Assignment. It could just as well be used to grade and provide feedback for a practical activity (for example). In that case there would be no submission. It begs the question why, if a teacher is expecting to assess a file submission, they would attempt to grade someone who hasn't submitted anything.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you from the prompt reply. What would be the best approach to implement a plugin to patch this situation? Would it be an assignment feedback plugin or perhaps a simple local plugin trying to block a grade change if no submission is found but it is possible to submit something? (Would assume this is do able)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: If the student doesn't submit, wouldn't the teacher grade this as a "0"? (However, some lenient teachers might grade this as 50%, or something like that.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: The issue is that teachers can give marks when a submission is required and the mark can be non-zero. For my setup this is an issue as the graders should not be able to give essentially fraudulent results. If a teacher could give a zero and only a zero this would make sense in my opinion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunately, I think you have a very unusual need. I've never seen a similar request. I can't think of a straightforward way to sort this. The easiest thing (relatively) would be a custom report to identify when marks had been given but no file had been submitted. Even that would be a lot of work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: 'Of course, it occurs to me that if you are concerned about your staff giving fraudulent marks then how do you know they even bothered to read the submission? You may have bigger problems than Moodle...' I guess wanting to avoid unnecessary permissions where possible may be a bit extreme at times. The observation of giving marks with nothing submitted being comparable to just giving a mark without reading the submission is apt. The fact that this kind of falsehood is easy to spot and fully logged makes it much less likely when compared to standard flaws of grading. I will discuss this with my colleagues and see if we can just accept that for now this is how things are and just work with the constraint. Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: The following scenario may also happen: A teacher would create an assignment and set a cut-off date. The student wouldn't submit on time. The student would write an emotional e-mail message to the teacher and will beg for an extension. The teacher wouldn't know about the "User override" option and will tell the student to just send him the file by e-mail. The teacher would review the submission and would mark in Moodle, because it would convenient. You would look at the relevant row in the submissions table, and think that the teacher gave a fraudulent mark.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable grading if no submission
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear James, For a temporary solution, I think you can set the Capabilities mod/assign:releasegrades to "Prevent" for your teachers. And assign a course manager to review all grades for assessments before releasing them to students. Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: All teachers receiving assignment email notifications. HELP!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steven, I'm guessing your teachers also have a site-level or category-level role on your Moodle site, and that users with that role are set to "Get a notification message when an [QUIZ] attempt is submitted". If yes, Go to Site Administration > Users > Permissions > Capability Overview Search for "mod/quiz:emailnotifysubmission" Click on Roles: All Click on "Get the overview" By default in Moodle, this will be 'Not Set' for all roles. However on your site, I expect it will be set for at least one of those roles. Click on that role and edit it to remove the capability.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Identified empty (not used) Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: you can use configurable report block to create reports I suggest you create reports to show the number of resources, activities , and announcements used in each course if the resources and activities are zero, then you can consider it "empty" courses. you can also show number of students in each course if no students are enrolled you can consider them not used too. this is a link for sql reports here is an example of report I used to show list of courses and number of files uploaded in each course ============================================== SELECT c.shortname as courseID,concat('',c.fullname,'') CourseName, cat.id,cat.name As Cat ,(SELECT COUNT( DISTINCT ra.userid ) AS Users FROM prefix_role_assignments AS ra JOIN prefix_context AS ctx ON ra.contextid = ctx.id WHERE ra.roleid = 5 AND ctx.instanceid = c.id) AS Students ,COUNT(l.id) AS Files ,(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( CONCAT( u.firstname,  " ", u.lastname ) ) FROM prefix_course ic JOIN prefix_context con ON con.instanceid = ic.id JOIN prefix_role_assignments ra ON con.id = ra.contextid AND con.contextlevel = 50 JOIN prefix_role r ON ra.roleid = r.id JOIN prefix_user u ON u.id = ra.userid WHERE r.id = 3 AND ic.id = c.id GROUP BY ic.id ) AS TeacherNames FROM prefix_course c LEFT JOIN prefix_resource l  ON l.course = c.id JOIN prefix_course_categories As cat on c.category=cat.id GROUP BY courseID, c.category ORDER BY cat.id, Files DESC

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to access moodle code and edit
ResponsesInList.Text: The changes not appearing may be the result of: Server Cache - maybe purging all caches would help: https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Developer_tools#Purge_all_caches Local (Web broswer) cache - Although purging all caches is supposed to force the web browser of the user to load the latest page from the server, I tend to use Incognito Mode (in Google Chrome) so no local cache would be used. However, please note the following regarding Incognito cache: https://www.quora.com/Does-incognito-mode-on-Chrome-use-the-cache-that-was-previously-stored Anyway, make sure that you are making the changes to the code of Moodle in a backed up environment, so you could go back fast to the starting position, in case something goes wrong, and when changing code, a lot of things can go wrong.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to access moodle code and edit
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nathan, Please see the following discussion from 2017: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=350680 and this page from Moodle Docs : https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Mobile_support_for_plugins#Options_only_for_CoreBlockDelegate Even if it was possible to view all the blocks in the mobile app, I don't think that would be good, UX-wise (UX = User Experience). Displaying blocks on a big screen is one thing, but displaying them on a small screen is another thing. At least in my opinion blocks are not the best element on a mobile platform - they take too much space. The same way most good websites have a version for desktop and a version for mobile, blocks in desktop should have a suitable equivalent in Mobile.

ResponsesInList.Title: how to change php.ini file Moodle uses
ResponsesInList.Text: I have Moodle 2.7.20 hosted on a shared hosting site (hostmonster).  I was having trouble with some php.ini settings not working and I realized it's because instead of using the php.ini in my public_html folder it is using this for the php.ini:    (from doing php info via Moodle) Configuration File (php.ini) Path /opt/cpanel/ea-php56/root/etc I don't want to use this one because since it's a shared server , I cannot edit it! Question is simple and I've really tried looking for an answer here and elsewhere to no avail: How can I just change the php.ini file that Moodle is using?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to change php.ini file Moodle uses
ResponsesInList.Text: That php.ini file is placed in your code by cPanel.  Use your cPanel to set version, php extensions your site will load, and parameters to setttings of PHP ... like max file size allowed to upload . Comments for what they are worth ... your version of Moodle 2.7.20 is very very old and no longer supported for any security fixes or code fixes from Moodle.org. A shared hosting plan means you are greatly restricted ... there are caps/limits which you cannot override. In anticipation of next question ... 'can moodle be hacked' by you or others to bypass those limits/restrictions... answer is no. And the follow up recommendation ... upgrade your shared hosting to a VPS ... and that's what tech support with provider will tell you as well! Best of luck! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Delete previously uploaded video file
ResponsesInList.Text: " videos uploaded as system files " Because of what you said above, a question ... in any course did you set up a file system repository and upload the videos there using any tool you have to upload files outside of Moodle ... like FileZilla or cPanel's file manager. Sign ... edit mode turned on, go to any course, look in course admin menu.   See a 'repositories' link?   That's a file system repository. If that is true, then the files could be located in your moodledata/respository/[somedirectory]/ folder/directory. where [somedirectory] above is a folder/directory you created via your servers folder/file management. Files in there could be removed manually by same tool/process you used to put them there thus freeing up space, but if you've linked to them in Moodle, those links will be broken ... ie, file not found error is certain. Also recommend, if above is the case, download those videos for archiving on your local machine before deleting. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Invalid Course Module ID
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Nigel, Having had a look at the code behind it and the database, although the exact same error messages are occuring for you on multiple courses, they can in fact have different causes. First cause is that there are grade_items in your database which are linked to activity modules which were either removed or marked as disabled. The second cause could be that there is a course_module record saying Course A has an instance (123) of Module B attached to it, but Module B has no actual record of that instance 123 in its own table. I have written some quicky and dirty cli scripts to fix both these issues for you, which I've attached to this post. They should be placed in /admin/cli/ They can then be run from the command line, by running: 
```text
    php /path/to/your/moodle/admin/cli/fix_old_grade_items.php
```
 and 
```text
    php /path/to/your/moodle/admin/cli/fix_invalid_course_modules.php
```
 Both scripts can be run on a specific course, by adding --course=123 to the end, where 123 is the course id. Both scripts can be run in 'dryrun' mode, which will show you the records its going to delete, but not actually do it, by adding --dryrun to the end. E.g. 
```text
    php /path/to/your/moodle/admin/cli/fix_old_grade_items.php --dryrun --course=123
```
 Let me know how you get on. Conn

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Basic version of Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rakesh, to answer your question, no there is no "basic Moodle" unless you call what is directly out of the box the basic edition. While the answers you already have cover the main issues, they miss two fundamental points, I suggest. We forget sometimes that when we started, certainly with me, Moodle was a awful lot simpler to learn and use. Moodle has had to grow over the last 19 years, and with that growth comes an increased complexity in use, tools, security and therefore administration. In response, or perhaps as an adjunct to, that increasing complexity, Mary has pointed out the ready availability of videos and MoodleDocs to cover the essential admin concepts and some guides. The other issue we usually overlook is that the environment in which Moodle runs had also undergone similar transformations. There is much more to learn about setting up and running not just the Moodle but the entire environment, making sure it all plays nicely together. In turn, this also impacts on the Moodle, taking advantage of newer technologies, like mobile Moodles and I am sure others will come along, like Moodle on a smart watch for example. The only advice that can really be given here is to build a test site then sit and play with it. Break it, if you can, reinstall it, fix something, add something, take something out. See what happens. In the meantime, just keep your production site running in the out of the box mode, it should pretty well run on its own with a minimum of fuss, as along as you don't change anything. You can pick up on the basics pretty quickly, and make sure you test everything on your test site before you do anything on your production site. Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When a user first enters a course they see a big, long list of all sections - How to prevent this?
ResponsesInList.Text: Here are two suggestions that I use: 1) I hide most sections and then turn new sections on each week. The combination of these two ideas works well for me.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to get Moodle Technical support?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello All, My institute uses Moodle to deliver academic credit courses.  Sometimes we need technical support.  For example, some students cannot access some video urls from Moodle. Is there any way to get fast expert technical support for Moodle? Thank You!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get Moodle Technical support?
ResponsesInList.Text: ﻿ Find a MP that does remote support: https://moodle.com/partners/ Advertise @ https://moodle.org/mod/data/view.php?d=54 Find an independent ... many can be ID'd in these forums ... and inquire. BTW , am an independent, but not seeking right now ... have enough to do! Best of luck! SoS, Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get Moodle Technical support?
ResponsesInList.Text: If moodle is using a URL resource for the video, check that the URL is correct. Copy it and paste it directly into a browser's address line. If it doesn't play in a browser, it will likely not play from a Moodle URL resource link. If it plays for some students, and not others, this is kind of strange behavior. Explore what browsers the students are using, and even if they are on a Mac, PC, Chrombook, etc. Also, you might want to provide a screenshot showing us the error message. Ken has already answered your question about getting expert technical support. I am not one of these technical experts. I am just an instructor who saw your question and wanted to provide you some ideas.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get Moodle Technical support?
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh, yeah ... one more thought if support coming from outside your entity and there is an expectation of resolution of the problem ASAP ... get support from individual/entity that's close to your timezone or from company that has folks working 24 hours a day. Why?   If you are on West Coast USA and support person/entity not having 24 hour support is half way 'round the globe there's a 'timing' issue. Recent experience in working with small city college site in a moodle march in Austrialia led to a situation where ... and this is a quote from technical person for that site ... 'you're going to fast!'    Hmmm ... tech support sleeping when I was working ... and vice versa ... I was sleeping when tech support working. :|  No international voice calls ... besides .... neither one of us wanted to 'loose sleep' over 'the march'. Anyhoo ... another 2 cents! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Stuck upgrading; can't point to the right PHP version?
ResponsesInList.Text: EASY (yeah, right!) enables user to set php version.  With the .htaccess file in place it did point to a version of PHP needed to run Moodle 3.x+->. When you removed the .htaccess file, your system defaulted to a version of php (5.6.x) which cannot be used to upgrade from 3.6.2 to 3.7.highest. So, put the .htaccess file back. ;) Blank screen and error 500 is what needs to be investigated. Using whatever you have to browse files find the config.php file in your Moodle code and see if ownership/permissions are correct - config.php needs to be readable by the globe but NOT writable but for the user under which your moodle runs ... which, on remotely hosted systems, could be the account login you use with provider. Moodle caches a lot ... and there is lots that changed from 3.6.x to 3.7.highest. Using file browser, navigate to moodledata directory ... that's * moodledata * directory. Inside there one should see: 'cache', 'localcache', and a 'muc' directories. remove the contents ... repeat remove the contents those directories ... safe to do as Moodle should rebuild them. Back to browser, refresh your browser ... fingers crossed ... we have a new moodle. Also, if the theme looks messed up it's due to major theme changes from 3.6.x to 3.7.x.  3.6.x used boost and a boostphase.  3.7.x has boost but no boostphase.   So, you might need to edit config.php and add the following line $CFG=theme='classic'; It's the only other theme that comes with a new stock 3.7.x.  Your site as a 3.6.x might have had an incompatible theme for 3.7.x 'SoS', Ken

Copy any mods/blocks/ folders from sxxxx.old into new sxxxx in same locations. mods go to mods blocks go to blocks theme go to theme. All the above can be done via your cPanel file manager. Once config.php and mods/blocks/themes from old 3.6 site have been *copied* into the 3.7 code now in /sxxxxxx/ Make sure the easy apache created .htaccess flle for verison of PHP to run is at the root of /sxxxxxx/ If you have an .htacess file above /sxxxxx/ that is re-directing all traffic from / to /sxxxx/   To avoid .htaccess confusion and conflict follow KISS. I have been running Moodle 3 for three or four years. I am careful about uploads (for example, I never upload videos to my moodle.) When my database got to being 1GB, my hosted server company said that my database had exceeded their hosted server specs of 1GB. So I had to go with a VPS, which I still run today. I now have 120GB of space, and I am at about 70% full. Yes, I agree about preserving Moodle analytics. You might want to start exploring a VPS, ahead of when your hosting company forces this upon you. I assume you have a Windows server because you like Windows. But think briefly about a Linux server, when many folks (certainly not all) seem to run.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Removing the option for Notes at Site Context

I suspect this is related to either a permissions issue, or you have assigned some/all teachers at the system/site context , or this is only affecting some teachers who have higher permissions elsewhere on your system By default, users can only view Notes that have been created within the same context to which their Role has been assigned (e.g. Site, Course, Personal/User). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New Users Load to Profile, then Preferences
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm presuming this is happening because you have required profile fields on a user profile which don't appear on signup? It happened to my organisation when we added a new profile after existing users already had an account, forcing an update of the new profile (as it's now a required field)  when they next logged in. Anyway, the real issue is that after updating the user profile from the page "(moodlesite)/user/edit.php" you are forced back to "(moodlesite)/user/preferences.php". This seems to be predetermined by Moodle core php and needs this to be edited in core code. You need to look at moodle/user/edit.php around line 192 (this may change depending on the version of moodle you are using) and change "$returnurl = new moodle_url('/user/preferences.php', array('userid' => $user->id));" to "$returnurl = new moodle_url('/?redirect=1');" This will take them back to the default landing page you have set. I recommend commenting out the old line (with "//") and adding the new one underneath so you can go back easily if needed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding multiple page
ResponsesInList.Text: No stop, don't do anything like that. Moodle is bandwidth light, until you start adding multimedia, then it gets a little heavy. With eighty videos, this could play havoc with your bandwidth if you have a lot of Users downloading videos at the same time. One thing you could try is to create a PDF with the links required in it. Or have a link to an external file somewhere on your server perhaps, outside of your Moodle that opens in a new window that then links to the videos. That way it doesn't use any Moodle resources to download or open videos. Or, you can have this file located on another server , through which you can get to the videos you need your Users to look at. Something else, I understand you can create a play list or a menu of connected videos. I am not sure if this relates only to your own videos or to any collection of videos you want to put together.  You may use this idea to create a number of menus or playlists to ensure your users only watch the videos you want them to watch. In either case, a single link to this menu item should also work to diminish the bandwidth use on your Moodle. Someone else may have more information than I do on this, as I only have my own videos on my channel, and none of them are publicly listed. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding multiple page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alessio, I think you have drudgery ahead of you whatever you do. However, here are a few pointers that may be helpful. If you haven't already, change your preferred editor to Plain Text - that way you're not having to change it every time you go in to edit a page - you'll see the html straight away. Create one page with an embedded YouTube video. If you can, install the mass actions block and duplicate your page over and over again. First you can duplicate 1, then you can duplicate 2, then 4, then 8, then 16, etc. so it won't take so long Then go in to each page - maybe open 10 at a time in tabs. You'll need to paste in the Video name in the title, and just replace the video ID in your embed code. The rest of it won't change anyway. Put on some good music while you're doing it and it won't be so bad!

ResponsesInList.Title: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everybody, I have 3 different courses (course A, course B and course C), each one with paypal enrollment and each one of them with with hundreds of active enrollments. I want to add an option so that new members can have a discount if they enroll in all courses at once. I think the solution for this is to create a new meta course, with paypal enrollment (with the discount price). Am I right? My doubt is: 1- Should I create copies of course A, B, C (without the enrolled users and their data), and then link their copies to the new Metcaourse. So they will enroll themselves after paying a fee and then have access to the new A, B and C courses. 2- I don't need to create copies of courses A, B, C. I simply need to create one metacourse with the paypal enrollment with the new price and link the existing courses to it. If this is the solution, should I set it up to add/create a group to the existing courses? Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: If Course A, B, C are already child courses, then what you're proposing is the most logical approach.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry, but I didn't get what you said. I'm not proposing anything. I've thought about two ways of doing one thing and I'm asking your help to decide which one is best As for courses A,B and C being child themes, I don't know if they are. They are the only courses that I have. All of them have manual enrollment with the paypal enrollment enabled. None of them are meta courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: It is a long time since i used meta courses, but from what I remember a meta course is most likely not what you need. This is the reason: Participants of a child course gets access to the parent course. So, current participants of A now have access to the new meta course. Same with the current participants of B and C. But a new participant to the parent (meta) course will remain in the parent course. He will not see the child courses, courses A-C.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: Let's call the metacourse, course D. What if course D is the parent course, for A, B, C. So student would enroll in course D via paypal with the special price and Course D would not have any thing in there rather than links to access courses A, B and C. Whoever is enrolled in Course A, would remain having access in Course A only, the same for B and C. Would that work?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunately it is the other war around: participants of only the parent course, course D, have no access to the child courses, courses A-C. On the other hand, there are no child only participants, say participants limited to course A. They will automatically have access to the parent course, course D. (That is the whole idea of the meta course.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok... thanks for clarifying. So what would the solution be? I need students enrolled in Course D to have access to existing courses A-C. Or there is no solution at all?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: As I said, it is the other way around: A-C will be meta (parent) courses. D a child course of all three. The caveat: If I remember correctly, you can't just make a normal course a meta course. You need to go through a duplication procedure somewhat similar to what you wrote at the beginning. The difference is that you will make three meta (parent) courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text:
Sorry, I misunderstood what you were saying in your original post, I interpreted it as your A, B, C courses were already Meta courses. Before you go any further, this link goes to the Moodle Doc  on Meta Course Links , read that, if you haven't already. Visvanath is correct, if your courses A, B and C are ordinary courses, you will have to duplicate the courses as Meta
Courses, without User enrollments, then re-enroll the Users in a set of child courses. Once you have done that, you can then create your new child course, D, link it to Parent Courses A, B and C then link it to PayPal and it should all work. You will just have to be explicit in how you advertise your course payment structure. For what you are trying to do, this is the safest way, I suggest. The reason I say this is that if a User wants only to enroll in 1 course, you put them into
the appropriate child course. If they want to enroll in all courses, then you can enroll them into a fourth course, D. That way, they do not interfere with each other, there is no crossover, all User data is located in whatever the course/s they are
enrolled in, and they only have access to the course/s they are enrolled in. The Meta course link Moodle Doc is now clear enough to allow you to do this quickly, but not without some fiddling about.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please, help with course structure
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for your help. I think it's clear now. I'll try to do it and if I face any issue I'll ask for further help. All the best!

ResponsesInList.Text: Nidhi, You can do that following the instructions here: https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Course_creator_role which show you how to add someone to the system Course Creator role. There is no automatic link on the Dashboard for such a role to create courses, but you can make one: - Add the Courses block to the Dashboard for them, then when they click the "All courses" link at the bottom of the block, the next page will have a "Add new course button" on it. - Or you can add a simple HTML block and in it put a link that loads that same page, which will look like this: http://yourmoodlesite.com /course/index.php where the button is, where you put in the correct url to your site, of course. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: do moodle has pdf viewr ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi! The mod_resource (File in the activity picker) is the one to have a look at. If you set the display options for the file to appear in browser, the pdf should automatically display using the browser's own pdf viewer/interpreter. Either add the mod_resource through the activity picker, then set the appropriate display options, or drag-drop the pdf to your course page, then edit settings to get to the display options. If the 'In browser' option does not appear, go to Site administration > Plugins > Activity modules > File (mod_resource) and make the display options available. Also, have a look at the Moodle Docs on this module: https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/File_resource

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Developing a chatbot for supporting teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't resile from my original comments, a chat bot would be nice, but why go to the extreme of making one? If I had a lot of people requiring it, and a large organization behind them, sure, it would be worth it. Most education organizations would, I suspect, have a teacher/student ratio of about 1:25, some lower and many more, higher. So the point at which the development of a chat bot to use in Moodle becomes a cost-effective solution is when? 100 staff? 200? Really, this is an old, old problem, and exists for every software package ever released, not just a Moodle problem. How about simply making videos of the most common problems and allow staff to access them? Would that not help people more if they have direct access to the information they need? Moodle doesn't change everything every new release. I am still uploading files the same way I did when v2.1 was released. I still add activities the same way. I added a disclaimer to a video on an old site I used to admin which said something like "This video contains up to date information on how to upload files to this Moodle, from v2.2 and forward. The video will change when the process changes. Any differences in appearance may result from changing the Theme, but the process will remain the same."  I unashamedly pinched an older term from a former Moodle employee, really tall, very clever and really nice guy (I forget his name) and called the series "2 Minute Moodles". I hope the people who took over the Moodle kept them going, but I haven't heard. I do the same things now, have accessible, comprehensive, short and single pointed videos. I am also adding the videos I am finding that are connected to the Moodle Docs that explain stuff, when I don't have time to make one. I am placing these videos into a single course for staff to access when they need them. So I have to ask, where is the need for a chat bot here? EDIT: The key is cost effectiveness. When making, using, training a chat-bot becomes a more cost effective solution, i.e. cheaper and easier than making videos, sure, I'll change my approach, but I suspect that won't be for a while yet.

ResponsesInList.Title: Frustrations: Moodle & Blinded Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Just wanted to share a front-line frustration from trying to mangle Moodle (3.5.6) into actually allowing blinded grading. This is frustrating, because when I'm running multiple stage assignments (e.g., they submit short essays in serial; receiving feedback on each), it forces me to reveal identities to release grades. This is frustrating, because I don't want to see who is writing on what topic, or who received what grade - I want the entire assignment process to remain blinded until the end of the project. Per https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Assignment_settings#Anonymous_marking , this is normal system behaviour, so I suppose this is a feature request to allow those of us who actually want to maintain blinding throughout an assignment or semester to do so.

ResponsesInList.Text: No, it's a totally reasonable question! The workflow I use is that I choose date X as the day I plan to actually grade assignments, and then make them due on date X-1. But, everyone in my class has a free 24hr extension, as long as they notify me before the due date. So, what I'd like to be able to do is to go in + record who took the extension in Moodle as they request them, then be able to see if it was on time or not (e.g., day X-1 if no extension, day X if extension) while still in blinded mode. As an aside, the workflow for the first request is that we have a three-part assignment where they select a common case study throughout the whole term. I'd like to be able to grade all three parts blinded before finally revealing identities at the end of the semester (i.e., go back and see what I said about assignment 1 when grading assignment 2). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frustrations: Moodle & Blinded Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: So we might be back to my original question. If only one (or two) students ask for the extension, they when you go to grade it after the due date, you know who this student is. This is no longer blind. (Even if only two or three students ask for the extension, it really is not quite blind.) Or, if you find that most students ask for the extension, why not simply set the due date to your cut-off. Why make nearly all students ask, knowing that they are all granted a one-day extension? Also, since you allow students to discuss what they are doing, you probably are not totally unbiased. If you forget who is who, why worry about blind grading? Do you feel that you really can't be objective when you see their name? Do you really mean that the most beautiful young attractive student whose name you have memorized is going to affect your grading of her assignment... that you can't force yourself to be objective? If what I ask is true, why not consider using a rubric so that you can blast through the grading of these assignments with fixed words (from your rubric?)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frustrations: Moodle & Blinded Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, The typical response is that somewhere between 10-20 in a class of 60 ask for the 24-hr extension. So, it's a nice level where I functionally don't know who asks for it, but it's also not the entire class. Hence my question of wanting to be able to note these during blind mode, because otherwise I have to grade, then unblind, then adjust grades based on who was actually late vs. not. Re: "why worry about blind grading," I do it because I am a human. Like all humans, I'm certainly not unbiased. I use blind grading because there is strong evidence that professors are subject to the exact same biases everyone else is. We know, for instance, that professors use significantly fewer superlatives in describing female students than male ones (Schmader et al, 2007). Meta reviews show that bias affects all level of grading, including university and collegiate, and that professors and instructors take into account much information other than the quality of the work in their grades assigned (Malouff & Thorsteinsson, 2016). And, we also know - to my specific feature request about keeping assignments blinded throughout the term - that performance on one assignment statistically affects our grading of the student's other subsequent assignments, which is known as the "halo effect" (Malouff et al, 2013). The reason to use blind grading consistently is that our grading biases can creep in via many different pathways. In your classes summing to 125 or my class of 60, it's not that bias only occurs if you know everyone's assignment... even if you just remember that one keen, engaged, high-performing student's topic, you're likely to subconsciously grade them higher because of the halo effect. I do use rubrics, by the way. However, the problem with bias is that it affects /how/ we use the rubric... that we don't use it consistently from student to student. Of course, as I mentioned earlier, there's a challenge: despite the strong body of literature demonstrating the vital importance of blind grading in all assignments by all instructors, personalized mentorship is just as important (e.g., feedback on topics, etc). This is where trying to explicitly fight to control biases comes in (acknowledging each of our limitations as a human, rather than claiming false objectivity), as well as trying to get participation up to such a point where I can overload my memory and try to avoid remembering their topics. Because you asked, they're submitting essays in this course on cognitive science. But I also do it in my ethics class and research methods class too - all three being places where "walking the walk" of being fair and empirically informed in my pedagogical methods is important. Hence my feature request. Best, Eric Works Cited: Malouff, J. M., Emmerton, A. J., & Schutte, N. S. (2013). The risk of a halo bias as a reason to keep students anonymous during grading. Teaching of Psychology, 40(3), 233-237. Malouff, J. M., & Thorsteinsson, E. B. (2016). Bias in grading: A meta-analysis of experimental research findings. Australian Journal of Education, 60(3), 245-256. Schmader, T., Whitehead, J., & Wysocki, V. H. (2007). A linguistic comparison of letters of recommendation for male and female chemistry and biochemistry job applicants. Sex roles, 57(7-8), 509-514.

ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, I understand. However, we are still human beings. I understand the research. But there is still a practical issue. In the U.S., when our president Trump tweets a simple paragraph, some people rate it high, and some low. Is this because people know the source? However, even if you didn't know the source, some would still rate it high and some low. This is because we are still humans, and we are each individually interpret what was said. Sure, you can add all kinds of overhead to this grading, like having a team of 20 instructors collectively grade each student's essay question. But this is a lot of overhead. Quite honestly, this is why I limit my use of assignments. They are really hard to grade. The best that I am able to do is to look for key items in an assignment. I teach business courses. The problem in business is that success can happen to non-standard methods. My guess is that Bill Gates and the (late) Steve Jobs would get bad grades for their business ideas because they were not replying with the "standard" or "expected" response. Of course, I love teaching quantitative business courses because 2+3 is almost always equal to ... 6? No, 5. And then, in my case, I also have international students. I can often tell that a forum post is from an international student, even before I look at their names. How do you remove this kind of bias? Anyway, I appreciate what you are trying to do. I am enjoying this discussion. As you can see, I am far from the expert on blind grading. Getting back to Moodle... Why not create two assignments, one titled "1st submission" and then another "2nd resubmission?" Then, in the grade book, create a grade item that would take the "maximum" of these two assignments? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Frustrations: Moodle & Blinded Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Just jumping back here to add a solution in case any other forum users come along in hopes of being able to do this. It works! If you click on the assignment to get to the summary page (i.e., the one with the due date, number submitted, etc) and click the gear icon in the top right, there's an option called "User Overrides". This allows you to adjust individual due dates by name, while /not/ unblinding the grading. That way, it will test whether each user was "on time" according to their individual deadline, but won't reveal who is who. As Rick mentioned above, if you have a class of 8 and only one requests an extension, of course, this won't be de facto blinded. But in larger classes where multiple people request extensions, it lets you grant them within the Moodle interface without having to unblind assignments.

ResponsesInList.Title: mdl_logstore_standard_log size problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, What version of Moodle 3.0.3 What is your operating system, what web server are you using, what database and what are the versions of everything (including PHP)? Linux, Apache2.2, Mysql 5.6, php 5.6 I've a problem that this table is 40G and keep growing. This table causing performance issues for all database transaction such as backup, etc. So i need answers please to below questions: What is this table used for? What is the risk of TRUNCATE this table? How to automatically keep 3 months records only from this table?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: mdl_logstore_standard_log size problem
ResponsesInList.Text:
This table is used to provide the reports shown in Site administration → Reports → Logs . Some third party plugins may also use this information. The risk of a TRUNCATE TABLE is to your records-keeping and data retention requirements. For example if you wanted to check the logs for something that happened last week the information would be gone. You can set a retention period for these logs under Site administration → Plugins → Logging → Standard log and changing Keep logs for to the required value. If you make that last change the site cron will delete older records but it won't do this in one go (it will delete as much as it can for five minutes then wait till the next run) but the table size will reduce over time. You could delete the older records manually, the statement below should work but make a backup of the database first: 
```text
DELETE FROM mdl_logstore_standard_log WHERE timecreated < UNIX_TIMESTAMP(DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 90 DAY));
```
 Then you could optionally run OPTIMIZE TABLE mdl_logstore_standard_log to recover space on the filesystem (assuming innodb_file_per_table is enabled). Note that both the DELETE FROM and OPTIMIZE TABLE statements may impact the site's performance when they're running. (Support for Moodle 3.0 ended in 2015, you should plan to upgrade your site to a supported version . Moodle 3.0.3 is seven updates behind the final update 3.0.10).
