ResponsesInList.Title: Re: mdl_logstore_standard_log size problem
ResponsesInList.Text:
You can check if the cron is working by going to Site administration → Notifications . If it is not running you'll see a message like "The cli/cron.php maintenance script has not been run for at least 24 hours". If you see this message you need to set up the site cron (your site will not work properly without it). You can check the cron is completing successfully by running it at the command line . If your cron appears to be working you can see check the oldest entry in the log table with the query: 
```text
SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(MIN(timecreated)) FROM mdl_logstore_standard_log;
```
 If old records are being removed, this date should move forward every 24 hours. The cron does not perform OPTIMIZE TABLE , you would need to do this manually. However, this operation can only recover space on the database server , it will not change the size of the database backup.

(good point) Hi all The problem has been solved! Thank you all for your input. Solution: If you are on a shared hosting plan and you have a 3rd party anti-malware company that uses a CDN to route your traffic through, checking for malware before going to the server. The firewall caching  is the problem. The caching level on the securi firewall was set to 'enabled' by default. This will cause session issues for Moodle. Change the caching level to 'site caching'. This caching level will respect the headers sent by Moodle. It may cache the page content if Moodle sends the no-cache header. Thank you all, Adam

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course completion - tow sets of activity conditions ((AND)AND(OR))
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Almats, I don't believe this is possible unfortunately - there have been similar questions in the forum in the past and no real solution. You say "Separate courses are not an option as they will have the same content and only different test" but there is a variation on this solution that you might be open to as there is still only one version of each piece of content: Have one course for all the learning activities . Therse were:   Checklist (activity), Checklist (block), Checklist (grading method) and Checkmark. But I am able to remove the profiles by hitting back and resubmitting the request the same amount of users to be removed. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Invalid course module ID when removing users
ResponsesInList.Text: Miriam Because some of these, such as the Checklist activity, are course modules, they will have entries for users who used them. Since the module itself has been deleted from the site, there's a missing course module id in the database . Basically, there still exists a reference to the module in the record of what the student did, but there's no module anymore for it to refer to. When deleting the user, it is trying to clean out such references and gets stuck because it can't find the module referred to. I think two things: 1) Did you first unenroll the student from the course? If the activities behave as they should, when a student is unenrolled, they should clean out that activity data. Should, anyway. Try that and see if that helps if you did not already. 2) For modules in a site that may have data in use, I usually prefer to simply disable them rather than uninstall them if no longer using them. Sometimes this is not always possible (for example when upgrading and the plugin may be too old, or if it is tossing out big errors), but generally having it sit there disabled is okay and helps to retain the data integrity meanwhile. Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: My teachers cannot see list of participants
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hendrik, Do you know if you changed the default 'editingteacher' role, to block or disable any permissions enabled by default? I found that disabling moodle/course:enrolreview disables the option of viewing participants in a course. This permission is enabled by default to allow editingteachers and managers participant and role management. If you need to change a role, for whatever reason, it's a best practice to not change the archetypical role, but create a copy of it and change the permissions there. That way, it's easier to roll back on an unfortunate or unexpected effect of enabling or disabling a permission .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz reports via Cohort?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Seb, Sync your cohorts to groups in the course. You can then filter your quiz report by group. Catherine

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz reports via Cohort?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Catherine, Thanks for the reply. If it's not to much trouble could you give me a guide on how to do this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz reports via Cohort?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Seb, Sure. Here's a high level instruction: Go to the course page that the quiz is on. Go to the enrolment methods of that page (Course administration > Users > Enrolment methods). I am assuming from your original question that your participants are enrolled by cohort sync. Go to the settings of one of those cohort syncs (see screenshot) On the 'Add to group' dropdown, Create a new group, save your change. Do this for each cohort. Now go to the settings of your quiz. Scroll down to 'Common Module Settings'. Set the Group Mode to 'visible groups' and save your change. Now go to the quiz report page. In the top left you will now see a dropdown list of the groups in your course. Choose a group to filter your report by that group.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need help with changing mysql configuration
ResponsesInList.Text: It's a bit more complex. One needs to be able to switch from Antelop to Barracuda. This is somewhat of a back-end database issue, and on many of these hosted servers, but not all, this is not allowed. Some later versions of MariaDB don't need this change, which is why I mentioned MariaDB. I think (maybe Usman mentioned in another discussion) that some companies like Bluehost are now using MariaDB as their default instead of MySQL . This situation has caught a lot of folks who want to run Moodle on a low-cost hosted server . Many years ago, I ran my Moodle on a GoDaddy hosted server, but then I upgraded to a VPS before this Barracuda stuff happened. To minimize your headache, search around a little because Usman had offered some ideas (maybe solutions) to a few other folks discussing the same problem. (Usman, hope that I am not misrepresenting you.) My guess is that this problem might go away with time. But until then... "Terminal" is a way of saying "SSH" access. Yes, GoDaddy supports SSH and FTP access to these hosted servers. In cPanel, search for either "SSH" and " FTP ." Sometimes you must "enable" these. Then, one needs client (meaning on your local computer) means of doing SSH and FTP. There are many FTP products that one can pick, and some are free (and quite good.) For SSH, if you are using a Mac, you actually already have an SSH product called "Terminal" so nothing else is really required. On a PC, one very popular SSH client is "Putty." And there are others. Knowing how to SSH and FTP into your server, and use these means of access are a bit technical, nothing too hard, and are skills that are recommended for working with bigger servers, such as a VPS. If you don't know, or learn how to use these, it becomes much more difficult to manage a server. There are folks here, like Usman and Ken, who are really good at helping people with commands. I am not a server-admin, but know enough to be dangerous. GoDaddy will answer questions like "How do I enable SSH?" or "How do I enable FTP?" But GoDaddy is a server company, and they don't support the many open-source products directly, so you can't ask them "How do I install Moodle?" If you are looking for this kind of support, you have to search around, or get a Moodle partner involved. Many of these fast one-click installer programs, like Installatron, are third-party products. They are not GoDaddy software products, they are only provided to try to help people less familiar with servers get something up and going. Even cPanel is third-party product, not GoDaddy. There have been times when I phone GoDaddy for cPanel help and they say "that's not our product, contact cPanel." (Actually, it might be cPanel that gives you the Installatron product, but I am not sure if Installatron is produced by cPanel.) Some folks like Ken, Usman, and Howard I really respect because they can manage their servers without any of these helper utilities... they know Linux. I am amazed with what they can do. Having said all of this, I have learned enough so that I can run my Moodle on a GoDaddy VPS, at a reasonable cost, and the server is rock-solid. I have been using a GoDaddy VPS for around 6-7 years. Someday I plan to make a video of how I do that, but I have been too busy teaching for my school.

ResponsesInList.Title: Is there a way of showing specific courses on the frontpage?

The purpose of this is because one of our platforms is using self-enrolment with approval, and we want to make sure those who approve course applications don't have to sort between users who should be able to see a group of courses and those who shouldn't. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is there a way of showing specific courses on the frontpage?
ResponsesInList.Text: Is this the landing page or the Dashboard ? If you make the Dashboard the User's homepage, problem solvered, it disappears altogether. Only the courses they are enrolled in appear, which saves a lot of angst for a large number of seriously insecure Users. If you're talking about the Front Page , a landing page, then you may want to have two Moodles. One sign on that is directed to either Moodle. You might have to talk to a Moodle Developer to get this working but it should be doable.If you're using an SSO to manage signon, then you can set that up depending on where you aim them. Two Moodles on the same server obviously need different ip addresses, but even an almost incompetent network admin should be able to set that up. You might have one called MoodleArts and the other called MoodleSTEM. Your SSO takes care of all the sign ins and as long as the Moodles have different cookie prefixes, say art_ and stem_, Admins can log into either Moodle at the same time. Good Luck.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle updates and Plugins :(
ResponsesInList.Text: The issue as I read it was having to put 50 plugins back into the codebase for the latest Moodle version you were using. ResponsesInList.Text: My typical plan of attack to ensure I can go backwards fast is to: Stop servers run manual backups of the databases, and of the moodledata folders. I 'stage' a new moodle folder with the latest version All sites have the same plugins, manually copy additional plugins to staged folder Rename existing moodle folder to OLD Create new folders Copy staged version to all folders Copy config from OLD to new folders for each site Bring servers back online one at a time Go to site, complete Moodle update. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle updates and Plugins :(
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Niall, The way we approached this was to rebuild the entire code-base with plugins and do dry runs of the upgrade on another test instance, once we were happy with that then at the point we renamed the folder it already had all plugin updates in it, so there was no need to copy them over whilst the system was down. An alternative to renaming is to point Apache to a different folder, though I am not sure how easy that is in IIS . To create a test instance like that you are either going to need a separate test domain , then rename all entries in config.php and your database from "livemoodle. domain .edu" to "testmoodle.domain.edu" Another option is to set up another server with the same code (which believes it is your live Moodle domain) and add a hosts entry on your PC for that IP address. This avoids faffing with renaming all your domain info but means anyone testing needs to update their hosts file on their PC to point at your test IP which makes it difficult to do larger scale testing with end users. Something else we did was to run multiple Moodle instances from a common codebase, so there is only one codebase to update, not one for each Moodle site. The main constraint around this is around things like themes. If you have hardcoded changes in different versions of a theme with the same name this would be an issue, in that instance you would have to create renamed copies of the theme. However that is less of an issue these days as most themes have admin settings to control colors, override css which resides in the database and caching should all be in the Moodledata directory... there maybe other considerations in current versions of Moodle, it is years since I did this, but if you are interested there is an old thread I posted here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=241901 In short you read in URL being called and use that to determine which moodledata and database to point at, so you can have a single Moodle codebase that switches between different moodledata / databases depending on the site being accessed. I have to say if I were doing this now (we outsourced hosting to a Moodle partner) I would be looking at using GIT to manage / pull down changes to multiple sites rather than running a single copy of the codebase.

ResponsesInList.Text: Sometimes reading other suggestions from other postings may not apply to users environment. The /usr/local/ location is a very strange place to have moodle ... a web based applicaition that typically runs under the user/group 'apache' on a stock CentOS Linux release 7.6.1810 (Core) server . Typically /usr/local is owned by root, nothing related to a web service is ever there, and should be left that way. drwxr-xr-x. 13 root root 4096 Apr 30 04:14 /usr/local Typically the web service on such a server has a 'home' directory defined by /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf fgrep 'DocumentRoot' /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf So maybe some more info about how you are trying to install and under what account is in order?  Is your server hosted some where?   With whom? And if hosted is the lease on a shared system? Those for starters as you say your server is a CentOS 7.2!!!??? which is about 4 Kernel updates behind!!!! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CAN'T INSTALL MOODLE  ON CENTOS-7.2: Data directory (/usr/local/moodledata) cannot be created by the installer.
ResponsesInList.Text: CentOS has a thing called selinux ... security enhanced linux ... and it will stop an installer from creating directories etc. out side of it's rules for httpd ...  the apache/webserver daemon. As root user: sestatus [ENTER] if you see Current mode: enforcing then that's why you are having issues. man setenforce will show how to set it to 'permissive' which will allow install. Is this server to be accessed by the outside globe after you have developed courses?  or is it a tinker thing? If the former, don't install using 'localhost' ... there will be a whole bunch of changes you'll need to make before users can access. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot delete some users
ResponsesInList.Text: so i tracked down the problem to: - there are entries in mdl_grade_grades which have an itemid that does not exist in mdl_grade_items - mdl_grade_items links grade items to the courseid of the course - on user deletion, moodle tries to create an event that includes the courseid of the deleted grade - if there is a grade for a user in mdl_grade_grades which does not have an associated grade_item, the courseid is NULL, thus the DB query fails, and the deletion is cancelled - in our DB there are 47000 grades in mdl_grade_grades which do not have an associated grade_item (!) - those 47000 grades are distributed over more than 4000 users (our user total is 16000). not only old users, but plenty of new ones (!!) - this means that 1/4 of all the users at our site can never be deleted (!!!) since new users are also affected, my best guess is that this is either a Moodle bug or a bug in a plugin we have installed. Please try to verify if your site has this problem as well by following these steps: SQL query: SELECT mdl_grade_grades.id, itemid, userid, courseid FROM mdl_grade_grades LEFT OUTER JOIN mdl_grade_items ON mdl_grade_grades.itemid = mdl_grade_items.id WHERE mdl_grade_items.courseid IS NULL If this query returns data records, then all of the userids in these records will be undeletable Please report back so I can see if this is an isolated problem at our site, or a bug in some installed plugin, or a general Moodle bug!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is this sort of teacher permission "set-up" possible?
ResponsesInList.Text: As a generic rule, almost anything can be done with Permissions and Capabilities. to get these exactly right though, can be a difficult task. The rules I have found to make this sort of thing work though are relatively simple: #1: DO NOT use existing Roles, ALWAYS create a DUPLICATE Role with a new title. e.g. Use a copy of the Teacher Role which might be named Tutor, or Supervisor, NEVER Teacher. #2: NEVER ADD a Capability, ALWAYS DENY #3: NEVER think you have it right. Always expect something will go wrong. #4: Trial and test EVERYTHING BEFORE making it live. 1. Is it possible to allow that teacher permission to add resources and activities BUT WITHOUT being having granting ability to delete / remove what has been created by the course creator in terms of pre-existing resources, activities, labels or topic content (HTML) - In other words can they add resources-activities-extra-LABEL content but not remove anything provided to them ? Yes, Look for the Capability of "Delete-" and if it is something you don't want them to delete, then make it "Deny" Look for those things you want them to add and make sure they are set to Allow. It is always better to look at everything and then assume you have missed something. 2. The same teacher cannot enrol extra users other than those pre-provided when they joined the site *for example by using a self service tool like the wonderful course merchant) is that possible? Yes, remove the Capability that allows them to enrol Users. 3. Need your advice here: Moodle says Cohorts are site-wide or course category-wide groups. The purpose of cohorts is to enable all members of the cohort to be easily enrolled in a course. OK but how is that different from a group or a child-course which only contains teachers and students. because if a teacher and class is placed into a child course - they can easily be enrolled into the 10 universal courses we have available, So whats the advantage (or disadvantage) of one approach or another? Use what you require. If you have no need to use Cohorts, then why even look at it? Moodle is set up to allow people to adapt it to their own needs, which makes it really flexible. That means there is a lot of uses to which you may never put Moodle. If your circumstances change, then you might, but until then... I think that if you are aware that there is a method of doing something differently that may be better than what you are doing, that is enough, as long as what you do works. It it stops working for you then you know you have an alternative.

ResponsesInList.Title: Failed email verification with OAuth 2 authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Hallo, I'm using Moodle 3.4.1+ I successfully set up OAuth 2 service: logging in with a Microsoft-account.  At first I had I had the option 'Require email verification' on before I enabled sending the ability of Moodle sending emails. When I tested the authentication the email was not send and the authentication was not completed. I since then turned 'Require email verification' off. Now When I try to log-in with the same Microsoft-account as during the test I get the message 'This account attends verification by email' or something along these lines because I use Moodle in a different language.  I need to use this account. How can I complete the verification without the email? Or how do I delete the failed login attempt so I can login again? The failed account does not show up in the list of users so I can not enable it manually. Thanks in advance, Joost

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Failed email verification with OAuth 2 authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Experienced same thing with a customoauth2 setup. No way for Admin level to confirm the account manually for an Oauth2 user as with the other methods of authentication IF the account was already present/existing.   Think it's an oversite really but here's where one could look: mdl_auth_oauth2_linked_login table. There is a confirmtoken and a confirmtokenexpires column(s). From what I was able to gather, the confirmtokenexpires (an epoch  time stamp) and the code gave user 30 minutes to check email and confirm the linking.   There isn't a task/cron job that I could find to re-notify the user ... ie, send another EMail and have the user step through the linking confirmation. This was on a test server so much experimentation ... my first guess at fixing was to manipulate that table and simply remove data from confirmtoken and confirmtokenexpires.   Asked the user to then attempt login again. Much to my surprise, the auth field in mdl_users table didn't change from manual to oath2 as *new* accounts did and user reported they could not login then with either method ... the 'normal' dialog box nor the button for the 'customoauth2' provider. Unfortuanately, the entity exploring this decided to go another direction and I couldn't try other things to fix it so what I'm suggesting is nothing more than a pointer. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Failed email verification with OAuth 2 authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks, Ken! your pointer worked.   I took the information from the table you suggested and re-constructed the link. First, query the table:  SELECT * FROM mdl_auth_oauth2_linked_login; Find the errant student listing, and use that information to re-construct the link: Here is what it should look like (replace << >> and all in between): <<YourMoodleHomeLocationURL>> /auth/oauth2/confirm-linkedlogin.php?token= <<Token>> &userid= <<userid>> &username= <<usernameMailboxid>> %40 <<emaildomain>> &issuerid= <<issuerid>> The usernameMailboxid is the part before the @ symbol and the emaildomain is the part after the @ Everything but the YourMoodleHomeLocationURL is contained in the table. I sent the re-constructed link to the student, and voila!  They were able to verify and enter the site. Prost!

Ok, since you appear to be a CLI person ... how about this ... One of the things missing in Moodle Admin UX is the ability to do a minimal site backup - that being an SQL dump of DB and a tar ball of current code.  Always advised before installing a new plugin, updating or upgrading core code, or as a matter of regular server maintenance ... perfect for one person sites or 'medium sized' Moodle sites. (probably not for large sites). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.7+ users keep getting logged-out
ResponsesInList.Text: Do you know which session driver you're using? "File" is the normal default for a single-node web server. Is Use database for session information checked or unchecked? Is this a single-node web server with no load balancing or clustering? I've encountered session issues when the session storage back-end has run out of disk space. Are the users "manual" internal Moodle users or are they being authenticated externally (e.g. LDAP )? Presumably these users are using individual user accounts and it's not Limit concurrent logins affecting a single shared user account?

Uhhh ... ++ This page should be using theme contemporary which cannot be initialised. Falling back to the site theme boost ++ says whatever you did to change the theme, didn't take. So one more item ... in config.php file of the active site, add the following line: '$CFG->theme='boost'; Check your moodlecode/theme directory via anything you have to browse files.   If you should see only boost, classic, and eugru directories.  Any other directories like contemporary ... remove. If successfully removed, do a query of DB like so: ﻿ mysql > select * from mdl_config_plugins where name like '%theme%'; +------+---------------+----------+------------+ | id   | plugin        | name     | value      | +------+---------------+----------+------------+ | 1891 | theme_boost   | themerev | 1568043843 | | 1953 | theme_classic | themerev | 1568043873 | +------+---------------+----------+------------+ 2 rows in set (0.00 sec) Notice there's only the two in that table. Issue could also be that LDAP sending characters that the DB won't except, In your config.php file, what does the line for 'dbcollation' say? What that shows must match DB.   3.7 now should be running not only Innodb but character set utf8mb4 with a collation of utf8mb4_something. run these two scripts to see (and maybe fix): from your moodle/admin/cli directory: php my sql _compressed_rows.php -i You should see: Database engine:       InnoDB innodb_file_per_table: ON innodb_file_format:    Barracuda Run php mysql_collation.php --list at the tail end of output, you should see something like: mdl_workshopform_rubric_config          utf8mb4_general_ci layout                              utf8mb4_general_ci mdl_workshopform_rubric_levels          utf8mb4_general_ci definition                          utf8mb4_general_ci Table collations summary for https://yourserver: utf8mb4_general_ci: 1494 which says all tables (1494 on the site I am looking at) have utf8mb4_general_ci collations. That collation must match what's in conflg.php. If you need to fix, ﻿ php mysql_collation.php shows how to fix.  Read the screen and type command with options to change. Now ... what language character set is your LDAP running?   Dunno how to find that out cause I don't run LDAP. In the set up of LDAP in your moodle: /admin/settings.php?section=authsettingldap It does have a setting for LDAP encoding - which, by default, is set to utf-8. and comment under that says: " Encoding used by the LDAP server, most likely utf-8. If LDAP v2 is
selected, Active Directory uses its configured encoding, such as cp1252
or cp1250. " Your LDAP should be version 3. Have no idea how many users need to be sync'd, but one of them is using a character in the data being pulled into Moodle, that Moodle doesn't like. That's all I can suggest. Emma ... handing this one over to you! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sync Users from MS AD to Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry, guys. Just saw this. Your problem is that you have a username with a character that moodle does not accept. Ken already pointed this out. I often find an errant space or apostrophe causes this. There are two ways to fix this: 1. As Ken already mentioned, there is a setting in admin setting to allow special characters in usernames. Find the setting and enable it. Rerun the sync. 2. Find the username that contains the special character and change it. Also noted, it appears that you do not have cron running. All your regular tasks are showing as never have run. You need to set up cron to run automatically. You can find instructions in the installation documents for your particular operating system.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Anybody use Moodle as a video feedback training forum?
ResponsesInList.Text: Others will probably have something different ... maybe even better ... the following reflects only my personal experience ... Presenting a workshop at a Regional Education Center was asked one time if I would mind if the ESC could video the workshop.  Said I didn't mind but ...  they didn't understand the 'but ....'. They had a portable video system on a cart with camera and the whole works ... but no one maned the camera.   They had two choices ... point the camera at my chair ... or point the camera at the projector screen to see the moodle server screen that was being projected.  At times that was browser showing the moodle site ... at other times it was a terminal window showing command line.   Didn't have any sophisticated system where camera followed the presenter nor any remote control to switch to projected image. As a presenter, I had habits from being a K12 classroom teacher .... never standing at the podium (in secondary school that podium was 'teachers desk') or for very long at the overhead projector to reveal the next overhead or draw a doddle on a 'slide'.   I actually walked around the classroom ... up and rows ... occasionaily stopping near a student who seem to need re-focusing their attention on class.  (this was before any 'clicker') The ESC recorded up til noon and then decided I wouldn't stay still long enough! Questions: video of a teacher teaching might need to get permissions from any student in the room in the event the camera captured their likeness.   Your situation? How long would this recording be? And, when finished, uploaded/posted or whatever, how are the assessors to assess?   If the assesors are to be peers, will those peers have some sort of easy check off or comment box form .... and how will those assessors actually be doing the assessing?   It was amazing what sort of student reaction can be elicited by a teacher 'look' or 'guesture'!!! The best moodle course I've seen (all things considered) was an American Sign Language course ... teacher was not deaf ... but taught F-2-F like she was for most of the F-2-F class... course in Moodle conducted the same way.   Students had to learn to 'read sign' in order to know what their assignments were ... and the assignments were videos of themselves 'signing' the assignment. K12 moodle (being used by many teachers) there were times when server was slow due to all the students in the ASL class uploading their 1 minute or so videos. Not saying it's a bad idea ... just more than tech involved. 'SoS', Ken

But one problem I have is that some of the students/teachers who are taking the course aren't yet teaching so I have been wondering how well "pseudo or pretend" teaching without a classroom or students would work. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Anybody use Moodle as a video feedback training forum?
ResponsesInList.Text: Need more info ... are these students in your Moodle to be K12 educators? " I have been wondering how well "pseudo or pretend" teaching without a classroom or students would work " For one, just standing in front of peers appearing to be clam and not sweating bullets is a gain in itself.  Got any speech ticks?   blah, blah, like ... blah, blah ... like, blah, blah ...  Count the number of 'likes' in the space of 1-2 minutes.   Hmmm ... that's something that becomes annoying ... to anyone!  A habit that must be broken and corrected. Can re-call many/many years ago having a "Methods and Materials" course for Secondary Education.  One week, all members of the class were to give a ' lesson ' with the other members of class to be the 'audience'.  All 'lessons' not to go over 15 minutes in length and was taught without the use of technology ... of any kind.   Those giving the 'lesson' never stepped beyond the 'podium' ... never asked a question of those 'pretending' to be students that required anything more than to parrot or yes/no ... definitely no 'opinion' or anything 'debatable'. To be honest ... one could have learned the same same things if taking a 'public speaking' course. How realistic was it?   Not very!  Just peer pressure ... that's all! Now if you were really 'devious' ... the week that students A, B, C, D, E, and F were to do their 'lessons', you could conduct a session with the other students and give them roles to play .... 'the class clown' ... the 'hecker' ... and so on and so forth. Get the idea? Your: " The idea for the feedback forum is mainly for teachers who are currently teaching and willing to record their classes. " Don't know that you could pull it off or not ... but video clips of real teachers in front of real students ... just clips - 5-10 minutes length.   Students with no classroom/teaching experience to watch video and observe focusing on criteria you establish for each clip.  The real teacher participating in such has to be really confident or very interested in improvement ...  No offense to anyone here in these forums but how many 'tenured professors' have an interest in improving their 'lectures'? How about this ... start the frist week with students teaching a 'lesson' using technology (self recorded videos) of no more than 5 minutes in length about anything for which they have a 'passion' ... that anything doesn't have to be anything academic - how about sharing a 'life hack'?   Have some fun doing it! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Advice on simplest way for non Moodle teachers to enrol themselves and class (Moodle 3.7)
ResponsesInList.Text: You have asked a lot of questions, but maybe I can address your enrollment questions. Consider looking into "self-enrollment." This is what I have been using for my students for quite a while. I am the only teacher in my Moodle, but self-enrollment should work for them. What I do is to create this self-enrollment method, with a password, then I email my students and tell them to create their own profile, then click on the course of interest, and enter their enrollment key. It's about as simple as that. You still have the option to manually enroll students and/or teachers. Yes, the spreadsheet method could work too, if you want to do the work for the student. In my case, I prefer to have students do this, but I am working with college-age students, not elementary-aged students (and teachers.) I don't use meta courses, so can't help with that. But you might want to think about just having multiple copies of the same course for each teacher. Yes, Moodle does support meta courses, but this might be more advanced than what you are ready for.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The load time of a stylesheet file is too long
ResponsesInList.Text: Do you have Theme Designer Mode switched on? Check in Site Administration > Appearance > Theme > Theme Settings. With this setting on, each stylesheet is loaded separately, isn't cached and may be compiled with each page load. You should only use this if you are doing development where you are making frequent changes to stylesheets. Otherwise, it should always be turned off.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle - Intranet
ResponsesInList.Text: What is an intranet?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle - Intranet
ResponsesInList.Text: An intranet is a company's secure private local network that is not meant to be accessed by anyone outside the company.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle - Intranet
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh, sure! A local area network (LAN) works perfectly even if it is not connected to the Internet , well except that it won't have access to machines which are outside the LAN. In any household which has a wired or wireless network the devices see each other even when the Internet connection is broken. Coming back to your question, you can install Moodle in your laptop, when it is connected to the Internet so that it will serve as a Moodle server once connected to the LAN. The MoodleBox is an example of a small but complete Moodle server made for such purposes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle - Intranet
ResponsesInList.Text: Talking of MoodleBox and correctional facilities - please read this https://moodlebox.net/en/news/caen-detention-centre/

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle - Intranet
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes ... can be run in that environment ... I imagine with some networking and Moodle module (tools) restrictions. Following is unsolicited ... but ... Much depends upon administration of this correctional facility and those that would be using it - purpose ... GED?  Training for employment?  College credits? etc.   Who would be instructors/teachers? Server itself would need inside out access to moodle repo (strongly recommend git ) for acquistion of core updates/upgrades (restricted ssh access).  Since admin of a Moodle can't be done 100% in Moodle Admin interface a cPanel like service might be required. And a technical thang ... how many participants at one time accessing? Other considerations am sure ... Experience with similar ... large ISD with what was called a 'Reassignment Campus' consisting of students from 3 High Schools and 4 Junior HS's. LDAP . 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting an email if the cron hasn't run for 24 hours
ResponsesInList.Text: Glenn, this feature of sending email when cron hasn't run, is not even seen in Linux systems. if have you setup your cron using scheduled tasks, then you will be able to view the log of successful cron run.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting an email if the cron hasn't run for 24 hours
ResponsesInList.Text: Usman, where can you see the report/log of successful cron runs?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting an email if the cron hasn't run for 24 hours
ResponsesInList.Text: This would be a nice feature. Unfortunately, the process that would do that checking and send the email is..... cron itself. This is a "who will guard the guards" problem. Something has to trigger the check. Your choices in Moodle are a page load or cron. Now, the Notifications page message you see is simply checking the last run times for all the various scheduled tasks. If no scheduled task has run in the last 24 hours, it assumes cron is not running and posts that warning. The logic for this is: "We make the assumption that at least one schedule [sic[ task should run once per day." says a comment in /admin/index.ph). So cron per se is not really being tracked but this was good enough. That's the situation for 3.5 anyway. This has changed somewhat in 3.7 where it is now checking the frequency of cron runs by each task instead. It defaults to 200 seconds. You can (only) tweak this interval in the config.php file. // Moodle 3.7+ checks that cron is running frequently. If the time between cron runs // is greater than this value (in seconds), you get a warning on the admin page. (This // setting only controls whether or not the warning appears, it has no other effect.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting an email if the cron hasn't run for 24 hours
ResponsesInList.Text: Related to this is: Why wouldn't cron run? Its not a rhetorical question. I am quite interested in people's experiences. In my experience cron will usually start but not always complete, sometimes because a fatal error occurs. Or sometimes because a task takes an inordinate amount of time. Also if an update to a plugin has been installed physically but the upgrade script has not run, cron will be suspended until that happens.

ResponsesInList.Text: It's not automatic but Moodle can block and allow specific IP addresses/ranges . When you say not reachable what message do you see? From office, i performed a traceroute, the query passed throught the network and is block somewhere (node 116.251.117.165  ). ps : red mark is our office. but in the same hour, from home (different ip address and different isp), the traceroute works fine and reach our website moodle (green mark) so, what is the problem ? from us ? from somewhere in the world of routeurs ? from country ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: our moodle platform is not reachable from our place
ResponsesInList.Text: Can you confirm that the Moodle site's domain name resolves to the same IP address at the office and at home? If you telnet to the IP address on port 443 (or port 80 if it's not an HTTPS site) from the office does this fail to connect? What message do you get? Traceroute is an inexact test as some hops may deliberately not respond. But I can't see that the office connection converges on the route taken by the home connection which I'd expect. There are two potential issues with routing I can think of: 1) the routing tables used on the outbound route and 2) the routing tables used on the return route. If it is a routing issue then first check with the local network support that there are no specific routing rules for the Moodle site's IP address. If you manage or have root access to the Moodle web server check that the routing table on this has no specific rule which may cause this. If possible run a traceroute from the server back to the public IP addresses of your home and office and compare these. The web server (e.g. Apache , Nginx) could have rules blocking specific IP addresses. Any routing issue that was external to both your office and the Moodle web server would have to be escalated to the ISP for your office's Internet connection or that hosting the web site. I'm assuming there's no web proxy in use at your office, if there is you'll need to be doing your nslookup, telnet and routing tests to/from this.

ResponsesInList.Text: You would be very unlucky for such a small update to break your plugins.

ResponsesInList.Text: Generally speaking, upgrading to the latest stable release is a good idea, as that gives you the latest fixes for bugs and security issues. I would, of course, suggest that you don't update your production system without running the upgrade in a test environment first, and ensuring that everything works as expected.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Australian VET sector
ResponsesInList.Text: The statement, "Remember: Moodle isn't free. You either pay a qualified in-house team, or you outsource extensively." is likely to confuse those who land here straight from web searches. Needs some qualification: - the Moodle software is "free" in the sense of "gratis". Visit https://download.moodle.org/ - the Moodle software is "free" in the sense of the four freedoms. See the https://docs.moodle.org/dev/License - the hardware is not free. You need some sort of a machine to run it. With some exceptions like the https://moodlecloud.com . - most expensive, the time, your time and the time any in-house or outsource personnel spend running it. (That is what the previous poster was talking about.) Well, except on this and other Moodle communities.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Australian VET sector
ResponsesInList.Text: Good point, I should have qualified that with the idea that no LMS is "free" in the long run. At some point, in some way, you'll be paying. If you already own the hardware, you need to pay for support, be it in-house or outsourced. If you don't own the hardware, you need to either buy it, or run it from cloud and then pay for support. If you don't pay for qualified support and run it with unqualified staff, it will either be ugly, too simple, or totally broken. You could just pay a provider to supply the instance and the support, but again, you're still paying. Either way, it's not free. Personally, I think Moodle is best, but it must be supported by a qualified team, who can code modifications and plugins as needed. But back to Moodle in the Australian VET sector, it doesn't provide everything it could/should out of the box. It simply was not built for our use case. The competency frameworks could provide that, but the amount of effort needed to import the Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) is staggering. You could build an import function with the stuff on training.gov.au (the devs are very happy to provide API style access), but you need to be able to code to create it. It also doesn't handle scales combined with rubrics, there's a bug that's currently open about how the scales don't report the correct grade when used with rubrics. There's no "exemption" function for RPL, the closest that exists is "Exclude" which is not visible to the student. This means that the student will see a nice blank spot on their grades for the item. You could hide them, but this has to be done manually (so does "exclude). Every way I look at it, Moodle simply is not capable of handling the needs of the VET sector. Not as a complete Learning Management System at any rate. I suspect the VET organisations using it are using it as a basic learning platform, and performing validations and such offline, or in another product.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  Error: Database connection failed
ResponsesInList.Text:
The error log shows: 
```text
2019-09-03T01:00:52.746889Z 0 [Note] InnoDB: Initializing buffer pool, total size = 128M, instances = 1, chunk size = 128M


2019-09-03T01:00:52.746952Z 0 [ERROR] InnoDB: mmap(137428992 bytes) failed; errno 12


2019-09-03T01:00:52.746964Z 0 [ERROR] InnoDB: Cannot allocate memory for the buffer pool
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  Error: Database connection failed
ResponsesInList.Text: Out of memory sounds really likely. There were 50 students in a class doing a short quiz and replying to a forum. To make it worse, as they haven't used Moodle before I was holding them back so the clicks were likely to be close together. The set up is low budget ( 1vCPU, 1 GIG) but I performed today flawlessly and quickly with 4 classes of up to 51 students. I intended to up the memory this morning but I had access problems so the setup was identical. CPU never cracked 50%. I will add a swap area on the disk. I did see the same error on students machines once or twice - I would expect the database to handle overloading by slowing down but everything was responsive. I will update the memory tonight to 2 GB and see if I can putty in tomorrow when the students are giving it heaps . Attaching photos of free and top ( but very quiet at present) Not a lot going on tonight. Upped the memory following a power down

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  Error: Database connection failed
ResponsesInList.Text: That sounds like progress. A 1 GB/1 processor/no core swap does sound under-resourced for 50 concurrent students. Hopefully with the extra memory and maybe swap things will improve. In general once MySQL has been allocated memory it will continue fairly normally even when the system is running out of memory until the kernel gets involved which will then look for something with lots of RAM to kill and MySQL will be a candidate. If the server system logs go back to when this originally occurred see if there are any messages like "kernel: Out of memory". If there are it should report which process was killed as a result. Also, in busy sites it's important to make sure PHP OPcache is enabled and configured correctly (e.g. check there is no warning in the Environment report and confirm the settings in PHP Info ) as this can significantly improve site performance and reduce load on the server.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing a quiz in a distance-learning course
ResponsesInList.Text: I used to do this with groups and duplicate quizzes with group restrictions. Make a group containing all current students, your quiz and restrict it's visibility to the group. Make sure you click the eye so it is visible to only the group members. When you need to alter the quiz, just duplicate the original one and make changes to it as needed. Create a new group with just the new student and restrict visibility of the new quiz to the new group. Rollover the same way each time you have new students. The teachers view will get cluttered, but students will only see the one quiz in which they are a member of the correct group.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Open training
ResponsesInList.Text: We looked at this for open access resources on one of our Moodle instances. The straightforward answer is that Moodle isn't designed to work like this, and having multiple users share a log-in is a bad idea. Moodle stores entered data against a user ID, which would mean any data created by anyone accessing your course could be overwritten or edited by anyone else. The "Guest" user, which is used to allow access without log-in, is explicitly prevented from being able to enter data for this reason. As an alternative, you could allow open registrations on your site to let people create their own account, then use an enrolment key to restrict access to course containing your materials.

ResponsesInList.Text: It could be that html for the video on the page is all messed up. That can happen in a number of ways. The most common of which is copying and pasting from one html editor into another. This copies the draft file url, and that draft file will not be present in the second html editor. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is there a way to send an automated series of emails to students when they complete the course?
ResponsesInList.Text: In a word, no. The closest thing is the event monitoring rules (See https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Event_monitoring#How_to_create_or_manage_a_rule ), which let you send an email upon course completion (or many other events) - but only to yourself. You could ask a developer to create a local plugin which implements an autoresponder. (Just don't ask them to duplicate Mailchimp wholesale though, as that would be prohibitively expensive, and send them the wrong signal that you're maybe not serious about this.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is there a way to send an automated series of emails to students when they complete the course?
ResponsesInList.Text: There are a couple of plugins for Moodle that can trigger a web hook when a Moodle event occurs. You can use this to ping a service like Zapier or IFTTT which will then relay your information to MailChimp (or Infusionsoft or whatever) to set up the autoresponder sequence. I know thats a head spin at first. But the result is that you can set up auto responders based on events in Moodle without any coding at all. You can see some discussions about those plugins here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=378947

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is there a way to send an automated series of emails to students when they complete the course?
ResponsesInList.Text: each instance of the Reengagment activity can be configured to send the same e-mail text multiple times on a schedule, however if you want different text to appear in each email (eg a different tip) you would need to set up multiple reengagment activity instances in your site. - one for each "tip" It might be possible to do this with reengagement but I'm not sure it would be the most efficient - I'm not aware of anything else built into moodle to facilitate this (although Justin's suggestion of zapier/ifttt could be an easier way to do it.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Assign role on category to a cohort
ResponsesInList.Text: On our site, each course category represents a department. In each category I have a "Staff" Cohort. I would like to enable everyone in the Staff Cohort to view all the courses in that category (as an observer, not a lecturer or student), without those courses all appearing in their course list. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign role on category to a cohort
ResponsesInList.Text: To get around this sort of issue, I have always created a specific Staff Role, which gives them specific rights in specific places, but not sure this will help you achieve exactly what you want. Individuals can be assigned Roles at the Category Level, but Cohorts are not. This is simply because if you have a large Cohort accessing editing capabilities at the Category level you have opened a rather large security hole in your Moodle, that's the logic behind the restriction, but not your intent. You could try assigning a role at the Category level that allows Staff to look at the courses. Create a new Role, base it on the Guest Role, if you like, and allow that Role to be assigned at the Category level. All you need do then is to test it, with a dummy user and work out what permissions and capabilities you really want the Role to have. Or you could use the Non-editing Teacher Role as the template and restrict Capabilities until you are happy it can only do what you want to to do. That's the best answer I got, unless someone has a way of doing what you want.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: self registration with out  any approval from admin
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Sivaprasad, Based on the way you have described your situation, I recommend that you try to think about Account creation (Authentication) and Enrollment separately, for now. As with any experience that you would create on the internet,
you should try to understand every single step that your users will go through while they register (Authenticate). I know it can feel confusing or even tedious, but it will help you a lot. Please make sure you read the documentation, and tell us where your experience is different from the documented expectations (we all started there!). Authentication/Account creation You mentioned that you do not want your administrator to be responsible for confirming accounts. That is exactly how the "email-based self-registration" plugin is intended to be used. Instead, users can confirm their own accounts by clicking on a link
that is sent to the email address that they provided during registration. This is considered a security measure, and it is a fairly common way for other web applications to handle self-registration. You probably had to do the same thing when you signed
up for an account here at Moodle.org! Are you sure that you do not want your users to do this? Try creating a test account on your system, and observe all the steps carefully. Users should be fairly comfortable with this workflow, if they've
ever signed up for an account on other popular websites. Perhaps your users do not have email addresses. However, you mention PayPal too, for which I believe that they need an email address. One possible problem could
be that the confirmation emails are going into people's Spam/Junk folders. That is inconvenient, but I would consider it a success, for now. You could try to solve the Spam problem later (read some links at the bottom of that documentation page), but
it can get very technical. Again, I think that general users are familiar with this scenario (things going to Spam), so you should just make sure that you remind them to check their Spam folder, in the meantime. As Mary mentions, other Authentications
options exist, but you should make sure you understand the tradeoffs. Enrollment There is a PayPal enrollment plugin that you could use, and there is a substantial documentation page for testing it and setting it up. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SQL Report Query
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hey Jonny , I think you want a query by which you can fetch all the users (institute) enrolled in particular course. You can do it by many ways. 1) use get_enrolled_users(parameter) function. It will give you the list of enrolled users in particular course. 2) use enrol_get_course_users(parameter) 3)Direct hit this query. It will give you all the information of enrooled users in particular course. 
```text
 SELECT ue.id AS ueid, ue.userid as user, ue.status AS uestatus, e.courseid as course,ue.enrolid AS ueenrolid, ue.timestart AS uetimestart,
             ue.timeend AS uetimeend, ue.modifierid AS uemodifierid, ue.timecreated AS uetimecreated,
             ue.timemodified AS uetimemodified,
             u.username FROM mdl_user_enrolments ue
              JOIN mdl_enrol e ON e.id = ue.enrolid
              JOIN mdl_user u ON ue.userid = u.id where e.courseid = $courseid
```
 Thanks, Mayank Tyagi

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Where's the Edit Group setting "Group messaging" in the Moodle database?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Albert! That information is not stored in groups table. It is stored by the core_message API and the table you are looking for is called mdl_message_conversations. The "Group messaging" setting is stored in the field called "enabled" inside that table. mdl_message_conversations also stores useful data like group name and group ID. If you need to see the members of the group you're editing, you can go to mdl_message_conversation_members and you will find them. Here is the code doing the magic: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/group/lib.php#L442 Regards.

ResponsesInList.Title: Gradebook not updated after quiz is completed
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I work for a University and we have 2 Moodle instances (for different specialties) running. I'm not sure this post should go here or in Quizz section or Gradebook section... Feel free to move it if necessary. We use Moodle 3.5.7 with php 7.0.33 and mariadb 10.2, and all latest version of plugins. We have a weird but very serious problem (bug ?) concerning the gradebook. W e have several courses, with Quizzes, some of them having completion conditions. The problem : Up to last week a student finishing a quiz had his grade reported in the gradebook. But, this week, back from holidays, i have complaints that users can't continue their courses because they can't access the next step : they should have a mark (any mark is ok for some course), but the mark does not appear in the gradebook, hence blocking the user, although he finished and sent his quiz and i can check that he actually had a mark (if i log as this student). There is no gradebook update after the user has his score. What i did : Obviously i didn't do (nor anyone) betwen the time it worked and it didn't, neither on the server , nor in the administration. I tried to take the test with another user : same result I tried to create a new course with a quizz : same result i duplicated the quiz : same result I duplicated the course : same result i exported the course on the other Moodle platform (same backend) : the gradebook is updated correctly. we upgraded the Moodle version and plugins : no better we checked that the cronjobs are excecuted and even with manually launching the cron (ex : \core\task\grade_cron_task) it isn't better. We checked the database for corruption : none So the problem concerns the whole platform (not some courses) concerns any quiz (with or without completion condition) Maybe a linked problem : we even try to delete all the grades for users attempts for the quizzes in a course (reset all completion attempts and all quiz grades), but strangely those grades are still there ! What can you suggest we check to resolve the problem ? Any administration parameters to check ? Any server action to perform ? Thank you in advance PS : We can't move all courses on a  new Moodle instance yet, it's very time consuming and we don't have any at the moment.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook not updated after quiz is completed
ResponsesInList.Text: A couple of thoughts on this: You might check the quiz settings in the gradebook and make sure the activity hasn't been accidentally locked.  Go to the grades area, go to gradebook setup, click the edit icon for the quiz.  There is an area that says locked.  If it is checked, uncheck it.  If you click Show more, check to make sure there isn't a lock after date as well. If that is the problem, you may have to regrade the attempts but it should resolve the issue. You might also check to make sure the entire grade book doesn't have a lock as well. Second--when you say the grade book doesn't show additional marks, do you mean mark=grade or mark=check (completion)? The grade book doesn't do check marks, only grades. Course/activity completion does checks and if cron isn't set properly, sometimes it will stop checking completed activities .  It is my understanding that there are actually a few different places to look at cron (I don't do this, but I've experienced issues with completion for activities going fine but course completion not and having to poke at cron). When you reset--did you delete the quiz attempts or just reset the quiz completion settings.  Those will repopulate and I think they repopulate with the original date information, so if the lock is on, it would still block this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade from 3.2 to 3.5.7 Recycle Bin does not restore resource
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to increase the https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Debugging level and get more extensive messages. Just a guess: Is it possible that the ownership or permissions of $moodledata/temp/backup has been changed? The web server must be able to create/delete directories under the above directory. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade from 3.2 to 3.5.7 Recycle Bin does not restore resource
ResponsesInList.Text: At first glance, web server has rwx to $moodledata/temp/backup web server 1, web server 2 and cron server all have attached moodledata directory shared. I do not believe we have configured a temp directory for each server, so shared. I was able to restore a course, but the recyclebin file restore was not successful.  I was and still am hoping it is a simple issue. When you restore from the recycle bin, is it a process which is run immediately from the webserver you are using (load balanced) or does it kick off a cron process to restore.  The reason I ask is to help determine which error log to look at.  web server or cron server.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade from 3.2 to 3.5.7 Recycle Bin does not restore resource
ResponsesInList.Text: Could be load balance confusion ... cron should run from only one of the servers. The recycle files are found in your moodledata/filedir ... which means to find them one needs to do a DB query for files tagged as recycled ... .mbz's ... they are small backups. Find the content hash values for those, then see if they exist .. cd /path/to/moodledata/filedir/ find ./ -name [contenthash] Once you get the path to the file do a quick check on mimetype of that file: file -b /path/shown/infindcommand Restoring a recycled file uses a restore from backup routine ... so check moodledata/temp/backup/ for log files larger than 0 byte and any folders/files contained therein. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade from 3.2 to 3.5.7 Recycle Bin does not restore resource
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Eric, I think you're probably running into this bug: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-66221 The recycle bin has had a bunch of issues related to the automatic backup settings but that one is still not quite fixed. In the meantime you should set backup_auto_activities to "enable" and it might fix it for you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade from 3.2 to 3.5.7 Recycle Bin does not restore resource

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade from 3.2 to 3.5.7 Recycle Bin does not restore resource
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry .... unfortunate choice of words ... 'tagged' ... ﻿ Something deleted will stay 'tagged'/labeled/marked/entry in column of mdl_files table as in recyclebin for 7 days. select * from `mdl_files` where `component` like "%recycle%" each found will be named backup.mbz but the contenthash is different. Eventually, those will be moved to 'trashdir' and eventually removed/erased from moodledata/trashdir/ 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: maintenance mode
ResponsesInList.Text: hi I want to enable teachers only to access moodle while the site in maintenance mode I enabled the capability for the editing teacher role https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Capabilities/moodle/site:maintenanceaccess but it didn't work I am realizing now that teacher has this role in the course and not in the front page but how I can use the above capability then?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: maintenance mode
ResponsesInList.Text: Why would you want to do that? The maintenance mode is purely there to advise users the site is currently unavailable. Why would teachers / content creators only be allowed access when it is 'unavailable' to students? The teacher roles are normally assigned in course context , whereas the maintenance mode bit should be assigned at site or system level. The only way to get that done, would be to create a system level additional role, to be assigned to individual users or a cohort of users, containing this and other permissions. That way you'd be able to differentiate between regular authenticated users and those who are teachers. I would, however, recommend finding another solution to the underlying problem...

This works well, but there is 1 problem: in Course Completion I have to set that #1 to #4 must be completed before completing the 'course'. There is no suitable alternative here. How do I set Course Completion so that students have to complete only 3 out of 4 activities ? Or do I have to manage the final test(s) in another way? Thanks for your advice!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook quiz totals
ResponsesInList.Text: This may be challenging as you have an in-progress course/quiz and I don't know if this will work for you. My normal practice is to setup my Gradebook before testing the course/ quiz/navigation activities as a student. Without this adjustment to the Gradebook, students will see the status of their first graded activity and assume that they have completed the entire course. 1. At the Course Administration pane, select Gradebook setup 2. Add a category 3. Adjust the weights Grade Items/100. (I use points that always = 100 vs. a rubric) 4. Hide the Grade Items 5. Hide the Grade Category. 6. Select Grades. Only students that have completed all activities will have a summed grade. Only the summed grade is displayed on a Student’s Grade report.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updates or Upgrades on moodle 3.4.2
ResponsesInList.Text:
As long as you follow the Upgrade process , your site will be updated in-place with all content retained. As for the version, it depends on your support and feature requirements. If you don't want to do a major version upgrade very often and still gets security updates, but are OK not having all the latest features, then using the latest LTS release (currently 3.5.x) is best.
If you want all the latest features, bugfixes, security fixes, and you don't mind having to do a major upgrade at least once every 12 months, the latest stable release (currently 3.7.x) is best. In our case, we do a major upgrade every 6 months, lagging roughly 6 months behind the core release of that major version. This keeps us up-to-date, and gives us plenty of time to test our plugins against the new version before its released. The page I linked above includes details of which versions are supported, and for how long.

ResponsesInList.Text: Welcome!  I'll probably not make what I did a habit! :| You asked via PM 'what was wrong' ... will take this opportunity to share my 2 cent thoughts on shared hosting and the 'traditional' description of upgrading a site. In typical shared hosting document root for web service is 'public_html' ... that's defined by web service config and as a shared user you cannot change that. Traditional directions for upgrading say to 'move moodle code out of the way' ... well, catch 22 right off the bat ... moodle code is in public_html ... not a moodle directory. In your situation you did have 2 moodle code directories inside the 3.4 code of you site ... both were higher versions of Moodle. Your site uses cPanel and SoftTac for Moodle installs ... did you originally use SoftTac to install the moodle?   That would put moodle code in public_html ... not in a 'moodle' directory. What I think I would do if having to use cPanel/etc. ... I'd use a 'moodle' directory and code in there ... just like 'tradtional' install/uprades would expect moodle to be located.  Then one could move 'moodle' out of the way. You say you want the moodle to be what folks see when hitting site ... fine ... use an autoforwarding index.html file with 0 seconds wait time (very old tech but still works) ... that forwards to /moodle/ Advantage ... you, the server admin, could install a tinker site in a directory called 'tinker'.  You are the only one that knows it's there ... you make no links from other pages that a search engine could find and follow. So now, when you want to tinker with something .... https://yoursite/tinker/ For directions on autoforwarding page: https://www.w3docs.com/snippets/html/how-to-redirect-a-web-page-in-html.html Now that you have your site like it is, I'd not recommend changing until you read up on search and replace tool in Moodle ... Moodle records every internal link and right now your DB has https://yoursite/ as where moodle is located. The other thing I'd recommend to you, is do read Moodle docs.  If you have a question ask!!!   Found evidence in your site that you had exported mdl_user table and then imported that table into db for newer version of Moodle by a different prefix ... mdlXXX_user ... thinking one could transfer all users from old site to new higher version site.   Same for the mdl_config table.   Had to imagine what this meant ... ' restore DB and mdl_user  ,  and restore mdl_confing ' in your first post.  Sure enough ... you tried a shortcut but ...  In both cases, nope ... nada ... will never happen.   3.4 -> 3.7 there could have been a major change (and was) to DB character set/collations DB structure ... etc. You won't see anything like the paragraph above,  @ https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Upgrading If you use Moodle docs ... and something goes wrong ... that's one thing ... at least those trying to help you are 'on the same page', so to speak ... but doing what you did and then not really describing that ... exactly ... sent folks helping off into a very deep and dark rabbit hole. I hate going down rabbit holes! :\ 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Editing Mode turns off after every alteration to course
ResponsesInList.Text: Editing Mode turns off after every alteration to course for some users - solved (in this instance for now) Moodle 3.5.3+ (Build: 20181116), PHP 7.2 (7.2.10.0.0.18.04.1), mysql (5.7.24-0ubuntu0.18.04.1) I am posting this to find out how wide-spread the above problem is. The last reference I was able to find in Tracker was regarding Moodle versions 1.8-1.9 in 2008. ( https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-11536 ) One responder to the post wrote "that the "editing" attribute of the collection $USER lost his value after each change on the course." No solution was offered and the thread was closed in 2013 after no more responses and the support for the versions ended. Our problem also affected only a handful of users regardless of the computer they used, operating system or browser. While editing their courses every alteration they saved turned off editing mode, making it tedious for them to maintain their courses. We eventually decided that it could only be tied to their actual user profile. In all cases we altered the Student ID in the optional section, updated and then changed it back. This seemed to reset the profile and the problem disappeared. At this point, we are assuming that the database entries for a few users have been corrupted and that updating the profile has overwritten this. I do not think it was linked to the actual student ID. There is also a possibility that this might also be linked to a problem we had with a course where the course completion data was not displayed returning the error message "Exception - call to a member function get_formatted_name() on null" After backing the course up, including the user data, and restoring it into itself the course completion data displayed correctly. Our dev server is running an identical environment to our live server and has not displayed any of these symptoms, even with the same user profiles. It would be interesting to find out if others have had or are having these issues and what solutions were put in place to solve them. We are still trying to track down what could possibly be the root cause. Regards, Malcolm Hay

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Find empty glossaries
ResponsesInList.Text:
Thanks again for your input. I think after some trial and error I now have what I want for Moodle 3.7.x: 
```text
SELECT mdl_glossary.name, mdl_course.shortname, COUNT(*)
FROM mdl_glossary, mdl_glossary_entries, mdl_course
WHERE mdl_glossary.id = mdl_glossary_entries.glossaryid AND mdl_glossary.course=mdl_course.id
GROUP BY mdl_glossary.id
ORDER BY 3
```
 The resulting list looks like this: And the glossaries with a count of 1 are indeed glossaries without an entry.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Find empty glossaries
ResponsesInList.Text:
The solution presented above only counts the number of entries in each glossary which is also useful but not what I wanted because it doesn't work with empty glossaries. So here is the query which actually finds empty glossaries: 
```text
select md_glossary.name, md_course.fullname
from md_glossary, md_course
where md_glossary.id not in (select md_glossary_entries.glossaryid from md_glossary_entries) AND md_course.id=md_glossary.course
ORDER BY md_course.fullname, md_glossary.name ASC
```
 The result is sorted table with the name of the glossary and the course name.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student's must read instruction page before viewing course?
ResponsesInList.Text: One way to accomplish this (depends how many courses are in your system and how many topics are in your course) is have a Page or URL Resource at the top of each course that links to this document of instructions. Then beneath it, a Choice Activity with only one choice in it - an agreement Statement. Set the Activity Completion to "Student must make a choice." You can then restrict every section in the course to be hidden until the Choice Activity is marked complete. This way, students only see the one activity when they enter the course until the Agreement is completed.

Support a Moodle 2.7.x right now where the entity is using webservices almost exclusively to admin the moodle in an automatted fashion.  One  un-intended consequence of this automation ... the ballooning of mdl_log_store_standard ... the 'who done it' table.   Every day the DB sql dump of that site increases about 800M - there are sooooo many webservices calls which are recorded that the traditional default reports that seek who did what when is rendered useless.   No way to exclude WS from a certain IP address in that report/tool.  And there is no admin interface to configure what info is collected - nor what to exclude if from a certain IP address, etc. Importing/exporting into/from etc. is handled by moodle in one of two ways generally ... csv or xml - webservices uses json?.  **IF** you could export from your .net app to something importable via those 'go-betweens', me thinks that's the approach.  You'd have to build that import script/plugin (a local plugin rather than core modification?) 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO Login script
ResponsesInList.Text: Right, I understand better now, thank you. When you log a user in to Moodle normally, this creates a session cookie in their browser, which is used to tell Moodle who they are logged in as whenever the browser makes another request (visiting a page, loading an image, doing an AJAX call, etc). This cookie persists until it expires, the user logs out, or the user closes their browser, depending on your settings. When you authenticate with Moodle via a web service, you create a token which can be sent with future web service requests to identify the user making the request, via the `wstoken` parameter. When Moodle recieves this token, it creates a new session for that user, which lasts for the duration of that request only. If you make another web service request, you need to send the token again. This token is valid until it expires, or is revoked. Does that explain what's happening a bit better?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO Login script

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO Login script
ResponsesInList.Text: If you've got the username and password to log the user in to Moodle, generating them a web service token isn't necessary unless you want to use it make web service calls as that user. If you want to be fully logged in to a Moodle session, you need to make some request in the user's browser that sends the username and password to Moodle and follows the login process. I'm not enough of an expert in SSO to be comfortable offering specific advice, since there's likely a tradeoff between security and convenience if you're doing this yourself, unless you're planning to implement a full standards-based solution. Some options might be to create an alternative login script in Moodle which you can send the username and password to, or to implement an auth plugin which accepts some token genereated when users log in to your student portal.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, in the quiz you've to go to "Restrict access " add a restriction and choose " Activity completion " and select your video activity. And in the video activity (url, file,...) in the activity completion check "Student must view this activity to complete it" and select "Show activity as complete when conditions are met" Maybe you've to do step 2 before step 1... But basically the keyword is https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Activity_completion_settings Hope it's help. Dominique.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add restriction to Quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: Restricting the access is the simple bit. However, videos are usually added to Moodle as a label or on a page. The restriction only allows you to “require view” - ie. I could start to watch and not finish, so pretty much useless as a restriction criteria. There are a couple of plugins which might be of interest which facilitate the tracking of a user’s viewing time - https://github.com/blackbean/moodle-mod_vimeo https://moodle.org/plugins/mod_videotime

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add restriction to Quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: You could also put it in a lesson , which I believe has the option to require a user to view the lesson for a specific time period before it can be marked complete. Still not an assurance that the video is watched, but it does work a little better than a page. Other video integrations, like VidGrid can track actual video completion and that may be another option.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to create a User based group?
ResponsesInList.Text: If that was the question you had this whole time (How to have the same groups/groupings in all courses without having to manually add it to every course), then looks like this plug in is going to work well for you. For those that want to do the same but cannot install this plug in you found, other ways to accomplish this task (though not as easily!) 1. Crest the groups or groupings on a csv and then upload that csv into each course using the "import groups" option 2. Create a csv that has 5 columns - 1. Short name 2. Full name 3. Username 4. Course1 5. Group1 ,(add course1 group2 / course1 group3 for creating additional groups in the course) then Enroll the same 'test student' into every course by having all courses listed on the csv - add the same group to the csv as well - it will create the group (and add the user to it) in every class that does not yet have the group 3. Create a new course. Call it "group template". Delete everything , even gradebook categories and blocks. Create all your groups in this course. Then you can do a full "import" of this course into any other to bring over the groups.
