Then, searching for information about MariaDB compatibility with Moodle, I came across this thread: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=387539 and thought that Howard's reply conveyed enough uncertainty that I should consider the possibility that MariaDB was the problem. A simple service status enquiry suggested a problem: [root@localhost /]# systemctl status mariadb ● mariadb.service - MariaDB 10.4.6 database server Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/mariadb.service; enabled; vendor preset: disabled) Drop-In: /etc/systemd/system/mariadb.service.d └─migrated-from-my.cnf-settings.conf Active: active (running) since Wed 2019-07-31 18:53:32 JST; 21h ago Docs: man:my sql d(8) https://mariadb.com/kb/en/library/systemd/ Process: 2147 ExecStartPost=/bin/sh -c systemctl unset-environment _WSREP_START_POSITION (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS) Process: 1209 ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c [ ! -e /usr/bin/galera_recovery ] && VAR= || VAR=`/usr/bin/galera_recovery`; [ $? -eq 0 ] && systemctl set-environment _WSREP_START_POSITION=$VAR || exit 1 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS) Process: 1195 ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c systemctl unset-environment _WSREP_START_POSITION (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS) Main PID: 1256 (mysqld) Status: "Taking your SQL requests now..." ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HTTP to HTTPS
ResponsesInList.Text: Stop apache - free up memory for large sql file editing. nano toedit.sql It will be slow to load Once loaded, '[ctrl][w]' (search) https://yoursite/ [ENTER] Takes you to first reference ... right arrow over to see the ending '/' [ctrl][w] to find next. Once you are sure of what you are finding do the replace part. '[ctrl][w]' then '[ctrl][r]' You will be prompted for what to search for again. Next prompted for what to replace with. Choosing 'all' may appear to hang.  It will be slow.  Let it run. Save after you see a menu again. ** might take hours ** Also see: See: https://docs.moodle.org/23/en/Moodle_migration#Migrating_a_complete_Moodle_site_-_method_1 example of sed command - without protocol (http:// -> https:// in front) or via sed - with protocol in front and trailing slash at end. sed -e 's/http:\/\/yoursite\//https:\/\/youresite\//g' toedit.sql > converted.sql sed will also be slow. Open another ssh session to server and as root user: top [ENTER] you will see nano peg the cpu to 100% at times ... always in 90's. Then create a new DB for Moodle ... import the converted.sql file ... change config.php file. Restart apache.   Try it out via browser. 'SoS', Ken

Since the quizzes haven't completed the course itself never completes and the badges are never awarded. The quizzes are set to complete when they have been viewed, AND the student has received a passing grade on the quiz. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quizzes not marked as completed??
ResponsesInList.Text: The cron itself might be running, at small intervals, but are the right cron jobs being run? Check it carefully. The other issue is to do with quizzes, and I am assuming that the quiz modules have been set up correctly, the quizes themselves may not necessarily be set to mark themselves as being complete, make sure the settings are right. The other thing may be that the badges setting have not been properly set up. Are the right badges set t the right courses? I don't suggest any of these things have happened, but these are the things I think are most likely to be out of sequence, or order or whatever, so these are the things I would check first. If you are confident that everything is right, go over it again, just make sure, you might be surprised.

ResponsesInList.Title: Un-suspend users on Course level? (Moodle 3.5.2+)
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Moodlers, For unknown reason some students appears with Suspended status in some courses. On site level their account is NOT suspended, only on course level. I do not know how to un-suspend them on the course level, not even even where to look for such  possibility. Have you dealt with anything like this? Any clues would much appreciated! Cheers! Chrysanthi

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Un-suspend users on Course level? (Moodle 3.5.2+)
ResponsesInList.Text: There could be a few reasons for this. - First check the enrolment methods for your course page. Are any of them disabled? - Failing that, it's possible that your students were enrolled manually on to your page but with an expiry date - See https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Manual_enrolment#Editing_individual_enrolment_start_and_end_dates - It could be that someone suspended a few students' enrolments in that course. To switch it back, select the students > click on the 'With Selected Users ...' dropdown> click on 'Edit selected users enrollments' > click on the 'Alter Status' dropdown, swtich it to 'Active' and save your changes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Απάντηση: Re: Un-suspend users on Course level? (Moodle 3.5.2+)
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear C Behan, 1. Nope, the enrolment methods are meta link and manual and they are both enabled. 2. There was no expiry date enabled 3. I am not able to edit selected users enrolment because: these are meta courses, so the gear (settings) icon is not visible next to the enrolment. When I go to the relevant child course, I do not even see the suspended users enroled in there. How is this possible? All the best, Chrysanthi

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Απάντηση: Re: Un-suspend users on Course level? (Moodle 3.5.2+)
ResponsesInList.Text: Chrysanthi, "When I go to the relevant child course, I do not even see the suspended users enroled in there. How is this possible?" This is possible if you have set the "External unenrol action" to one of the two "Disable course enrolment" settings in Site admin > Plugins > Enrolments > Course meta link > Settings . This setting determines what action the parent course should take when the user is unenroled from a child course. The options for that setting are (in 3.5): Unenrol user from (parent) course Disable course enrolment (that is, suspend the enrolment in the parent) Disable course enrolment and remove roles (that is, supend the enrolment and also remove any assigned roles in the parent, eg student) This sounds like what you are seeing in your course. If one of the two Disable options is set, this is exactly what should happen, and would explain why the user is not in the child course anymore (they were unenroled in some way), but in the parent course their enrolment was suspended instead of being removed entirely (unenroled). The Moodle default value is "Disable course enrolment and remove roles". So if those suspended users in the Parent course also have had their roles removed, then this is the setting in your site. Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Importing course from other Moodle instances (different versions) [3.5.1+]

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help setting up a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello. I don't think this is particularly related to courses or course formats so I'll move it to the General help forum. You can do what you want using separate groups and with the teachers also in the same group as their students and with the capablity for them to see all groups removed. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help setting up a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. Create a role based on the teacher role but remove the ability to see all groups. 2. Put each school in a separate group with the appropriate teacher in the course. 3. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What are Course summary files limits?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, a) What are the limits on it in terms of resolution ?... Whatever the source image size ... it seems to be scaled down on the home page ... does anybody know to what? The image size source can be anything. Boost theme and most of the theme are responsive. The size is in pourcentage of your screen or of the element where the image is included. If you do a display image in the browser you'll see your image in full uploaded size. You can change that by adding some css. .coursebox .content .teachers, .coursebox .content .courseimage, .coursebox .content .coursefile, .coursebox .content .customfields-container { width: 40%; } .coursebox .content .courseimage img { max-width: 100px; max-height: 100px; } So your image in homepage of a course cannot be bigger than  W:100px H:100px; b) Should this 'Course Icon' be visible anywhere else on a standard
site? (Have I missed a setting somewhere limiting its scope to just the
home page?) At least In the list of course too. And in the dash board.  In the dashboard the css is different you'll only see a part of the image. .block_myoverview .dashboard-card-deck .dashboard-card, .block_recentlyaccesseditems .dashboard-card-deck . dashboard-card { width: calc(33.33% - .5rem); } c) Is there another way of doing something with the home page list of
courses to make it visually more distinctive? I believe that I am using
the Boost theme (which I like because other themes seem crowded. I am
very happy to insert CSS etc. ... if I knew where! Yes, you can do it by choosing a different theme, with more possible customisation like https://moodle.org/plugins/theme_adaptable But if you really want to stay with Boost You can also change css of your theme search for scss in admin (theme_boost | scss). Now you have to know what to achieve. if you add that in the theme scss you'll have bigger image in the homepage. You can change background color add more space add borders... .coursebox .content .courseimage img !important { max-width: 200px; max-height: 200px; } You can use browser tool to identify classes or elements id to customise. Hope it's help. Dominique.

ResponsesInList.Text: There is a difference between suspended status and active status. Suspended status is like getting suspended from school: you're still an active student at the school, but you're temporary suspended from participating (ie logging into the site). Suspended status is a site level context , not a course level context Inactive status is set from a course by course context. Suspended status at the site level does not automatically make users inactive at the course level as this can hide their grades from the teacher. For manual enrollments, you can suspend and inactivate at the same time, but you have to know what classes the user is in (a student information system is useful here). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM - not working when Chrome browser first opens
ResponsesInList.Text:
SSO with NTLM is normally a case
of the browser going to the login page causing the server to send a 401
Unauthorized response containing the header WWW-Authenticate: Negotiate and there may be other WWW-Authenticate headers saying what mechanisms
are supported. If the browser supports one of the supported mechanisms it
should reply with a corresponding Authorization header. You could try looking at the network tab in the Chrome DevTools to see exactly what is happening and comparing the requests and server responses for working browsers and not-working-first-time browsers to see if something different is occurring. I'm wondering if multiple authentication mechanisms are supported by the server and one lot of browsers are attempting this first and failing but not proceeding automatically to the next. Is the Chrome version consistent between the working and not working browsers?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM - not working when Chrome browser first opens
ResponsesInList.Text: The version of Chrome is consistent. I have taken a look at the Apache access.log log file on our Windows Moodle server. Below are two extracts. The first is from a PC that failed the log in. The back button was pressed and the login page resubmitted by clicking on the log on link again and a successful login achieved. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM - not working when Chrome browser first opens
ResponsesInList.Text: We usually recommend that organisations drop the use of NTLM and move to using saml2, - it's a lot easier to maintain and set-up (especially if you are using Azure AD) - If NTLM is giving you grief it might be worth dropping our auth_saml2 plugin in and just using that for SSO instead of battling with NTLM.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM - not working when Chrome browser first opens
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dan and thanks for your reply. We don't have Azure AD. What would I need to do to get this working? What information is required?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM - not working when Chrome browser first opens
ResponsesInList.Text: ...I've tried installing the plugin from the zip file (drag and drop) - It just seems to hang at the validation screen in Moodle. When I go back in to Moodle it isn't installed...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM - not working when Chrome browser first opens
ResponsesInList.Text: Could it be that the affected browsers have stored credentials, possibly using basic authentication? Check Chrome's password store to see if there's anything stored for the Moodle site. (I think Chrome can also use Window's password store so credentials could be managed via Control Panel but if IE isn't affected that's unlikely to be the case here). As a test try an incognito window on one of the affected computers and see if the problem still occurs.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM - not working when Chrome browser first opens
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Leon I will look into this. I have since made a breakthrough in isolating which computers are affected. We have two AD groups for workstations. One for staff workstations and one for students. The PCs that don't work are the student ones. If a member of staff uses a staff PC it's fine. If they use a student PC it causes the issue. This is all pointing to a GPO applied to the student workstation group. Each group has a different GPO, so the Chrome policy for staff is slightly different to that of the students.. This also explains why the only room we have for students that is running Windows 10 works fine. It has a completely different policy applied. It's all the student PCs running Window 7 that are the problem. Now I just have to try and work out what part of the GPO is causing the issue...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM - not working when Chrome browser first opens
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi again Leon. An update. I have software I manage the network with (Impero). This has a function called Mimic script that allows me to send keystrokes to a remote computer. If I send commands to jump to the URL window, type in the URL , press enter and then immediately open a new tab, the login works. It still works if you then use the browser normally i.e. type the address. It still works when you close Chrome and re-open it! However, if you log out of the PC and back in gain it stops working until you run the mimic script again...

ResponsesInList.Title: [Urgent] Mistake in submission report query
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone. ResponsesInList.Title: Using modules in the versioned REST API
ResponsesInList.Text:
I have modular APIs 
```text
MyProject.Modules
    Module1
        Logic and Repositories
    Module2
        Logic and Repositories
MyProject.RestApi
     Controllers
```
 I have created 1 version of the REST API (Uses ID (int as ID)) I want to create a new version that will use UUID (the previous one remains) There will also be new endpoints What to do with modules? For the new version of the API I will have to change the database queries in the Repository, name the methods, etc. think it'll largely depend on what your modules are encapsulating, if they are purposefully holding distinct versions or whether they are holders of a business domain e.g. Module1 is for loading users. If Module1 is loading users, and let's say you had the following pseudo code: 
```text
public class UserRepository

    public User GetUser(int userId)
```
 Then, having this would be returning the same class so perhaps would naturally be within the same repository: 
```text
public User GetUser(guid userId)
```
 I've purposefully not mentioned interfaces to keep the example simple, but lets say you had IRepository indicating the repository is responsible for returning users, then it doesn't matter if they are being returned by looking up guid or int, they are both related to a user. However your repository code made become quite bulky, so your Repository could simply be encapsulating two separate classes and presenting a unified user getting interface. However one the flip side, you may not wish you consumers of the existing Repository to also be reliant on a method they are not using (following the interface segregation principle https://scotch.io/bar-talk/s-o-l-i-d-the-first-five-principles-of-object-oriented-design#toc-interface-segregation-principle ) Is this solution be right? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: forum posts are not sent out as email
ResponsesInList.Text: hi, after digging a bit into the could i could resolve this issue myself. for forum posts that are sent out via email adhoc tasks are created and my adhoc task concurrency limit was too low. so these tasks where in the database , but actually never executed. this is what i did: Login as admin Navigate to Site administration -> Server -> Tasks -> Task processing Set "Scheduled task concurrency limit" to 1 Set "Scheduled task runner lifetime" to 10 minutes Set "Adhoc task concurrency limit" to 100 Set "Adhoc task runner lifetime" to 100 minutes with the next execution of the cron job emails where sent out fine. If I had known that this message "Scheduled task complete: E-Mail-Versand aus Foren (mod_forum\task\cron_task)" just means we created ad hoc tasks internally, but did not really send emails, i would have interpreted this sentence "Skipping processing of adhoc tasks. Concurrency limit reached." differently. anyway problem solved - just posting my solution for others who might run into this issue. thomas

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Invalid Login for one user via LDAP authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunately, I have the most embarrassing question to ask: are they entering their username and password correctly? Are they able to log in to other services that use your LDAP server for authentication? When I look at my user logs, I believe that error ID 3 corresponds to an incorrect password. "Login failed for user 'me@example.com'. Most likely the password did not match (error ID '3')." You might want to confirm that their username in Moodle matches the corresponding field in your LDAP system. Should their username include the domain ? In our LDAP setup, we have set "User attribute" to "mail" so that people need to login with their full email address, not just the username. All that said, I have encountered a problem where my setup was fine, and the user could authenticate to some services... but not others, including our Moodle. I do not administer the users in our LDAP system, so I had to punt the issue to our IT department. I believe the issue was related her being logged in to another device with a bad password, and our system's policies for dealing with that situation (which possibly does not apply to you). My best recommendation would be to collect as much information as possible and really isolate the problem. - Ray

ResponsesInList.Title: Category Administrator
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, I am running a moodle for a institution that has several campus. Each campus is a category so I would like to have an Admin for each campus/category. Manager access is not enough because it doesn´t allow them to create and upload users. Is it possible to have a role for admin access at category level? If so how? And I don´t want one admin from one category to see the courses from the other category. I´ve searched the forums but haven´t really found a solution. Or maybe I don´t understand the solution. Here are two that asked the same question: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=106274 and https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=115438 Thanks in advance! Version: Moodle 3.6.4 (Build: 20190513) Delbert

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Category Administrator
ResponsesInList.Text: What you are effectively looking for is multi-tenancy... Moodle doesn't do that. In general everybody can "see" all the courses on the site - although they can only access ones they have permission for. Your basic solution is to give Manager access at the Category level. If you also need them to manage user accounts then you need to create a new role with only those capabilities and assign them to that role at the Site/System level. Accounts are a site-wide thing - they can't exist restricted to categories. If you are determined to have full separation, have a look at www.iomad.org which is Moodle with multi-tenancy features bolted on. All of that comes with more complication which I would ask yourself if you really do need.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Category Administrator
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok that makes sense! I´m not sure if many people have requested something like this but it might be helpful to have a role already created with those capabilities that a admin category might use. Just as a suggestion Thanks for the help!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Category Administrator
ResponsesInList.Text: The general feeling, I believe, is not to proliferate roles. Given a bit of thought you can quickly come up with loads of them - all adding to the potential confusion.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Guys I'm having a desperate time with my latest version of moodle at the moment. Not sure if its moodle itself or whether its a setting.  In my moodledata folder in root of my host there is a folder temp/backup. In this folder it keeps adding files which after approximately 24 hours it shuts down my site as my host max disk size is 20gb and it keeps exceeding it. I emptied the folder and the my disk size went from 20gb down to 3.6gb and then i was able to use my moodle website. Can someone shed any light why moodle keeps putting files in here and how do i stop it? I have checked in my admin for automated backups etc and is disabled.  Be grateful for any help as always. I am running Moodle 3.7+ (Build: 20190530) Thanks Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle backup issue 3.7+
ResponsesInList.Text: For a start... do you have [ Cron ] running properly? Do you have automated backups enabled? Switch on Debugging (all the way to Developer. Leave it a few hours and then scour your web server 's error log for anything that sounds related. I suspect something is broken but let's hope it causing a log entry.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle backup issue 3.7+
ResponsesInList.Text: When Moodle makes a course backup it creates a copy in temp/backup which temporarily increases the Moodledata size. The resulting backup file is then moved into the Moodledata filedir folder (by default) and the files in temp/backup are removed. If they don't get removed that means a backup is failing. The other process that will create a course backup is the course or category recycle bin which works by creating a backup before a course or category is deleted. I know you've checked but automated backups are the most likely culprit. Check Site administration → Reports → Backups and confirm there's no recent activity. The temp/backup folder contains subfolders for each backup and should contain a .log file. The modification time of this file should give you a clue as to when the backup was started which may suggest a culprit. This time may tally with a "Course backup created" event in the site log .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'loader' of undefined
ResponsesInList.Text: So what changed? Go through your logs and see if there was something that changed at the time this error started occurring. But you will need to detect the cause quickly. However, check your moodledata folder, make sure that has not been tampered with. There should be some kind of log to detect if and when the moodledata folder was last accessed. Be aware, this kind of error, can become a piece of string, that is, it just keeps getting longer and it is easy to be monstered by. Provisional response, reinstall the codebase. It is better to find the cause, but don't spend too much time on it. If nothing presents itself soon, refresh the codebase. If the error persists, then it is likely to be a database or moodledata folder error, which makes it easier to track.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle Wan Access With Apache2
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, I installed a moodle in ubuntu 16 following this step by step, https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Step-by-step_Installation_Guide_for_Ubuntu The system is working, but the wan access it's not working, I'm missing something in the apache2. I can access to the http://mydomain from wan, but when I use  http://mydomain/moodle I'm recieving the error of the image below, for some reason the apache2 is no loading the moodle server and is showing my internal ip address.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Wan Access With Apache2
ResponsesInList.Text:
In moodle's config.php, you set a variable called 
```text
$CFG->
wwwroot
```
 . Moodle will only allow itself to be accessed from this address. If you access it via another address, it will redirect you to the `wwwroot` address. What's probably happening here is that `wwwroot` is set to `http://your.i.p.address/moodle` . When you go to `http://mydomain/moodle` over WAN, it successfully reaches your moodle site, realises you're trying to access it via a different address, and redirects you to `http://your.i.p.address/moodle` . Since you can't access your local IP over the WAN, you see the error page. The simplest solution to this is to set `wwwroot` to `http://mydomain/moodle` , then make it so that when you're on your local machine, `mydomain` points to your local IP address, not your public one. Depending on your setup, you could do this using a local DNS server, or more simply using your /etc/hosts file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating a new activity plugin with Skeleton builder (or a better way?)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Welcome to the community Jay. In Moodle there are different sorts of plugins with slightly different requirements. The activity plugin in the /mod/ folder requires a table for instance settings. If you're plugin is called "minigame", then you should have a table called "minigame". Have a look at the other mod plugins in the file db/install.xml. So you would need to have your own file there 
```text
/mod/minigame/db/install.xml
```
 The minimum fields you would require would be: id, course, name, intro, introformat, and timemodified. You can add other fields, depends on how much configuration you want to give to your teachers. Following on from that you would need a form to edit those settings, and that will be mod_form.php 
```text
/mod/minigame/mod_form.php
```
 Again, look at some other plugins. It's a good idea to have a lib.php file as you can hook into some autoloading functions. This is useful if you want to load up and trigger some javascript or change navigation menus. If you do a search in the code for ' get_plugins_with_function' you'll find a list of functions you can add to your lib.php file. e.g. for "extend_navigation_course" you would need the function "mod_minigame_extend_navigation_course" with the appropriate signature defined in the get_plugins_with_function call. Your lib.php file should also contain functions that will perform actions when an instance is added: minigame_add_instance minigame_update_instance minigame_delete_instance ... Again look at other plugins for examples. And this is also where you might add events, if you need. Also grades, though I've not needed to play with that interface, so someone else might need to chip in on that. I hope that gives you enough pointers to be getting on with.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Deleted gradebook item still visible with error after deletion
ResponsesInList.Text: Just a note for anybody experiencing this.... Module deletion is an example of an 'adhoc task'. These are tasks that are simply set up to run by the cron and the next possible opportunity. They will run *last* after everything else has run in the cron. They do not appear in the list of scheduled tasks in the admin settings (as they are "one off" tasks). The problem comes if the task fails. If the task throws an exception it will be re-queued but with a delay. The delay gets longer on each failure up to a day. So, if something is going wrong the task will quite quickly retry once a day. You are unlikely to spot this. If you run out of ideas and suspect this, check the take mdl_task_adhoc. Check for instances of '\core_course\task\course_delete_modules' with high 'faildelays'.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Fatal cron error concerning locks
ResponsesInList.Text: Had a similar issue ... strange error .. not seen before and server been running just fine for years!!!  Don't re-call the details now, but through investigation had to do with clean up of the locks in moodledata/lock ... cron/task runs, whatever it runs, moodle locks so no new data etc. can sneak in there until the cron/task completed.   Once done, lock is cleaned up/cleared. What I did ... removed the contents of moodledata/lock/ (after creating a quick backup of it - just in case) ... moodle repopulated on next cron run. Issue seem to go away. In scheduled task there are Analytics cleanup \core\task\analytics_cleanup_task Predict models \tool_analytics\task\predict_models and a Train models \tool_analytics\task\train_models You could run the last via command line to check. moodlecode/admin/tool/task/cli php schedule_task.php --execute="\tool_analytics\task\train_models" That should by pass any topics addon, shouldn't it? ResponsesInList.Title: Hidden Courses and Import
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have a fairly recent problem that I am not sure has always been the case or not, but within our system, we have set hidden courses as completely hidden from teachers and student, but for some reason, when a teacher goes to Import, they are still able to see and even import from the hidden courses they are attached to. I have tried all the Hidden permissions (not set, prevent and prohibit) and can't work out why this may be happening and can't seem to find any other permission that relates to importing other than turning of the import permission completely. Has anyone got any suggestions that may help me please. Amy Edit: using Moodle 3.3

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hidden Courses and Import
ResponsesInList.Text: Amy, It looks like the import process is only checking if the user has the capability moodle/backup:backuptargetimport allowed in the target course(s), which of course a user will have by default if they enrolled in it as a Teacher. Import does not know or check if the course is hidden from the user. In fact, it doesn't even bother to check if the user enrollment in the target course is suspended or not A possible workaround is: If you change the enrolment in the target course so the teacher is actually in the non-editing teacher role, this will do what you want. Or if you don't want to use that non-editing role for some reason, you could clone the Teacher role, remove the import permission from it, and change the user enrolment role from teacher to this new "no-import-from" teacher role in the target course. In either case, both accomplish the same thing: the course will not show up on the list of courses to import from because the user does not have that capability allowed there anymore. Of course, if you have a lot of courses, this would be a lot of work depending on why you are hiding the courses from the teachers (eg old archives you don't want them to see or use anymore but you need their enrollment still there.) Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.7.2 Installation Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not sure what version you have: Moodle 3.7.2 hasn't been released yet. There is a Moodle 3. 6 .2 but the latest 3.6 release is 3.6.4 which is what would be recommended for a new site. From your description and screenshot it looks like some content isn't being loaded, JavaScript files are needed to respond to the click so maybe the browser wasn't able to load this. Your screenshot also shows blue and red squares by each field. These should be icons as shown in the screenshot below, which indicates the browser can't load images either which probable has the same cause. Issues like this can occur when a site's URL has changed from http: to https:. Can you confirm what you're using to access your site and whether $CFG->wwwroot in config.php (in the root of the Moodle source code folder on the server) matches this URL, importantly that the http: or https: prefix matches. Moodle sites can only have a single URL which is set in config.php and this must be the URL used to access the site. You can't set your site up as http: and access it using https: without updating this setting. Your browser's network monitoring page (e.g. Firefox Network Monitor ) can help show which files that a page is trying to use can't be loaded.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Completion icon
ResponsesInList.Text:
That icon only shows in the Course Overview block in Moodle 3.5 and earlier, and only if activity completion is NOT enabled in a course ( see Moodle docs ). You can hide it using custom CSS ... 
```text
.progress-chart-container {display: none;}
```
 but it will also hide the completion percentage display for courses where activity completion IS enabled. It depends on your theme where you add your custom CSS, but in Boost, go to Site Administration > Appearance > Themes > Boost > Advanced settings and add it in the 'Raw SCSS' box. The Course Overview block has changed from Moodle 3,6 onwards - see https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Course_overview

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I boost the speed of notification?
ResponsesInList.Text: Having had some experience at mail servers ... Are all the receipients on the same mail server system?  Where you control where the mail is sent as well? If not, even if you configure your moodle server as best you can, email servers on other might reject ... you could then have a flood of failed notifications coming back to the mail services on your moodle ... thus eating up resources and taking away from normal moodle processing. Whatever server is set up to send 1000+ messages had better have spotless mx, dkim, spf, and any other config for the blockhole/ spam checkers. Your answer/solution ... me thinks ... a very robust SMTP relay that does have mx,dkim,spf, etc. and that you can control ... SendGrid?  Mailgun? or other such SMTP relay is advised. Nearly all mail servers have sending limits - number of messages ... and it's not 1000+ in one minute. Note also that PHP's mail() function opens a new socket for every mail sent. If you're looping through a large recipient list and sending a message to each one individually, you could quickly run out of sockets. A realistic expectation should be taken. https://sendgrid.com/ https://www.mailgun.com/ You might consider mailman on a dedicated server. https://www.list.org/ Now if you are wondering how this forum manages to send mail to many users, consider that behind this server interface is Amazon - probably more than one server ... and located in multiple geographic locations.   Check the header of a message you get from this server to get an idea. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Site Backup.Please Help
ResponsesInList.Text: i am trying to move my moodle 3.7 test site from an ubuntu 18.4 Live Server to my live site.I am hoping to do a backup on the test site and then restore on my live site.i have copied the moodle and moodledata folders into a backup folder already but i am failing to copy the mysql database using my sql dump.It is asking me for a password and i have used the information in my config.php file.I need to do this as a matter of urgency so please any help would be greatly appreciated.i am not a linux guru so please be patient!!!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Backup.Please Help
ResponsesInList.Text: With mysqldump you specify the user account name with -u , and the password with -p with no space after (or no -p if there's no password), e.g. I might back up my moodle36 database with: mysqldump --single-transaction --default-character-set=utf8mb4 -u root -p the_password moodle36 > moodle36.sql Where the_password is the password for my MySQL root user. MySQL has user accounts and these user accounts can have different privileges. The user account in config.php may not have the privileges to do a backup. The user account with the most privileges is root (this is different from the Linux root user). So if it's your server you should know the password for the MySQL root user. The MySQL user Moodle uses, the one in config.php , might have enough privileges for a backup if you use the $CFG->dbuser and $CFG->dbpass values but it sounds like you've tried this and it hasn't worked. If it's still not working, let us know what commands you are using and what messages you get when it doesn't work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Backup.Please Help
ResponsesInList.Text: Hie Leon I have tried your solution but it still asks me for a password. I am currently using the username and password that is in my config.php file(dbuser and dbpass) the command that I have used so far is as below: mysqldump -uUsername -pPassword moodle> ./backup moodle.sql Once I enter that it asks me for a password. I am flabbergasted as to which password this is. please help

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Backup.Please Help
ResponsesInList.Text: Can you send a screenshot of the command and it asking for a password? You can obscure any sensitive info like the password itself. The reason I ask for this is that this command shouldn't ask for a password. If you put -p with no password it will ask for a password but if you put -pPassword it will try that password and if it fails it will show an error. Note that if you have a space in the backup filename you must use ./backup_moodle.sql or "./backup moodle.sql" .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Backup.Please Help
ResponsesInList.Text: Hie Leon. Thanks a lot.I have attached the screenshot below.I hope you can make head or tail of it!!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Backup.Please Help
ResponsesInList.Text:
So as I said: specify the password with -p with no space after: 
```text
mysqldump -u username -ppassword moodle > ./backup/moodle.sql
```
 It looks like the lines where you tried my command ( mysqldump --single-transaction ... ) worked, there's no error message just a warning. However you will have overwritten the backup file, ./backup/moodle.sql , with the subsequent failed attempts. So just run the command again with no space between the -p and the password and it should work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course completion problem
ResponsesInList.Text: So, course completion is a combination of activity requirements and course requirements.  You did not identify what your activity conditions are in combination.  Are you using the course grade or grades to pass on your quizzes? If each quiz requires a certain number of points to pass AND you require all four quizzes complete and put 60 in the required course grade, if a student does not achieve the required number of points on one quiz but exceed the required number on others to total the 60 points, they will not get marked complete on the course because the quiz requirement wasn't met. Conversely, if you want them to get 60 points total but also want them to get 20 points per quiz, if they get 25 on two quizzes but only 5 on the other two, they will still have 60 points but didn't get an adequate score on two quizzes. SELECT u.firstname, u.lastname, r.shortname AS role,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Completion Not Working
ResponsesInList.Text: The progress bar on the dashboard shows activity completion and not course completion - so if your single activity SCORM pack is complete then it will show as complete even if you don't have course completion set. However, assuming you have set up Course completion as well as activity completion (and marked that SCORM activity as required for course completion ) then check in Site administration > Server > Scheduled tasks that the task 'Calculate regular completion data' is running frequently enough, such as every minute. You need to make sure the cron is running properly on your site, since all course completion is handled by cron tasks and does not happen immediately in the way that activity completion does.

ResponsesInList.Title: Disable browser caching in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Is there anyone who knows if it is possible to disable browser caching in moodle. Regards, Peter

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Peter,
Can you give a bit more detail? What would you like to prevent the browser from caching and why? This will help us give a better answer.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:
ResponsesInList.Text: I made some changes to a user profile in Joomla. These are synchronized with Moodle via webservices (Joomdle). These changes are processed in the Moodle database , but some of them are only visible after I clear the browser cache. This applies, for example, to the avatar and the username shown in the header. When i can prevent Moodle to use a browser cache, I do not have to bother the user with that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:
ResponsesInList.Text: In general, you don't want to disable browser caching, as that will seriously degrade performance for your users. When moodle outputs the user's avatar, it adds ?rev=123 to the URL , when 123 is the value of the `picture` field in the user table. If you change the user's picture, you should increment this value to prevent caching issues (since the URL is different, the browser will not use the cache). Other text fields in the database might be cached on the server by Moodle, but the browser cache should not make a difference here. Try purging the Moodle cache following the update and see if that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanx Mark, Purging cache doesn't help. I've tried that allready. Emptying the browser cache does. That's why i would like to try and see how much the performance is degrading after i disable the browser cache.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:
ResponsesInList.Text: Completely disabling caching is really a web server question rather than a moodle question. You should be able to configure your webserver to send the appropriate headers with each request that prevents the browser from caching it. The exact way to do this will depend on the web server software you're using, a web search should find the instructions you need.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Set time out for an activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Different activities have different settings to control them, so you might want to be a little more specific. Also, you might need to explain what you mean by "close automatically." The example that you gave seems to be an "Assignment" activity because you mention " upload ." For an assignment, there are three "Availability" settings: Allow from, Due date, and Cut-off date. If you use a Due date, Assignments uploaded after this due date will be tagged as overdue when you go to grade them. The Cut-off date disallows submissions after its date. The concept of a timer does not exist for Assignments, but it does for Quizzes, but is based on when the student begins, not from the day that it is administratively turned on.

ResponsesInList.Title: Using completion to add users to a group
ResponsesInList.Text: OK this is a bit unusual, so I'm not sure it's possible. We have ~120 students per year go through several courses in groups of about 10-12 each month. At the end of the year all students need full access for revision, but when they move on to the next topic we don't want them to get notifications and forum posts for content they've already covered. Historically the course admin manually added all users to groups for each monthly batch, and it was a lot of effort, especially if students swapped groups (this is replicated over several courses). This year we're trying something new, and auto enrol all students to the course, but make activities such as forums hidden unless they are a member of the relevant group - which they join using a group choice activity. When they finish their rotation, the students remove themselves from the group so they no longer get forum posts and can focus on whichever topic they are now studying. Everything appeared to be working perfectly until it came to assignment submissions. The problem is that if students remove themself from the group before their assignment is graded, they disappeared from the list of students to be marked. Manually adding them back to the group makes their submission reappear. I thought of a few ways to work around this - the main blocker seems to be that the topic section is set to hidden unless they belong to the group, so even although the assignment isn't using any group setting it is still being affected by the activity being hidden (as far as I can tell). What I'd ideally like to do is automatically (eg using conditional activity settings) add students to a second group if they submit the assignment, and allow users in that group access to the assignment, but I'm not seeing any way to achieve that. The alternative is a much less satisfying fudge of letting all students see all sections and just limit specific activities such as forums. If there was a way to link collapsed topics format to group membership that would do a lot of what I'm looking for (if member of group x, show topic x, otherwise retract topic). Hoping somebody out there has a suggestion! Cheers, Gordon.

ResponsesInList.Title: Enrolling in course more than once
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a course that staff use to access resources for mentoring and record information about a student. This is fine when they only mentor one student and will only ever mentor one student but in reality they often mentor more than one at a time or mentor one after another. I'm looking for a way to have staff be able to enrol in a course more than once and then ideally be able to pick which instance of the course they want to access when the choose. Really not sure if that is something that can be done so open to other suggestions of how to achieve this without staff having to create different accounts with different email addresses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Enrolling in course more than once
ResponsesInList.Text: It sounds like what you're imagining is that a user can access a course, and have a separate set of user data on that course for each student they mentor? I'm afraid that's not going to work using Moodle's standard activities . Most activity plugins are written to store data against the instance of the plugin, and the user creating the data. To achieve what you want, you'll need a plugin that stores data against another user who is the subject, rather than the author, of the data. In the past I've used the ILP block for this, although it's not currently maintanied. There might be something else similar out there. You might also be able to do something clever with the database module, where you can select another user as a field in each record?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrolling in course more than once
ResponsesInList.Text: It sounds to me like you want the mentors to be able to access student data for all their students but not for students they don't mentor.  You may already have a mentor role created, if so, this is easy. Make sure the mentor role is set up to only see their groups. Then create groups in the course(s), one for each mentor. Assign the students and the mentor to that group.  Make sure the course and relevant activities are set to separate groups.  Then the mentor logs in and only sees grades/assignments for their students. If the issue is several courses, you could create cohorts for each mentor (at the top level or category levels) and assign the cohort to the course (enroll by cohort) and assign them to the group directly through enrollment.  This way, if the mentor gets new students or loses students, you can add/remove them from the groups automatically with one change (make sure that if you remove them from the cohort that you either add them through a different cohort or manually ensure enrollment to make certain you don't lose their participation).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.5 uploading a backup file results in 404 error
ResponsesInList.Text: **Resolved** We had to change the following: Modifying the IIS 7.0/7.5 configuration (Windows Server 2008, Windows Server 2008 R2) First increase activity and request time outs (allows large files to succeed on slow connections) FastCGI Settings > Edit (Right-click on PHP application) Set Process Model > Activity Timeout to '3600' (one hour) Set Process Model > Request Timeout to '3600' (one hour) Next set 'Maximum allowed content length' Request Filtering > Edit Feature Settings: Set 'Maximum allowed content length' to your desired file size (in bytes) e.g. '536870912' for 512MB (default is approximately 28.6MB) I hope it helps other. Cheers!

ResponsesInList.Title: LTI and secure access
ResponsesInList.Text: We have a course that we would like to make available through another non-Moodle LMS to another organization through the LTI process. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LTI and secure access
ResponsesInList.Text: AFAIK , for an LTI connection that is made between sites, the LMS they are using becomes the parent and the LTI unit becomes a child of the parent LMS course. To restrict access to that LTI unit, from the parent LMS, the course accessing the LTI unit will have to be separate from another course if you want to restrict access to it. You will have to use the security settings of the parent LMS to get that to work properly, I would expect.

ResponsesInList.Title: Extending the support period for the November releases
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Colleagues This is my first post on Moodle.org, so please forgive any mishaps or unintended breaches of etiquette. My name is Steve Powell and I head up the e-Learning team at Lancaster University. Some of you may know me from the Moodle Users Association or Moodle Moot. My proposed topic of discussion is whether Moodle HQ would consider extending the period of support provided for November releases. Here at Lancaster, we upgrade Moodle once a year during the summer. As you would expect we take the May release. It might seem that there would be plenty of time between May and September to upgrade Moodle, but in practice this is not the case. There are a lot of modifications/plugins that we need to refactor and test, and that takes time and we aim to make the new version available for staff to try as soon as we possibly can. This is because we know that the majority of academic staff are by and large unavailable in the months of July and August. Staff are tied up with marking, conferences and often spend the summer months away from Campus. As a result, teaching staff will often only see the new version of Moodle in September when they come back to teach. So just before teaching begins, when academics and support staff are already overloaded with work and under stress, the upgrade, far from being perceived as an improvement can be viewed as yet another issue to deal with. I feel sure that the picture I am describing (not very well I grant you) is not unique to us. The biggest change that I can see that could really help us is if Moodle HQ can extend the period of support for November releases so that we could take the November release, but actually deploy it during the following summer (July/August). This would mean that November releases would in effect be long term releases. This would give the development team more time to deploy the upgrade, and give staff a real opportunity to look at the next release and understand what new and exciting features it provides, building a sense of anticipation rather than anxiety. I would be interested in knowing whether other users would recognise the picture I describe, and would consider this idea of value. If other members do think this idea has merit Thank you Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: invaliddatarootpermissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, the rights on moodledata should be different. Generally the web server only needs read access to the Moodle source code but needs read/write access to moodledata. The documentation covers the basic setting up of permissions . There are also security recommendations to harden this further . It's the web server user that needs read/write access to moodledata, this might be apache if you're using Apache , so you can try granting only this. You might need to first change file and directory ownership to this user with chown . You should make sure that the site's cron is run as the web server user (i.e. not root) if you lock the moodledata rights down. If you need more help let us know if you're using Apache or Nginx or something else as the web server, and the output of ls -lh /path/to/moodledata so we can see the current user and group ownership of files and directories. In general if you want to try out different settings do this first on a test site/server if possible.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: invaliddatarootpermissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle won't change the permissions or ownership. In fact a non-root user ( apache ) wouldn't be able to change the ownership to root on a Linux system. Back to my original reply: "make sure that the site's cron is run as the web server user (i.e. not root)". If the site cron is running as root then any changes it makes will be as the root user so any files or directories it creates will be owned by root. The site cron should be in the apache user's crontab. If the web site is running as user apache and so is the cron then all the files and directories in Moodledata should be owned by that user.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: Re: invaliddatarootpermissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello I checked and I don't see anything in the cron that changes the rights to root:root. The server is run in apache and the permissions on files and directories in apache are also executed. Do you have any other leads, please? thank you

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: invaliddatarootpermissions
ResponsesInList.Text:
To clarify the point about the site cron: this is a script, …/admin/cli/cron.php , which gets run normally by the server's cron service. Each server user account can have a crontab (list of commands to run at scheduled times), the root user can have a crontab and so can the apache user. These commands are run as that user, i.e. if it's in root 's crontab it's run as root . Moodle activity run through the website will be performed as the apache user so any files created will be owned by apache . Any files created by the Moodle cron script will be owned by the corresponding crontab user account. To check this you can run the following commands as root : 
```text
# crontab -l


# crontab -u apache -l
```
 The second command should list the Moodle cron. If the first lists this or any other Moodle script then that's probably why you're seeing files owned by root in Moodledata. I apologise for repeating this point but I think it's the most likely explanation. If you still see files in Moodledata either created with root ownership or changing to be being owned by root then somewhere you have a process running as root performing these actions. In your post the modification time on /var/www/moodledata/temp/filestorage (owned by root ) is 07:00 which is a suspiciously "round" time, i.e. on the hour, which again suggests that a scheduled task is involved. I hope this helps. If you're still getting nowhere, post the output of the above crontab commands so we can see the status (remove/obscure any sensitive information).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: invaliddatarootpermissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for reply It's perfect. I hadn't noticed that the cron was running as root and not as apache. I will see in the next few days 0,15,30,45,45 6-22 * * 1-5 sudo -u apache /usr/bin/php /var/www/html/admin/cli/cron.php

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: invaliddatarootpermissions
ResponsesInList.Text:
Instead of using sudo in root 's crontab entry, add an entry to the apache user's crontab. You can edit the apache user's crontab with: 
```text
# crontab -u apache -e
```
 then add the line: 
```text
0,15,30,45,45 6-22 * * 1-5 /usr/bin/php /var/www/html/admin/cli/cron.php
```
 And remove the existing line from root's crontab.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Calendar - get rid of icons in display, taking too much space
ResponsesInList.Text:
1. Eliminate the icons to get more space for the text of item... 
```text
.path-calendar .maincalendar .calendarmonth ul li .badge.badge-circle {display: none;}


.path-calendar .maincalendar .calendarmonth ul li .icon {display: none;}
```
 2. Make the font size of text a bit smaller... 
```text
.path-calendar .maincalendar .calendarmonth ul li>a {font-size: 0.9em;}
```
 3. Make the item text wrap in cell ala spreadsheet style... Note that will make your rows different sizes... 
```text
.path-calendar .maincalendar .calendarmonth ul li>a {white-space: normal;}
```
 Note that 2 and 3 are actually the same element, so combine them if you want both: 
```text
.path-calendar .maincalendar .calendarmonth ul li>a {font-size: 0.9em; white-space: normal;}
```

Hi all,

Just in case anyone else encounters this issue, I've just upgraded from 3.4.x to 3.6.x and experienced the "Duplicate entry '1-admin' for key 'mdl_user_mneuse_uix' " error. After a little head scratching I realised that I'd forgotten to update my config.php file. This is described in https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/MySQL_full_unicode_support but somehow I missed this step (which is vital):

Adjust the $CFG->dboptions Array in your config.php to make sure that Moodle uses the right Collation when connecting to the MySQL Server:
$CFG->dboptions = array(
…
'dbcollation' => 'utf8mb4_unicode_ci',
…
);

ResponsesInList.Title: Assign Users to Courses at First Login via Cohorts (Moodle v3.6)
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Moodlers, I'm currently working on a project for the NHS and the deadline for go live is fast approaching.  The number of staff impacted by the Single Clinical Portal we are launching, is a little over 5500 staff.   T he Clinical Portals Digital Content (The Learning Materials) are broken down into Courses 1 to 5 & 6 to 8 at this point, and before we announce that everything is good to go, I want to be able to action and test before go live the following experience for staff. SIDE NOTE:  Moodle is Connected to LDAP / AD so that all staff across the trust can self register for an account when they login to Moodle v3.6 with their default system Username and Passwords.   The Data Centre Services team have configured this, and it works perfectly. This is where I need a little advice and guidance Once the learner has logged in, I would like moodle to automatically assign all users with a default set of courses (CORE COURSE CONTENT ITEMS 1 - 5) automatically, the moment their self registration account is created. I then want the learner to see course content items 6 - 8 but only when course content items 1 - 5 have been completed and passed . Is this possible with the use of Cohorts? Can you advise me please to which subjects in the portal I should be researching. My sincerest thanks in advance Mark Jones

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign Users to Courses at First Login via Cohorts (Moodle v3.6)
ResponsesInList.Text: There are third party enrolment plugins, Auto Enrolment and Course Completed Enrolment , which may do what you want. They list support for Moodle 3.4 but I've had a quick test on Moodle 3.6 and they seem to work okay. The Course Completed Enrolment plugin only matches completion of a single course however so it may not work for you. Auto Enrolment with Enrol on set to "User login" appears to meet the first requirement.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Assign Users to Courses at First Login via Cohorts (Moodle v3.6)
ResponsesInList.Text: It turns out there's another AutoEnrol plugin which has some additional functionality such as the ability to filter which users are automatically enrolled, e.g. to restrict this to LDAP users only. Also, Moodle 3.6 versions of all three of these plugins are listed on their Versions page.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign Users to Courses at First Login via Cohorts (Moodle v3.6)
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a similar setup and have been using cohorts to do what you describe at least for part #1 What I've done is : I Mapped a couple of fields from Moodle to their profile in AD (You can use either a profile field like company / department or use a custom profile field.)  I've set these fields as locked and update on every login. I use Autoenrol cohort to add my users on login to cohorts dynamically based on the user profile field. I use the cohort sync enrollment method (The one that ships with Moodle) to enroll all members of a cohort to the course As for Part #2, I'm not sure it can be easily done: https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Course_completion_FAQ#How_can_I_prevent_my_students_accessing_course_2_before_they_have_completed_course_1.3F However, you may be able to accomplish it by using the External Tool activity and setting up LTI enrollments. ( https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Publish_as_LTI_too l) Using some form of activity completion to limit access to the External tools. -Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: Deleting Course
ResponsesInList.Text: Did the 'more info this error link' link to anything useful ... a page that had suggestions as to what to do/try? When anything is deleted from a 3.6 moodle now a recyclebin is in play.  Check servers setting for recyclebin. Set recyclebin to show all the time ... go into the course and see if there is a recyclebin link in the course admin menu.  Should be able to delete what it shows in that display. After X days, gets moved to trashdir which when cron runs trashdir gets emptied if the task scheduled to run., Could be a lot to delete if you have been making backups of the course and the backups are stored in your private file area. Check your moodledata/ directory ownerships and permissions - especially moodledata/temp/backup/  to make recyclebin links it uses the backup code to create small .mbz files ... backups ... of modules removed. And in Site Admin - Server - PHP info, check the settings for 'time for a script to run', memory a script can consume, etc. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: Deleting Course
ResponsesInList.Text: The error was/is: "cannot_empty_backup_temp_dir" Use what ever tool you have to browse files on your servcer - cPanel/ Plesk /Webmin/ and command line shell (ssh) are such tools. Path to your moodledata directory can be found in your moodle code's config.php file. Ownerships/Permissons kinda depends upon how you are hosted ... shared hosting?   If so, moodledata/temp/backup/ might belong to your login account. Did you find the setting for recyclebin and set it to always display? When you go into the course that you cannot delete is there a 'recyclebin' link in the course admin menu? 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Sharing a VPS for Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text:
I am looking at Hosting
for my Moodle for next semester. My first option is

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: Re: Sharing a VPS for Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: What I did when I was upgrading my GoDaddy server is that I purchased their "Value" VPS, with a discount coupon of maybe 20-30%, for only one month. This cost me around $30. You have to be careful that you know how to cancel it. Then, I experimented several times configuring the server and Moodle. It's kind of fun. When you want to start over, you just "reprovision" the server and you are back to square 1. Of course, keep careful notes so that it's easy to repeat what you have done. When I was comfortable, I canceled the one-month subscription and purchased a Deluxe server for 3 years, at a discount. One can explore and negotiate the discount, but typically 20-30%. A 3-year purchase got me to that effective $35/month cost. I felt that I needed, and could afford, the Deluxe server. I did this back in January of 2018, around 20 months ago, and my server has never gone down. It has been my most solid server-moodle installation ever. Of course, I do tweak the server and have some auto-update software running. I do like that I have cPanel, because it gives me, a novice server admin, some easy tools for doing things on my server, like changing the database and tweaking php. This is GoDaddy, but my guess is that one can do the same thing with other companies. Realize that GoDaddy doesn't provide much support for this experimenting. Nor do they touch Moodle. You can always ask them questions, and they will do their best to help, but they tend to not provide software installation help. They expect you, the VPS admin, to know what you are doing. Server-side problems they can help with. James, I do recall that you have been at this for a while, so you might be a good candidate for experimenting on your own. It might be the best $30 that you have ever spent, or wasted away.

And don't know how a droplet would initially bring up a DB server either ... a standalone box ... below. max_connections defaults to 151 in vr 5.x so no problem there. Initial usage may not show it but after usage innodb_buffer_pool_size normally has to increase and along with that innodb_buffer_pool_instances. To make sure Moodle never tries to use DB for sessions, might be wise to set $CFG->dbsessions=0 from the get go. As courses get used, backups of them become more important and so, depending upon how courses have evolved, another tweak in advance ... max_allowed_packet The 'goal' is to keep the DB server/DB's lean and mean! Including those times when away from school (and you are also) and students might be accessing via their devices. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sharing a VPS for Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi James Sorry, I didn't follow the whole discussion. Mainly because I don't think sharing a VPS to run multiple Moodle instances by multiple system administrators makes sense. Firstly, for a VPS costing USD 5 - 40 per month the admins will lose much more coordinating the group. Secondly, a VPS is already a shared resource, the virtualization doing the partitioning. On the other hand, informal sharing of a dedicated server makes sense. They are more expensive. But each Moodles instance has access to much more resources, as long as the peak activity of the Moodle instances do not overlap. On top of that it is environment friendly, less energy burnt per Moodle instance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hiding blocks on dashboard not working
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Franky, I'm unaware of any bugs in that direction, but the following may be happening: For site admins, there are two places where you can change what is being displayed on the user's dashboard : - your own personal dashboard (../my) - the dashboard configuration page (../my/indexsys.php) If you're hiding blocks on your own dashboard page, this will only affect your own dashboard. If instead you wish to rearrange the dashboard for all users, go to Site administration > Appearance > Default dashboard page. Here, you can rearrange blocks, set them to (in)visible etc. Once you're done, be sure to hit the Reset Dashboard for all users, so your changes can be deployed for all users. If you don't want certain blocks to be available to users, when they in turn edit their dashboard, be sure to go to Site administration > Plugins > Blocks > Manage blocks and use the 'eye' icon to disable blocks. Here, you can also use the 'lock' icon to lock certain blocks, so they can't be changed by individual users. Hope this helps,

Trying to reconnect... Connection id: 1234576 Current database: Moodle_database +-----+-------------------------+--------+-------+---------+-----------+--------------------+------+----------+-------------+------------+--------+--------------+--------------+ | id | docid | itemid | title | content | contextid | areaid | type | courseid | owneruserid | modified | userid | description1 | description2 | +-----+-------------------------+--------+-------+---------+-----------+--------------------+------+----------+-------------+------------+--------+--------------+--------------+ | 999 | mod_glossary-entry-999 | 999 | post | after | 1999 | mod_glossary-entry | 9 | 8 | 0 | 0000000001 | 9 | post | NULL | | 888 | mod_glossary-entry-1888 | 1888 | post | after | 1888 | mod_glossary-entry | 9 | 9 | 0 | 0000000001 | 9 | | NULL | +-----+-------------------------+--------+-------+---------+-----------+--------------------+------+----------+-------------+------------+--------+--------------+--------------+ 2 rows in set (0.94 sec) MariaDB [Moodle_database]> And also: Where are you seeing the "MySQL server has gone away" error? This isn't a problem with MySQL, it is simply a timeout that is being encountered by whatever script is generating the error. If a script opens and uses a MySQL connection, then does something else outside of MySQL for too long (more than the wait_timeout which is set to 180 seconds), the connection times out and is closed. If the script then attempts to submit another query to MySQL without first re-opening the connection, it is told that it's connection is no longer open (MySQL server has gone away). Good programming practices would include a re-open of the database connection after anything that might cause much delay since the last MySQL query was made, however this is all too often not the case. This would not explain why global search reports "Error reading from database" though, as that error is instant. The following is logged to /home/moodlesite.com/public_html/search/error_log indicating the problem with the global search: [03-May-2019 18:49:40 Europe/London] Default exception handler: Error reading from database Debug: Can't find FULLTEXT index matching the column list SELECT * FROM mdl_search_simpledb_index WHERE (owneruserid = ? OR owneruserid = ?) AND contextid IN (?,?,?,?) AND MATCH (title, content, description1, description2) AGAINST (?) LIMIT 0, 10 [array ( 0 => 0, 1 => 0, 2 => 2, 3 => 1465, 4 => 26, 5 => 2733, 6 => 'test', )] Error code: dmlreadexception * line 486 of /lib/dml/moodle_database.php: dml_read_exception thrown * line 1245 of /lib/dml/mysqli_native_moodle_database.php: call to moodle_database->query_end() * line 1400 of /lib/dml/moodle_database.php: call to mysqli_native_moodle_database->get_records_sql() * line 184 of /search/engine/simpledb/classes/engine.php: call to moodle_database->get_records_select() * line 790 of /search/classes/manager.php: call to search_simpledb\engine->execute_query() * line 684 of /search/classes/manager.php: call to core_search\manager->search() * line 151 of /search/index.php: call to core_search\manager->paged_search() Upon checking another Moodle installation using the mdl_search_simpledb_index, I was able to see the "mdl_search_simpledb_index_index FULLTEXT" index existing, where it was not existing on your database. I was then able to use an export of the structure for the table on that database to create the index using the following MySQL query: ALTER TABLE `mdl_search_simpledb_index` ADD FULLTEXT KEY `mdl_search_simpledb_index_index` (`title`,`content`,`description1`,`description2`); As you can see from https://moodlesite.com/search/index.php?q=test the search now works properly. Hope this may help someone in the future.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alter Moodle Administrator
ResponsesInList.Text: I’m fairly sure that there is no capability that specifically controls themes; it’s tied to the permission for " Change site configuration ", which will allow much more than just selecting a theme. But if you allow category and/or user themes in Site Administration > Themes > Theme settings , then the teacher role can choose the theme for their course from the list of installed themes, and any role that is allowed to edit the category settings can choose a theme for that category. Themes are "inherited" from a higher context , so if you set a category theme, it will be used by all courses in that category unless overridden in a course. You might also be interested in this plugin: https://moodle.org/plugins/block_theme_selector - it uses the setting for "Allow theme changes in the URL " which can also be found in Site Administration > Themes > Theme settings and allows any user to change the theme for a particular session, but only for their own view. See https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Theme_settings for more info.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alter Moodle Administrator
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Surya, There is a clear distinction between a site administrator and a user with a site level assigned role 'manager'. The first has access to all things site administration, including configuration, the latter only has access to users and courses, and some features that don't necessarily fall under 'configuration'. Theme changes are considered config changes. This means a user needs to have site administrator permission to change themes, if this applies to the entire site. If the theme changes only apply to a certain category, enabling category themes (Site admin > Appearance > Theme settings) would allow a user with a 'manager' role assigned at category level to change themes for a specific category.

ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, MySQL 5.7 is compat with 3.4. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Re: Is MySQL 5.7 compatible for Moodle 3.4?
ResponsesInList.Text: From the information/error in logs you shared, looks like an issue with your DB being overloaded with trying to manage session info. So here's some docs to look at: https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Session_handling https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/Sessions_FAQ Depending upon size of site and just how hard one wants to make admin of Moodle, try this to see if it doesn't make those errors go away in your logs: In config.php add a line just below the line that defines 'admin', like this: $CFG->dbsessions='0'; That turns logging sessions to the database.  Takes affect immediately.  No need to restart any services ... apache/httpd/nginx nor mysqld. Does login speed up?   See any more errors in server logs? Now for an admin level person ... your info about the session is larger ... thus larger sessions file. You should see in moodledata a 'sessions' directory and as folks login, a sessions file is created for them. To un-do ... just put // in front of that line you added. The original question asked if MySQL 5.7 was OK to use with Moodle 3.4.   It is. Now if you are still having issues, suggest installing and running MySQLTuner.   Could be you need to tweak DB settings. https://www.google.com/search?q=mysqltuner 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Error reading from database on upgrade to Moodle 3.7
ResponsesInList.Text: I am doing a beta upgrade of 3 instances of Moodle 3.4.latest to 3.7. To set all collations to utf8mb4, I did a dump of each database to a . sql file; did a search and replace for utf8 (to utf8mb4) and for _general_ci (to _unicode_ci). Then I imported the modified .sql file into a blank 3.7 database. The data folders were cloned as well and the config file was added to reflect each new instance. Two of the upgraded installations went flawlessly, but one encountered an error. Any ideas on what was different about this attempted upgrade? The error generated is cited below. ========== Debug info: Unknown column 'ctx.locked' in 'field list' SELECT bi.id, COALESCE(bp.id, bs.id) AS blockpositionid, bi.blockname, bi.parentcontextid, bi.showinsubcontexts, bi.pagetypepattern, bi.requiredbytheme, bi.subpagepattern, bi.defaultregion, bi.defaultweight, Stack trace: line 486 of /lib/dml/moodle_database.php: dml_read_exception thrown line 1184 of /lib/dml/mysqli_native_moodle_database.php: call to moodle_database->query_end() line 761 of /lib/blocklib.php: call to mysqli_native_moodle_database->get_recordset_sql() line 1499 of /lib/pagelib.php: call to block_manager->load_blocks() line 975 of /lib/pagelib.php: call to moodle_page->starting_output() line 1295 of /lib/outputrenderers.php: call to moodle_page->set_state() line 112 of /index.php: call to core_renderer->header()

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error reading from database on upgrade to Moodle 3.7
ResponsesInList.Text: " Any ideas on what was different about this attempted upgrade ?" Nope ... no Vulcan Mind Meld possible! but ... when you did the search and replace ... ' did a search and replace for utf8 (to utf8mb4) and for _general_ci (to _unicode_ci)' ... is that how you did it ... exactly? Reason asked ... if one searched for _general_ci and replaced with _unicode_ci that might hit tables that had utf8_general_ci. and they are now utf8_unicode_ci.   Character set might be a mix of utf8mb4 and utf8 In moodlecode/admin/cli/ there are some mysql scripts to help. ﻿ mysql_compressed_rows.php, mysql_collation.php, and mysql_engine.php All have help screens when issued with php nameofscript.php for options/switches. Run: php mysql_collation.php -l at the bottom of that scripts output a summary of tables ... Table collations summary for https:// server : utf8mb4_general_ci: 1453 All should match ... same collation. Can fix using same script with proper option. 'SoS'. Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re: Error reading from database on upgrade to Moodle 3.7
ResponsesInList.Text:
So from the error: 
```text
Debug info: Unknown column 'ctx.locked' in 'field list'
```
 locked is a new column added to the mdl_context table in Moodle 3.6. It should get added to the database as part of the upgrade process and if two out of three of the test upgrades were successful it suggests this is working correctly. What the upgrade process does is check the version in the database and if it's below the level of the new version applies any changes necessary. You could check the version of the 3.4 site that had this issue to see if it's the expected value, e.g.: 
```text
SELECT name, value FROM mdl_config WHERE name = 'version';


+---------+---------------+


| name    | value         |


+---------+---------------+


| version | 2017111301.01 |


+---------+---------------+
```
 and in version.php checking the $version line, e.g: 
```text
$version  = 2017111301.01;              // 20171113      = branching date YYYYMMDD - do not modify!
```
 These are example values from Moodle 3.4, yours should be similar starting "20171113".

ResponsesInList.Title: Submiting assignment on ba=ehalf of students
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there an option in Moodle for teachers to submit an assignment on behalf of their students. Not sure how to find out which version of Moodle I am using. Thanks. Emily

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Submiting assignment on ba=ehalf of students
ResponsesInList.Text: As the teacher, open that specific assignment. Then, click on the View All button. Ensure your filter is set so you can see the student (who you want to submit for on their behalf) in the list of students. Near their "grade" button you will see and "Edit" button - click on Edit to reveal more options - select the "Edit Submission" option. You will then see the submission box/text box from that student' point of view. Complete the submission by clicking the save/submit button.
