ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cron Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: In many years participating in these forums, don't think I've ever seen anyone report this very same thing ... even though a Google search hits on many similarly reported issues in other applications/situations.  Most of them, in looking them over, most appear to have solved their issue by updating GhostScript and or Imagemagik on their systems. No, I would not ignore it. See it's linux by the cron command and have a suggestion ... Re-direct the output of the cron job to a log where you might be able to see more information than what you get via email. Since it's linux, should be able to do this as root user: touch /var/log/moodle-cron.log Assuming your logs are kept in /var/log/ That creates a blank - empty - file. Then, in the cron job itself change the ending to redirect to the log. Change this: /usr/bin/php  /var/www/clients/client1/web1/web/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php >/dev/null to this /usr/bin/php  /var/www/clients/client1/web1/web/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php > /var/log/moodle-cron.log 2>&1 Since the cron job is supposed to run every minute now, one can 'watch' the moodle-cron.log file in realtime using: tail -f /var/log/moodle-cron.log To see what else might be going on. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Inactive but still accessible courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, Sure, what you're describing is most definitely possible, but with a few remarks: Active courses (visibility: Show, startdate before now, enddate after now or NULL) will be shown with the All or In progress filter in the Course overview block. Inactive courses (visibility: Show, enddate before now, course completion optionally set) will be shown with the All or Past filter in the Course overview block. Hidden courses (visibility: Hide) will only be shown to users who have a role in the course with the permission 'moodle/course:viewhiddencourses' set to Allowed. As long as a user remains enrolled in the course, he/she will have access to his/her materials and results. For courses with an enddate in the past, or that have been completed, these courses should be read only.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Inactive but still accessible courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rachel, Context freezing is still an experimental feature that needs further elaboration. On a production site, I would try to avoid even thinking about the option, until it is no longer experimental. If you do want to freeze a course context, it is frozen for all users enrolled in it (as far as I know). This would not really be a useful option, in my opinion. In the situation where you run the same course various times a year, with another set of active participants, you could consider the following: create a 'master version' of the course duplicate the master version for every time you're running the course manage any changes that may occur in the master version, so the latest iteration of the course is always available to the newest group starting the course enrol a new group of participants in the latest copy of the master version apply an end date that suits the period these participants will be in the course This way, all users only have 1 course in their Course Overview on their Dashboard: the one they were enrolled in. This course automatically moves from In progress to Past, when the end date has passed. If, for some reason, your Moodle instance is restricted in terms of size and storage, and these restrictions prevent the above mentioned, use Course completion criteria instead of the end date to have the course marked as completed (and moved to Past) for those groups of participants who have successfully completed the course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Customizing Default Profile Page
ResponsesInList.Text: There’s a common misconception that the default profile page shows all information that displays on the profile page which you can then edit and/or change the layout. The reality is that you can add additional blocks onto the default profile page, and those blocks can be added to the left, right or middle of the page. But it does NOT allow you to remove or change the following blocks, or to change the layout/order of these blocks: User details Privacy and policies Course Details Miscellaneous Reports Login activity Mobile app (only displays if Mobile web services are configured) These are all ‘fake’ blocks and cannot be removed through the normal blocks administration interface. So, your screenshot is showing as expected. Click on the top right button - “Blocks editing on” - and you will be able to add blocks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle integration with ECHO 360
ResponsesInList.Text: Given that Moodle does not have a "roll over" function, what are you doing at the end of the semester? I believe that Echo360 uses the course id to link the course to the relevant videos. So, if you backup and restore you will have a different ID and the links will be gone. It seems that the reasonable solution is to take a backup for archive purposes but to just 'reset' your live courses so that the ID does not change.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle integration with ECHO 360
ResponsesInList.Text: This is definitely not a practical solution for us. This would remove all logs of student activity, and student assignments and related grades would have to be cleared out each time (which also means marking of all student assignments and grading/regrading would need to be finalised before rollover). It would provide no record of teaching activity for audit purposes, and it also removes the opportunity to record what teaching content was provided to what students at a given point in time (eg in case of complaint by a student), and requires staff to request restore of archived pages in order to access materials they may wish to refer to or reuse. It would also mean that students are denied the opportunity to revisit previous learning materials for revision purposes, so only ever see a year’s worth of course content etc. My suggestion would be to add a checkbox during restore that allows the user to specify whether existing links should be restored or not. If Echo uses the course id, then perhaps this course id could be copied to a new field in the mbz file for Echo link purposes, eg 'originalechocourseid' Thanks

You need the Configurable Reports block - https://moodle.org/plugins/block_configurable_reports - see screenshot for similar report created with this plugin: The sql for the above report is... 
```text
SELECT

CONCAT('
', u.firstname ,'
')

AS 'First Name',

CONCAT('
', u.lastname ,'
')

AS 'Surname',

CONCAT('
', c.fullname ,'
')

AS 'Course',

DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME
(p.timecompleted),'
%Y%m%d
 
%d %M %Y
')
AS 'Completion Date',

DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME
(u.timecreated),'
%Y%m%d
 
%d %M %Y
')
AS 'User Created'

FROM
    prefix_course_completions AS p

JOIN
    prefix_course AS c ON p.course = c.id

JOIN
    prefix_user AS u ON p.userid = u.id

WHERE
    c.enablecompletion = 1

AND
    p.timecompleted > 0

%%FILTER_COURSES:p.course%%
%%FILTER_USERS:u.lastname%%
%%FILTER_STARTTIME:p.timecompleted:>%%
%%FILTER_ENDTIME:p.timecompleted:<%% 

ORDER BY

    p.timecompleted DESC
```

ResponsesInList.Title: My Moodle site redirects to 127.0.0.1! (Moodle 3.6.3)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, I have a Moodle website hosted at my house using XAMPP. I port forwarded port 80 (TCP), and tried to connect to my website from a different network using my external IP Address (my Moodle site is located at C:\XAMPP\htdocs\start\moodle). I tried typing in [IP Address]/start/moodle, but instead of connecting, it redirected me to 127.0.0.1/start/moodle. Any ideas on why this might be happening? Thanks, xHyperSource.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: My Moodle site redirects to 127.0.0.1! (Moodle 3.6.3)
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle will only allow itself to be accessed using the address defined in $CFG-> wwwroot . Presumably you have this set to http://127.0.0.1/start/moodle , so trying to access the site via your external IP instead will result in a redirect.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: My Moodle site redirects to 127.0.0.1! (Moodle 3.6.3)
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you! I'm pretty sure this fixed my problem. I'm kind of new with Moodle so... Also one more question, is there a way to make my moodle site accessible from both 127.0.0.1 and using my public IP address (other than hosting it somewhere else)?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: My Moodle site redirects to 127.0.0.1! (Moodle 3.6.3)
ResponsesInList.Text: Not exactly, but you can make it accessible from both inside and outside your network. The simplest way would be to sign up for a Dynamic DNS service like afraid.org . This will give you a domain name (e.g. mymoodlesite.afraid.org) that always points to your public IP address, even when your IP address is changed by your ISP. Set your $CFG->wwwroot to use this domain name in place of your IP address. Then, on your machine, add a rule to your hosts file to point mymoodlesite.afraid.org to 127.0.0.1. This means that when you go to that domain name on your machine, it will go to your local IP address, but on any other machine it will go to your public IP address. In either case, Moodle will see that you're accessing it at the configured domain name, so it will be happy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM pass grade working with Moodle to obtain certificate
ResponsesInList.Text: Ruth, et al., Ruth's screenshot looks like it is from Articulate Storyline, which is the content authoring program I'm most familiar with. I'll give several observations here (based on my understanding of how SCORM works with Moodle.): The setting shown on the screenshot indicates SCORM will send back "Passed" or "Incomplete" to Moodle. This value will be stored in the database table, mdl_scorm_scoes_track, field cmi.core.lesson_status. The value returned to Moodle is determined by settings in the Articulate Tracking settings (a config page not shown in Ruth's screenshot).  If Tracking is on the number of slides viewed, then Passed or Incomplete is returned based on the number of slides viewed, and the numeric value stored in the Moodle grade book is 1 ((Passed) or 0 (Incomplete). If Tracking is based by a score in a SCORM test, then the raw score of the test is also passed to Moodle and placed in the grade book instead of a 0 or 1. I would have to look through your SCORM settings, your SCORM package and grade book to give a definitive answer. But, here are some things to look at: What is the maximum score on the test/quiz in the SCORM package?  Also, which Articulate Result Slide is reporting the score? Are you using the correct Result Slide? What does your grade book show as the maximum possible score for the SCORM activity? Are you confusing raw score with percentage score in your Moodle settings? If the maximum raw score on the quiz is 25 points and the user received 20 points, then that is 80%. The more I think about your problem, I believe it is related to this. I hope this helps. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Change meta tag robots
ResponsesInList.Text:
Go to Site Administration > Security > Site security settings and check the setting for “ Allow indexing by search engines ”. This determines whether to allow search engines to index your site. "Everywhere" will allow the search engines to search everywhere including login and signup pages, which means sites with Force Login turned on are still indexed. To avoid the risk of spam involved with the signup page being searchable, use "Everywhere except login and signup pages". "Nowhere" will tell search engines not to index any page. Note this is only a tag in the header of the site. It is up to the search engine to respect
the tag.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automated course backups only occur every second day, not nightly
ResponsesInList.Text: First, any hashnamed directory you find in moodledata/temp/backup/ could be removed manually without any ill affects.  If you find a .mbz file in one of them, it's probably a valid backup that you can 'move' out to another location. If you were on linux, one could actually watch what was going on in there with a linux "watch" command and I do that from time to time on one troubled server to see what's going on. Trouble with removing those contenthash directories is only when Moodle is trying to use one.  So to manually clean it out, turn off Automated backups for a little while and manually remove. How many courses do you have? Of the backups you do have, which courses are the largest (have the largest .mbz file)? Do you have any idea as to how long backing up all courses would take? Those questions ... possibly extended below ... (*) Course ID 1 is the front page of Moodle.   It is a 'course' and the reason you get thrown to your profile/landing page using the URL for the course id 1 is the way it should behave. One can see in your screen shot of Last Execution, the front page backup scheduled for 31 Dec. ... while you don't see years there, would assume that means 2018 ... ie, this year. Unfortunately, autobackups doesn't have a options to exclude course ID's in it's configuration.  As long as you have automated backups turned on and scheduled to run, course ID 1 will be included (cannot hide front page) .... and will always be the largest course in terms of the logs.xml you found. Until this is reported as a bug ... and someone at Moodle HQ takes a look at it ... status quo will be the same. Alternative work-around for now? ... suggestion and below is brief description of what I've had to do with one K12 site. * there is a script in code/admin/cli/ that will backup a single course ... backup.php.   On one site I admin there is a team taught multimedia course whose basic content contains 60 Gig ... without students and student work.   As course is used every academic year, it grows depending upon the number of students enrolled and I have seen it as high as 130Gig. It's that one course that always kills autobackups.   So to 'work around' that, I have created two bash shell scripts that run through a list of course ID's ... largecids.txt is a list of course ID's whose base is 30Gig plus.  The 'largecoursesbu' bash shell runs backups on those courses via the admin/cli/backup.php script only on a weekend beginning early Sunday AM. The other bash shell script I have runs though a course ID list of all other courses excluding the large ones and runs more frequently through out the week. Autobackups config is set to manual - ie, run from command line. Autobackups task is turned off but the clean up is checked/set not to kick in when running cron jobs out side of Moodle to backup courses. NOT ideal ... not perfect ... but suffices for the site. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automated course backups only occur every second day, not nightly
ResponsesInList.Text: One more thing .... you've shared the autobackup settings for your site.   Have you reviewed/read what those options do and decided if an option 'fits' your goal or not? LIke number of backups to keep ... and maximum number of backups to keep.   If saving to both filedir and to a designated directory, check the designated directory for backup files ... are all 1000 courses there? ﻿ There are 3 tables related to backups. mdl_backup_controlers - this table is updated on each course backup. mdl_backup_courses - this tracks courseid, laststarttime,lastendtime,laststatus,nextstartime. If laststatus is 0 then backup failed. query the mdl_backup_courses table to see how many have 'laststatus=0' Those might be your problem courses ... for whatever reason. If the scheduling is off ... messed up ... one might have to truncate mdl_backup_courses ... leave the table and it's columns, just remove all data ... to get a better idea of problem courses ... and regain 'crontrol' over automated backups.  Since that's the tracker truncating that table means moodle has no knowledge of automated backups ever having been run and thus, all courses might be backed up. I had to do that with the mdl 3.1 site I mentioned in previous post. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Localhost works Remote FQDN does not (Moodle 3.6.3)
ResponsesInList.Text: I just finished installing Moodle 3.6.3, on my iis server I am able to go to http://localhost or http://moodle and get to the starting page.  When I try to go to http://moodle on a remote computer it will not load the page.  I checked DNS and it resolves to the correct IP, I checked the firewall on the IIS server and it's not blocking port 80, I added http://moodle to the iis bindings.  It's feeling like a Moodle/php setting but I'm not sure where to look.  Any ideas?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Localhost works Remote FQDN does not (Moodle 3.6.3)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Check the IIS logs to see if the request is being received. These are in C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles\W3SVC ? (where ? is the IIS site number). For my test site, here's Firefox requesting the site home page ("GET /") and getting a "200" (i.e. OK) response: 
```text
2019-05-09 14:41:02 10.0.2.15 GET / - 80 - 10.0.2.15 Mozilla/5.0+(Windows+NT+10.0;+WOW64;+rv:66.0)+Gecko/20100101+Firefox/66.0 - 200 0 0 9765
```
 The client and server IP addresses are the same (10.0.2.15) because the browser is on the same server as IIS. If the request isn't listed then it's a server or networking issue, not a Moodle issue. You could try telnetting from the client to the IIS server to confirm this can connect on port 80, e.g. 
```text
C:\>telnet moodle 80
```
 (You may need to install the standard Telnet client). If this fails then something is blocking the connection. Your browser may be using a proxy server so it may be the proxy that is unable to resolve the name or connect to port 80.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Change Online User Minutes to Hours
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't know. However, you could use custom SQL .  In my own case, I use the Configurable Reports add in for custom SQL (there are other plug-ins, too.).  Here is the SQL that I run to see students who have logged into my Moodle in the last hour.  Of course, one could easily modify this to any time. # Shows users logged IN LAST hour SELECT firstname, lastname, from_unixtime(lastaccess) AS LastClick, timediff(curtime(),time(from_unixtime(lastaccess))) AS LastAccess FROM prefix_user HAVING LastClick > now()-interval 60 MINUTE ORDER BY lastaccess ASC

ResponsesInList.Text: Does anyone have experience working with Pearson (Education) regarding course design/curriculum development?

ResponsesInList.Text: I have worked with them in the past. Dave

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Pearson (Education)
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for your reply, Dave... How do you find some of their products particularly the MyLab feature...?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Pearson (Education)
ResponsesInList.Text: Jonathan, I can give you my perspective about some of these publisher's web offerings.  I have seen, and have used a few, of these products, in particular, McGraw-Hill, Pearson, and Cengage. The subtle thing about these publisher products is that they seem to be competing, in a subtle way, with LMSs!  As one digs into what they offer, some will provide the ability for you to create content pages, quizzes, and assignments.  Doesn't this sound like what Moodle, Blackboard, D2L, and Canvas do?  However, it appears that the publishers are not aggressively trying to replace a school's LMS, they are trying to get paid "per student."  From what I have seen, a student needs to spend maybe $35 to $50 for the "key," or be forced to buy a new textbook that comes with the key.  New textbooks can cost as much as $250 more than used textbooks.  So publishers are willing to make their money in a different way. Some of these products can be configured to seamlessly connect to an LMS, often avoiding a double login.  Kind of nice. But, what can these products do that the LMS cannot do?  Well, some LMSs have poor "quiz engines."  So, using the publisher's website can be a plus!  This is what I would probably do if I had to use my school's Canvas product.  But Moodle's quiz engine is great.  So I get test banks from the publisher and import them into my course. Some publisher products provide PowerPoints.  But I prefer to create my own PowerPoints, sometimes using what the publisher provides, modifying them, and posting them on my Moodle. Some publisher products provide online textbooks, sometimes crosslinked to quiz questions.  Yep, maybe a nice feature.  But I often wonder if this makes it too easy for students to "get the correct answer" instead of "learning."  So I am neutral about this feature. Some publisher products provide a grade book.  Well, Moodle's grade book is much more powerful than any of these publisher grade books.  However, some LMSs have weak grade books, so the publisher's grade books can compete with these other LMSs. So, I have not been convinced to go the publisher website route, yet.  Simply using Moodle provides me a better educational delivery method.  And there is no extra cost to the student for using Moodle.  Students can buy the textbook from a variety of places, and if they search a little, at a dramatically lower cost. Maybe some of what I have said will provide opportunity for others to think, and post.  I am always open to other ideas and perspectives.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Change front-page of Adaptable theme.
ResponsesInList.Text:
I would create a child theme based on Adaptable. https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Creating_a_theme_based_on_boost Within your child theme you will be able to create a layout (in the layout folder) as below - my theme is called ld35: Then in your theme's config.php file make this the frontpage layout: 
```text
$THEME->layouts = [


    // The site home page.


    'frontpage' => array(


        'file' => 'frontpage.php',


        'regions' => array('side-pre', 'side-post'),


        'defaultregion' => 'side-pre',


        'options' => array('nonavbar' => false),


    ),
```
 Hope this makes sense, Dave

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site News and Announcement Emails Not Being Sent
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there I just resolved this issue for my site.  I used this post from 2009 in doing so! https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=119704#p524928 All the email settings and subscription settings were fine on our site.  (Previously I'd had problems with automatic emails caused by * see below!) ResponsesInList.Title: Video Player plugin - Moodle 3.5 Boost theme
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello All, My company will be streaming videos from the MS Stream service. I can add a URL resource to my course and link to the video. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Video Player plugin - Moodle 3.5 Boost theme
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, The simplest (but not the fastest) way to add your Microsoft Stream video in Moodle would be to use the embed code provided somewhere on the video page and paste it in a piece of HTML somewhere in Moodle (in a label or a web page for instance). If the text editor in Moodle doesn't strip your HTML code, that should work flawlessly. Another option would be to get a URL pointing to an mp4 version of your Stream video (I don't know if Stream allows that). In this case, just pasting this link in Moodle (using the URL resource or in a piece of text) will embed the video thanks to the multimedia filters of Moodle. A third possibility would be to create a custom filter which would automatically convert a Stream video URL into an embed code. This would require some development. I haven't used the Generico plugin but it could help in this endeavor: https://moodle.org/plugins/filter_generico Otherwise here the doc from MS about embedding a Stream video thanks to oEmbed: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/stream/embed-video-oembed Cheers!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Video Player plugin - Moodle 3.5 Boost theme
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, It is very easy to add videos using the built-in Atto text editor in Moodle. In fact you used virtually the same editor to write this post! Add either a Label or Page resource to your course In the Content section, click on the Insert or edit an audio/video file icon in the toolbar Click on the video tab Copy and paste the URL to your video into the URL field Click save to close dialog box Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Save and and Display Voila! You should see your video in all its glory. I highly recommend that you watch this video to learn all you can do with the Atto editor

Generally Moodle uses filters to display videos in videojs. So it sees a link to something that looks like a video, and it tries to turn it into a video player. ResponsesInList.Title: Remove "Anyone in the world" from blog posts?
ResponsesInList.Text: Using Moodle v3.6, and boost theme. However, I have tried other themes, and get the same thing. The words "Anyone in the world" are appearing in blog posts. Is there any way to remove this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove "Anyone in the world" from blog posts?
ResponsesInList.Text:
When you create a blog post you can set a privacy level, ie. who may see the entry. There are three options: Yourself ie. your blog entry is a draft Anyone on your site Anyone in the world If you want to hide it, you can add this to your custom CSS : 
```text
.blog_entry .audience {display: none;}
```
 Remember though, that if you do hide it and you're using different privacy levels for different posts, it will be very difficult to know who can see what.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Submissions Time Stamp Issue

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Submissions Time Stamp Issue

Everytime you submitted to the assignment, a new log entry was added to the logs, so you should be able to make your case.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upload users + htmleditor
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, The htmleditor setting is a preference and is NOT kept in the mdl_user table of your Moodle database, which is why the CSV file does not support changing the htmleditor. Instead, the editor preference is kept in the mdl_user_preferences table of your Moodle database. @Tim - Since you say you do not have access to the database, are you able to install plugins? If so, install the adminer plugin, and use it to get to the table. If you can get adminer installed, you can use it to export JUST the mdl_user_preferences table of your Moodle database as an SQL file. Also use adminer to look for and get the id number for the '500' users you want to change. Edit the exported mdl_user_preferences sql file and add a row for each of  the 500 users with the preference set to atto. Import your altered file. When those users next edit something, the editor will be atto. I have tested this and it works. Note: I used a copy of the original exported file, so I could put the table back like it WAS, if things went haywire! I used LibreOffice and copied and pasted as "text" to get the correct format. When adding the new entries to the end of the sql file, make sure that the original last row ends with a comma, along with each new row, and your new last row ends with a semi colon. Make sure each new line has a unique, one digit greater, id number. Import your new file with adminer and verify your results are correct. Another note: When I was making my new rows, I did it in LO Calc so I could use the drag and copy function to auto increment my new row numbers and user id's. Just had to make sure the first row was set to the correct beginning numbers. HTH AL

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hiding Dashboard Blocks based on roles
ResponsesInList.Text: HI - Since the dashboard is not in the context of a course, removing the "student" or "teacher" view capability will work here. Instead, you need to make a Mask! Basically: You'll make a new role that is applied at the block= level. It wont' have to have any permissions set (just 3 removed). Then place all of your teachers in it and on your Dashboard set up page / reset the dashboard, and then you're all set. Create Mask 1. Site Admin - Users - Permissions - Define Roles 2. Click Add a New Role 3. Choose 'No Role' as the arch type 4. Give it a name (ie. Dashboard Mask) 5. Check off  "Block" context 6. Leave everything else as "not set" and scroll down to the bottom of the page where you see the "Block" section: Change the following three permissions to "Prohibit": "Edit a Block's settings" "View Block" "Manage Blocks on a Page" 8. Click save changes. Apply the Mask 1. Site Admin - Appearance - Default Dashboard page 2. Click "Blocks Editing On" 3. In the Course Overview Block, click the Cog and select "Assign Roles" 4. You'll see your Daskboard Mask listed and a '0' - click on "Dashboard Mask" 5. Add all of your staff to it ( you will just have to maintain this as you get new staff members ) 7. Navigate back to Site Admin - Appearance - Default Dashboard page 8. Click "Reset Dashboard for all users" This works for me on Moodle 3.4

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hide Navigation bar (Front Page)
ResponsesInList.Text: HI Big Picture, I think you're looking in the wrong place to solve your problem. It is a default feature of Moodle to force users to log in to the LMS and show a login page that has no top bar in Boost. There's no need to hack in any code or change an SCSS preset. Instead, give this a go: Open Site administration > Security > Site security settings and look for the setting labeled 'Force users to log in'. Tick the box and save settings Check in another browser to see what the result is when going to your LMS's main URL . You'll see the user has no other option than to log in, and that there's no top bar on that log in page. If you're unsure about this, have a look at the corresponding Moodle Docs : https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Site_security_settings#Force_users_to_login

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Which SQL Table captures Course Activity Reports in Moodle Database?
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, here is the one that I developed.  See if you understand it.  I don't guarantee that it will work for you.  Also, it doesn't do anything about "groups," but maybe you can figure this portion out for yourself. SELECT      ls.ip, from_unixtime(ls.timecreated, "%W, %M %d, %Y, %h:%i:%s %p") AS ActivityDate, NULL AS DueDate, m.name AS TYPE, q.name AS Activity, NULL AS ItemGrade, qa.sumgrades AS Grade, q.sumgrades AS MaxGrade, cm.course, cm.section AS Topic_Number, cm.id AS Act_ID, cm.module AS Act_Number, ls.userid AS User_ID, NULL AS Itemlink, cm.instance, cm.visible, cm.completion FROM mdl_course_modules cm JOIN mdl_modules m ON m.id = cm.module JOIN mdl_logstore_standard_log ls ON ls.contextinstanceid = cm.id JOIN mdl_quiz q ON q.id = cm.instance JOIN mdl_quiz_attempts qa ON qa.id = ls.objectid WHERE ls.courseid = 44 AND cm.visible = 1 AND ls.userid = 1364 AND ls.action = "submitted" AND cm.module = 16 ORDER BY cm.module, cm.section, cm.id, ls.timecreated

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2 web server(general & cbt only) ,  1 database
ResponsesInList.Text:
Yes, it is possible. You can install moodle on 2 web server, and pointing both of them to single database server Just adjust file config.php 
```text
$CFG->dbhost    = 'localhost'; //
```
 You should change it to IP:3306 like : 192.168.1.5:3306, and make sure that your database configuration allow remote access from your web servers. The other thing that you have to adjust is line 
```text
$CFG->
dataroot
  = '/home/disk/moodledata';
```
 Like database, all your web server have to pointing into one moodle data directory. You can use NFS - for example - to mount one storage server into both web server. For both web server, it should use two identical version of Moodle. You can do it manually (install it one by one), or you can use something like rsync. Regard Reza Ervani Sekolah Terbuka Rumah Ilmu Indonesia

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Transfer hosting of Moodle site from MoodleCloud to SiteGround - Restore Issues of MoodleCloud Site Export
ResponsesInList.Text: It's likely to be something to do with the database version and/or collation. 767 bytes is the stated prefix limitation for InnoDB tables in MySQL version 5.6 (and prior versions). In MySQL version 5.7 and upwards this limit has been increased to 3072 bytes. MoodleCloud will almost certainly be running using utf8mb4_unicode_ci collation. See https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/MySQL_full_unicode_support

ResponsesInList.Title: Creating multiple users per department
ResponsesInList.Text: We have many departments and would like tocreate users and include the department and job they have to be able to offer specific courses to specific job titles and or departments. I would like to know what would be the best way to go about this when uploading the file and if it's possible to alert users per job title. Moodle 3.6.3 (Build: 20190311)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating multiple users per department
ResponsesInList.Text: As usual, there is more than one way to skin this particular cat, or quaff this brew or whatever old saying you prefer. The common theme here is your user upload file . You can set it up to assign anyone to Roles or courses as you please and change it by editing the original file, e.g. add in a delete column and give it a value of 1, if completed or 0 if continuing or enrolling. You can even change Roles by editing the csv file and so on. Each of the links below go to specific Moodle Docs , which might help you gain a better understanding of how you can achieve what you want and should open in a new page. 1. Create separate Roles for each different job title and/or department. This will eventually become so clunky and likely unmanageable so be prepared for a lot of extra work. 2. Create separate Categories. Assign people according to the Categories . Much more manageable even if this means you have to duplicate courses. 3. Use meta course links . Create child courses for individuals and assign each child course to the required meta course. 4. A simpler method of all these options may be Cohorts . I am sure others will be able to add more information here too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP
ResponsesInList.Text: What have you got for User attribute (on the LDAP server settings page). For AD this should normally be sAMAccountName (the NT4-style username without the DOMAIN \ prefix) or userPrincipalName (the Win2000-style username, e.g. username@domain.ext ). When a user attempts to log into Moodle, if LDAP authenticates them Moodle will create a new account if one doesn't already exist. There's no need to create LDAP users in Moodle. So if the site can connect to the LDAP server double check the LDAP server settings page in Moodle against the documentation . Contexts is another value to check, the AD users that you're giving access to must be in one of the LDAP contexts specified here. When set up correctly you should be able to log into Moodle using the AD username (which will depend on the User attribute as explained above) and the AD password. For future reference: there's a forum specifically for authentication questions such as LDAP.

ResponsesInList.Title: Self Hosting Questions & Advice
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have read all the info on Moodle's website, and searched the forums for specific information, and while I found most of what I was looking for, there are still a couple of gaps. I assume things like operating system and browser requirements are just as per our normal site where we're hosting it. A few things I want to confirm: 1. Will I still be able to create learning pathways to direct users through the courses I need them to complete? 2. As we're self hosting, no-one else will be able to see the content 3. It's not mobile enabled, so learners would need to complete the learning on a laptop/desktop 4. There's no tech support - you are responsible for downloading the latest version whenever there are bug fixes, etc. And now for my questions: 1. Does the learner get a personalised dashboard ? 2. Is the design customisable? 3. Can I include the quiz functionality? 4. Is gamification an included feature? 5. Are surveys an included feature? 6. Can I upload a SCORM package that I've created on something like Articulate? 7. Will results will be stored, and can I run reports? 8. If, at some point in the future, I wanted to take the content from Moodle to another LMS, can I export as SCORM from the locally hosted version? 9. Is there support for languages other than English? Sorry if I'm recovering basics, but I just couldn't seem to find the clear answers that I need to present the solution to my superiors. All help and advice appreciated!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Self Hosting Questions & Advice
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi I don't buy that you've "read all the info on Moodle's website" For one it is immense. And then some of the most basic questions wouldn't have appeared in your list. But don't worry, we all were there. Going through your questions I can say that you are looking at the right thing: an application for web-based teaching, either as e-learning (100% on-line) or blended learning (on-line and face-to-face mixed), for a closed group. As a bonus, the product is Free Software https://docs.moodle.org/dev/License and will run on fully Free and Open Source software chain. But you must understand that Moodle is not tailor-made for you. So it will not be a 100% fit. You need imagination and have to put an effort to make Moodle does what you want. In my opinion is definitely worth looking at.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Self Hosting Questions & Advice
ResponsesInList.Text: For the things you want to confirm: 1. Will I still be able to create learning pathways to direct users through the courses I need them to complete? Yes. See https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Learning_plans 2. As we're self hosting, no-one else will be able to see the content Access to your site is entirely under your control. 3. It's not mobile enabled, so learners would need to complete the learning on a laptop/desktop The standard Moodle Themes are responsive and work well on mobile devices. So do many of the third party plugins themes. There is also a generic Moodle mobile app which works out of the box with the latest versions of Moodle. You do need https enabled though. Your IT team and/or people in these f orums will be able to advise you further. 4. There's no tech support - you are responsible for downloading the latest version whenever there are bug fixes, etc. Help can be given on a voluntary basis by members of these forums, many of whom have been using Moodle for a very long time and have lots of experience with the software. That said, “support” normally means a priority response service, and the forums cannot give you that. You can also engage with a Moodle Partner for more formal arrangement. For your questions: 1. Does the learner get a personalised dashboard ? Yes 2. Is the design customisable? Yes, but very dependent on the theme you are using and your willingness to learn. 3. Can I include the quiz functionality? Already included. 4. Is gamification an included feature? There are elements of gamification, and plugins that extend that. 5. Are surveys an included feature? There is a Feedback activity for surveys and evaluations, etc. You will also see a Survey activity, but that’s about assessing and stimulating learning in online environments. 6. Can I upload a SCORM package that I've created on something like Articulate? Yes - see https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/SCORM_FAQ 7. Will results will be stored, and can I run reports? Yes 8. If, at some point in the future, I wanted to take the content from Moodle to another LMS, can I export as SCORM from the locally hosted version? You can export user and course data, but not in a SCORM format. 9. Is there support for languages other than English? Yes - but there are two aspects to this: the language of Moodle and the language of the content - see https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Language

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Self Hosting Questions & Advice

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Self Hosting Questions & Advice
ResponsesInList.Text: Jon provided excellent accurate responses to your questions.  Thanks, Jon.  I'll add a few comments. You can export entire courses and import them into another Moodle site. You can also export many course activities as IMS Common Cartridges and import them into any LMS that supports IMS. -Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Permission to View Suspended Students?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi ben - when you say the teacher cannot see the suspended students, do you mean 'inactive' students? Meaning, if you go to a course's Participants page, is the student(s) in question listed as 'inactive'? If so, have the teacher go to their course's gradebook or gradebook setup page. Then, in the admin block click on "setup" so it toggles open, and click the "Preferences: grader report" link Then, at the bottom of that preferences page, ensure the "show only active enrollments" dropdown is set to 'yes' Having this set to "yes" should enable any teacher to see the grades and submitted work of students who are inactive in the class. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.6.2 - Ip address
ResponsesInList.Text: Suggest changing the approach. Configure the virtualized LAMP Moodle server configured with a FQDN ... something like mymoodle.somenet.net.  In the VB config of the that instance ... set DHCP as one would normally. Use your workstations host file to map a 10. to the FQDN of mymoodle.somenet.net.   If the workstation is a laptop and you carry it back and forth to work makes no difference then what IP address the server gets if using the host file map 10.x.x.x or 192.168..x.x ... all map to the FQDN mymoodle.somenet.net. To make a line in-active in /etc/hosts just add # in front. To activate a mapping line remove the #. Moodle config file does not change and there is no need to run search and replace for all the internal links that moodle might have recorded using IP addresses. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SMTP error

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best content management practices
ResponsesInList.Text: Interesting question about tracking versions. Okay, so let's stick with this PowerPoint file example, call it PPT01.  PPT01 is created on my Mac.  However, it is in a folder that is defined as a "web site" to Dreamweaver.  At the click of a button in Dreamweaver, Dreamweaver synchronizes everything from this "site" (which is simply a folder on my Mac) with my production server.  So my process is edit PPT01, then synchronize with Dreamweaver. Only one copy of PPT01 is on my website.  Correct, no version control on my server (so to speak.) But, let's return to this file on my Mac.  My Mac always has a USB external drive hooked to it.  On my Mac, I am running TimeMachine, a very easy yet very effective way to back up a Mac.  TimeMachine has backup logic that makes incremental copies several times an hour, then several hours of the day, then several days of the month, etc.  It also has some logic to clean up excessive backups.  So, PPT01 is being watched, and backup up by TimeMachine.  For example, right now, this USB drive (it's a 3.5TB drive) has around 105 backups dating back to 2/22/2017. So, if I ever need to go back to an earlier version of PPT01, I do it using TimeMachine.  It's easy to step backward and restore an earlier version of PPT01.  TimeMachine is even smart enough to ask "Do you want to replace your current file or keep both."  In my many years of working with computers, both PCs and Macs, TimeMachine has been one of the most effective backup solutions. I run my own small moodle, around 12 courses per year, 500 students per year.  I don't know what I would do if I were running a university moodle. Obrigado, for your offer to provide a tour for me on my next visit to Portugal.

ResponsesInList.Title: Graded Activities (SQL Query)
ResponsesInList.Text: Is it possible to get all graded activities in a course using SQL query, where I want to display module id and module name (not module type). I tried : SELECT gi.courseid, cm.id AS "moduleid", gi.itemname AS "modulename", gi.itemtype AS "type" FROM mdl_grade_items gi LEFT JOIN mdl_course_modules cm ON cm.course = gi.courseid WHERE gi.itemtype = "mod" AND cm.deletioninprogress=0 AND cm.course=3 GROUP BY cm.id The query shows all the activities in a course, where I need only graded activities. Appreciate your help!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Graded Activities (SQL Query)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Does this work for you? 
```text
SELECT gi.courseid, cm.id AS moduleid, gi.itemname AS modulename, gi.itemtype AS type


  FROM mdl_grade_items gi


    INNER JOIN mdl_course_modules cm ON cm.course = gi.courseid AND cm.instance = gi.iteminstance


    INNER JOIN mdl_modules md ON cm.module = md.id AND md.name = gi.itemmodule


    WHERE gi.itemtype = 'mod' AND cm.deletioninprogress = 0 AND cm.course = 3;
```

ResponsesInList.Text: I have been working on some of this, trying to duplicate what is in the complete report, but with more detail.  I have found that I have to create a query for each kind of activity.  My code below is only for a student in a course (you should see this), and it is only for "Assignments."  I have more complete code, but it is work-in-progress.  I wanted to share this code just to bring in a slightly different perspective. SELECT ls.userid, ls.ip, from_unixtime(ls.timecreated, "%W, %M %d, %Y, %h:%i:%s %p") AS ActivityDate, from_unixtime(a.duedate, "%W, %M %d, %Y, %h:%i:%s %p") AS duedate, m.name AS TYPE, a.name AS Activity, NULL AS ItemGrade, ag.grade, a.grade AS MaxGrade, cm.course, cm.section AS Topic_Number, cm.id AS Act_ID, cm.module AS Act_Number, ls.userid AS User_ID, NULL AS Itemlink, cm.instance, cm.visible, cm.completion FROM mdl_course_modules cm JOIN mdl_modules m ON m.id = cm.module JOIN mdl_assign a ON a.id = cm.instance JOIN mdl_assign_grades ag ON a.id = ag.assignment JOIN mdl_logstore_standard_log ls ON ls.contextinstanceid = cm.id AND ls.userid = ag.userid WHERE cm.visible = 1 AND cm.module = 1 AND ls.action = "submitted" AND ls.component = 'mod_assign' AND cm.course = 44 AND ag.userid = 1364 ORDER BY cm.module, cm.section, cm.id, ls.timecreated

ResponsesInList.Title: Ats.: Message errors in moodle 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I found the answer. The problem was with database . The user who was not able to see his messages was involved in the conversation with a user who had ID equal to -10 in the table "message_conversation_members". I have checked the conversations table "message_conversations" and found the conversation with the same ID which was pointed as "conversationid" in the conversation with user with ID = -10. I tried to change the user ID to positive number in the table "message_conversation_members" for that conversation. I used the ID user who was not able to see his messages. The exception message disappeared  and the user started seeing his messages. However, I have also checked if there is a such message with the same "conversationid" in the table "messages". There were no such message. It seems that for a some reason (for internet connection disappearance) the right message was not written into the table "messages" and the user ID -10 was written into the table "message_conversation_members". This became a critical exception for the new version of Moodle. I don't know would be this a problem for an earlier version of Moodle, but for the 3.6.2 version it became totally. By the way, I have also checked the table "message_conversation_members" and found more 9 records with the user ID lower than 0. It was the same number -10. And there were no messages in the table "messages" with the same conversation ID which was used in the record with user ID -10 in the table "message_conversation_members". Therefore, I deleted all these records from tables "message_conversation_members" and "message_conversations". I hope the problem was solved or on the future I will know what to do. However, there is another table "message" in the database of Moodle. I don't know yet when this table and its records are used, but I found much more records (about 5K) with user ID -10 in this table. All messages which the user of my case had in the system were recorded in the table "messages". So, who knows where the problem arise with these records in the table "message". I hope that my explanation of my situation will help someone who get the same problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ats.: Re: Ats.: Re: Ats.: Message errors in moodle 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I don't know if there are any official fixes. I had not found anything more than this forum post by Phuong Hoang when I was trying to fix the problem. Later I have just stopped searching as I managed to fix the problem. For me worked this method: I opened the Moodle database through phpMyadmin and opened the table "message_conversation_members" (of course there is the prefix "mdl" or etc. in the title). I searched for the records with user ID lover than 0 (< 0) in this table. I found 9 records. All they had the same number -10 in the field "userid". I opened another browser window with Moodle database and opened the table "message_conversations". I searched and deleted step by step all the records with conversation ID which I found in all these 9 records in the table "message_conversation_members". In this table the conversation ID is in the field just "id". I opened the third window (however it may be the same of the step 4) with Moodle database and opened the table "message_conversation_members" again. Now I had two windows with the same table. This time I searched and deleted step by step all the records with conversation ID which I found in all these 9 records earlier in another browser window. Each time I found two records with the same conversation ID in the field "conversationid". One was with a normal user ID, one was with a user ID equal to -10. I deleted both records for each conversation ID. All these steps helped me to solve the problem. Maybe in these steps should be another one to open the table "messages" and try to search for the records with the conversation ID which you will find in the table "message_conversation_members" with user ID lower by 0. However, I didn't find any records therefore I don't think that this step is necessary. It would be really nice that Moodle authors could check the problem as I had this situation again. I repeated all these steps and I solved the problem again. However, I don't think that it is normal and it seams that this problem appears in different servers with different installations of Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Force users to move through quizes one at a time
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eric, Have you tried to set each succeeding quiz to have a restriction based on the previous quiz being marked complete with completion set to, Student must view this activity to complete it? If you also click on the eye next to the restriction, they will not be able to see the succeeding quiz until they have at lest viewed the previous one. You might also want to set the grade attempts allowed to 1 only and make sure they know that, along with setting extra restriction on attempts so that browser security is set to, Full screen pop-up with some javaScript security.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Force users to move through quizes one at a time
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi If a quiz has only essay questions, then the grade is nul, and the activity completion can't be set to "Student must receive a grade to complete this activity". If the quiz has just one question of any other type, these are automatically graded.  When the student submits, this question has a grade, and the essay questions are pending. In this case, "Student must receive a grade to complete this activity" works (I think). You can then restrict the next quiz to require that the previous one was "completed". Regards Brendon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Force users to move through quizes one at a time
ResponsesInList.Text: You could make the essays separate from the quizzes but keep them part of the sequence. "Assignments" have an option of being marked as completed once they've been turned in but before they've been graded.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Prevent Duplicate Enrollments with 2 Enrollment Methods?
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you talking about https://moodle.org/plugins/enrol_badgeenrol ?? It doesn't seem to override the enrol_user() method core enrol class - so the answer is that if the badge enrol plugin 'fires' it will override the original enrolment details (which instance it was and the timestamp) with its own details. So - the behaviour is down to the plugin but the default is to record the last instance. You can only be enrolled once, however, it's just the details that change. You can't have a "duplicate" enrolment. This is only really an issue if you disable the enrolment method in the course. In that case, it also prevents users who were enrolled using it from accessing the course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Prevent Duplicate Enrollments with 2 Enrollment Methods?
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, I look again and I stand corrected. This is the code... https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_36_STABLE/lib/enrollib.php#L1943 It is indexed on the instanceid (the id number of the particular instance of the enrolment plugin for the given course) and the userid. If this doesn't match it will create a new entry. So, yes, if the plugin does nothing to prevent it, there can be multiple enrol table entries for the same user in a single course. Clearly, this is only possible where the enrol plugin does nothing to prevent it. As I mentioned above - this may make sense. If they are legitimately enrolled using two different plugins then they remain enrolled if one of them is hidden or deleted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: course week remains hidden from students
ResponsesInList.Text: Mary is much better at these questions than I, but I will give you some thoughts and answers. The 3 and 14 represent times of the day.  So what I see is that this item, whatever it is, is never really available to students with your current settings because your Available and Deadlines are the same.  I don't use "Lessons" in my courses, but I do use quizzes, assignments, and forums, each having their own way of setting availability and typically a deadline. My guess as to why they are the same is that this is the default condition, and it is the best way to prompt you to change them. Yes, you can make everything immediately available by removing (un-checking) the "available from" checkbox.  This un-checking disables this restriction. Yes, there is a student view.  You get to it by clicking the little down-arrow to the right of your profile picture. When you make some changes to these settings, such as unchecking the Available from item, future backup/restores of your course will retain many of these settings (but typically not the dates, just the settings.)  So if you do make these changes, you can be more confident that when you hand off your courses to others that these other folks will have a better starting point than you have.  And you will be better at explaining various Moodle features to them, too.  This is referred to  by some as "continuous improvement." ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Kees, Intriguing.  I've been thinking about it for a few days and did try: 
```text

```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HELP  Security iframe with javascript
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kees, I came across this video on YouTube last night: - and looks as if what is going on could be a possible editor XSS attack security flaw.  So I'll have a hunt in the Moodle Tracker and see what I find. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kees, I've raised MDL-65316 if you'd like to comment etc. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HELP  Security iframe with javascript
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kees, In both of those cases, the script is only executed locally in the user's browser, at the time it is input/submitted. This is known as self-XSS, and in these cases is not considered a security issue (you can execute the same scripts already within your browser's console). The difference between these and the Google example in Gareth's linked video, is that the Google example was reflected when visiting a certain URL , so was easy to send to other users and have it execute in their browser. The cases you have outlined require a user to manually input the script themselves, and don't impact other users. In the case of messaging, that does seem like a minor bug (since it isn't showing a 'preview' in the way forum does, I wouldn't expect anything to execute at all), so it may be worth reporting that in Tracker , if no similar issue already exists. Though that doesn't need to be flagged as a security issue, I would suggest any issues of this nature that may have potential security implications are best raised directly in Tracker and not on the public forum (details are outlined here ). That way, if vulnerabilities are identified, we can fix them and disclose responsibly. Thanks, Mick

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Internal Error 500 on Server
ResponsesInList.Text: Error 500's are a generic catch all ... hard to track down without inspecting your error logs.   Case in point ... new hosting is using mod_security by default ... it's on .. the error log will reference the url that a mod_security rule triggered and will tell the web service to return to the browser error 500 thus cloaking mod_security. ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle and MS SQL Server 2008 Connection
ResponsesInList.Text: I am trying to install Moodle 3.63 on a Windows 2016 server running IIS 10 with PHP 7.2.14. I am running the initial setup from the Moodle web page in my server ( Database Settings). I want to connect to a MS SQL Server 2008 database that I created, but am stuck on the database connection page. I get the following error: Error: database driver problem detected The site administrator should verify server configuration Microsoft Drivers for SQL Server for PHP are not installed or not configured properly. Using the PHP Manager within IIS, I enabled php_sqlsrv_73_ts_x64.dll and php_sqlsrv_73_ts_x86.dll, but still get the error.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle and MS SQL Server 2008 Connection
ResponsesInList.Text: You say you have PHP 7.2.14 so you'll want the DLLs corresponding to PHP 7.2, i.e. php_sqlsrv_72_….dll , not php_sqlsrv_73_….dll . According to the PHP download page you should be using the Non-Thread Safe build of PHP when using IIS. If this is what you have you'll need the _nts_ versions of the DLLs (not _ts_ ). Presumably you've got the 64-bit build of PHP so you'll only need the _x64 DLL, not the _x86 one. The Microsoft Drivers for PHP for SQL Server depend on the Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server so you'll need to install this too. The exact version of the ODBC driver varies with the PHP driver version so check this: there's a link to these details under System Requirements of the Microsoft Drivers for PHP for SQL Server download page . To confirm the SQL Server extension is working I do the following: add the SQL Server extension to php.ini (e.g. extension=php_sqlsrv_72_nts.dll ) and then run php -i at the command line checking that 1) there are no errors and 2) the extension is listed in the output. ( php -i also tells you if it's the 64-bit or 32-bit PHP build, and whether it's the Thread Safe or Non-Thread Safe build).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle and MS SQL Server 2008 Connection
ResponsesInList.Text: I found this good post that explains what you mentioned. So I added the following lines in the PHP.ini file and was able to connect extension=php_pdo_sqlsrv_72_nts_x64.dll extension=php_sqlsrv_72_nts_x64.dll I checked the PHPinfo and it was activated. The problem now is that now I am getting the following message after installing the Microsoft ODBC Driver 11 for SQL Server . Error: Database connection failed It is possible that the database is overloaded or otherwise not running properly. The site administrator should also check that the database details have been correctly specified in config.php SQLState: 28000 Error Code: 18456 Message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 11 for SQL Server][SQL Server]Login failed for user

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle and MS SQL Server 2008 Connection
ResponsesInList.Text: That message looks like Moodle has connected to a SQL Server instance and was rejected, the most obvious explanation being that the credentials are wrong. Do you have SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) installed on the IIS server? If so you can use this to test the SQL Server connection by trying to connect with the same user credentials and database server details that you're using for Moodle. If they work in SSMS they should work in Moodle, but if they don't work in SSMS then they won't work in Moodle and you'll need to fix that first.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Registering students from my website to moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: The best I can do at this point is to wish you the best of luck in your endeavors. Creating a PHP bespoke website and trying to interface that with the Moodle database via custom PHP code is a huge task. The one suggestion I have is that you configure Moodle to allow email-based self-registration. It will work something like this: Enable and configure email-based self-registration on Moodle. Create your courses.  Each course will have a url with a unique id.  To find the url go to the course and copy the url from the browser. On your website add that link to the "Start Course Now" button.  The person will be redirected to the Moodle login/account creation page. After filling in the personal profile details the person will be able to access the course. I also suggest you read through Moodle documentation for developers and administrators.  Moodle uses bcrypt for password hashing.  See https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Password_salting .  Also refer to the PHP manual, https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.password-hash.php . Moodle authentication documentation https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Managing_authentication (alternate login URL ). You might also look through Moodle plugins .  E.g. see https://moodle.org/plugins/auth_userkey If I was setting this up, I would build on the work already done by other experts - use WordPress/WooCommerce/Edwiser Bridge and Moodle. In the end it will be less expensive, faster to develop, easier to do and much easier to maintain. Regards, Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: user id'0' is updated the passwords of other users automatically
ResponsesInList.Text: First - highly recommend you make a backup of your database . The some scripts, such as the one suggested you run, requires 'superuser' credentials to the database server.  The scripts use config.php file ... DB host, DB user, and DB password to talk to the DB server.   The DB user you have in config.php doesn't have privileges enough to alter the DB or tables in the DB. Make a backup of the config.php file ... in moodlecode/ ... cp config.php config-php.back Fix: edit config.php file. Copy the DB user and DB password lines (duplicate them).   Paste them back into the config.php just below the original lines (do NOT remove the original lines for you will make them active again). In the copies of those lines change user to the superuser and of course the password as well. Comment out the original lines that you copied using // in front of them. No need to restart any service.   Just go to moodlecode/admin/cli/ and re-issue the command. While you have superuser creds in config.php, might want to run php mysql_collation.php -l also and fix **IF** the collations of some tables do not match the other tables. Running that script should end with a summary ... some what like: Table collations summary for host: your_DB_collation: 1453 The number above is number of tables/column that match collation. If you have that line active in config.php then moodle is expecting all tables to have that collation. Please see: https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/MySQL_full_unicode_support Once fixed, you might want to re-edit config.php and comment out the superuser cred lines by putting // in front of them and re-enable the original user/password by removing the // in front of those lines. After checking things out on your site, strongly suggest making a full site backup: code, moodledata tar balls and an sql dump of your database.   If site is functioning, remove/erase any previous backups of the DB you have archived as they would take you one large step back if you restored using them. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Text: oops ... my mistake ... column name is 'contenthash' ... and NOT 'contexthash'. Think at this point not only cron but also apache should be shutdown. In your screen shot,  I see "numbered' directories .. like 1, etc.   Those look to be (without reallly seeing them) old course ID directories from when the site was a 1.9 (old file system).   They probably contain only moddata/###/###/and then a very old certificate file that was issued to a user ... probably long since gone from your system. Manually remove contents of moodledata/trashdir ... might consider writing a bash shell script in moodledata that does that upon execution of the script. Because you could not make a query (disk space issue), let's hope your databases are not now corrupt. I also saw a 'my sql ' directory in moodledata ... that's NOT the directory for the MySQL is it? Typical install of MySQL on Linux boxen (CentOS/Ubuntu) use /var/lib/mysql for the directory for databases/files related to MySQL.  *** NOTHING *** else but mysql files should be in there.   In config of MySQL default location is /var/lib/mysql and the only way to override that is shutdown MySQL ... move ... and edit my.cnf with the location where MySQL can find the DB files.   You didn't do that, did you? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 3.4.2 - Moodledata directory over 120Gb filling itself nonstop with backups
ResponsesInList.Text: First, 3.4.2 is old ... that series is now 3.4.8 and is supported for security fixes only now. So in your plans, think I'd upgrade - but not right now ... let the dust settle ... you are gaining on it. Manually remove those old course ID numbered directories in moodledata ... by now, they serve no purpose other than taking up space and a distraction for true server admin folks, like yourself. I have at least 5 sites that I've maintained over 6 years that have been marched through 1.9.highest to 3.5's and 3.6's now.  Early on however, beginning with the first upgrade from 1.9.x to 2.1.x, used git .   Highly recommend git for updates and upgrades - that's if there isn't a lot of customizations to core code. Wouldn't **ever** look to direct DB manipulation unless all other means were exhausted (don't think you are at that point now).   Quiz is very complicated. If I re-call correctly making a backup of a course that contained links to the top level quiz is really backing up the entire quiz bank ... lots of processing ... and if many questions had images/videos/audios etc. in them well ... large courses ... takes longer remove them. After things settledown a little, there is a hidden tool in moodle called 'health' ... accessible only by direct URL as an admin level user.   One of the things it does is inspect quizzes and then list issues it found + provides SQL solutions. Yes, you could spin up another moodle and begin again from scratch .. but if you are going to allow teachers to make no user backups of courses (which might have problems of which you are yet aware) you could be 'poisoning' (so to speak) the brand new and shiny Moodle.   Wonder how many support calls you can tolerate like that. Instead ... might be a better approach to backup courses ... no users ... yourself via command line looping script using code/admin/cli/backup.php where the backups are saved to a directory outside of moodledata on that NAS you have now, and provide those backup files to teachers IF they wish to restore.   You'll be able to spot troubled courses.   Troubled course backup ...  don't provide a backup for the teacher to use.   Yeah ... sounds cruel ... but having teachers restore means they haven't learn anything of the new version.   Teachers that have to rebuild will learn the new - besides, they actually might improve their courses! You could do both ... work on cleaning up and upgrading what you have (learn alot that way) and at the same time spin up new. Moving forward though, think one thing one could take forward is understanding that moodles are not install it once and forget them.   They do require maintenance and best to keep them updated. My 2 cents, of course! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: How to calculate course end date from a student's enrollment date?
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a four-week self-guided course that I want to allow students to enroll in and start attending the course the same day. I also want course sections to become available automatically once a week. The weekly course format will make sections available weekly, but counting from the course start date. That only works if everyone is starting the course at the same time, and in my case, I want the appropriate section to be accessible for each student independently. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to calculate course end date from a student's enrollment date?
ResponsesInList.Text: Four separate courses with start and end date conditions. The second, third and four courses have restrict access conditions, that will not allow the students to progress. There is also a new plug-in for automatic enrollment based on previous course completion, that you could look into.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to calculate course end date from a student's enrollment date?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Robert, Have you seen the Self enrolment method you can set up for your course? It boasts a lot of features, one of them being the 'enrolment duration' field where you can set up how many days/weeks/months an enrolment may last, counted from the moment a student / user signs up for the course. Combine this with this activity restriction plugin: https://moodle.org/plugins/availability_days That way, you can make sure the sections open on a time set such as enrolment + 7 days, + 14 days, + 21 days and +28 days if you want to.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.x vs 2.x for theming
ResponsesInList.Text: I am not a themer but I do work for Moodle and I would definitely NOT recommend Moodle 2.8. It is no longer supported.  I would always recommend using the latest Moodle version, especially if you want to appear professional in your course offerings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.x vs 2.x for theming
ResponsesInList.Text: One main reason to go for Moodle 3.5 LTS or higher is the fact that it's themes are built upon Bootstrap 4, whereas older versions of Moodle (2.x) don't support that. My recommendation is to build with Bootstrap 4, Moodle 3.6 or higher. Customisation is done in part through custom SCSS. There's a lot of documentation in this in the Moodle Docs Developers manuals (click the link to read)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Amount of time spent in course
ResponsesInList.Text: I will be the first person to give you the somewhat standard response.  No. This is not a fault with Moodle, it is just that computers are unable to track "time spent."  For example, if you are reading this post, then leave your computer to take care of other business, then come back and click on the next post, how much time have you spend in this forum?  How do you expect the computer to know that you stepped away? Well, having said this, you might find some ways to attempt to deduce the amount of time.  Moodle tracks "clicks." It will be up to you to figure out what the student was really doing between clicks.  Good luck. Might you be able to explain how you or your school sees how much time a student is studying for courses (meaning without any computers being used), either inside or outside of the classroom?  For example, if a student is in the classroom, but attends to a text message on their phone, is this counted as "study time?" I am just providing thoughts and trying to help you understand why moodle doesn't report bogus data.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Amount of time spent in course
ResponsesInList.Text: You might have a point if your course happened to be a "speed reading" course, but that's about it.    If the course does happen to be a Speed Reading course, you could build the reading into a quiz, follow it with assessment questions, and use the "timed" quiz feature to limit the quiz to (let's say) 30 minutes. Might you be saying that you believe that the student who took 15 minutes to read a story and gets a "B" on the assessment is somehow better than the student who took 2 hours to read a story and gets an "A?"  Or are you saying that if the story causes the one reader to stop, reflect, and think about each sentence, that you don't want to encourage this?  Or are you saying that the one student, who already knows something about a topic and can scan the reading and do well on the assessment is somehow better than the student who might not be familiar with the topic and takes longer?  I ask these questions to better understand what you are trying to identify and why.  I can't say that I have seen course (or learning) objectives ever stated as "The student will be able to xxx and yyy, in 20 seconds ."  Well, just my thoughts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Amount of time spent in course
ResponsesInList.Text: Let me explain a bit more. I am a training director at a company and am producing trainings for sales, service, and users. Especially for the sales and service trainings, I have to convince our distributor network to have their employees complete these trainings. To help encourage them, it would be helpful to be able to include an estimate of how long the course takes to complete. I was hoping to be able to use the experience of the first few participants to complete the course to be able to provide an estimate of time required to complete the course. Of course, the time required will depend on the experience of the participant, and I have nothing against someone just taking the quizzes and finishing a course in 15 minutes while someone else has to do all the readings etc. and takes 2 hours. But these salespeople and service technicians already have so many demands on their time, that if I tell them a training will only take 1.5 hours and they spend 4 hours, then they are less likely to do further trainings. So one of my constraints in designing these courses is keeping an eye on how much time it takes. The complete time in course from the Course dedication block is helpful, but if the course is taking longer than I imagined, it would also be good to know which activities are drawing that out. That would be a signal that that particular content is less familiar and might possible require additional background training. That is what I currently want to measure, as difficult as that may be. But even as a professor at the university (my last job), I tried to be conscious of how much time my students were spending per week on my class so as to not overburden them. If it is a two credit class and the students are spending 20 hours a week on it, then I am doing something wrong. Would some kind of activity tracking not be helpful, or am I stuck just asking students how much time they spend, which is equally fraught with inaccuracies? Thanks, Aaron

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Amount of time spent in course

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Amount of time spent in course
ResponsesInList.Text: Okay Aaron, I do understand where you are coming from. Well, you are the designer and probably the fastest at taking your own course.  How long would it take you to take your course?  This is probably the minimum. Then, ask someone else to take your course.  Maybe a colleague, maybe someone who represents your common "student," maybe your 8-year-old child.  These values now establish a range.  Then, you say "This course can be completed in xx hours." When I design my university courses, I let the course objectives establish the learning activities.  I don't pay attention to time.  I let my experience also guide me.  For example, in my Operations Management course, I think students should be able to read a chapter a week.  But I wouldn't give them 10 books each week to read on a topic. Oh, I should mention that your estimate for what a 2-credit-hour course should take.  The U.S. Government has already established the guidelines.  I cannot recall the exact amount, but it's approximately 40-hours per credit hour.  These guidelines were established when the U.S. Government discovered that some universities were cheating on government scholarships, etc.. (A school would get maybe $500 from the government for a student's 3-credit-hour semester course, but the course was fluff, involving very few lectures and assignments.) Another, oh... yep, schools trying to prove these 120 hours for a 3-credit-hour course didn't know how to measure, so some resort to asking students.  What do you really expect a student to say? They don't keep track of time either?  It depends on the incentives.  If the school gives an "A" incentive for "speed" (as a simple example) then the student says "10 hours."  If they give an "A" to the student who spends the most time, then the student says "400 hours." It still seems to get down to "assessment." What did the student learn?  This is the best measure. Well, this causes me to end up supporting Howard's reply. I should mention, we are not arguing with you.  We are simply trying to share our perspectives about the realities of not being able to measure "learning time" and that it is an often misconceived idea.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Class seating plan?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ideas for getting a signature for newly enrolled students
ResponsesInList.Text: If you’re on v3.4.5 or above, you can do this with site policies - see https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Policies Alternatively you could set up a feedback activity - see https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Feedback_activity Neither option will give you a ‘wet’ signature / e-signature though. There are a number of e-signature laws across the world which define what constitutes a legally binding e-signature. Just typing a name on a form and clicking submit has several issues that prevent it being upheld in a court of law. For it to be legally binding, there must be a way to prove the typed name belongs to the person it represents. IANAL (but I have worked for a Regulator) but I think it would be a fairly reasonable assumption that the person logged in to your Moodle site with a unique username and password, and logged evidence of their IP address, is the person actually agreeing to the policy, as far as is reasonably practical in an online environment.
