ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CRON JOB
ResponsesInList.Text: You cPanel should have a 'Terminal' icon which is for using command line on your server . When first clicking, you should find yourself in your home directory. Server is using Easy Apache for the purpose of running multiple versions of supported PHP.  The cron needs to find php-cli and not the php executable that's used by Apache for the web. So first command to use: which php [ENTER] That will show the path to the first php executable it finds. Let's say that shows /usr/bin/php Let's find out if that is for the web or cli ... /usr/bin/php -v **IF** the output of that does **NOT** show PHP 7.1.26 (cli) ... see the CLI in ()?  that's not the CLI PHP needed to run cron. Next command ... this one might take some time ... let it run. find / -name php I don't run a system that uses Easy-Aapche so I cannot show exactly what that command would out put, but you will probably see more than one line and in the lines a reference to ea-something. Is here one for /usr/local/bin/php? If so, try /usr/local/bin/php -v Do you see the correct version of PHP (the one you want to use for Moodle) and the (cli)?   If so, that's the one you use in the setup of cron. I've had to find the cli php on no less than 4 remotely hosted VPS servers on 4 different providers this way to get cron running as it should.   And, if running Moodle 3.6.x there is now a setting for 'path to php' which suggest one needs to set. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

If you wanted to limit it to a group, you could use Moodle groups to control access to that resource. I find limitations in each of these methods. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrict Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi py robert, This can be done by creating a new role derived from the editing teacher, that has the following permission disabled: moodle/site:accessallgroups This permission is by default disabled for the non editing teacher, so assigning this role to TA and TB should do the trick. In that situation, TA and TB won't be able to edit the course contents, but they would be able to only grade the students in their own group. Add TA to student group 1 containing S1, 2 and 3, and add TB to student group 2 containing S4 and 5. More info on the capability in the Moodle docs .

ResponsesInList.Text: One way to do this is to create a course named something like "shell" or "template," and create a backup of it.  Then, whenever you need a new course, create the new course starting with the backup. ResponsesInList.Title: Role to view only participants in group
ResponsesInList.Text:
I have three roles in mind: participant, manager and lets call the third one group leader . Say for example I have two groups, alpha and beta ,  the participants will be placed in one of each (participants being alpha_01, alpha_02, beta_01, beta_02, etc). In each of these groups there will be one group leader called. They are not expected to complete assignments assigned to the group, but they should be able to see the grades of all the participants in their group , but not of other participants. ResponsesInList.Title: SOLUTION: Query for enrolled users without mdl_role_assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a repost of https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=362674#p1462556 by Thomas College - I had a similar problem and worked out how to do it, so thought others may find the information useful. This query should return any role assignments (by roleID, but that's simple to change) for all enrolled users in a specified courseID. SELECT (SELECT CONCAT (u.firstname,' ',u.lastname) FROM mdl_user u WHERE u.id = ue.userid) AS user_name, cr.rid AS role_id FROM mdl_enrol e JOIN mdl_user_enrolments ue ON ue.enrolid = e.id LEFT JOIN (SELECT ctx.instanceid AS iid, ra.roleid AS rid, ra.userid AS uid FROM mdl_context ctx JOIN mdl_role_assignments ra ON ra.contextid = ctx.id WHERE ctx.contextlevel = 50) AS cr ON cr.iid = e.courseid AND cr.uid = ue.userid WHERE e.courseid = **insert course ID number here** Modifications I can think of would be to show this for all courses (group by courseid), to show roles by name or shortname depending if they're user-specified roles or not, and to use this as a subquery, for example if you need to compare it to which group the user is in (this is what I've used it for). Happy to help with anything I can surrounding this.

Re: faildelay on adhoc task is very high - 86400
ResponsesInList.Text: Each time a task fails, the fail delay is doubled. After 24 hours (?) the task is discarded, though deep down I am pretty sure i have seen tasks that hang around for way longer. So I doubt this. In this case 86400 is 24 hours, so its been failing a lot to arrive at such a long fail delay. It can be that the task takes too long to complete on a single cron running. Ad hoc tasks are performed after all the scheduled tasks are run, and if one of those takes most of the cron interval your adhoc task never gets its day in the sun. You will need to investigate if its a naturally long task that just needs more time, or if its throwing an error. There is probably a better way to do this, but a quick way is to run the cron job from the web interface : [your moodle url]/admin/cron.php You might need to uncheck "execute cron from command line only" and might want to set a password: do that all at : [your moodle url] / /admin/settings.php?section=sitepolicies When you cron in this way you can see the output of cron in your browser. Look for adhoc task output at the end ... and sadly be aware that you might not see your 86400 task for up to 24 hours. So you probably want to reset the faildelay in the database in order to test. (Somehow I think there is a better way than this ... perhaps someone else can advise ...)

ResponsesInList.Text: Some time ago you shared some info about your RedHat Enterprise Release 7 server that indicated you were using Software Collections repo. https://www.softwarecollections.org/en/scls/rhscl/httpd24/ Unfortunately, that's about the only page available to others/public.  All the rest of them require one to be a Red Hat Enterprise customer - ie, not open to the public  internet. That's significant. Am almost willing to bet that the PHP is also in a 'diffirent loccation' - thus as I discovered in 4 different VPS systems using easy-apache and on Google Compute Engine the php-cli which is what is needed to run cron was ***NOT*** in the suggested location of Moodle docs . ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrollment Report
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't know about a "report." However, if I wanted to know which course a student is enrolled in I would just click on the User, and look at their "Course details" area (an example is shown below.) A more elaborate way is to write custom SQL .  For example, I wanted a list of students who were enrolled in 2 or more courses of mine, so I wrote this SQL.  Maybe this code will help you write your own.  You can also explore SQL shared in the ad-hoc contributed reports web page. SELECT rj1.firstname, rj1.LastName, rj1.coursename, rj1.FinalGrade, rj1.CourseIDNum, rj2.count FROM rjfinalgrades rj1 JOIN (SELECT studentid, count(studentid) AS COUNT FROM rjfinalgrades GROUP BY StudentID HAVING COUNT(studentID) > 1) rj2 ON rj1.StudentID = rj2.studentid ORDER BY rj2.COUNT DESC, rj1.studentid, rj1.courseidnum DESC

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Users cannot view or send messages - "Error reading from database"
ResponsesInList.Text:
The "MySQL server has gone away" message tends to be a result of timeouts in MySQL (or MariaDB ). If you run the following command in the MySQL shell or in phpMyAdmin and reply with the results: SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES WHERE variable_name IN ('wait_timeout', 'max_allowed_packet', 'net_read_timeout', 'net_write_timeout'); The values on my system are: 
```text
+--------------------+---------+


| Variable_name      | Value   |


+--------------------+---------+


| max_allowed_packet | 4194304 |


| net_read_timeout   | 30      |


| net_write_timeout  | 60      |


| wait_timeout       | 28800   |


+--------------------+---------+
```
 There are posts on here suggesting increasing max_allowed_packet to 512 MB. I should say that these timeouts would come into play if clicking on "send a message" is taking a long time. If it is there may be an error in the database table (possibly related to the corrupted database issue). Find out where your MySQL/MariaDB logs are (mine are in /var/log/mariadb/mariadb.log , yours may be somewhere else) and check these for errors. You may need to repair a table.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.2.1 is not sending email.
ResponsesInList.Text: One reason why a server's PHP mailer might not be sending out messages is that the server doesn't have the software for sending email (one of which is called, "sendmail") installed. Installing this missing piece is probably the simplest way to get email working. On Ubuntu 16.04 for example: sudo apt install sendmail For other server types install the sendmail package the way you normally install stuff. Then clear out any SMTP configuration and give it a whirl. Errors are typically logged to /var/log/mail.log so you can look there if it still doesn't work. For External SMTP servers, often there is a connectivity issue (ports not open, firewall, dns fail etc). This is more difficult to diagnose as there are more possible causes. Often you can simply test the connectivity by pinging the smtp server, but even that is sometimes blocked by the smtp server. Hope this helps

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.2.1 is not sending email.
ResponsesInList.Text: All true but it's usually not a good idea to make your Moodle server (effectively) a mail server. In many cases the necessary ports will be blocked at your organisations firewall (to stop people doing exactly this). On top of that, unless you go to loads of trouble in setting it up many sites will simply refuse to accept your mail anyway as they will just assume you are a spammer . Always better to track down a reliable SMTP mail host and let somebody else have the mail problems. Consider a couple of other things too... If you are sending mail from (e.g.)  users@somedomain.org, do you have the 'right' to send messages on behalf of 'somedomain.org'? There are mechanisms in place (e.g. SPF records) which will try to stop you. You may have to speak to the owner of somedomain.org to get this permitted. It can be very tricky to diagnose mail problems. I would start by taking Moodle out of the loop and trying to contact your SMTP service from the command line.   Here's some useful information... https://www.port25.com/how-to-check-an-smtp-connection-with-a-manual-telnet-session-2/

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Default Dashboard ignores 'hide' setting of blocks?
ResponsesInList.Text: Manage blocks Whatis :- Hiding_a_block Whereis :- Site Administration -> Plugins -> Blocks -> Manage blocks There is a common setting to hide blocks like calendar, private files, online users, latest badges and upcoming events, etc. under 'Manage blocks' setting in 'Site Admin'. So, if we hide these blocks from here, the blocks will be hidden from all including admin. If we need to hide some of the blocks on dashboard only from students (and keep those visible for teachers and admin), then we need to configure the ‘Default dashboard’ view in this case. Moodle’s default dashboard Moodle Docs - Setting_the_default_Dashboard The additional blocks on dashboard like private files, online users, latest badges, calendar and upcoming events are now visible only to admin and teachers and are hidden from students. The setting for this is done as follows Go to Site Admin -> Appearance -> Default Dashboard page; Turn blocks editing on Click on the settings icon for 'Private files' block Click on 'Permissions' In the row 'View block', under col 'Prohibited', add 'Students', 'Authenticated user on front page ', 'Authenticated user' and then click on 'Back to block: Private files' at the bottom Repeat steps 3-5 for the other blocks, i.e, calendar, latest badges etc. After this, click on 'Reset dashboard for all users option' (available besides the 'Blocks editing' option) Note :- In ‘Clean’ theme, it works as desired; but in ‘Boost’, some students were still able to see the blocks on their dashboard. So, in order to get these blocks hidden for all students in theme ‘Boost’, here is the way that worked for me - After clicking on ‘Permissions’, in step 4 above, you get a page listing a set of capabilities for that particular block; here, we need to add ‘Student’, ‘Authenticated user’, ‘Authenticated user on frontpage’ in the ‘Prohibited’ column for all the ‘Capabilities’ in that block. Same goes for every block you want to hide from students.

ResponsesInList.Title: What can I do with Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi. I'm trying to figure out what I can actually achieve with moodle for our organisation. We currently use the platform to deliver content and record assessments for our learners for our distance based and blended learning courses. A student can begin a course at any time and there is no real set duration for completion. Tutors can view student submissions and mark/provide relevant feedback. This is all fine. We have a separate crm system to manage all the administration of our students such as bookings, payments, certifications, existing qualifications, etc, etc. Is Moodle the right platform to handle the admin as mentioned in the previous sentence or is Moodle "just" there to deliver the learning? I have to put a business case forward on the best way to proceed. Stay as we are or integrate everything into Moodle if possible. I've also briefly read about the upcoming release of Moodle Workplace. Will this help? Any advice or opinions would be welcome. Many thanks, Paul

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What can I do with Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: What can't you do with Moodle? There is an Attendance plug-in that can track classroom attendance, there is a Face-to-Face plugin that allows people to sign up and teachers to take attendance. I use F2F.  It has some quirks but generally works well.  There are several options for course payment stuff (I don't do that). Custom Certificate can be issued when specific tasks are complete and it saves a copy if you want one.  Cohorts could be used to assign people to a group of courses for specific qualifications.  You could probably issue a certificate from a hidden spot in the site main page when specific courses are complete (I've never tried it but I bet you could figure it out...) There is Configurable reports or Adhoc reports where you could create reports that pull a student's full course record or compile data. When people ask me "Can Moodle do..." My response is "Of course. It might not do it the way you envision it, but it can do just about anything."  A better question is "What can't Moodle do?" I don't have an answer for that one.

ResponsesInList.Title: Setting up a bank of courses across categories and for reuse.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello. I'm fairly new to Moodle Version 3.1 but I've been tasked with setting up the following platform: A suite of qualifications, each of which consists of up to 6 or 7 courses. Some of the courses can be cross-qualification, so if a student has passed course A for qualification A, then the system will need to pick that up as already passed if the student progresses through different qualifications. So far I have created a category for one of the "Qualifications" and I've added several courses into that category. I've included an empty course in the category and linked the other courses in the category using the Course Meta Link function to manage enrolments. Is this the best way to do it? The other main requirement is the re-use of courses as they change from time to time. So we need to have Course A, B, C etc. and also course resources such as quizzes, or a group of videos or documents, stored in some sort of resource library where a resource or course could change and then be applied to any new enrolments for that course. But! the existing/current students on a course must still see the original course/resource that was applied to them when they were enrolled. Thanks in advance, Paul

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting up a bank of courses across categories and for reuse.
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. Create a template course (Business101_Template) - This course is your current working version that you keep up to date, no students are enrolled in the course and is used as a template for a course that students are enrolled into. 2. Copy this template course and use a naming convention that allows you to track version eg. Business101_v1.1 3. Enrol current students in Business101_v1.1 4. Content changes so you update Business101_Template with these changes 5. Business101_Template is copied out to new course and new students are enrolled in Business101_v1.2 In terms of enrolments you could use cohort sync, course meta link or a combination of both.  There are other alternatives also but you will soon figure out what is more manageable in your situation. Probably have a few other ways you could manage this as well.  You want to probably set some business rules around content changes and when they happen for example at the start of every semester / term so you don't have a huge amount of work managing this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't remove [Deletion in progress]activities Moodle 3.4
ResponsesInList.Text: It could be that another task is blocking everything. This happens if the adhoc task fails. Have a look in your mdl_task_adhoc to see if it's filling up.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't remove [Deletion in progress]activities Moodle 3.4
ResponsesInList.Text: Can you please tell me where can I find that file. I am fairly new to Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't remove [Deletion in progress]activities Moodle 3.4
ResponsesInList.Text: mdl_task_adhoc is a database table. When Moodle tries to delete things from the Rubbish bin, it queues up the items to be deleted in this table. When cron runs it basically runs to processes: scheduled tasks & adhoc tasks. Course module deletions get put in the mdl_task_adhoc table. If you're able to view the cron logs, you'll see if the adhoc tasks are failing. It may showing a "locking" error. If it's failing this way, cron just stops, so it never gets to run any other adhoc task.

Now, course grades get re calculated quickly when I delete a module from any course

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Make a public course visible in My Courses for all students.
ResponsesInList.Text: Guest access and allowing anyone to access the course does not enrol someone in it. A course will only show in My Courses if a student is actually enrolled in it. That’s by design - that list is supposed to be a filtered list of courses that are relevant to a user rather than them always seeing the entire list of courses that might be available on the site. You may need the Autoenrol plugin or something similar. See https://moodle.org/plugins/enrol_auto for more info. You could create a cohort and enrol the cohort into the course, but you’ll still need a way of adding people to the cohort when their account is created so the Autoenrol plugin is probably your best option.

ResponsesInList.Title: Upgraded Moodle site not translating some language strings when sending email
ResponsesInList.Text:
A few weeks back I upgraded my Moodle 2.1 site to Moodle 3.5.2 (3.6 wasn't out while we were testing...) As part of the upgrade I needed to change the language strings that create the emails that get sent to students when they enrol, or are enrolled in courses. I have customized the welcometocoursetext string in the core and enrol_self components to: 
```text
Hello {$a->firstname} {$a->lastname},




You have been enrolled in the "{$a->coursename}" course on the {$a->sitename} site. You now have access to this course and can begin your learning path...
```
 The problem is that Moodle is only doing some of those "variable substitutions". Instead of replacing the {$a->sitename} , {$a->firstname} and {$a->lastname} variables with the text linked to those variables the email contains the actual {$a->sitename}, {$a->firstname} and {$a->lastname} variables as text, like this: 
```text
Hello {$a->firstname} {$a->lastname},




You have been enrolled in the "Maths 101" course on the {$a->sitename} site. You now have access to this course and can begin your learning path...
```
 So, it's printing those actual variable names instead of the text associated with those respective language variables.  The exception is that Moodle IS correctly translating the {$a->coursename} variable and showing the correct text, "Maths 101". So, why is Moodle only printing SOME of the language strings? It should be: 
```text
Hello Mary Jane,




You have been enrolled in the "Maths 101" course on the ABC University site. You now have access to this course and can begin your learning path...
```
 I have purged all the Moodle and browser and server caches, but that doesn't seem to help - users still get the emails with those variable names printed in the body of the emails. My Moodle runs on a cluster of Windows Server 2012 R2 VM 's with an F5 load balancer and: IIS 8.5 FastCGI PHP 7.2.9 NTS File cache: Wincache (v2.0.0.8) - configured as the session.save_handler... Opcode Caching : Zend OPcache v7.2.9.0 I'm stumped! Does anyone know how to resolve this? Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Global Search display order (Moodle 3.2)
ResponsesInList.Text: Apologies if this is not the best place to post this... We have recently installed Global Search with Solr in Moodle 3.2 on a Windows 2012 R2 server running IIS 8.5. We're very pleased with the way it's working and would like to understand it better. At our last development meeting I was asked to find out where in the code the order of the search results is determined and how this is done. I'm struggling to do this and wonder if anyone could help me. The developer Prateek Sachan says the following in both the forum post https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=227805 and the development page https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Global_search_(GSoC2013): The results will be based on "relevance weightage". For example: Case I: Lesson A contains 1 occurances of "batman superman" (as a phrase..both words are together) Lesson B contains 10 occurances of batman and 6 occurances of superman. If a user searches for "batman superman" Lesson B will have higher priority (or relevance) as comparerd to Lesson A Case II: Lesson A contains 10 occurances of "batman superman" (as a phrase..both words are together) Lesson B contains 10 occurances of batman and 6 occurances of superman. If a user searches for "batman superman" Lesson A will have higher priority (or relevance) as comparerd to Lesson B However, I'd like to understand the ordering at a more granular level than that, e.g. how a "relevance weighting" is calculated and how, within a particular relevance weighting, the results are ordered. I've read that from moodle 3.5 onwards it is possible to upgrade the Global Search plugin to determine your own ordering but we are not in a position to upgrade the site for a while yet. Many thanks for your help. Alyson

ResponsesInList.Title: Emails On Course Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Guys, Totally new to Moodle and, hopefully, some background will help. We're currently using a paid-for LMS system for our corporate training and, quite frankly, it sucks. after a bit of searching Moodle seems to be coming up top of the list and we're seriously considering switching to it, sticking it on a server and ditching the old system. While I've had a play with it briefly (v3.4 and have to say that it looks really good - being able to get our existing SCORM files in is a Godsend) we do have some things that we need to be able to do and, so far, I haven't been able to figure out. Hence the question. What we need to be able to do is, when a student finishes a course, email the course teacher the details of the student, whether they passed or not, what their pass mark was and the name of the course that they just passed. We have code that can pick that up, generate certificates and then email those certificates to the user but the key things is being able to get emails sent out automatically. Can Moodle generate those emails? If so, can anyone show me how to do that (step by step as I'm a complete noob to the system)? I've tried installing the mod_CheckList plugin but couldn't then figure out how to wire it up to a course (or even add it as a block) - yes, this is the 'idiot level' that I'm at. We'd also need, if possible to be able to generate reports showing who'd taken courses (possibly including the answers that they gave to individual questions). Again, can Moodle do things like that? Mucho gracias

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Emails On Course Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: The quiz module will send an email saying your quiz was received...It might also send a you passed one but I'm not sure.  I quit using that feature a long time ago. My experience is that Moodle doesn't do a lot of automated emails (hounding or completion notification; it does send messages about forum posts and graded assignments).  But there are some (free) add ons that do email super well. That said, it will tell student when they have completed and, with the right combination of activities , will provide a certificate. First, the add ons: Certificates : there are two options--Certificate and Custom Certificate.  Both work really well. I've used both.  I can't say I like one more than another.  They're different from each other and equally cool.  Custom takes some brain at the teacher level, Certificate takes some admin set up.  It just depends on what you want. I think both versions will email the certificate to the user (and the teacher, if you want it). Reports: You want transcripts? You can build them.  I've used Configurable reports.  If you know any sql , you can build some super powerful reports. There is also an Adhoc Reports module.  I've not used it but people seem to like it. SQL, of course, takes some brain, but it works and you can specify who can see what reports.  At my last job, we had Transcripts that staff could view for themselves, lists of transcripts supervisors could review and much larger reports that training managers could review (based on department). Moodle does have some native reporting (there is a Grades overview report available for each user on their profile and it may be available to teachers in enrolled courses) but it historically hasn't done much student level reporting, only course level.  In 3.3, I think that may be changing but haven't had much time to look into it. If you're really looking for course completion--that's native and super cool. I think what you really want is a feature that demonstrates course completion.  Moodle absolutely has that: First, you enable completion at the site level (I think it might be in advanced features) then you turn on course completion in your courses (and set it to default in new courses); set activities to 'complete' when conditions (like passing score) are met; set quizzes and scorms (if applicable) to a grade to pass, then set the 'completion' criteria (must get credit for SCORM A, review document C and complete the quiz). You might also look at Badges.  They're pretty fun.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Melanie, That's really useful and I think I found the settings that you detailed...except for the final bit. So the way I have it setup is as follows: Site Administration>Advanced Features>Enable Completion Tracking (On) [Course] > Course Completion > General (set to 'Course is completed when ALL conditions are met' [Course] > Course Completion > Condition:Activity Completion (On for all SCORM packages in the course) Then I hit a 'what do I do next?' bit. Have you got any suggestions for plugins that we should be looking at that can do that or resources we should be looking at? Thanks Neil

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Emails On Course Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: So, you've got the checks populating and the completion status block/option is reporting completion? The Moodle Certificate module will issue a electronic certificate version--you could use it and modify the language pack for the email to provide information about when will get an "official" printed copy by mail (or in person, whatever you do) and then use the saved pdf to print each certificate on the fancy paper, adding whatever nifty-ness you need before sending/giving it.  I can't think of another way for it to auto notify anyone of completion.  And, it will notify both teachers and students that the certificate conditions are met.  Maybe you make the certificate less of a certificate and more of a placeholder--you've completed and your certificate will be forthcoming...? That said there is some new messaging stuff coming with 3.5...maybe that will be one of the enhancements?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help with old Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Would help to know at least what operating system it runs on.   Makes a diff in directions. Below are for a Linux flavored server. Version can be found via version.php file in moodlecode.   Typically, code was in /var/www/html/ or /var/www/html/moodle/ As root: cd /var/www/html/ fgrep '$release' version.php Gaining admin access ... In the original install of Moodle, user ID 2 was (might still be) the initial admin user and the default login name was 'admin'.   That might have changed over time, but assuming it didn't, one can do this with manual accounts ... id 2 or the admin account was such an account. To verify it still is use the db user and password seen in config.php file with this query of DB (assumes My SQL and using the DB for moodle which can be seen in config.php file of the code). ﻿ mysql> select id,auth,username,firstname,lastname,email from mdl_user where id = '2'; If that shows: |  2 | manual | admin cd /var/www/html/admin/cli/ php reset_password.php (works only for manual accounts) ... so you would give 'admin' (following example output above). You will be prompted for the new password.   Since we don't know what settings are for passwords, use 8 letters, one cap, one none alpha-numeric, one numeric in the password. If that goes well, go to the site with browser and login with admin/yournewpass. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Database backup and cron
ResponsesInList.Text: Having been talking with my sysadmin about setting cron to run every minute ( per the recommendations ), I wondered whether this could cause a problem with site backups . Specifically - if cron runs half-way through my backup routine taking a copy of the site's database , could the backup end up with part of the database from before the cron and part from after? Could this result in an inconsistent database should we have to restore from it? Thoughts?.. Cheers, Dave.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Database backup and cron
ResponsesInList.Text: It comes down to two things: what database system is in use ( MySQL , MariaDB , PostgreSQL , etc.) and what tool is used to perform the copy of the site database. With My SQL and MariaDB when using mysqldump to perform the backup, it's recommended that --single-transaction is used to ensure that it "dumps the consistent state of the database".

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Database backup and cron
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Leon - that confirns my suspicion, and - even better - gives me a solution!

ResponsesInList.Text: Using 3.5.3 In a discussion forum, a student pasted the following URL into their post: https://www-jstor-org.libproxy.csustan.edu/stable/j.ctt14bszg0.6?Search=yes&resultItemClick=true&searchText=young&searchText=adulthood&searchUri=%2Faction%2FdoBasicSearch%3FQuery%3Dyoung%2Badulthood%26amp%3Bacc%3Don%26amp%3Bwc%3Don%26amp%3Bgroup%3Dnone%26amp%3Bfc%3Doff&ab_segments=0%2Ftbsub-1%2Frelevance_config_with_tbsub&refreqid=search%3A3d110a9d4369a9ef557ebecfbb633246&seq=6#metadata_info_tab_contents The student did not make the URL into a link using the ATTO link tool while typing their post. However, upon saving, the no one could view the post.  Instead, Moodle churned and churned and finally the browser reported a general connection failure. When I edited the post directly in the database and removed the URL, the post displayed as expected without trouble. We have URL and image filtering enabled on our system.  My suspicion is that the URL and image filter was trying to make the URL a link and somehow was choking on the content as it tried to display the post.  I don't see any characters in the URL that might cause a problem (everything seems correctly escaped), so the only other reason is the length of the URL. Is there a character limit for the url filter?  If so, is that documented anywhere?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Removed student from a cohort, grades and assignments missing
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bradford, Do you use manual enrollment of cohort members or cohort sync enrollment? There’s a setting hidden in the manual enrollment modal under advanced which enables the recovery of old grades upon re-enrollment. If the users haven’t been deleted from the server, this should help a lot. In the case you did delete the users, there’s not much one can do to restore such a user.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I simply make courses derive from one basic course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Miki, To my knowledge, this is not how Moodle works. While there are many ways of creating duplicates of courses (using Import or upload courses + 'templatecourse' field being my favorites), there's no automated script updating the course content in copies when something is updated in the Master version of it. One of the reasons why this should be avoided, in my opinion, is the fact that you don't swap textbooks or tests while your learners are using it, but instead modify your course content and layout after carefully evaluating it's last run. This prevents a lot of unrest among your teaching staff and students/learners. Most activities (with completion enabled) for instance, are locked for any changes that might affect overall course completion for users. The questions associated with a quiz can't be modified in the quiz itself, in terms of text and answers after attempts have been registered for it. That being said, you can duplicate a master course infinitely through Upload courses with a CSV that contains the 'templatecourse' field pointing to the master course's short name. Depending on how complex your master course is, this can be a bit of a stretch for most Moodle servers, but it is probably the best way of creating a large number of duplicates.

ResponsesInList.Title: Need guidance on how to get this started...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Moodle Community, I am new to Moodle and LMS in general, so please bear with me. Here is what I'm trying to accomplish: I want to develop a free training program that can be widely disseminated to students. We are planning to develop the training via Adobe Captivate and track the training via Moodle. But the problem is, I have no idea where to start with getting Moodle set up. I just need a step-by-step guide on what I need to do to set up Moodle to where I can just focus on the Look and Feel of the website, rather than worrying about the back-end stuff (system administrator, database stuff, etc). What I need from Moodle is to simply track the progress of the participants and report general data on the training (number of people completed, length of time it took, most missed questions, etc.) My questions: Can you give me an estimated cost for having our IT guys set up Moodle? What other factors do I need to be thinking about right now to launch this project successfully? Once Moodle is set up, what's next? How do I customize my website and my website URL ? I'm viewing Moodle as a type of website, is this correct? Or do I need to still get a website to use Moodle? Any help is much appreciated! Regards, Calvin Do

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need guidance on how to get this started...
ResponsesInList.Text: Calvin, The easiest and fastest way to get started with Moodle is to create a free Moodle Cloud account, https://moodlecloud.com/ . You will be provided with a Moodle instance ready to go. The free account has limitations, but is a great way to get started. there are also very inexpensive paid versions available. Documentation on everything Moodle is available at https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Main_page . You also might want to get familiar with Moodle by logging into the sample Moodle school, Mount Orange School, https://school.demo.moodle.net/ , with different roles, Manager, Teacher, Student, etc. If you want to setup your own Moodle instance, you will need a webserver - either your own, or one through a web hosting company.  Installation instructions are available at https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Installing_Moodle. Most Moodle instances are installed on a LAMP stack = Linux, Apache web server , MySQL (or Maria DB), and PHP.  There are basically three components to any Moodle installation: 1) a database, 2) a file storage location for moodledata files (content) and 3) the Moodle code files which run on a web server. If you have a savvy IT staff, they should be able to setup a server with Moodle in a half day or so.  Someone who is really familiar with Moodle can do it in a couple hours. There are two cautions I have with respect to web general shared hosting companies (e.g. GoDaddy, BlueHost, HostGator): 1) do not use Moodle installation scripts provided by a hosting company. They often are not configured correctly and result in an installation that does not perform correctly. 2) Most of the inexpensive hosting companies provide shared hosting services - the web server is shared among a number of clients. That level of hosting often does not provide the resources and software versions required by Moodle.  I would consider a managed VPS hosting service such as Liquid Web, HostWinds, or Just Host. An advantage of using Moodle as your LMS is that you can transfer your database and data to any server. So, no matter what you start with, you can move your installation to another location later.  Even if you begin with a free MoodleCloud account, you can export the database and data, and install that on another server. As far as your content - Adobe Captivate. If you create Captivate learning modules publish them as HTML5 with SCORM 1.2 or xAPI (also known as TinCan). Moodle does not support SCORM 2004. If you use xAPI you will also need to create a Learning Record Store.  However, there are many tools in Moodle that you can use instead of creating Captivate SCORM or xAPI modules. I would also consider using H5P, https://h5p.org/ . There is a great Moodle plugin for H5P. There is a bit of a learning curve for Moodle, as with any software package. I suggest starting slowly and taking small steps. Floyd Saner

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need guidance on how to get this started...
ResponsesInList.Text: Floyd, you have said this very well. I'll add a little more. Commonly, in many typical courses, the three most used student " activities " are quizzes, assignments (uploads), and forums (discussions.)  If these are important to you, Calvin, begin learning these activities on your MoodleCloud account. 3a. Learn, learn, and learn.  In Moodle, there are many "?s" scattered all over to help you understand features.  Also, at the bottom of most web pages in Moodle, there is a link to " Moodle Docs for this page." 1. I would say somewhere between $10US and $1,000,000 US, depending upon how good your IT guys are. 2. Get some folks to try your Moodle and experiment as much as you can before launching. 3b. Moodle is one of the most "customizable  LMSs.  I would focus on functionality, before the appearance, however. 3c. Yes, Moodle is an application that can present itself as a website, just like any other application on the web (WordPress, Amazon, eBay, etc.) 3d. As Floyd said, you need a server.  For guidance, let us know how "big" you think your needs are, meaning the number of "students," the number of courses, an idea of "how much activity" you expect. Relative to your desire to track "length of time," in general, this is difficult because computers most typically only know about "clicks" and do not know what the student is doing between clicks. As you are probably seeing, when you have questions, ask here on Moodle.org. Also, consider attending a MoodleMoot.  These are fun gatherings where you would be able to meet people involved in using and supporting Moodle, and great to learn things by attending presentations, or simply talking with folks.

Hi Rachel, You could try viewing your course in Boost theme without upsetting your entire organisation for the sake of debugging the issue. One prerequisite is to have your site admin enable 'Allow theme changes in the URL', a setting that can be found in Site admin > Appearance > Theme settings. This enables an individual user to switch to another theme by adding a type of prompt to the URL of the page in Moodle you'd like to check. What you'd add: 
```text
moodle.url/course/view.php?id=12345
&theme=boost
```
 or 
```text
moodle.url/
?theme=boost
```
 You can replace the 'boost' bit with the short name of any theme installed in your Moodle instance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: where are the books administration page or menu ?
ResponsesInList.Text: The Book activity is not a additional plugin, it’s included in the core distribution. As a site admin - go to Site Admin > Plugins > Activity Modules > Manage Activities You should be able to see “Book” listed in the first column. You will also see a number in the second column, and a eye icon in the fourth column. The number denotes how many Book activities are deployed across your site. Click on the number and it will show you the courses that are using the Book activity. Is the eye open or closed? If closed, Books are disabled across your site. If you’re not a site administrator, you will need to find out from someone who is whether the Book activity is enabled or disabled. If it IS enabled, then as an admin or a teacher and when IN a course, with editing turned on, you will be able to edit the settings of a Book and it’s contents. Question - is the Book activity you restored on the same site as the one you backed up? If it is and YOU can’t see the restored Book, then how did you back it up?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error reading from database when deleting courses (Moodle 3.5)
ResponsesInList.Text: The error says a table doesn't exist in the database.  There are 3 tables related to the old assignment in core code: ﻿ | mdl_assignment                       | | mdl_assignment_submissions           | | mdl_assignment_upgrade We need to find out if they do indeed exist.  Cannot do that from Moodle interface.   Must use a mysql client (cli) or phpmyadmin. MySQL CLI Client: From an ssh session in the server where the database for moodle resides: mysql -u DBUSER -p'DBPASSWORD' - DB variables seen in config.php of code of your site. Let's say the DB used for your Moodle is called 'moodle'. At the mysql> prompt, type: mysql> use moodle; [ENTER] Next we see if the tables for the old assignment exist: mysql> show tables like 'mdl_assignment%'; [ENTER] Should show you this: mysql> show tables like 'mdl_assignment%'; +-----------------------------------------+ | Tables_in_moodle (mdl_assignment%) | +-----------------------------------------+ | mdl_assignment                          | | mdl_assignment_submissions              | | mdl_assignment_upgrade                  | +-----------------------------------------+ 3 rows in set (0.01 sec) Also we need to know the version of you MySQL server. Again from ssh mysql -V [ENTER] Minimum version for MySQL for running 3.5.x of Moodle is: 5.5.31 Now this last question ... relates to " a week ago like a charm and we changed nothing, neither directly in moodle nor in the server config " Are you hosted on a shared server? If so, who is provider? 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot delete / expunge large files from course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Russ, Two points: 1. This might seem a bit like jumping through hoops but it might help: I run a query from time to time using Configurable Reports to identify large files: SELECT * FROM prefix_files WHERE prefix_files.filesize > 524288000                              (this is 500mb in bytes) I look at the context id to find where a file is located in the UI. Say my report says I have a large file in context 1348. I then go to [mymoodlesiteurl]/admin/roles/permissions.php?contextid=1348 I go back one step along the 'breadcrumb' at the top of the page. I am now in the place where the file is located and can delete it. 2. Moodle will retain a 'deleted' file in its database for a week (I think, - certainly a few days). If a week hasn't passed yet since you removed the files, then wait a few more days! Hope that helps. Catherine

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot delete / expunge large files from course
ResponsesInList.Text:
Thank you all again for your help. Utilizing your suggestions, here is the final process we used to resolve the issue (since Moodle was not auto-deleting them as expected): We determined that the files that had been uploaded were all
listed in the mdl_files table so we searched for them using MariaDB [moodle]> SELECT id,filename,filesize,contenthash FROM
mdl_files WHERE filename LIKE '%.mp4'; The contenthash item looks something like dd06d738c2b8366c30eb436fc3a8722efe7d10aa That is the name that moodle uses to store the file under
moodledata/filedir.  The arrangement of filedir is two layers of stacked
directories labeled 00 – ff which gives a total of 65,025 possible locations
for the file.  Fortunately the find
command works quickly [stelmn@jadzia filedir]$ find -name
"a7e9bd81247d508c8e9cb5e3314c6be7c5d5ca55" -exec ls -lh {} \; 2>
/dev/null -rw-rw-rw-. 1 apache apache 676M Mar  4 16:06
./a7/e9/a7e9bd81247d508c8e9cb5e3314c6be7c5d5ca55 And confirms that the file exists and shows the path to its
location.  You can then move to the
directory and delete the file manually or simply use a single command to do the
find and remove in one step. [stelmn@jadzia filedir]$ find -name
"a7e9bd81247d508c8e9cb5e3314c6be7c5d5ca55" -exec rm {} \; Finally we used phpMyAdmin to remove the entries from the
mdl_files table.

Can they use their phone to record your presentation in the lecture theatre/training room... yes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Get data about the_task_scheduled  and detailed info on all tasks list somewhere?
ResponsesInList.Text: The 'component' is the part of Moodle that this task belongs to. e.g. 'core' is tasks that are part of the core Moodle functionality 'mod_forum' is tasks that are part of the 'forum' activity in Moodle. The 'classname' tells Moodle the name of the PHP class that has the code to run that task. These are stored using PHP namespaces, to allow the correct code to be automatically loaded. All 'core' tasks are found in the /lib/classes/task folder in the Moodle code. All other tasks are found in the relevant plugin, e.g. 'mod_forum' tasks are found in the /mod/forum/classes/task folder, 'enrol_ldap' tasks are found in the /enrol/ldap/classes/task folder. The filename for the task will match the last part of the 'classname' - e.g. \enrol_ldap\task\sync_enrolments will be found in /enrol/ldap/classes/task/sync_enrolments.php 'Blocking' means that the task will block all other tasks from starting whilst it is running (normally different tasks can run in parallel) - it is defined in the db/tasks.php file for each plugin and normally doesn't change. 'faildelay' is how long a task is delayed for if it throws an error during execution (this is so that the delay can be increased each time, to avoid a failing task being called too often). 'customized' records if you've gone into the admin settings page for the scheduled tasks and changed the default schedule for the task. As for the long list of different tasks, you would have to open up the code for each one (based on what I've written above) and read through the comments in the code in order to understand exactly what each task is doing.

ResponsesInList.Text: so how is the actual file deletion delay work and triggered to delete the files physically then? That is strange no?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Get data about the_task_scheduled  and detailed info on all tasks list somewhere?
ResponsesInList.Text: It isn't particularly strange, no. All files in Moodle have their content sha-summed to get a unique name for each. This allows for de-duplication of data. The same file uploaded by 30 different people, or existing in 30 different courses only exists in the moodledata directory once. To this end we have a `files` table in the database . Each use of a file is known as a stored_file . Additionally we store draft files. If a user has uploaded a file but not saved it (or in certain other situations like editing), copies of the file are stored in a "Draft file area". Files remain in the draft file area for 4 days be default. A scheduled task runs daily and removes any stored_file in any draft area which was created >= 4 days ago. When a stored_file is removed, we remove the record of it from the database. If there  are no other uses of that actual file behind that stored file then it is moved to a trash directory within the moodledata directory. A scheduled task runs periodically and removes all files from that trash directory . Both of these tasks are extremely lightweight and highly unlikely to contribute towards the issues you have been seeing. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Get data about the_task_scheduled  and detailed info on all tasks list somewhere?
ResponsesInList.Text: How do we set the faildelay setting and what metric is used to measure it? For example, 0 obviously means not delay but what about 1 or even 5 or 7, or say 11? is that measure in seconds, minutes, hours, days? etc?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Get data about the_task_scheduled  and detailed info on all tasks list somewhere?
ResponsesInList.Text: The faildelay is set automatically by the  task API. It is a time in seconds. When a task runs, if it fails, then we will retry it. Rather than retrying immediately we gradually back-off by increasing the amount of time before we retry. This is used when calculating the "nextruntime". The magic happens in the task manager and applies to both adhoc and scheduled tasks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Reliable streaming server
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick The MediaConvert service is just the file conversion part of the solution. In the old days a streaming server would stream the portion of the video/audio that was requested, at some quality level. In these "serverless" days, the media is converted into shorts snippets of say 5s in length, at different qualities. The player then requests the quality and portion of the video it wants, by requesting the correct file(s). So all the hard work happens at file conversion time,  and the playback happens without a server. This is why many players have "HLS" plugins, to support this arrangement. You would chain it together with S3 (and maybe Cloudfront) to handle the storage and delivery of the media files. Amazon rarely makes it easy on you, by letting you know how much it will all cost. I actually use the AWS Elastic Transcoder service, which is older and I suspect slowly going to fade away. For all the transcoding it does it is cheap. But the real benefit is that its possible to chain all these services together to make processes. Having written all that, I realize I have strayed us off the garden path a bit. Its not a simple solution for media hosting unless you really want to get into all of that. And depending on the original poster's needs, Vimeo might be better because its not so complex.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle display "Sorry, maintenance in progress". Please help
ResponsesInList.Text: Seems that the site is stuck in maintenance mode. Can you try to navigate to your Moodle url and tack on /login/index.php to the URL ? See if you can log in as a site administrator via that method. Depending on the maintenance mode, you may or may not be able to log in this way. If you are able to log in this way, then you can disable maintenance mode. For example, if your Moodle site is at https://www.example.com/lms then manually try https://www.example.com/lms/ login/index.php If you cannot log in this way, then you would need to disable maintenance mode from the backend server -side.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle display "Sorry, maintenance in progress". Please help
ResponsesInList.Text:
HI Edwin The steps which you can take to restore your site back are: Appending ‘/login/index.php’ in the URL of your site name – If you add ‘/login/index.php’ in the site URL then you can access the login page of your Moodle site e.g. if your site is running with a domain name http://yourdomainname.com then you can directly type http://yourdomainname.com/login/index.php in the address bar of your browser. It will allow you to login into your Moodle site and turn off the maintenance mode in the settings through Site Administration > Server > Maintenance Mode. Directly trying the URL – http://yourdomainname.com /admin/settings.php?section=maintenancemode which will again takes you to the login page and then redirects you to the maintenance page where you can turn off the maintenance mode. Through Command line (CLI) – 
```text
     cd moodlecode/admin/cli/
```
 
```text
     php maintenance.php --disable
```
 Through Database – If you have database access then also you can deactivate the maintenance mode by changing the variable named “ maintenance_enabled” to “0” in the “ mdl_config table “. (that’s a zero.  1 is on) Editing the config.php file – If you have access to your config.php file then you can add the following line in your config.php file: 
```text
$CFG->maintenance_enabled=0; (that's a zero and be sure to include the ';' at the end of that line.
```
 Also check for a file maintenance.html in the Moodledata directory and delete it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: course backup via back.php - why is there no file showing?
ResponsesInList.Text: Backups, by any method (automated, looped bash shell script, or single from backup.php cli) use moodledata/temp/backup directory to build the backup.  Process creates a directory to use there by a long name ... like aohqwefghqweldewqasdlfj To watch what's going on in there: Login as root user cd /path/to/moodledata/temp/backup/ ls (list to see the temp backup directory ... will use the example above) cd aohqwefghqweldewqasdlfj watch 'ls -l;df -h' This 'watch' command will show a listing of directories and files in the build directory as they are created (at some ponit no new files/folders will be created - process is populating directories) and show how much disk space one has available - refreshes every 2 seconds by default. When the backup build is finished, the last step is to *copy* the built .mbz file to it's destination. When watch command starts to error ... ie, can't list files cause they have been removed. Quit watch ... press q. cd /path/to/destination/ ls -l You should see your backup file. All the above is sorta opening pandora's box if the cli backup fails.  No I cannot do Vulcan Mind Melds and answer future questions in this thread if the above fails.  Not without more info ... accurate also! The standard troubleshooting things ... check web server error logs etc. for clues. No info ... no guesses possible! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Preventing users from blocking other users
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings, everyone I am using Moodle 3.6, which was set up in a Linux CentOS machine, along with MySQL 14.14 and PHP 7.2. We use this environment in a higher education institution to educate students through distance learning. My employers want me to prevent students from blocking their teachers on Moodle's built-in messenger. According to them, teachers usually inform their students about future activities and exams through this communication channel, but students often block it. Then, they skip some activities and exams and blame it on their teachers who, according to them, did not send any information regarding the skipped activity/exam. These incidents are used by some students as an excuse to extend deadlines for these activities/exams. I found out in a forum post from 2008 ( https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=108042 ) that user message blocking could only be disabled by code. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Files "Missing from filedir and external storage"
ResponsesInList.Text: Happen to be working though this very same thing with a site that had in error used the same moodledata directory as another site on the same server .   What a mess! ﻿ First, if you could clone the code directory, DB and minimally moodledata/filedir to another test server environment with moosh installed one could tinker with it to see how it works ... or doesn't.  Obviously doing this could be massive and if there were to be any hickups in what you did, don't want to wreck production server. moosh -n file-dbcheck > filedbcheck.txt IF they are on disk but NOT in DB then there are no links to them in Moodle. One could use a looping bash shell script to remove them. #!/bin/bash for i in $(cat ./filedbcheck.txt) do echo 'File in que:' $i; rm $i done echo 'Done!'; OR, if you had room to do so, rather than rm $i one could do a mv $i /safekeeping/ where /safekeeping/ was a manually created directory. But what are they? For investigation of that - bash shell script that loops through the above and shows mimetype; #!/bin/bash for i in $(cat ./filedbcheck.txt) do echo 'File in que:' $i; file -b $i done echo 'Done!'; File in que: /home/customerlogin/public_html/moodledata/filedir/00/0c/000c6a087a2a60e7757b83d35ab8ee87a1262da2 HTML document text File in que: /home/customerlogin/public_html/moodledata/filedir/00/25/00251b315b2ceada2dc53472bc5d9c0ff21bb13f UTF-8 Unicode English text, with very long lines, with no line terminators File in que: /home/customerlogin/public_html/moodledata/filedir/00/94/0094f387d402335d20321d7a27b04e1b70e4fb07 HTML document text File in que: /home/customerlogin/public_html/moodledata/filedir/00/9e/009ee54b612b13142a118319e411f2a92fbeba41 PDF document, version 1.7 File in que: /home/customerlogin/public_html/moodledata/filedir/01/17/01173864bd348636826491860b7ef063f2b5dc58 PDF document, version 1.7 File in que: /home/customerlogin/public_html/moodledata/filedir/01/52/0152b84372b0b393aee5b2f7d1ddfc2395857034 PDF document, version 1.7 File in que: /home/customerlogin/public_html/moodledata/filedir/01/7f/017f22518d140a627cbb9a43f3d5d1dfc5e9ea1d PDF document, version 1.7 IF there were any reference displayed above indicated a gzip file ... probably a backup of a course and might be worthy of keeping. Save those lines from filedbcheck.txt file to another text file 'keep.txt' and use keep.txt to move those files out to a 'keep' directory.  Later one can inspect those files by renaming individually and one at a time like mv 009ee54b612b13142a118319e411f2a92fbeba41 somebackup.mbz Then inspect the .mbz file ... tar zxvf somebackup.mbz moodle_backup. xml which extracts just the moodle_backup.xml file.  Looking at the top 20 lines of moodle_backup.xml might give enough info about the backup to decide if one needs to keep it or not. The moosh command to delete however wants the id column info of the row. Delete Moodle files from DB and possibly move them to trash. File IDs can be provided as arguments or on the standard input (with moosh file-delete -s). --flush option will remove the trashcan directory. Example 1: Remove files with IDs 10,20 and 30. moosh file-delete 10 20 30 So we have to find the ID number of the file. It's on the cloned test server where one could try: moosh file-delete -s | moosh file-dbcheck Note the commands are the other way round. Discalmer ... nope spelled it right ... your mileage might vary ... please don't hold me responsible! Strongly suggest cloning what is needed to another test server and trying things out there first! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Text: ﻿ You've got one of those 'double whammies'! :\ I don't.  But thinking outloud here, what about: file-datacheck Go through all files in Moodle data and check them for corruption. The check is to compare file's SHA to their file names. moosh -n file-datacheck On the system I am working on a glitch in hosting led to an index.php file present in moodledata/filedir/ which I hid ... mv index.php .index.php The command above kicked this out: /home/customerid/public_html/moodledata/filedir/.index.php Checksum does not match filename. That sounds lke moosh did see the file ... checked the database but couldn't find a checksum for that filename in the DB - didn't exist in DB. Yours might show one or more of those aweful contenthash references. f5fb96e8ef5e044b8f0cc9020876a4347e5fe3d6 Depending on how many, think now working with mysql client might be in order. Query mdl_files for filename like 'f5fb96e8ef5e044b8f0cc9020876a4347e5fe3d6' - and show filesize. If we know that's an orphaned DB reference, then change the query to one of removal of the row. If attempting bash loop, the text file looping through contains one liners of nothing but the contenthash. and in the 'action step' of the bash shell script my sql -u root -p'password' -e "use moodle;delete from mdl_files where contenthash = '$i';"; $i is one of those contenthash listings in the text file being looped. You could take it slow and steady ... rather than doing all of the contenthashes in the file do just one or two to see how that goes.    I usually have trouble at the end of such commands ... getting the = '$i';"; thing above right! :\ OR once get your list of contenthashes, remove one row via mysql> prompt. ResponsesInList.Title: Export students results in a workshop activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have setup a workshop with peer evaluation. I can access the results in moodle but I was looking for a method to export students results in a csv, ods or xls file but I couldn't find a solution. We are using Moodle 3.5.4+ Can any one help me on that ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Export students results in a workshop activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Zied, That's not too difficult if you know where to look If you'd go to your course and open Grades from the navigation bar (supposing you're using a Boost based theme), you're going to find a number of export options from the drop down menu at the top of the page. The more traditional path would be: Course menu > Grades > Grades administration > Export , where you can choose from the following export formats: OpenOffice spreadsheet Plain text file Excel spreadsheet XML file Once you're there, you'll find all the activities listed, with checkboxes next to them, so you can select which ones to export. For the Workshop activity, you should find 2 lines: [Workshop name] (task) [Workshop name] (assessment) Selecting both of these will assure you'll have all the numbers you're going to need. If you happen to need the user feedback as well, be sure to expand the Export format options to tick the corresponding options there. There's also a lot of information on this in the Moodle Docs on the subject .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Google Chrome/ Running Flash
ResponsesInList.Text: Charles, Ken's reply is the ultimate correct solution.  The issue has nothing to do with Moodle.  Moodle, and the Moodle resources/ activities , run in a web browser. The issue is that web browsers and mobile devices no longer support Flash for a host of reasons. Even if you try to implement a work-around solution for yourself (e.g. changing your browser settings), other users on the site will still encounter problems. There is a Moodle plugin that reports all instances of Flash content on your Moodle site, Flash Apocalypse . This is a helpful tool to determine all the modules that need to be updated. If you do not have access to the Captivate source files, you are in for a big job. If that is the case, there are tools available to extract all the components from a Flash file, but you will then need to reconstruct the Captivate project from the individual components.  In the end, that is not a bad idea because it provides an opportunity to redesign and develop modules that might be outdated. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: adding student's name & surname to attempt review
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello! I would be grateful if someone could suggest how to hack the page 'mod/quiz/review.php?attempt=###' so as to display the name and surname of the student who took the quiz on top of the table of the attempt review details. I see the student's name, surname and profile picture on the left, in the navigation block, which is excellent for an on-line use of the attempt review activity, but when I print the attempt review (for record storage), that is not included (=BIIIIIIG problem). The arrow in the picture points to the place where I would like to display the student's information (the box in red). My moodle version is 3.0+ (Build: 20151209) Hope someone could help. Massimiliano

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: adding student's name & surname to attempt review
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Massimiliano, Not recommended to hack core files and the Moodle you are using is no longer supported. However, since your Moodle is no longer supported, the odds are you will not wipe out your hack with an upgrade. So this is pretty easy to do. Open  the file for editing at: yourmoodle/mod/quiz/review.php Go to the blank line at line number 229 and add two more blank lines. Past the following code into line 230: // This will add a name line under the grade. e.g. Name Owen Money. $student = $DB->get_record('user', array('id' => $attemptobj->get_userid())); $summarydata['user'] = array( 'title'   => get_string('name', 'quiz'), 'content' => new action_link(new moodle_url('/user/view.php', array( 'id' => $student->id, 'course' => $attemptobj->get_courseid())), fullname($student, true)), ); Save your modified review.php file. Verify that it works by going to review a quiz results, and you should see something similar to the picture, even when Appearance is not set to show the user picture.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cannot approve or deny data requests
ResponsesInList.Text: cron is set to run automatically every 19 minutes If possible, make that interval shorter. The main cron.php is supposed to be executed as often as possible. In recent versions it should be ideally every minute. Only then it is able to effectively distribute the workload of all the scheduled tasks. Please refer to https://docs.moodle.org/en/Cron for details. As far as I know, the incoming subject's access requests go through pre-processing phases executed as ad-hoc tasks (in background, asynchronously) prior the admin's / privacy officer's input is expected.

ResponsesInList.Title: Tips to help manage recurrent blended course
ResponsesInList.Text: Forgive me for this rather general query, but I'd like to pick your brains to help me manage the following situation : I'm responsible for a 4 week long (college level) blended course. This course is offered multiple times to multiple sections (groups)  over the course of a term.  A number of learning resources and activities (forum, quiz, assignments) are offered online. The course is given by a number of lecturer that have different levels of knowledge about Moodle. We create one Moodle course per section. This process is repetitive and time consuming, especially when it comes to updating the dates for various activities. We do have the "dates" report plugin, but it doesn't make things much easier. It is not rare to "miss" one date. Not dramatic, but annoying. Does anybody know of any tools or techniques that would this task simpler? Among my peeves is the fact that there is no easy way to identify dates that don't make sense (i.e. dates that are before the actual declared start date of the course). Another problem is that there is no way (it seems) to randomly "repopulate" existing groups. You have to create new groups, and thus change all the relevant access restrictions. Any ideas you might have concerning these issues is welcome. Thanks! Best, Eric

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle - users kicked out during quiz "This computer was not authorized for this exam" before they got kicked out of exam/quiz.
ResponsesInList.Text: ﻿ According to an old doc https://docs.moodle.org/33/en/Quiz_settings Extra restrictions on attempts Require network address You can restrict access for a quiz to particular subnets on the LAN or Internet by specifying a comma-separated list of partial or full IP address numbers. This is especially useful for a proctored (invigilated) quiz, where you want to be sure that only people in a certain room are able to access the quiz. For example: 192.168. , 231.54.211.0/20, 231.3.56.211 There are three types of numbers you can use (you can not use text based domain names like example.com): Full IP addresses, such as 192.168.10.1 which will match a single computer (or proxy). Partial addresses, such as 192.168 which will match anything starting with those numbers. So two labs with how many students total ... all taking the quiz at the same time? Were there any error logs associated with this event?   Both moodle logs and raw server logs. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrictions and Activity Completion

ResponsesInList.Title: How can I bookmark Moodle in English posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All I am trying to find a way to bookmark posts that I may want to return to in the Moodle in English forum so that I can easily re-find them in the future.  I started to Subscribe to helpful forum posts, but now can't find how to see a list of all my subscribed threads. Can someone please tell me how to find my subscribed threads or suggest another good workflow for bookmarking threads, which I am not part of? Also when I do a forum search the results display the whole post in the list, instead of simply listing the post headings.  This can make it very difficult to scroll the list for the right answer to my issue.  Is there a way to set my search result page to only show the headings/summary in the list. Thanks Christine

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I bookmark Moodle in English posts
ResponsesInList.Text: I assume that you mean here, in Moodle.org.  But the process could be the same for courses within you school's Moodle. I can provide some ideas, but other people here in Moodle.org will share more. First, at the bottom of every post, you will see a "Permalink" link.  Click on this, and Moodle will show you the URL of this exact post.  Then, using your browser, you can add a Bookmark.  In many browsers, you can create a structure for your bookmarks, so you might create a folder for "moodle.org."  In most browser's, you can create a title, which could be the subject of the post or anything that you wish.  This is one method.  (I don't do this, however.  But you used the word "bookmark.")  I should mention that when I tell students "See my post..." I embed this Permalink as a hyperlink to "See my post..." and then when students click on it, they are taken right to my post! Since Moodle emails you posts, you can save your most important posts using your email client.  This is what I do on my Mac.  On my Mac, I can even "tag" emails with colors.  I tag my most important posts with an "orange" tag. As you have discovered, Moodle does have a Search feature for forums (which I should mention doesn't exist in the other major LMSs, like Blackboard and Canvas.)  Quite powerful.  No, I do not know if Moodle can show you only the subject in its search results, but this might be an interesting feature request!  However, a simple subject listing might not let you easily see where your search terms occurred in the post, so there are some trade-offs.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I bookmark Moodle in English posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick Thanks for the suggestions.  You are correct I am looking for better workflow ideas to improve my searching on Moodle.org when trying to troubleshoot Moodle admin issues. As an eLearning developer, moving more into LMS Administration, I had in mind the search and bookmarking features available on the Articulate heroes community.  I will follow your advice and get myself more organised to save/bookmark interesting posts via my browser or some other third party app. Any other tips anyone want to shares about how to upskill my LMS Administrator skills via Moodle.org community forums would be welcomed. Thanks Christine

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I bookmark Moodle in English posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Christine, I use bookmarks in Firefox browser...a whole bunch of bookmarks. Took me a while to realize, you can organize them by adding various folders. Make the folder names are meaningful to the type of bookmarks being set in each folder. e.g. I often name folders based on the Moodle forum names. Another method I had set up in a Moodle years ago, that got trashed, so I don't have the preset anymore, is to create a database activity for saving bookmarks. I had a couple of drop down menus so I could easily set info about the type of info the link was for. And, since database activity entries can be searched, it made it pretty easy look things up later.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I bookmark Moodle in English posts
ResponsesInList.Text: How about the User Favourites block? https://moodle.org/plugins/block_user_favorites

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I bookmark Moodle in English posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Christine, The problem that I have is that there are so many good ideas that trying to keep track of them does become difficult.  Yes, I have some bookmarks organized in my browser.  I have some ideas in my Moodle.org email inbox (by the way, I filter every post that I receive from Moodle.org and send them into a specific email folder), I print some items to PDFs and put them in an organized folder on my computer. The most helpful technique that I use is to have a file called "Moodle Notes" where I keep track of everything that I am doing in my Moodle.  For example, every update is noted in my Notes.  Every time that I make a setting change, I note it.  My entire install procedure is noted.  Important UNIX commands are in this file.  Etc.  And sometimes when I see a tip that I want to explore, I have a section in my Note for "Future Investigations." If you haven't explored installing a "local" version of Moodle, you should.  I find that having a local version helps me experiment and learn.  (I use MAMP on my Mac.)

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I was wondering if anyone knew of where I could find php_solr compiled as a windows dll for php 7.2 and nts. We are looking at ways to implement the global search on our set up, windows server php 7.2 as mod_fcgid so nts. I have had it running using php 7.1 in our test environment, but we have already moved 7.2 on live and cannot go back. I have looked but I cannot find the php_solr dll compiled for php 7.2 on the repo and I have even tried compiling it myself but I cannot seem to get it to work (top edge of my knowledge there) Any advie greatly appreciated Charles

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Solr php 7.2 / 7.3 Windows nts
ResponsesInList.Text: You said 'any advice' ... so here goes ... with justifications? Run Simple Search instead. Why? If I am correct about your setup ... Windows running Apache ? Running Windows and Apache ... apache not native to windows.  If one has to manually compile the php_solr dll now, what about in the future when Moodle releases a higher version and requires a higher version of PHP to go along with that?  Compile again? Solr requires Java ... another service ... on another port ... and yet another attack vector for those who would try to do harm to your site.   The indexes for solr search are really in the java app. Many moons ago the only way one could get an AMP stack was to compile each piece with proper supports.  It was a pain in the arse.  While it was very educational, decided it was also a lot of work ... that had to be repeated too frequently. Gotta enough to do with adding more, so I changed my mind set. So to 'future proof' (as much as one can) ...  suggest you might  be better off using Simple Search. my 2 'sense' ... nope, spelled it right! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Solr php 7.2 / 7.3 Windows nts
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks. I get what you're saying. At the moment this is a research project for us to improve how we use search. As to the why: we've been running in house search plugin for a number of years and it works at a level similar to the simple search with a few things specific to us thrown in, it works pretty well but the extended features (such as file contents indexing and word variants) are whats attractive to us. I'm not worried about apache on windows as we've got that dialled in now, all the components can be sourced readily from php and apache lounge etc,  its just the php_solr module that's an issue. As for solr itself, if we were to use it it would be on a server we use for such occasions that is not externally accessible outside our network and is locked down as much as possible. Thanks tho Charles

ResponsesInList.Title: Help please family
ResponsesInList.Text: How can I hide the students information from other students? There are seeying each other personal  information, Step by step please.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help please family
ResponsesInList.Text: This would have been better asked in the General Help forum, which is maybe why you didn't get a response sooner as it has nothing to do with the Chat activity. You can hide certain bits of information: see the docs or you can entirely disable a student’s access to view other students by editing the permissions for the student role: Edit the 'student role' under: Site administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles Click on the "Advanced options" button to show all the options for capabilites (Not Set, Allow, Prevent, Prohibit) Search for moodle/course:viewparticipants Select the 'Prohibit' option Save changes The 'participants' link will still show in the Navigation block, and the student can see their own profile - but they can't see other information about students.
