ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz results
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Louis, It is normal for me that when I make a forum entry, I get an email copy of it. As for typing characters that do not normally appear on your keyboard, it is easily taken care of. I do it all the time when working on, or creating new keyboard layouts for the typing tutor plugin, MooTyper. To me this is the hard way. Go to Start > Windows accessories > Character map. My default font is Courier New with character set of Unicode. Scroll down through the table of characters, until you see the one you need. Click on it, then click on, Select, then click on Copy. Go to where you need to type the character and Paste it. Repeat for other characters as needed. The reason I think this is hard is that it is easy to overlook the character when scrolling through the table. My preferred method is to just install the Windows keyboard driver for each language that I create a MooTyper keyboard layout for. Then any character for that language is just two clicks away. On the bottom right of your screen, click on Eng US, or what ever language preference you are using, and then click, Language. In the new window popup, click on, Add a language. In another  new popup, start typing Croation. After the third letter you should see two Croation options., so click on the one you want, then click on Next. Remove the check marks for Set as my Windows display language, Speech, and Handwriting. Click on Install. After a short time, your list of Language preferences at the bottom right of your screen should include, Croation. To use it, select it, type the letter you want, then switch back to English. Of course this method does require you to know which key the č is mapped to. In this case it is the semi-colon. This takes a whole lot more time to explain and setup, but using method two to type, č, only takes two mouse clicks to switch to Croation, then two more to switch back to my normal English.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz results
ResponsesInList.Text: By the way, do not worry that having extra Windows keyboard drivers might impact your computer, it's speed, or it's ability to work with Moodle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Applying Moodle on a large University
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Adam, An interesting question with a lot of interesting answers as well. I've seen both multitenant and big single Moodle implementations in universities I've worked with. There are a lot things to consider before deciding in favor of one or the other: How's your organization's application administration set up? Do you want to host on-premise or in the cloud? Does Moodle have to be set up to interface with a Student Information System, an Identity Provider or external authentication platform? Does every department need a specific configuration, or is most of this covered in one general config? Do you need to interface with tools like TurnItIn or similar for plagiarism detection? ... Setting up connectionsfor multiple Moodles to a SIS, to authentication, to an IDP or an external service like TurnItIn may not always be possible and will most definitely increase your workload in configuration and troubleshooting. In that sense, it seems logical to set up one big cloud-hosted Moodle with enough hardware capacity to cater the needs of the entire uni. Also, consider this for a multitenant set up: What happens when a student in department 1 (Moodle 1) wishes to take electives from department 2 (Moodle 2) and department 4 (Moodle 4)? He/she won't have a central dashboard outlining all of his/her course details, but 3 or more. He/she may have SSO access to all Moodles, but has to manage his/her dashboards from different URLs. In the last few years, I've seen various successful Moodle implementations in academic / higher education with well over 15k users running smoothly.

ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks a lot for your help. I've developed a Moodle before but of one faculty, it was the Information Engineering faculty at my university, now they want to apply it on the whole university. The first problem is: I think the university (Tishreen University) has about 50k students, and I'm afraid that Moodle won't handle this number of students. The second problem: Each faculty has its own organizational hierarchy, and a student from one faculty cannot see or has any action with the other faculties. I've seen such multitenant called IOMAD, can you please tell me if it is a good solution. I think it would be after some modifications, but I've been told that IOMAD lacks documentation and buggy!!!! ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Applying Moodle on a large University
ResponsesInList.Text: Adam, RE: Your first problem.   Moodle can easily handle 50K students. The issue is not Moodle, it is the capacity and configuration of your web and database servers.  There are quite a few sites with over 100K users, see https://moodle.net/stats/ and https://www.moodlenews.com/2017/lets-dispel-the-notion-once-and-for-all-that-moodle-is-not-scalable/ Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Applying Moodle on a large University
ResponsesInList.Text: Adam, The way I configure Moodle for multiple divisions in an organization is to create separate course categories. Each category can have its own theme and front page . I then assign Managers to each category. It is not true multi-tenancy, but does work fairly well if you do not need to totally isolate access among the various divisions. Totara is a Moodle fork that handles multi-tenancy and hierarchical admin roles very well. Also, Moodle just announced Moodle Workplace that is due to be released mid 2019.  This version will have many of the features currently in Totara. IOMAD provides a basic multi-tenant / hierarchical structure on top of Moodle. It is very easy to add to or remove from current Moodle sites. The main problems I've encountered with IOMAD are a lack of documentation and code that can be a bit buggy. There is a GitHub repository for reporting bugs and tracking issues. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic Allocation of Course Module Content by Role Upon Moodle Account Self-Registration.  Is this possible? Please Help!
ResponsesInList.Text: Here are two suggestions. 1 is not as neat, but is less work - 2 is visa versa. 1) There is an enrolment plugin called enrol_auto. This can point to certain attributes and then decide whether to let users in based on attributes in their moodle profile. Where we ran moodle (before the VLE was switched, political decision), we had it protecting staff only pages. And pulled in a Staff or Student flag (per user) from an AD attribute we specified. e.g. on a staff training page, a rule was set so 'if Institution = Staff, let them in'. This assumes you have the attribute you need in AD (or have access to their MIS/IT people, to the point they can provision an attribute for you). 2) You can use Database Enrolments - you'd need a script to auto-provision the pages (as in, get a list of users from AD, and for each run, write a db row which has their username and the moodle course ID they need to see - and run this daily to make sure new starters are covered, maybe remove old users from pages when they leave the organisation), but we've had that working before for certain parts of the site. This would need a lookup to their 'role' either from AD or another database. For the record, I have implemented both. But as we're mostly using a completely different VLE now, I'd need to reread the manual for the Database method to remember exactly what format to make the database table needed for approach 2.

This is operating system dependent. Sure there are methods for Windows, e.g. https://docs.moodle.org/en/NTLM_authentication . But I am not familiar with them. We have a couple of specialists in the forums though. - Automatic enrollment: Analog to authentication there is https://docs.moodle.org/en/LDAP_enrolment . For a major operation like this, you may want to get an offer from a Moodle Partner - user authentication is something which easily irritates the user!

ResponsesInList.Title: Page API external usage
ResponsesInList.Text: Can we use the Page API outside Moodle to create new pages that are related (i.e collect and insert and update) to Moodle database ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Page API external usage
ResponsesInList.Text: Probably not like you're thinking. The Moodle Page API is concerned with building the HTML of a page - HTML headers & title, adding links to Javascript & CSS files, etc. - rather than being a API for content management. If you want to create web pages of content, you need the Page resource . Conceivably you could build something to post content to Moodle's new Page resource code, but I'm not sure how easy or reliable that would be. HTH , Dave.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grader Report issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Josue Emmanuel, Yes, this configuration is quite easy to do. Create categories in your grade book. Provide a name for each category that is descriptive of the graded activities/items you want in that category. You can select and move items in the grade book into the desired categories.  Also when you create a new graded activity you can specify which category it should be in. Use Natural grade aggregation for the entire grade book and for each category.  Apply any custom weighting to the items. Carefully read through the Moodle documentation on grade book setup https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Grades (English) https://docs.moodle.org/all/es/Calificaciones (Español)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grader Report issue -  grade book setup options
ResponsesInList.Text: Jose asked another question in a private email.  I'm duplicating that here because it might be helpful to others. Question:  "On the same token, I would like to ask you about how I could hide the follloeing functions to my teachers. I would definitely thank your HELP."   The question was how to hide/remove the grade book setup functions so teachers cannot change grade book settings. Response: Jose, There is no easy way to remove all those grade book editing capabilities for teachers.  Here are some suggestions: There are two teacher roles:  a) Teacher , and b) Non-editing Teacher .  A Teacher has full control over the course. A Non-editing Teacher can facilitate the course but cannot create/change/delete content, and has limited capability on the grade book setup.  So, you might consider using the Non-editing Teacher role in cases where you want to limit what can be done to grade book settings. However, be aware that this also removes the ability to edit the course. There is an admin setting where the grade book configuration options can be set to a drop-down menu instead of tabs.  This makes the settings options less visible and might be all you need.  Teachers will still be able to access them, but might not see the drop-down menu.  To eliminate the tabs on the grade book go to Site administration ... Grades ... General settings .  Scroll down the page about halfway to the Navigation method setting.  Change that to 'Dropdown menu'.  Save the change. Regards, Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  moodledata folder
ResponsesInList.Text: The 'right way' happened during initial install of each moodle. First, to be on the safe side, I'd backup the target site for the first copy ...  target site is your moodle2. The following is a possible 'fix' If you already have a moodledata for the first site ... check it's config.php file for that path and name. Let's say that config.php file says: /home1/hostnname/public_html/moodledata (there should be a hidden .htaccess file in there to prevent anyone with a browser from crawling moodledata due to it's location in public_html Manually make a directory for site 2 In your example you might have adjust 'hostname' ... I have not below. mkdir /home1/hostname/public_html/moodledata2 Then recursively copy all the contents of /home1/hostname/public_html/moodledata to the directory you just created ... from the directory /home1/hostname/public_html/moodledata cp -rp * .* /home1/hostname/public_html/moodledata2 That assumes you have enough space to do this. The cp means copy ... the -r means to recursively copy and the 'p' preserves ownerships/permissions. Then change the config.php file for site 2 to point to new moodledata2 See if that works. Then repeat for the other site. Can tell you beyond a doubt you will have orphaned files in filedir of copied data directories and/or incorrect data in mdl_files table that linked to files in the site you copied to. Lots of re-linking to do. Best of luck! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Cron Won't Run
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm running Moodle 3.5.3 on Ubuntu server 18.04LTS. I downloaded a TurnKey Linux virtual appliance to help ease set up. It's running, and people can login, our trainers can create content without issue, but there are a couple of quibbles that I think are related. First, as I understand from documentation, when you add a user to a cohort that it enrolled in multiple courses, the user should automatically be added to those courses as well. That isn't happening. Second, when an announcement is created in a course, it doesn't notify the users via email. While that could be related to my email set up, I think it's also related to the fact that Cron isn't running correctly, or at all. I've had this server up for 3 weeks, and I have Cron tasks that are scheduled to happen every 15 minutes and they have never run. I've had to manually run the cohort sync, but even though it executes without error, it isn't actually syncing new users. How would I go about checking what's wrong with Cron? I've looked in the documentation, and that didn't yield enough detail to get me started.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cron Won't Run
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been researching this issue, and managed to find that cron.hourly isn't running as it should. Here's the error message that I receive. From root@moodle  Mon Jan 21 19:17:01 2019 X-Original-To: root From: root@moodle (Cron Daemon) To: root@moodle Subject: Cron <root@moodle>    cd / && run-parts --report /etc/cron.hourly MIME-Version: 1.0 Content-Type: text/plain; charset=US-ASCII Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit X-Cron-Env: <SHELL=/bin/sh> X-Cron-Env: <PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin> I've tried to search for the error message, but have had no luck finding out what it means.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cron Won't Run
ResponsesInList.Text: It took a good bit of digging, but I was able to find out what the error meant. The script in /etc/cron.hourly/moodle looks like this: ﻿ #!/bin/bash su www-data -c "/usr/bin/php /var/www/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php > /dev/null 2>&1" The problem comes from having su at the beginning of the command, rather than sudo. If we finger www-data, we find that the shell is /usr/sbin/nologin. Thanks to this forum post on StackExchange, I was able to learn that su always runs the shell written in /etc/passwd, even if using su -c as above. That makes su incompatible with /usr/sbin/nologin. Armed with better information, I tried changing the command in the script. I changed it to look like this. sudo -u www-data "/usr/bin/php /var/www/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php > /dev/null 2>&1" I tested it, and alas, it still didn't work. At this point, I'm guessing that something about the TurnKey Linux set up screwed up cron. Also, every time I manually run the cron.php file manually, it breaks Moodle. I can login, but all of the formatting is gone, and it's just a jumbled mess.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cron Won't Run
ResponsesInList.Text: Qualifications for this response:  NONE Don't run TurnKey .. .but have had to do something similar on remotely hosted dedicated VM 's. TurnKey Linux is Debian based distro. https://www.turnkeylinux.org/about They do have a knowledge base ... have you searched there? Was the install one that included Moodle? something like: TKL 13 Moodle VM Do you see somthing for cli when issuing: php -m *shows php modules/extensions) See anything that suggest 'cli'? Sluething on which php command line environment is finding first. As superuser in system/ssh, look at the environment of the shell: env [ENTER] You'll see a PATH line.   Copy that path line to a text document on local computer. which php [ENTER] That should show the full path to the php executable ... but is it the one needed for command line? Find out: /path/to/shown/in/which/php -v If see a (cli) in the output of above command that's the one needed for CLI sciprts. If, however, see cgi-bin or something like that, that's the PHP for the web service ... can't use that one for CLI scripts. To find where it might be, has to use the find command ... and crawl your entire system to see where the php-cli might have been hidden.  As superuser of system ... if in sudo you can sudo -s then provide the password of the account you login with to 'stay' root. find / -name php [ENTER] That will take a long time ... be patient. All that find will list are not necessarily php executables sooo ... now it's time to list those locations long and see attributes on the 'php' if a file ... One of the hits for the find command might be /usr/bin/php As an example: [root@server ~]# ls -l /usr/bin/php -rwxr-xr-x. 1 root root 4856520 Jan 12 10:10 /usr/bin/php we can see it's a file and executable. Uhhh ... no offense, but don't understand TurnKey on Ubuntu.  Looking for an 'easy button'?  Those sometimes turn into 'not so easy to run nor maintain'.   Devil is in the details which are kinda like 'one off'.  And one can find all sorts of info on Ubuntu ... fewer resources for TurnKey. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Text: You could create a Feedback activity on the front page (make sure you have “Allow Full Anonymous” switched in the settings) - and then link to that from the Course Summary box. See https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Using_Feedback#Guest_surveys If you’re using 3.6, you can set Stealth mode on the Feedback activity so it won’t be seen by anyone unless they have the direct link (which will be in the course summary). Before 3.6, you can add the Feedback activity via the Main Menu block and then hide the Main Menu block (do NOT hide the Feedback activity).

For some reason it seems like the installed PHP version will get automatically upgraded to the latest PHP major version (like PHP 7.1 to 7.2 to 7.3) when running "apt-get update ; apt-get -y dist-upgrade" even though I can't see what dependency that would cause that. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Php script names
ResponsesInList.Text: Pardon the long response ... but ... You appear to be hosted with a provider that offers multiple versions of PHP ... some of which have reached end of life and probably shouldn't be used by any customer. Running the cron script in 3.4.x code does require the higher version of PHP (7.0 ... which also has reached end of life).   The docs at Moodle show how to setup cron on linux systems that are standalone ... ie, not the linux  distro as built/modified by provider.   Thus, the directions that show /usr/bin/php as the path actually is correct on most systems, on your providers system offering multple versions is in-correct. So ... how to fix ... From your ssh shell into your account, type: env [ENTER] Look for a "PATH' line with variables/paths. I can't share with you what that should look like on your system. Will say that showed me on a remotely hosted system with a provider that shall remain nameless ... right now ... that the customers environment found the php5 first and thus would not run any of the scripts in moodlecode/admin/cli/ which includes the cron.php script. The following probably not yours but here's what it looked like on the system upon which I was working: PATH=/usr/local/cpanel/3rdparty/lib/path-bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/opt/cpanel/composer/bin The command which php would show /usr/bin/php ... but that was NOT the php for CLI but for the web. whereis php if whereis available on your shell, showed other paths ... not included in the environment. To set up the cron job on that system, had to use the path to the PHP version 7 cli ... which on that system happened to be in /usr/local/bin/ As a test, once you find the paths to the php executables: Use the full path to php to see the version and which: php -v on the system in the example here showed this: PHP 7.1.26 (cgi-fcgi) (built: Jan 14 2019 19:44:52) That's the PHP for the web ... see the (cgi-fcgi). However, this one /usr/local/bin/php -v shows PHP 7.1.26 (cli) (built: Jan 14 2019 19:44:32) ( NTS ) see the 'cli' above. So in the path to php in the setup of the cron job on the example system: /usr/local/bin/php /full/path/to/moodle/code/admin/cli/cron.php Then worked as expected. All the scripts in moodlecode/admin/cli/ then all require the path to be: /usr/local/bin/php ... Hope that helps. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

During the academic year we run face-to-face teaching with Moodle for support, for modules that are in Moodle as 18 courses.  The students have two full academic years in which to submit assignments after which they are classed as late and can only achieve a pass, with six months grace in which to submit late assignments. Right now we enrol students using cohort sync and manually un-enrol after the appropriate duration and use assignment due dates within Moodle.  With many future different enrollment dates and therefore many different assignment due dates this is not going to work. I would appreciate any suggestions from those with much more experience than I have. Fi

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrolment types and assignment due dates
ResponsesInList.Text: I administer Moodle for a college with an enrollment of about 1300 students. We have both in person and online courses. I use two enrollment/unenrollment methods: 1. Students are enrolled through LDAP . Since we already have all of the students in LDAP, we make groups of students based on course IDs and use the core LDAP enrollment plugin. I'm not sure what the rest of your infrastructure looks like for students, but if you have LDAP you can manage them that way. This is great because it automatically manages the enrollments and I don't have to worry about it at all. https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/LDAP_authentication https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/LDAP_enrolment 2. Teachers are enrolled via CSV upload (this is probably best for you). CSV upload is very easy to learn and quite powerful. It's also good because most databases will give you a CSV file to work with, making the transmission of information from whatever database manages enrollment to the Moodle fairly easy. it's not automatic like LDAP but it's easier to set up and manage from scratch. https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Upload_users With LDAP, students are suspended when unenrolled in the LDAP manager. With CSV, you can either suspend or unenroll using another csv upload. It all depends on where you get your enrollment information from.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Urgent Help: Additional HTML Code.
ResponsesInList.Text: I solved it, but for whoever interests: Simply access the moodle database , and manually remove the field that has changed. In my case I used this query: UPDATE mdl_config SET value = '' WHERE name = "additionalhtmltopofbody"; After that it was necessary to clear the Moodle cache, just go to the folder \moodledata\cache\, and rename the folder cachestore_file, for example, to cachestore_file_bkp and then restart the Apache service.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Backup: Error 500
ResponsesInList.Text: Please, i really need help...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Backup: Error 500
ResponsesInList.Text: Suggest checking server error logs for entries just before the 500's in the log. And, try turning on debugging and then try backing up the same course. Unfortunately, error 500's don't have one specific reason.  Not only that, but depending upon how one is hosted, protective services on your server could be the reason for the error.   Those protective services (like mod_secure) report back to apache a 'false error' rather than disclose the real reason. It could be you just have under-powered hosting ... those really cheapo accounts on some systems. Got linux?  Have ssh access into the moodle? If so, one can backup a course via a backup.php file in moodlecode/admin/cli/ While that does take apache out of the loop, those hidden protective services might be disclosed. If you could provide a little more on setup ... operating system, where hosted and how hosted, etc. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What's going wrong? I can't send a message?
ResponsesInList.Text: mmm Not a good idea to go from v3.0 to v3.6, so yes, very likely there was something changed in, say, v3.3, which is required in v3.6. Go to Site Admin > Development > Debugging and in Debug Messages, change it to "ALL reasonable PHP debugging messages." Check out the results and see what error messages you might be getting. In the mean time, you might want to check through some of the Messaging documentation about what might be happening.  Alternatively, you might have some PHP coding experience, so check what might be different here, by looking at this page describing the Messaging API The only other alternative is to restore your v3.0, upgrade to v3.2, then v3.4 then v3.6. That way you may also catch any number of other developing problems. Suggest though do it on your test Moodle with the last backup of your v3.1 database , and when complete, you should be able to replace the codebase and the database as well as the moodledata folder all at once. Not an easy trick, and I have only ever performed such a drastic strep once before, it worked, but there was a lot of angst and effort beforehand. (Other reasons though.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Groups in moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Here's how we do it. Create the forum. In the Description box, enter the instructions you want everyone to see. Make groups. An editing teacher in each group creates topics. If you create topics outside of a group, all groups can view the topic, but none can reply. To allow teachers to only view their group, go to course settings > groups > group mode > separate groups; force separate groups > yes; default grouping > none

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: File Selector Not Working
ResponsesInList.Text: Suggest 'host file trick' would make the migration 'easier' as far as keeping the same FQDN. In a Mac, one would edit the /etc/hosts file and add a line that would be checked before DNS is queried (same could be done on Windows workstation although not as easily).   Entry looks like: xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx moodle.bviu.org newmoodle where xxx.xxx is the private IP of the new server.  The 'newmoodle' is only a shortcut/aliased name which one would not be using when migrating a server to new digs. With that entry in hosts file one would not be able to see the real site ... only the one being migrated/updated/upgraded. No need to do search and replace on DB then ... before or after migration.   The only change to make it live is change DNS (outside and inside) to point to the new 10. (or private IP) mapped to the same outside IP.  DNS propagation time is relatively short these days - and one can help that along little by digging the DNS server for your domain ... external DNS as well as internal DNS. On the old server, login as admin, go to Server Admin,  Environment, update the component. In the drop down list for which moodle version, yours would should Moodle 3.3.x to begin, select each newer/higher version and see what Moodle says about PHP version and MySQL version and any other environment item it checks. There's your 'roadmap' for planning the updates/upgrades on the new server. On the newer server ... PHP version is?  MySQL version is? One can get too high with PHP and thus incompat with 3.3.x of code. https://docs.moodle.org/33/en/Upgrading#Check_the_requirements https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Moodle_3.3_release_notes#Database_requirements Might need to look at the same docs for the target version of Moodle. In addition, on the new server ... locate nginx error logs ... don't run nginx myself .. and php error logs ... php error logs could be in directories where the error occurs to see if you can't get clues as to the error screen shown to you. Command such as: find ./* -name error_log from the moodle code directory  would show locations of those error logs and one could, of course, view them via cat. Also, on the new server, seLinux running?  Is it in enforcing mode (default)? Check with: ﻿ sestatus Running anything extra on new server for security/protections ... php related?   Hopefully not something old like suPHP. And lastly ... the error screen doesn't mention if it's nginx or connection to DB server.  Check the MySQL logs as well. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Until now I have hosted Moodle environments for clients on shared web hosting platforms by different providers (not VPS or dedicated servers) and these packages have been sufficient. It seems that now it is not possible to install Moodle on these shared hosting sites since they do not allow for the environmental prerequisites of Moodle 3.6, in particular the MySQL database structure (Barracuda table format instead of Antelope and innodb settings). Please see image attached. When you try to install Moodle 3.6 on a shared hosting package these critical environmental issues are flagged and it is not possible to complete the install. The problem comes that when you try to implement the required changes to the My SQL database through the cPanel on the shared hosting site. It is not possible because barracuda is not supported on these types of packages and making the innodb changes is also not possible. The leap in cost from a shared hosting package to a VPS or a dedicated server is prohibitive for certain smaller institutions. Can anyone enlighten me on this? For example, is there a a workaround to the flagged critical environmental issues in order to be able to complete and use the install where barracuda is not supported and the innodb changes are not permitted? Or is there a provider out there that offers the shared web hosting package that supports minimum requirements for Moodle 3.6?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: This causes masses of confusion... Barracuda is only required to run utf8mb4 otherwise it is optional (although you will get a warning). What is your current charset and collation?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: I changed it to utf8mb4_unicode_ci as I thought it was a requirement but these critical errors were showing up before I changed it. I can't get past the page in the images attached since I can't change to barracuda. But I made this change after I saw these errors. I can't get past this environmental checks page until the two critical errors are resolved. I'm attaching the config.php contents (minus sensitive info) if that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you *sure* they were critical errors? They were probably just orange warnings. Changing the character set and collation without changing to Barracuda is what threw up the red warning.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: They are errors that don't allow me to proceed with the install. These errors came up during the install process, without me making any changes. I had created the database and the data directory and then launched the install using the URL where the Moodle code is installed. As you can see from the image, I only have the option "Reload" at the bottom of the page. But as I cannot change to barracuda on the shared hosting site reloading makes not difference.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Yeh - that's *now*. But if the character set is utf8 rather than utf8mb4 you won't get these errors.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: OK. For now I have solved this cul-de-sac by deleting the config.phy that the install had created, changing the charset and collation to UFT8 and starting the install process again. This time, although the warning comes up it is not critical so I am able to proceed and complete the install. I notice that there was a long discussion on the problem of Barracuda in the shared hosting sites elsewhere. Thanks for your help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: "solved this cul-de-sac" ... congrats! Don't think you mentioned what version of MySQL shared hosting is running. Granted you've solved the current hickup ... but ... on shared hosting, could be facing other issues when the provider decides to upgrade their MySQL from (am guessing) 5.7 - whose EoL is ﻿ Oct 2020 at present) to 8.0(x)? Might be worth striking up a conversation with hosting provider about shared DB server ... and the version of PHP as well. Not all providers are the same ... have been involved in assisting a couple of Moodle admin's whose hosting providers have upgraded the PHP on shared systems, thus breaking the very old version of Moodle they were running (yes, should have been upgraded years ago). Even after transfer of account to their 'dedicated'/VPS for an increase in hosting fees, of course, it was interesting to discover that only PHP 5.6 (reached end of life) and PHP 7.0 (also reached end of life) were available. Now a days, me thinks, attempting to find the 'fine print' in shared hosting offerings requires asking the right questions ... which is difficult if you don't know what you don't know! :\ 2 cent thoughts. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Indeed, Ken, "for now". Exactly the problem. You've hit the nail on the head, and also, as you say, applies to the much pricier VPS option too. For the record, this new install is to replace a 2.9, which ground to a halt on the same hosting service for exactly the reasons you point out - auto upgrade of php and mysql leaving Moodle code inoperable. In this case I was not even able to back up courses and restore. All has to be done manually, although I'm still looking at exporting and importing MySQL tables data to try and save some time. Hosting services update without notice and then advise after the fact , it seems hoping for some congratulations when, in fact, you could throttle them. Accepted, sysadmins should be on top of this, but on the ground experience shows that there are many instances when this just cannot happen. Yes, the small print - why search it out. We see "Moodle" as an option for the shared offering and assume it works. Or we see "Softaculous" knowing that it facilitates Moodle install and just believe it is all designed for what we need. You will never find the issues discussed in this thread until it is too late, I mean after contracting the service and working in the environment. Great input and useful for many scenarios, I imagine.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL requirements in 3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Matthew, its good to see both Howard and Ken helping you along. If you have SSH access to your hosted server, consider backing up your MySQL database and moodledata folders, and moving them down to your own computer.  Here are examples of code that worked for me on my old Bluehost hosted server.  You might need to study this code, make changes, and apply it to your own.  I think that it is a good idea to have a backup of what was last working for you. For the database: mysqldump -urjerzmoodle3db -p --opt -rmoodle3db.sql moodle3db For moodledata: tar cvfz moodledata-backup.tgz ../moodledata/ Many hosted servers will provide SSH access (if you ask).  Without SSH, one typically might use phpMyAdmin from their control panel for the database backup, and for moodledata, one can often use the "FileManager" utility that hosted servers tend to provide. These backup usually end up on your server, and you still need to move them to your computer.  I don't know how big your Moodle install was, so these files might be quite large and hard to move around. Howard and Ken will let us know if there is a better way.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hendrick, In your case, I strongly advise using a video streaming service such as Vimeo, Wistia, or even YouTube to embed videos in Moodle. Most streaming services have viewing privacy settings that prevent general viewing.  I use Vimeo quite often, and they have a setting where the video can be private and embedded only on a specific domain .  The cost is quite reasonable.  Several advantages are: The servers are optimized for streaming videos. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Reduce video size when uploading?!
ResponsesInList.Text: I use a lot of videos in my courses, so I will give you a few of my own idea. 1) As you can see, we all advise against uploading big files to moodle, and videos are among the biggest, of course.  Videos make Moodle backups much larger, causing other issues, and often the server that is serving your Moodle is not optimized to deliver videos.  In my own case, as an example, my videos are on my school's video streaming server. 2) You cannot prevent students from downloading or copying videos.  For example, a student can use their smartphone's camera to record the video.  And there are other easy ways to copy anything shown on a computer screen.  So I suggest that you consider getting this idea to "prevent downloading" out of your head, and to not let it constrain you. 3) I forget which Vimeo service one needs to buy, but the second or third tier Vimeo product can provide you a fully qualified URL for your video.  This is the one to embed into your Moodle course.  It will appear that the video is in your Moodle, but the video is actually on the Vimeo server.  I don't sense anything in your writings that you are trying to avoid the cost of Vimeo's service.  It's your choice, to avoid individual accounts, you have to centralize all videos to one account, which lacks convenience.  So, which do you prefer with Vimeo, convenience or cost? 4) The speed of recompressing a two-hour long video depends upon your computer and software.  If the time is too long, get a faster computer or faster software.  Also, be careful to study compression settings.  There is always a trade-off between quality and size.  For small videos, I tend to use 720x480, with a target bitrate of around 2Mbps.   Of course, mp4.  For simply "recompression" I have a product on my Mac called "Total Video Converter Pro." On my Mac, it takes less than 5 minutes to recompress a 2-hour long video. As you can see, videos present challenges, and there are many ways and many trade-offs to consider. Okay, here's a demo.  I am sharing with you below one of my course videos which is 1440x960, 4Mbps target.  This video is 259MB in size, 28 minutes long, and is on my university's video server.  Below is how it would appear in Moodle.  Only people in this discussion will see this video. (Yes, I cannot prevent you from downloading it, if you wish.  It is copyrighted, so if you do decide to use it in your course without my permission , and I find out, I will sue you for not getting my permission. The more money that your school has, the more aggressive I will be in my lawsuit.) http://streaming.iowa.uiowa.edu/business/rjerz/bas/Excel-Tables_and_PivotTable.mp4

ResponsesInList.Text: After further investigation, it appears that there are two aspects to completion from a database standpoint. The first is in the table I noted, regarding whether the activity is completed. However, making the record exist as completed is not enough to unlock the activity for that user. The second part, as far as I can tell, is the building of records in the course_modules table, where a reference is made in a record to the id of a previous record, regarding whether that record (which reference the course_modules_completion table?) is reporting a state of completion. So, because the records in course_modules are built as an activity is accessed, it does not appear that an activity which has not been accessed is able to be marked as complete. As best as I can tell. If anyone wants to chime in, feel free. My plan at this point is to create a second course group which allows access without completion tracking, and enroll "completed" students into those courses accordingly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: v3.6 Which DB table can be used to pre-set lesson progress completion?
ResponsesInList.Text: For those who might read this in the future, I was able to figure out how to achieve what I wanted originally: enter information into the database so that an activity for a student can be pre-set marked as complete before they view it (because they completed it elsewhere in a different system). I'm not sure why the following is needed as a two-part process, but if a record is inserted into the mdl_course_modules_completion table with the proper: coursemoduleid userid completionstate='0' viewed='1' timemodified=unix timestamp And then the same record is updated so that completionstate is set to ' 1 ', then the activity will be considered as completed on a refresh of the page, for example, and a check mark will be shown. Any next restrictions of activity will be unrestricted. Not sure how it will work as a batch process, due to whatever happens between those two steps (maybe a cron job?) but if I get that far I might post more.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Menus and tabs not working after upgrading to Moodle 3.4.1
ResponsesInList.Text:
I know this is an
old post, but I observed identical symptoms and this was one of the
few results that Google found, so I wanted to share my experience. In my case, the
issue was caused by junk metadata stored in Mac OS resource forks
related to the quarantine feature of Mac OS. When I packed up the
Moodle directory for upload to the webserver with the tar command,
the metadata was split into separate hidden files, and that metadata
somehow ended up interspersed in some dynamically generated
JavaScript. The solution is to create a clean tarball with the
metadata stripped out. The way I did this was to tar the directory
from within a Linux virtual machine running in Parallels. Another option is to
set an environment variable before you tar up the directory, as
explained here: https://superuser.com/questions/259703/get-mac-tar-to-stop-putting-filenames-in-tar-archives Although I haven’t
tested that method yet. Anyway, I hope that
helps someone suffering from phantom metadata in their JavaScript.

ResponsesInList.Title: Course Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All - I am new to Moodle Administration. I am working with an installation of Moodle (2.12)  in the section on Completion Tracking, it was NOT set up to select  the individual activities within the course to be included in the Aggregation Method (Aggregation Method set to ALL). When I updated these selections for the activities to include them (Completion Tracking), I thought this would update the Course Complete column in the Course Completion Report.  It did not. Can anyone tell me why and what I need to do to make that column be correctly updated?  I want to know which students successfully complete all activities in a course and as a result have completed the course. Thanks Lisa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lisa I do not have a Moodle 2.1.2 to try it out on, but course completion info is calculated during a "scheduled task." Or in the old versions of Moodle (which you have) when the "cron" job runs. These are background tasks that run every X minutes or hours in the background. See the FAQ #1 here: https://docs.moodle.org/21/en/Course_completion_FAQ (Moodle version 2.1 docs) It might be that your completion data will not be displayed until that has been run. And you site might not have a cron job configured to run. Or it might be configured to run very infrequently. If so on the Site Administration notifications page there is often a message saying that " Cron has not been run for 24 hours."  See here for information on cron(its tech'y). https://docs.moodle.org/21/en/Cron The quickest way to try it out, is to run the cron job from your web browser, from the site administration area of your Moodle at: [your-moodle-site]/admin/cron.php Fingers crossed it works. If it does and it has not run in a long time, it might take a while

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing students from disable notifications
ResponsesInList.Text:
The capability you want to disable is... 
```text
moodle/user:editownmessageprofile
```
 You should edit the 'Authenticated user' role and un-tick the Allow for that capability.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing students from disable notifications
ResponsesInList.Text: It works like a charm! I found out that this capaibility set to "Allow" to  "Authenticated user", overrides the settings for the other roles set to "Prohibit". ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I screwed up & deleted the Clean theme
ResponsesInList.Text: Good!  Glad to hear it.  Just a word of caution ... account/site backups are only as good as when they were made.  Example: so if the last SiteGround account backup was made a week ago and that's what is restored ... yes, the code gets reverted back (problem solved there), but so does the database on an account restore.   Moodle sites that are used on a daily basis might now be missing student work.   Besides that, there is the database files themselves ... RackSpace, as an example provider, warns that raw copy of files and raw restore of database files are a risk and that they cannot be held responsible when full-filling the customer request should the db files be corrupted.   The same is probably true of every hosting provider . Dodge a bullet? Lucky you!    Uhhhh ....  safer yet not to be in the line of fire!   Strongly suggest setting up a daily sql dump of the database that reside on the server itself.  SiteGrounds restore will include those .sql files.  So it's kinda like insurance if the raw copy of files gets putzzed at least OP has one .sql file to restore.    That suggestion should attract attention of some community members who would suggest taking that a step further. Bottom line is ... one can never have enough backups ... account, site, and the parts an pieces that make a moodle run ... code + sql dump + moodledata/filedir (last one a minimum). In many years experience at hosting remotely and running Linux/open sourced apps like a Moodle, never regretted taking the extra time to backup and archive remotely those backups. Am sure you will have a better/restful weekend! Good thinking on your part! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get a list of courses with no participants? Or courses with no recent activity?
ResponsesInList.Text: I think that the answer is "use custom sql ." For example, below is a query that I created that shows students how have been in my Moodle in the last hour.  Of course, this can be modified for any time frame.  (Please suggest improvements to my SQL.)  I am posting this simply to get you thinking. Also, consider voting on my Tracker item: MDL-19190 .  This is a request to add filtering of users by "not in any course." # Shows users logged IN LAST hour SELECT firstname, lastname, from_unixtime(lastaccess) AS LastClick, timediff(curtime(),time(from_unixtime(lastaccess))) AS LastAccess FROM prefix_user HAVING LastClick > now()-interval 60 MINUTE ORDER BY lastaccess ASC

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get a list of courses with no participants? Or courses with no recent activity?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks, this is what I'm doing currently. However, we are moving from self-hosted to hosted and I probably won't have the same level of DB access in the future. But for now, some queries if others might benefit from them also: /* Courses sorted by their modified date, date in a human readable form */ SELECT cou.id, cat.name, cou.fullname, cou.shortname, cou.summary, FROM_UNIXTIME(cou.timecreated, '%Y-%m-%d') AS created, FROM_UNIXTIME(cou.timemodified, '%Y-%m-%d') AS modified FROM mdl_course AS cou, mdl_course_categories AS cat WHERE cou.category = cat.id ORDER BY modified ASC; /* Return the number of enrolled participants for each course */ SELECT e.courseid, COUNT(ue.id) FROM mdl_user_enrolments AS ue, mdl_enrol AS e WHERE ue.enrolid = e.id GROUP BY e.courseid; The latter won't give the empty ones but it's easy to do a "NOT IN" query based on these courseids.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Giving learners a title as an achievement/reward?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Adrian, There is a Moodle built in way you can manually do this, BUT, it requires admin access and the results will be shown THROUGHOUT your Moodle site, so it might not be appropriate. As admin, go to Site administration > Users > Permissions > User policies. In both the Full name format, and Alternative name format, add, alternatename, so that you have,  "alternatename" firstname lastname. Note that I use the double quotes to make the entry stand out from the regular name. Also as admin, you probably want to go to Site administration > Plugins > Authentication > Manual accounts and lock the Alternate name field so students cannot grant themselves a title. If you use other authentication methods, check them too. Now, when you want to add a title to a user, edit their profile and type it in the Alternate name slot.

ResponsesInList.Text: Having read the whole post, I want to add in a bit.  While scorm can give you some reporting as the instructor (as previously described), it will not provide students with any reports other than their final grade, assuming the package reports grade rather than just complete/incomplete or passed/failed.  To give students feedback, you need have something built into the quiz within the scorm. Most authoring software gives you some option for giving feedback and some will let you choose to have results emailed--Lectora used to (but I'm not sure that's true anymore, last time I tried it didn't work the way I wanted but I might have been aiming for something more complicated), and there are ways to get Captivate and Camtasia to do it. That might be possible for iSpring, but in my (limited) experience, their product is less sophisticated than those--but I think their help pages for QuizMaker give you some options for emailing the student their report. The short answer is--you need to set up some sort of feedback in the scorm for your students, assuming you have the source file and can edit it.  If you don't, and can't, my suggestion would be to put it in quiz or lesson in Moodle. And you can access reports on an individual level using the reporting tab in the Moodle activity.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to export all courses with student name and grade book?
ResponsesInList.Text: Below is what I use for this purpose.  My query might contain more than what you need.  I based this off of what I saw in Moodle's "Ad-hoc queries" web page. SELECT DISTINCT gi.courseid AS CourseNumber, gg.userid AS StudentID, gg.finalgrade AS FinalGrade, u.firstname AS FirstName, u.lastname AS LastName, u.email AS Email, c.shortname AS CourseName FROM mdl_grade_items gi JOIN mdl_grade_grades gg ON gi.id = gg.itemid JOIN mdl_course c ON c.id = gi.courseid JOIN mdl_user u ON u.id = gg.userid JOIN mdl_context ct ON ct.instanceid = gi.courseid JOIN mdl_role_assignments ra ON ra.userid = gg.userid JOIN mdl_user_enrolments ue ON u.id = ue.userid JOIN mdl_enrol e ON e.courseid = gi.courseid WHERE gi.itemtype = "course" AND gg.finalgrade IS NOT NULL AND u.suspended = 0 AND u.deleted = 0 AND ct.contextlevel = 50 AND ra.roleid = 5 AND ct.id = ra.contextid AND ue.status = 0 AND e.status = 0 AND e.id = ue.enrolid AND c.idnumber > 0 ORDER BY c.idnumber, u.lastname, u.firstname

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Admin and All Manager role can't delete Course ( 3.2.5+ 20171013  )
ResponsesInList.Text: If a Site Admin can't delete a course, then someone may have made a change to that Role's Capabilities and Permissions. Go into Site Administration > Users > Permissions > Check System Permissions. Search for an Admin and then check their permission set, and when on the page, look for "Delete courses". If that is set to "Yes" then you will have to go into the database and delete the course from there. To do that, go to the courses table and select the course you want to delete, and edit the field "deleted", change the value to a 1. After which, you are going to have to track down the cause of this error. To get into the database, use a tool like phpMyAdmin or similar, and find the courses table.

ResponsesInList.Title: Disaster recovery
ResponsesInList.Text: `Curiouser and curiouser!' cried Alice.. I don't care what you consider a disaster, as long as you don't find my disaster funny! @Howard, to answer your question about taking a backup during the break between two exams: If the second exam destroyed the server, at least you have a backup of the first exam. (I am assuming that the two exams are conducted sequentially, with a sufficiently a long break in between to take a backup.) I understand your point, there is nothing called a snap-shot in mid-air. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disaster recovery

I paid for my lunch using my phone. Databases containing my and the vendor's account balance were updated and I departed with a sandwich. If the vendor believed there was a possibility the database update would be lost, with the money remaining in my account and me  walking off with a free sandwich, they would refuse electronic transactions and insist on cash.  Seamless recovery whenever a database fault occurs is not only possible but essential in financial services. There are ways to snap-shot a database. A database dump freezes it at a point in time. Each incremental dump re-enacts the CRUD operations up to the time of the incremental dump. Replication copies each CRUD operation onto a slave database in near real time and  procedures can be practised and tested to swap from crashed master to the slave. Databases can be run so not a single committed transaction is lost. 
That may be beyond the capabilities of many Moodle installations and it
is certainly impossible using the Moodle menu backup option but I think
it would be considered standard for a large institution running exams.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple course backups per day
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not a DBA but my understanding is each database has an internal log which records every CRUD action. This log guards integrity - a failure before a commit allows rollback of the several table inserts, changes and deletes which make up a single transaction. At some point in this log, every transaction is committed to the database and so this log can be truncated periodically to remove all committed actions which change the database. Automatic truncation can be turned off and all committed transactions up to a timestamp can be dumped to an incremental backup before truncation. This backup is not of the tables of the database but just of the actions which affect the tables so it should be lightweight and not cause locking. I set up such a backup for a bank database - a daily full database dump and an incremental every 15 minutes. This was mirrored to another site and an offline database which was kept in sync by the backups so a complete failure only needed a database swap. Recovery could also involve restoring the full database and then sequential restores of the incrementals. There may be dozens but the load is a single SQL command which is pasted into a script.  I would rather do that than tell a client a days work is lost. Not sure if MySql works the same but if I was serious about my small Moodle site, I would try to do the same.

ResponsesInList.Title: Dealing With Course Propagation Across Thousands Of Instances/Tenants
ResponsesInList.Text: Context We are running Moodle 3.1 and have thousands (approximately 2,500) of Moodle instances/tenants (e.g. separate database per tenant) running in an AWS stack (e.g. single MySQL RDS server ).  We chose separate instances because they represent difference customers and with GDPR , privacy, security, ability to move data/tenant to another region, etc. we opted for that route to keep the data completely isolated per customer/tenant. Issue Every tenant needs to have the exact same course content (which changes monthly).  Trying to keep all the courses across all tenants in sync has been very problematic. Proposed Solution We Are Considering (welcome any/all feedback) Setup a master tenant (per AWS region) that isn't used by any customer but it contains all of the relevant course content for all tenants. Within each tenant, replace the relevant course tables (not the ones being written to like completion data) with views that point to the master moodle instance.  For example, tables like mdl_course, mdl_course_categories, etc.  To be more specific, [CREATE VIEW mdl_course AS SELECT * FROM master..mdl_course].

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Dealing With Course Propagation Across Thousands Of Instances/Tenants
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Cameron, It is a challenge to deal with 2500 instances/tenants. You may try moosh to automate the process. 1. You will have a master course, from which all 2500 instances will be restored. You update your master course when you need it. 2. After the update you will run a (night run) cron job that will copy/restore the master course to the instances: 
```text
moosh course-restore -e backup.mbz 3
```
 You can run it in cron/batch by generating the relevant course ids. the cron job needs to be run once when you have a new version of the course. Please refer to moosh docs for more info https://moosh-online.com/commands/#course-restore

ResponsesInList.Text: I tried searching around but couldn't find exactly what I'm looking for. I'm attempting to set up a site with some paid courses. I currently have a test site up. When a new user fresh off the web clicks on a course, instead of taking you to a page that describes the course (and the stripe enrollment) is, it takes you to a login page. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Navigation guidance
ResponsesInList.Text: This is always a difficult question to answer, and the answer is always wrong, depending on your perspective. 1. Moodle security will always take precedence for anything that you want to put inside your Moodle, so don't try to fight it, work around it. There are a number of options: a. Create an Information Category, that allows Guest Access, but they still have to enter the Guest role and password. b. Add to the Front PAge a HTML block entitled "Course Information" and it holds nothing but links to the course information you want your users to see. c. Links can be directed to a directory on the server that is outside of the Moodle directory. It simply holds the course information files you want potential Users to see and links back to the Front Page. There are likely other ways to do this, but this seems the simplest to me. Why mess potential users about with logging in as a Guest when you can give them the information they want in a different way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Evaluation using moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle has a blind marking feature if that helps. Anonymous marking Sometimes known as 'blind marking', anonymous marking prevents assessors from seeing students' names on submissions. Instead, they will see randomly generated Participant numbers. (The student view of the assignment does not change.) This is also the case if student comments have been enabled. Because of the nature of anonymous marking, the students cannot see the final grade until all of the students' names have been revealed. If you are grading an assignment using an advanced grading method such as a rubric, the rubric will also be hidden from students' view until the names are revealed. To reveal student names after you are finished grading, look under Assignment settings > Reveal student identities . Feedback comments will appear whether or not student names are hidden or revealed. Note that this level of anonymity might not suit the privacy requirements of your organisation. See MDL-35390 for more details. Users with the capability mod/assign:viewblinddetails can view student identities and participant numbers (in Moodle 3.0.3 onwards). Edit: Source link - https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Assignment_settings

Are the tutors assigned as Teachers? Or Non-Editing teachers? Or a specialized role? Teachers can see all groups.  Not sure on NET.  You can limit specialized roles to only see their group (look in groups documentation about parent roles), as long as they are assigned to the group(s) you want them to see.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Exception - Resolving timed out after 5515 milliseconds
ResponsesInList.Text:
Looks like a DNS issue of some sort.  You've not disclosed information concerning many things, so if you can, check the configuration of your DNS on the device/computer and see the DNS servers the device/computer is configured to use.   Then from a terminal or network tool you have on that device, check resolution of well known sites ... like www.google.com .   Then check resolution of your site. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign a teacher
ResponsesInList.Text: Teachers are assigned to courses, but have you tried then assigning the Teacher to the Group? Or is it that Teachers can access a course then reach which ever group they want to? Or do you want to restrict Teachers to specific groups? I'm not sure this can be done, but have a look at the Permissions set, if they are enrolled in a Group and they can't see Groups then can they see their own Groups. If you want to restrict Teacher to seeing only their own Students then Groups may not be an appropriate way of doing that, you might want to look at Course Meta Links as an easier alternative. Teachers are Teachers in the Child course, so can only view their own students. Everything you would do in an ordinary course is done in the child course, except editing course materials, without impacting the Meta course. Editing the Meta course materials impacts on all Child courses but nothing else is done in the Meta course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign a teacher
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chatusvi, In addition to this, there are a number of other steps you could take: Set the course to use separate groups (course settings > Groups). You can either force group mode or choose not to. Add the teachers to the appropriate course groups. You will see a list of users in that group, sorted per role. If you don't want teacher A, who is a member of course group A, to see course group B, disable the permission ' moodle/site:accessallgroups ' for the role ( Moodle docs on the permission: https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Capabilities/moodle/site:accessallgroups ). All this should help you create the separated groups experience in a course.

Hope this maybe helps someone.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle SQL Report: Display Students Who have not Completed a Course
ResponsesInList.Text: The query below is the one that I use to show me all students and their final grades.  I actually have this in my Configurable Reports.  I will give you the CR (prefix_) form of this query.  You might need to add one more WHERE clause to filter on gg.finalgrade.  Notice that I am also filtering on final grade IS NOT NULL.  Maybe you would want "IS NULL" to find students who do not yet have a final grade.  In my case, if the student had received a grade on any item in the grade book, they will have a final grade.  If you are using Activity Completion, you would need to add something in the query to filter on it. Well, this is a start.  I began this by looking at some of the contributed queries first, and then modified it.  I cannot guarantee that it is 100% accurate, but it works well for my needs. SELECT DISTINCT c.shortname AS CourseName, u.firstname AS FirstName, u.lastname AS LastName, u.email AS Email, gg.finalgrade AS FinalGrade, c.idnumber AS CourseIDNum, gi.courseid AS CourseNumber, gg.userid AS StudentID, 3 AS moodleversion FROM prefix_grade_items gi JOIN prefix_grade_grades gg ON gi.id = gg.itemid JOIN prefix_course c ON c.id = gi.courseid JOIN prefix_user u ON u.id = gg.userid JOIN prefix_context ct ON ct.instanceid = gi.courseid JOIN prefix_role_assignments ra ON ra.userid = gg.userid JOIN prefix_user_enrolments ue ON u.id = ue.userid JOIN prefix_enrol e ON e.courseid = gi.courseid WHERE gi.itemtype = "course" AND gg.finalgrade IS NOT NULL AND u.suspended = 0 AND u.deleted = 0 AND ct.contextlevel = 50 AND ra.roleid = 5 AND ct.id = ra.contextid AND ue.status = 0 AND e.status = 0 AND e.id = ue.enrolid ORDER BY c.idnumber DESC, u.lastname, u.firstname

ResponsesInList.Title: Embedded videos in label not displayed
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I need help with an issue i'm having. I embedd a video in a label, but after i exit it's not displayed on the course page. Also, i created a tab section in a label using html, but when i try to switch through tabs they are not working. I'm having this issues since i upgraded to Moodle 3.6. Does anyone know of a fix, i would hate to have to revert to my previus version of Moodle (3.4). Thank you!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  Embedded videos in label not displayed
ResponsesInList.Text: It sounds a lot like an issue with filters. The html editor adds videos either as links or as video players(video tags). In the case of the former a filter will turn that into a player. If it is video tags , these will appear as videos even when still in the html editor. Its unlikely that video tags will disappear after that, though it might fail to play. If the videos are failing to appear at all, check that you have the multi media plugins filter enabled at : site admin->plugins->filters->manage filters If you have another media filter, such as Poodll or Video Easy installed, first disable those and just leave one media filter enabled.  Then check. If it still fails, also check the course administration menu because filters can be enabled and disabled from the filter menu there also. If the player shows but it just doesn't play. Are you sure that you did not copy and paste the media URL /player from another activity? Copying and pasting media URLs in Moodle usually breaks them. Because the files are not in the right place in the pasted location for the link to work. For tabs, these usually rely on Javascript to change the tabs states. You can not just paste the tags into the editor. The editor will just save the last state of the tabs and that is all you will see. You will need to use a plugin which supports tabs to make this work.  There are a number in the plugins database ... https://moodle.org/plugins/?q=tabs

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: GROUP BY IN MOODLE DATABASE API

Sorry... read your post properly (this time) The error means exactly what is says... your SQL is incorrect. Something like... 
```text
select city from {global_latlong} where iso2 = 'SG' group by city order by city
```
 is correct to produce distinct list of cities. You can't get a grouped list of '*' because they are all different. 'Group' doesn't make sense.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Theme is automaticly disabled after purging cache
ResponsesInList.Text: So, if you were having trouble with the original migration, adding another step is probably not going to make it easier unless you were running a version of php that is too new for 3.1.  Can you tell us what trouble you were having with the 3.1 move? If you want to continue with the 3.6 install: I am presuming that you also have imported the database ? You also need to make sure that all the plugins that you installed in the original installation have been added to the new installation.  On the original site, go to the plugins overview page and filter for additional plugins.  Then you will need to make sure that all of those plugins are also added to the 3.6 version by downloading the appropriate version and adding that to the appropriate folder in your moodle code (mod/blocks/themes etc).  You are probably missing your theme folder. If you continue to have trouble with the theme not showing up after installing all the plugins, you can manually delete the cache and localcache folders from the moodleDATA folder (not the moodle code folder) and that should resolve that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Theme is automaticly disabled after purging cache
ResponsesInList.Text:
To find out all contributed plugins you can also check the "config_plugins" db table and look for lines where "name" = "version" and value is different from main version of core plugins. That is 
```text
SELECT plugin


  FROM mdl_config_plugins


 WHERE name = 'version'


   AND value NOT LIKE '20180514%' (for Moodle 3.5) (20181203% for Moodle 3.6)
```

In addition, these course are repeated lock stock and barrel on a near weekly basis to different groups. Whilst the course only last a few days, I want the users to have access to the MOST resource material for a significant amount of time (2 year), but potentially would like to close off other material (and perhaps assessments ) in a shorter amount of time (say 1 month). I want the users in the different groups to be able to interact with each other, to share ideas and knowledge and to build up a community, and I would like any changes I make to the material to be reflected to all users, no matter when they took the course (assuming this is the material they still have access to. As such, I would rather use the same single repository of information, so that any changes I make are reflected in the courses. Having looked at how Moodle deals with courses and how I can recreate courses, it seems like I need to backup and copy the material. This would then seem to me to create different repositories of information, so lead to a divergence of material content. I'm not sure if I could use a single course and groups, but then how to I limit the content to users within those groups based on different time bounds? I do have one other need in that some of these courses are going to be "private" so only specific user should be able to sign up for them, but the material will still be the same and I still want them to be apart of the overall "community". ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating reusable course and modules - converting from face-to-face only delivery
ResponsesInList.Text: In response to this part: "Whilst the course only last a few days, I want the users to have access to the MOST resource material for a significant amount of time (2 year), but potentially would like to close off other material (and perhaps assessments ) in a shorter amount of time (say 1 month). " I would offer that you could break your resources into two parts. One part directly relating to the course itself, that is the short term material, and the second part, the long term material in a common repository, or another course. There is one issue though, unless you are dealing with Maths or Science, the resources of courses change all the time, as the course evolves. A quadratic and how to resolve them doesn't change, for example. Same with science theories and formula. The approach to teaching and learning these things may change, but the technique itself doesn't. It would not be unreasonable to expect that longer term material gets less relevant over time, it just falls out of step with current thinking, so there needs to be a review and renewal process in place to keep up with the changes around all learning materials.  Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Text: I've read most, but not all, of this thread. Sorry this is longer than you want. It was apparent to me when the new file system appeared in 2.0 that a major reason for it was that the 1.0 system was insecure. If you knew the path to any file, you knew the path to all files. Thus, the current, fairly useless draft file hoo hah doesn't work for multiple uses of the same info because how do you find the original file? And, the file doesn't go away until NO link to it exists, at which point Moodle deletes the file. BUT, you the human have to remember where the links are and delete each of them. Our solution is to have files external to Moodle.  We have a dedicated server as a repository. Why do I love this solution? Because BensFile1.docx can be linked to many times and can be altered in just one place. (You still have to remember where the links are and delete each of them.) Now to "modules." You've got a topic or section or activity in one course. It links to content external to Moodle (cf. above). You import that section or activity (that's Moodle speak) from the original course to all the other courses. Typically, for us, this is stuff like the Don't Plagiarize warning, the how to upload your assignment info, the play nice in the forums directions. Hope that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating reusable course and modules - converting from face-to-face only delivery
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh heck, I reread your last post and realized you mean "make a book and have it propagate to all my courses." That's not difficult. You revise in one course and then you import from that course to all the other courses. Be very careful not to have legacy files in the source course or they will import into all your courses with disastrous results. Be aware that when you import, the item you import goes to the *numbered* section that is the same in the importing class. (All sections are secretly numbered by, surprise! a computer program.) So, if you've got "Don't Cheat" in the third section of your originating course, it will import to whatever is the third section in your target course. You'll need to move it where you want it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating reusable course and modules - converting from face-to-face only delivery
ResponsesInList.Text: Chris, I think that I am understanding you.  Let's take, for example, an individual topic that has one quiz in it.  Let's call this quiz "Rectangles in Geometry."  And let's say you love this quiz, and so do others.  Sure, others can import this quiz into their course. But I sense that you want to go a step beyond this.  If in the first course you decide to change the due date, for example.  I think you are asking if there is any way that this change in one course can be propagated to the other courses? And your slight frustration comes from my (novice) answer, no, can't do that as far as I know.  Courses are independent. Changes to quiz questions, for example, can immediately make their way into every course where the question is used.  That's because of Moodle's Question ( database ) Bank.  But you can't do what I think you want to do.  Quiz questions might be only one example where sharing works well.  I don't use lessons or pages.  However, the way that I keep my course content separate from my Moodle does allow changes in my course content to propagate to all courses where used. So getting back to your question, "Does anyone do this?" I would say "Not me."  But that's because the courses that I teach don't overlap with topics.  I teach different courses.  That being said, if I do want to use a common video across courses, I can.  But that's because my videos are external. Moodle does have its own file system, as others (Visvanath) have pointed out.  But quite honestly, I find it more awkward than my external website approach. No, let me say another thing.  Next semester, I am teaching several sections of the same course, but these are slightly different sections because one is online and the other is face-to-face, so I have some different resources for each course.  In Moodle, I have decided to use one course, and groups (for the two different kinds of sections.)  Moodle's "groups" are very powerful.  So in my one course, around 80% of the resources are common.  For the 20% different content, I am hiding/showing resources to the appropriate group. Back to your question (again), doing what I think you propose brings along some difficulties in logic?  Let's say you have 5 courses and you could share a topic across all 5 courses.  If these 5 courses had 5 different instructors, who controls the changes?  If instructor B makes a change in Course B, do you want that change to go back to all courses?  I am one who thinks that the "change logic" will become quite difficult. The LMS product, Canvas, provides (they have a name for it that I cannot remember right now, so I will call it...) template courses.  There is a "master" course and "slave" courses.  Changes in the master get pushed to the others, but this is only one way.  If a course below makes a change, it doesn't get pushed upwards.  Some think this is great.  I see no use for it. In my own case, I always start a new semester's course based upon a previous semester.  So 90%-95% of everything is ready to go.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating reusable course and modules - converting from face-to-face only delivery
ResponsesInList.Text: Chris, your desire to have synchronized course content is the tough part, with any LMS.  I am not trying to imply that Canvas does this well, but it does offer a one-way method of making cookie-cutter courses.  If you want your instructors to independently make changes and push them upwards, they cannot.  Also, Canvas' implementation of groups is very week, and there is not a shared database for quiz questions.  Having said this, you should explore Canvas and other LMSs.  Maybe one will fit you better than the other. I have never encountered an LMS that can do what you want to do, but I have not worked with every LMS (just the four or five market leaders.) As an idea, here is one approach.  You can start a semester or term by building one "master" course, as a team.  Then you make copies of it for each instructor to use.  They go ahead an use it, and improve upon it.  Then, after the course is over, you get the instructors together to talk about what has worked and what has not.  You then build a new "master" course, make copies for other to use, and this process continues.  There might be a point where one instructor says "I prefer my own version better than the Master. Just start my new course with a copy of my old course."  Moodle would handle this scenario quite well.
