ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Deleting old courses (moodledata)
ResponsesInList.Text: Files associated with a course are not removed if the files are linked in another course. If files are removed (from view), they are moved from the normal storage area (moodledata/filedir/) to moodledata/trashdir and remain there until the cron/task job runs to empty the trash - last I checked that was 4 days from the time of the deletion. The file system itself ... no longer are files stored in humanly recognizable names, but rather, a contenthash value and the humanly recognizable filename is associated with the contenthash in a column of mdl_files in the DB. So working with/finding deleted files might require a DB query: select filearea,userid,filename,filesize,contenthash,timecreated,timemodified  from mdl_files where filearea like '%recycle%'; From a bash-shell script I have to do the query above and dump to a text file, looks like: [root@ server cli]# ./getrecycle filearea    userid    filename    filesize    contenthash    timecreated    timemodified recyclebin_course    2    backup.mbz    1581308    65d80bf797a246d0d737214d460a6d9a6187c54c    1540932182    1540932182 recyclebin_course    2    .    0    da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709    1540932182    1540932182 recyclebin_course    2    backup.mbz    1603299    efd3b7750647f503fb65bca66f066321765b0b84    1540942382    1540942383 recyclebin_course    2    .    0    da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709    1540942383    1540942383 recyclebin_course    2    backup.mbz    1601119    85188b6b7fe42c490ea3cf0c90ecb85ede78a9f0    1540942982    1540942982 recyclebin_course    2    .    0    da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709    1540942982    1540942982 The time columns are epoch time stamps. Taking the 2nd to last line above and executing the following commands from moodledata/filedir: ﻿ [root@server filedir]# find ./ -name 85188b6b7fe42c490ea3cf0c90ecb85ede78a9f0 ./85/18/85188b6b7fe42c490ea3cf0c90ecb85ede78a9f0 [root@server filedir]# ls -l ./85/18/85188b6b7fe42c490ea3cf0c90ecb85ede78a9f0 -rw-rw-rw- 1 root root 1601119 Oct 30 19:43 ./85/18/85188b6b7fe42c490ea3cf0c90ecb85ede78a9f0 [root@server filedir]# file -b ./85/18/85188b6b7fe42c490ea3cf0c90ecb85ede78a9f0 gzip compressed data, from Unix Personally, I'd like to see a recyclebin directory in moodledata to deal with deleted files/courses/backups etc. by themselves rather than having to mess with filedir ... especially when server has a space crunch ... needing space *NOW* ... would know where to go and know that removing files manually (never advised but, we do what we must) would not have adverse affects.  But also know that something that sounds simple, isn't ... when it comes to the core code.   That's my 2 cents as a hacker ... ie, not a true programmer. Also, not sure when this recyclebin stuff showed up in moodle code ... above from a 3.3.8+ version of Moodle and know same is present in a 3.4 and a 3.5.   Below that? A lot of this is automated via task which run when the main cron is run ... which should run every minute now.  Check the task list for scheduling the clean ups.  Is your cron running every minute? Also, there is a command line utility for Moodle called 'moosh'.   It has a few commands for files/filedir and meta data in DB.    See: http://moosh-online.com/ and http://moosh-online.com/commands/ 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle video topic

ResponsesInList.Text: Going to mark this one as resolved as have found out what is causing the issue. /vol/filedir is a mount point to an S3 Bucket, which uses s3fs. Not ideal, but ensures it doesn't stay out of service for now.

ResponsesInList.Text: If you upload your video to your course (easiest way is drag-dropping it in your course page), it will be automatically turned into a Label with the video 'embedded' in it. By default the VideoJS player displays it quite small, but you have the possibility to toggle the full screen option for your video. Also, if you manually add a video to your course through the ATTO or TinyMCE editor, by using the Add media button, the tab that contains all your video settings has a few options to modify the dimensions so it can be displayed in 800x600 if you wish. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle freezes with thousands of sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, totally agree about being cautious about editing the DB directly ... never a recommended method to fix an issue.   But in this case, if one leaves the DB in that state, how will the site be affected in an update or an upgrade of code, or other processes that might involve the tables? A 'safer' way ... make an sql dump of DB.   Create a new DB by same name but with a '2' at end of name.  Import the dump.   Edit 'moodle2' - in other words, deleted those rows. In Moodle, put site in maintentance mode, then change config.php ... comment out the line that points to the old database, add the same line back to config.php and point to the newly imported DB.  Next access will be pointed to new DB.   Check troubled course.  Check other things.   If OK, take site out of maintenance mode. Probably best to remove the old database eventually - to prevent confusion later. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle freezes with thousands of sections
ResponsesInList.Text: I would suspect that Ken is right, it is unlikely to work any other way. The reason I suggest this is that working directly with the DB is often easier and safer than trying to work though the Moodle interface. OK You got the course into a hidden Category, but it is still on the server , still in the DB, and it needs to be removed entirely, I would think. However, I would add that this is why I keep test sites, duplicates of the production sites, to the Moodles I have server access to. These are on a NAS I purchased specifically for this. I would do as Ken suggests, make an SQL dump, import into the appropriate test site, edit the config.php file. Using phpMyAdmin , I would commit the DB edits, then test it thoroughly If it works, and there is every reason to believe it will, export the SQL dump to the production site. Done this on the odd occasion and never had reason to regret it. The key is the test site, if that goes wrong, it doesn't matter.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle freezes with thousands of sections
ResponsesInList.Text: True totally safe on a clone of production.   Agreed. OP has used the term 'production' which suggest there is a test site that is a clone of production.   Been my experience, however, that the test site, after a period of time, isn't the same as production any more - moodle version slightly behind, courses also, etc.  It more than likely doesn't have the DB/course issue.  And might have to undergo the same tweaks as performed on production to get to certain points. So to make sure the test site is in the same condition as production, OP will need to clone it again ... everything ... including moodledata. Working with a database that is a clone of the DB that has issues on production server is in the same environment, under the same FQDN, etc., etc.   It the edits to the test DB fail for some reason ... it's just the DB itself .   Code hasn't changed, apache service hasn't changed, etc., etc. Therefore, me thinks, shorter time to resolution of the problem is clone the DB on production and work with that DB clone. OP has options. ;) 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using .swf flash in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Before using .swf think it wise to read: https://redmondmag.com/articles/2017/07/25/adobe-ending-flash-support.aspx " On Microsoft's side, the Edge browser will continue to ask for permission to run Flash throughout this year and "into 2018." It'll ask once on the first visit. However, in "mid to late 2018," Edge will require permission each time to run Flash. Internet Explorer will run Flash without requiring permission throughout this time period. However, in "mid to late 2019," Microsoft will disable Flash by default in both Internet Explorer and Edge, and while users can reenable it, they'll have to provide permissions each time to use it. By the "end of 2020," Flash will be gone from all supported Windows versions and "users will no longer have any ability to enable or run Flash. " The browser makers are getting out of the 'plugin' business. Firefox right now prompts user for permissions to launch SCORM 's (as an example) if they are old and using .swf's. As far as .pdf's, browsers really don't display them by browser alone ... handled by whatever users have on their systems to launch and display. You might look into hosting documents on a system that provides documents as URL links with access permissions controlled outside of moodle.  At any time, you, the owner of the file, can revoke such access. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: is my site's security compromised
ResponsesInList.Text: Uaer ID 2 is the first account created in your Moodle. It's an admin level account and when some automated process is used one will see that user ID along with 'cli' (command line). It does NOT mean someone has accessed your site via ssh and did anything to it. Check server settings for account expirations ... what you shared shows 9 Sept. over a month ago.   Example: if a users account wasn't confirmed account has 7 days before account considered by the system to be an account that was incomplete and to be removed and the system automagically does that. But then again ... site is a version 3.0 ... old ... no longer supported for any code fixes OR for any security updates.  Moodle is now 3.5.   While Moodle security is pretty good, *nothing* is a fortress that cannot, either by application flaws, or that which is used to run it ... like the PHP vr. 5.5.30 behind your Moodle ... be compromised/hacked. As the notification messages about new versions available says ... 'strongly advise ...' upgrading your Moodle. Check your servers environment and update the component to see what will be required to upgrade.  One thing will be your version of PHP, for sure! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: School's Report Cards
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all I have 2650 pdf report cards generated from school's oracle system to be shared with all students. The management wants me to share the generated report cards with each individual student on Moodle, each to see this own report card only. Is there any way to bulk upload these files to their Moodle account or private files? Please someone direct me. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: School's Report Cards
ResponsesInList.Text: I would think that is actually outside Moodle's remit. A bulk upload to every student individually would be difficult. Moodle is aimed at the individual student, which is why a there is not a lot of obvious or simple bulk handling features, even though the list is growing, slowly. I suspect this could be a feature of a companion application called Mahara . Many organizations use Moodle and Mahara together, and with an SSO, or LTI even, it can be almost seamless switching between the two. The installation of Mahara is not as simple as Moodle's but it is still a useful tool.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: School's Report Cards
ResponsesInList.Text: These pdf 'report cards' have to be generated from something.   Does your school have a 'student information system'?  Am guessing your school does. Some of those 'student information systems' have begun to expand what they do ... one actually has quizzes now.   Makes sense cause the 'official' gradebook for students is in the student information system ... not the one in Moodle.   They also have a 'parent portal' interface for parents checking up on their child. So before "jumping' off into what could be adding to complexity, check with whatever generates those report cards. Another ... a school systems usually provide every student some disk space to store files ... may not be internet accessible ... but then again might be.  Would hope that admins of those systems are not restricted from those user directories. Bottom line, 'look before before you leap'. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: PayPal IPN Error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey all, To start, this is a v1.9.14+ problem. I'm aware of the issues with running such an out of date system, so please skip any suggestions related to updating the version. The system does not seem to be throwing any errors. However, I have not actually tried to take the system down so I can thoroughly run the debugger. The system is a custom LAMP setup. Versions are: MySQL 5.7.23 PHP 5.6.38 Original problem definition: When a user signs up for a course, they get redirected to PayPal. On the PayPal site, they are able to pay for the course and all of the relevant information is correct. When PayPal makes the return call to ipn.php, the user gets sent to the pending status page. Problematically, the admin are not notified of the issue and the student is never enrolled. Actual Problem: I believe PayPal has finally fully dropped support for HTTP 1.0 and possibly stopped accepting socket connections directly to www.paypal.com . Moodle 3+ current fix: The new approach uses curl and connects to https://ipnpb.paypal.com/ instead. Problematically, the code uses a custom class for curl that I have not had time to go over in detail. Consequently, I'm not sure how portable this solution is. Most recent attempt: PayPal has posted a solution here: https://developer.paypal.com/docs/classic/ipn/ht_ipn/#do-it . My most recent attempt at a solution is more or less a direct port of that code into the original ipn.php code. Although this has not been tested in detail, yet, I just wanted to reach out to the community in case someone else has found a more elegant solution. Thank you for your time, M

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving from Moodle to another
ResponsesInList.Text: There is no such thing as a silly question here. And this is the first time I have seen this question I think and actually an interesting question. Are both versions the same? If so, have you tried to import courses? Importing is easy inside a Moodle, but don't know about an external Moodle. You will also run into the issue of importing data and course materials but not Users. Alternatively, just do a complete backup of one Moodle, courses and students all, and then restore the file to the other Moodle. I really don't know enough about this topic to say it will definitely work. Also, are the authentication processes the same on both.. e.g. LDAP ? If so, could you export the Users from one to another with a third party tool? There are plenty of them around, and for different server environments too. If you are using Active Directory from the Dark Side, I understand you can use some of the built in tools, like LDIFDE, but that doesn't give you a csv file. You could try and get the Admin to run another built-in tool, Csvde, to generate a csv file, but make sure you get the passwords too, or reset to "changeme". The problem is where do you upload the users to? Obviously the LDIFDE file will go directly to the active directory, I've never done it, no-one has let me near their servers... (I did see this little IT gnome stroking a server cabinet last week mumbling something that sounded like "My precious-s-s-s", not sure what that was all about.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving from Moodle to another
ResponsesInList.Text: In addition to ... some checks.   You've given version of Moodle ... assume to be the same on both servers. Moodle B - the one you are moving courses from Moodle A - the one that will eventually end up holding all of your courses. IF Moodle A is a clone of Moodle B ... probably have very little to do in prep for restoring courses from B to A. However, if not a clone think some checks and maybe prep/changes to config might be in order. Check the addons on both servers.   Any addon being used in B but not present on A, install same addon on A. While themes is a plugin and Moodle A will adjust to a default theme if the course theme not present, that's not true of all addons. Full course backups could be very large.   Moodle doesn't have a tool to show the size of a backup prior to backing up a course.   Pick what you think is the 'largest' course first on B and do a full backup with users.   Look at the size of the .mbz.   Check Moodle A for size of file to upload ... phpinfo will show those that variable.   Adjust Moodle A so that uploads during the restore of courses won't fail due to size of file to upload. Under same topic of full course backups could be very large ... Check the DB server setting of Moodle A  for max_allowed_packets.   That  might need to be increased on Moodle A. Please see: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/packet-too-large.html (you've not said what DB is being used so am assuming MySQL . Some other PHP settings you might want to increase ... besides max uploads ... if you've never restored a large course to Moodle A and the courses from Moodle B might be large, etc.  consider tweaking some PHP settings ... time for a script to run, memory a script can consume are two that come to mind.   Those variables/settings can be seen via phpinfo on Moodle A. Concerning users and how they authenticate ... are both B and A using the same authentication methods for users? If so, there shouldn't be issues **unless** the locations of the Moodles involved are on different networks and behind different firewalls, etc.. My 2 cents. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is it possible to Backup all courses with in one time?
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, Narit.  This script that I wrote will do a complete backup.  This backup could then be reinstalled on any similar server .  I use my backups to regularly install a copy of my production moodle into my experimental ( MAMP ) server, on my Mac. Some parts of this script will need to be modified for your own server.  I am providing mine as a (good) example.  You would certainly need to modify some lines, for example, the line with a password. I cannot provide a step-by-step instruction of how to modify this script.  You just need to study and learn. To use this script, it has to be somewhere (in a safe spot) on your server, and then it gets executed with a CRON job. Appreciate that in these server/moodle systems, there is great flexibility about how the administrator wants to do things, which is why step-by-step instructions are difficult.  How does one get from Chicago to New York City, or from Paris to Rome?  Many many ways. I should also mention a few more things.  I run this script only once each day (during the early U.S. morning hours.) Some might want to run it more regularly.  Also, this script does a rolling (or moving) seven-day backup.  It assumes that your server has space for these backups.  Some might want to combine this weekly backup scheme with a longer, like monthly, backup scheme.  Also, it is good practice to mirror these backups to a secondary location.  I am not practicing "good practice" yet, but it is on my list of things to do. Disclaimer: I am not trained as a system administrator.  I am only sharing what I have learned.  It seems to work for me.  Others will provide more help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic backup fills up disk on daily basis.
ResponsesInList.Text: Yeah the backups can take an awful lot of space. They're basically zips of all your course content. You may be able to mitigate the amount of space by reducing the number of backups for each course, and not backing up courses that haven't been updated. We fiddled a lot with these, but it never got to a level our ops guys were particularly happy with. In the end, for us, ops do a daily snapshot of the server, and we rely on trash mechanism in Moodle to recover short-term deletions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Event Trigger
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I want to have my event trigger contain the number of assignment, for example, someone granted extension for an assignment and i want to get an email with the assignment number, example who granted, who was granted, the course name and the assignment number 1 or 2. Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Event Trigger
ResponsesInList.Text:
So you'd need to create an event observer in a plugin (perhaps your theme, or a local plugin) for the \mod_assign\event\extension_granted event. Here's some documentation on event observers: https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Event_2#Event_observers If you do a search in the code for extension_granted, you'll find the code that creates the actual event, and from there you'll see what data you'll be fetching in your event observer. 
```text
$data = array(


    '
context
' => $assign->get_context(),


    'objectid' => $assign->get_instance()->id,


    'relateduserid' => $userid,


);
```
 So you can see that the objectid will be the assignment id you're after, and the relateduserid will be the student for whom the extension has been granted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot restore - says its missing course.xml file
ResponsesInList.Text:
@Blair .. thanks for additional info ... nothing appears to be wrong there.  Cept what was this item: Release: 07.20.2018 Have a 3.4.highest and have not yet experienced the issue ... but others have reported similar. Hmmm ... one more thing to check ... do this right after another failure ... missing some.xml. in moodledata/temp/backup/ Moodle has to un-compress an .mbz then build a plan to restore.   backup .mbz is un-compressed in a contenthash named directory consisting of a bunch of letters/number ... some thing like qewaskfhasksaflasfsdhghene go to moodledata/temp/backup/ and see if there are any directories like that ... if so, go into them and list the files. A completed un-archiving will have a 0 byte moodle_backup.log and the road map for restoring a moodle_backup.xml.   You should also see other .xml's related the content moodle was attempting to restore ... a course directory is matched with a course.xml and is the roadmap for contents of course directory. Is the missing .xml there? If the archive is good ... which you've checked locally .. then the only other thing I could think of that might cause this is a task ... part of cron job ... Scheduled Task One is: Clean backup tables and logs
\core\task\backup_cleanup_task the restore processes actually uses temp tables to build those plans to restore - it's restoring a un-archived backup. What is the task setting for the above ... little gear icon. There is also a 'Run Now' link. The defauilt settings for that task is 10 minutes  after the hour,every hour, all days. You could turn that to disabled ... but remember where you found it and what the setting was. While you are looking at task ... see if there  is anything else that might relate to restoring.   Don't turn off a bunch without really thinking it through and making note of what you turned off.   We could be causing problems else where. Go back to that moodledata/temp/backup/ directory and remove all files folders ... we want a clean directory for the next attempt.   It is safe to remove any/all files in moodledata/temp/backup/ Now attempt a restore. Success?   Check moodledata/temp/backup/  See a 0 byte .log file?  No contenthash type directories there. If you see a .log file that's larger than 0 bytes look at it ... it is ascii text and a cat nameoffile.log will display.   Got one of those?  Share back here. Have another one to restore?   Restore that one ... Success? Did the sporadic happenings go away?   etc., etc. We have to find a way to replicate the issue or really determine what caused it to submit anything in Tracker as a bug. Fingers crossed. If you have command line and can su to root ... cd moodledata/temp/backup/ watch "ls -l"  will show in realtime folders and files being created ... then eventually removed.  [ctrl][c] to quit 'watch'. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assigning students to individual course resources
ResponsesInList.Text: Dmitri, little by little I might be seeing what you struggle with.  Yes, let's assume a course with 100 resources in it. Here is what I do, which may or may not apply to your own specific needs, but might help with your thinking. First, I group resources and activities by topic.  In a typical course, I might have around 15 topics each with around 6-8 resources/activities.  (You can see where I get my 100.) Next, I never turn on all the topics at one time.  Each week I make a new topic "visible."  In this method, I am trying to "pace" learning.  I do agree that if I had turned on everything at the beginning of the course, it would overwhelm students.  So at the beginning of my courses, students only see about 5 items in the common "top" block, and around 5-7 items in the "week 1" block. Last, I do use the  "collapsed topics" add-in, and I show student how to "collapse" topics that we have finished.  So I leave some of the cleanliness concerns up to the student to manage.  At the end of the course, if a student decided to un-collapse all topics, they would be able to sit back and appreciate all of the things that they have done, and learned, in this course. Two more things worth mentioning.  I do "highlight" the current topic.  I also use Moodle's "activity completion" feature which allows students to check-off items that they have completed.  This helps students manage their own position within a course. Below is a screenshot of how this works in one of my courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Face2Face Plugin Errors
ResponsesInList.Text:
If what you post above is exactly what displays...it sounds like you typed in the html directly in the text box rather than using editing features or adding the html to an html area.  If you click the Show more buttons option in your wysiwyg editor and you have a text editor that allows you to modify html (Atto or TinyMCE), you can look for an icon that looks like <> or and that allows you to edit the html.  In HTML, your text looks like this:

<h4><strong>Date:</strong> Monday, 3 December to Wednesday, 5 December 2018 (3 days)<br /><strong>Session Time:</strong> 08:30 - 16:00<br"

As for your second issue...I don't have an answer--not a database person and haven't had the issue.  Are there upcoming sessions? Do they show up as signed up when you look at them?  What version of F2F? If your Moodle version doesn't match up with a compatible plugin, this can result in problems.  Looks like an older (but not old) version of Moodle--you may need to upgrade sometime soon. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Face2Face Plugin Errors

So, you see in your wysiwyg that there is a button on the bottom row next to Font size that is <>?  Click that and look at the html.  I bet the html will be weird, if not seriously ugly.  If it wasn't typed in the box as html, it may have been cut and pasted from Word or something similar...sometimes pasting has weird effects--I think the same thing happened on my site a while back--clear out all the formatting and re-do it in the details area. identified in other fields.  You can also add fields to your sessions options (like...location,
venue, room, etc) which can cut down on details, too.  You do have to fiddle with the default email text to get those to show but it isn't too hard.  If you've got a vendor, you might be able to get them to take care of language pack stuff. ResponsesInList.Title: Easy way to see (and switch) which course items are hidden
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have a small, technical question: is there an easy way to see (and switch) which course items are visible/hidden for students? Rationale: Very often I copy previous editions of my courses and create new ones by only modifying old items and adding new material. The problem is that I have to hide or make visible large number of items in each course module (but not all of them) and the changes happen over long period of time (entire semester).  Therefore it is vital for me to know what is visible/hidden and to be able to easy switch it. Other solutions I am aware of (but are insufficient): a) It seems that the new Moodle versions show visibility by graying items. But it doesn't work when the items use colors (which is my case). And changing visibility requires entering menu for each item, which takes time. b) Switching to student role and back to teacher role is time consuming and requires memorizing what is visible (in student role I can see what's visible but there I cannot change the visibility, hence have to switch back, enter the editing mode again, change visibility and again switch to the role of a student to see if I have done everything right. Other (old) solution: There used to be an eye icon in old Moodle versions, but now it is hidden in a menu placed at the right hand side of each item. If there was a way to take it out of the menu to the item level, then it would be a solution to my problem. Or maybe there is a better solution? Any help would be appreciated! Best regards Janusz Jabłonowski

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Easy way to see (and switch) which course items are hidden
ResponsesInList.Text: Why not just move all of your "hidden" items to a single course section that is invisible to students? You then know exactly what is visible and what is not, and you can simply move them/make them visible as needed. This would save you having to switch roles, but not editing visibility en masse. You can check out the Mass Action Block plugin ( https://moodle.org/plugins/block_massaction ), though it's technically only updated to 3.4 (test it with 3.5 and see if it works without any particular issues). In theory this block does exactly what you would like to do for batch editing of visibility. Some commentators said it works in 3.5, some have experiences where it won't, and others says it works most of the time. It also depends on the course format being used as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Features for quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm going to agree with Howard except on your last question--you sell access to a course.  A course is made up of activities (which include quiz--you choose which activities you use.  A single activity format course could simply be a quiz).  Purchasing access to a course, you can take the quiz however many times is allowed (the quiz will be set by the owner to allow a number of attempts). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issues accessing Moodle from external IP
ResponsesInList.Text: Initial Moodle installs best done with fully qualified domain names (FQDN) from the get go - IMHO .   Sounds like initial installation done with private IP first and now attempting to access from outside and inside. Got a FQDN for the server? What's in config.php?  IP or FQDN? Server might have a firewall that is allowing only certain blocks of IP addresses to access. Config of web service itself could also come into play. When you are testing access to the server by outside IP are in actually on a computer that's inside the LAN/WAN?   If so your traffic is looping the networks boundary firewall ... traffic initiated from inside a private net hits gateway for outside internet and then has to re-enter the private network.   Some boundary firewalls might see that is 'funny business'. Check web service error and access and error logs. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

In case someone cannot locate the php.ini file, the following must be done: -Create a phpinfo.php file with the following command on it: <?php phpinfo() ?> - place the phpinfo.php file in the root of your site: www.yoursitename.com/phpinfo.php - look for the following " Loaded Configuration File : it will give you the path to the php.ini file "

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign Students or groups to Teacher
ResponsesInList.Text: You might have to make a copy of teacher role and modify permissions a bit to limit who they can see (or modify non-editing teacher to editing options)...but the long and short is that you can create groups, force separate groups (I don't usually force, but you can--only they HAVE to be in a group to be able to do anything with it forced), add students and specialized teacher roles to the groups and it is done.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign Students or groups to Teacher
ResponsesInList.Text: This is very easy. You need to put the teachers into the same group as the students. You also need to put the course, or the relevant modules, into separate groups mode, and finally you need to ensure that the teachers do not have the moodle/site:accessallgroups capability. Since MDL-55981 in Moodle 3.2, new installs only grant that capability to editing teachers and do not grant it to non-editing teachers. Prior to 3.2, all types of teacher had this capability. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Jason problem in Messages
ResponsesInList.Text: We were having that same error. After debugging the response, as Gareth J Barnard suggests, we discovered that the problem was that "Debugging emails" was set to active in the site configuration. If this setting is active, the response after a new message is posted is a list of SMTP related messages, which are not valid JSON. After deactivating the debugging emails option, the error disappeared and the messages plugin works as expected, without the need to reload the page with every message. Kind regards.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.4 Office365 sign on
ResponsesInList.Text: You need at least two accounts to be able to login to the moodle without using any other authentication method.  IF, the system providing remote authentication is ever off line/down or there is some network hickup, no one will be able to login to the moodle. User ID 1 is the guest account ... even if you don't allow guest access, leave the guest user in mdl_user. User ID 2, is the original installer person ... that is a manual account ... many have left the default user name to 'admin' when installing initially.  And if you haven't done so, create another manual account  that does not use external authentication and that is also set to one of the admin level users. Thus, leave the login form for manual accounts ... do display the o365 button to login, however.  If you need to make it clearer for users, edit the language files related to login screen. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM integration
ResponsesInList.Text: To be fair, a massive amount of the display issues come from: 1) Custom site themes. 2) The SCORM package itself. The most common problem with 2) partly relates to the way Moodle embeds the SCORM package within an iframe - loading the SCORM api within the same window. We do this because JavaScript /SCORM is really fragile, and intermittent communication issues are common when your API sits on a different window from the actual SCORM package. There are a number of things you can do to improve the display of your SCORM packages - either by adjusting your custom theme or adjusting the SCORM package itself. We also have a couple of tracker issues that could provide some nice ways to improve this: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-62057 (should be relatively easy to implement if someone wants to put some time into developing a patch!) If not - hopefully I'll find some time to look at this sometime. I also had a proposal here that provides a way we could inject some custom css into the SCORM package to fix the display issues from within the package: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-50401 That is a bit hacky - and it would really be better to fix the css within the SCORM packages themselves but this is not always possible.

ResponsesInList.Text: I figured out how to modify the theme in order to get rid of the "course" view tab (pint "3." in my previous post). Add below code to your custom CSS of your theme: .block-myoverview .nav.nav-tabs li.nav-item :nth-child(1) { display: none; } This will eliminate the "timeline" tab. So now there is only the "course" tab left. As there now is only this one left, you actually also can delete this one, too - ie. hide both of them - by adding this custom CSS to your custom .block-myoverview .nav.nav-tabs { display: none; } This will eliminate both tabs. ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  URLs changed via DB query not reflected in course
ResponsesInList.Text: Issue is fixed -we run VMware CentOS servers comprising a file server , a DB server & a web server. Process I followed was stopping the web server, then on the file server deleted all files & folders in both moodledata\cache\ & moodledata\localcache\ via rm * -rf . Then rebooted both the file & DB servers and once these were up rebooted the web server. Did find the initial logon was extremely slow but assume this was due to the cache having to be rebuilt -other users logons did not have the same slowness.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to permanently delete a student from Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: From Site admin > Users > Bulk user actions, it is possible to delete a user. The user itself will not be deleted from the mdl_user table in the database , but will get a value of 1 in the 'deleted' field, indicating that it's status. From Moodle 3.5.2 onwards, there's a lot of GDPR compliant tools on board to help you correctly process a data deletion. If you meant to remove a student, including his/her data from a course, then unenrol the user from the course. This can be done from the Enrolled users or Participants page in your course. The user account will still exist, but he/she will no longer have access to the course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Hosting and backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Q1. Moodle 'admin' password lost Answer: https://docs.moodle.org/en/Administration_FAQ#I_have_forgotten_the_admin_password Q1. Linux super user (root) password lost Firstly, this is not a Moodle question. Secondly, although it may not wipe out the data, a mishap can make the machine unbootable. If you don't know how to repair, for all practical purposes you lost the data! As others have mentioned, there are two approaches to this: a) boot the machine from an external medium, for example a USB memory stick, mount the system partition, wipe out the encrypted password from /etc/shadow. At the next boot you can log in without a password, then set it anew. b) stop the boot process at the boot manager, typically GRUB2. Edit its parameters so that the machine goes to single user mode, which doesn't need a password. Then change the password. You might have to remout the system partition in read-write mode. There are plenty of help in the net. You have to find out a one which fits your machine. All that said, a machine with no maintainer has no future! ;-(

ResponsesInList.Text: Sir V might be taking a well deserved rest ... so I'll pickup the slack a little. Ok, you've been able to change the root password to the server now and you desire to get Moodle running again (the goal to fix what's wrong with what you have).   In order to do that some information is needed.   The following for a CentOS server. As root user issue the following commands: uname -an That will tell us what version of CentOS ... makes a difference in where things are located, ownerships/permissions of files and folders and addressing the issue in the first post ... @ https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=375705#p1514803 Other info: php -v - tells us what version of PHP installed. php -m - tells us what modules are loaded. mysql -V - tells us what version of MySQL client and therefore what version of MySQL server installled and finally, what version of Moodle. Moodle code is typically installed in /var/www/html/ on CentOS servers, so ... cd /var/www/html/ ls -l version.php config.php That shows us ownerships/permissions on two key files for moodle code.  If the above command fails to list those files, then your code could be located somewhere else and we'll need to find it. The version of Moodle is found in the version.php file: fgrep '$release' version.php The config.php file we might have to edit to add lines from config-dist.php so we can get debugging turned on and thus find out more about the error reported in first posting of this thread. Uhhh ... that's probably enough 'homework' for now ... how about we start with the above? Please ... the output of each of the commands above will be in the terminal from which you could copy the text output, paste that info in a txt file, then use that text file to come back here and respond (text is much easier to see/understand than screen shots). For other reference should you find you need them: Debugging via config.php file: https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Debugging#In_config.php If you start to edit files, make backups of them as they exist now so in case you make a mistake we are not making the issues worse. For example: you plan to edit config.php for debugging ... copy the original file to a .bak file: cp config.php config.bak Your config.bak file is now the backup and you can edit the config.php file now with 'insurance'. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Random Wrong Answers From a Set (Formula Question)
ResponsesInList.Text: I am wondering if there is a way to have a question that has a large set of text answer (20+) to randomly select three wrong answers but always maintain the correct answer in a random position in the 4 answer choices. To be more specific, I want to put up an image (an animal of some kind for example) and ask the students to tell me what the image is.  Because the answer will never change, I cannot have it as part of the random set. I want to limit the number of distractors in the answer set to only 3 wrong answers so that the question will have the right answer, and then three random wrong answers that are chosen from the set.  All 4 of the answer possibilities need to shuffle (i.e. the correct answer shouldn't always be in the same 0-1-2-3 position. Thanks to whomever has an idea they are willing to share.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Random Wrong Answers From a Set (Formula Question)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Daniel, So far as I know, there is no direct method of doing what you want with a multiple choice question. Before I retired I used to simulate it in a limited round-about-way. It is a lot of work to set up, the first time, but then I was able to use it for years without having to make any changes. Basically, I create a question category for each question. In each question category, I created a multiple choice question with one correct answer, and three distractors. I then duplicated the question a bunch of times, leaving the question and correct answer untouched, but changing one or more of the distractors in each copy. I generally found that 10 versions of the question in each category was enough. When creating the quiz, I set it to randomly select one question from each of the categories, with shuffle answers set for each question and shuffle the question order. To further help prevent students from being tempted to cheat, the first quiz of the year, I had them walk around the computer lab so that they could see for themselves, that even though everyone was getting the same questions, the question order was shuffled, the answers were different, and on those rare occasions where the answers were the same, the answer order was shuffled. So, if they tried reading an answer off another computer screen, it was going to be a total waste of time. It also helped that I started using a ten minute time limit for the quiz.

ResponsesInList.Title: Updated SCORM file to course???
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, My question is this: if I ' replace ' this existing course file; Will it screw up any students that are in the middle of this course? e.g. Will it reset their progress through the SCORM file in any way if they are like half way through? Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updated SCORM file to course???
ResponsesInList.Text: If you updated the same SCORM content file, without renaming the course/file most systems handle the minor changes gracefully and do not orphan the student's who have completed the course. Students that was mid-course, will have to start over. Normally, if it is a rather large course, I would send out a notification to encourage students to complete or not start the course by a specified date. Informing them, that they run the risk of loosing their course progress and then make the update after the provided date. 6000 learners on a 90 minutes, we only lost 3 student's progress - and they were informed before the update. However, if you content had a major change, I would think you would want all students to "retake" the new, revised course.

If you copy the URLs from the display page of another activity So to re-use images, you should select them from the recent files in the repository system .. Or upload them again .. ResponsesInList.Text: I finally found out what the problem was to solve this.  I am using Windows Server 2016 and iis to host my Moodle site.  Turns out it was a setting in iis that was prohibiting the uploads.  I also set all of my file size settings in my php.ini to 1024 to make sure that moodle wasn't prohibiting the file based on size.  Once that was done, I did a little digging into iis and found that my file size was being limited here as well.  I found the setting by selecting "Default Web Site" and then opening "Request Filtering" (Picture).  Then Selecting "Edit Feature Settings..." (Picture 2), I found that the maximum allowed content length was set to 30000000 bytes.  So I changed it to 1024000000 bytes (Picture 3) and then restarted iis.  This fixed the problem. I am still a little baffled though because before changing these settings it still allowed me to upload videos that were 50+ MB without any problems.  It just hung up on 2 of the videos.  However, the 2 videos now upload fine......  It may have something to do with how the videos are uploaded, perhaps something to do with compression etc. but I don't know. Thanks to everyone that offered me help with this.  Especially Ken Task who spent a lot of time with me troubleshooting this!! Dustin


ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Attendance authenticity
ResponsesInList.Text: The problem with this entire approach is that it cannot in any way validate a student's actual presence. We have had problems with online courses where students log in, do something else, just doing something that resets the idle clock every now and again, but do not do the work. In the end, if they attend a course just downloading the materials they need, then log out, who is to say they have not attended the course? Obviously, they have to present a report, a finding, an essay, a video, whatever the assignment demands that is of sufficient standard to prove their actual work ethic and understanding of the work required. We now accept this as demonstrable proof of "attendance". Who cares if they only spend a few minutes in the actual course, as long as they have a product that meets the requirements, why bother with attendance? Why is it even an issue? If the student is in a classroom, then surely the Teacher is monitoring the presence of the student? Sorry, that seems a bit strident, but I am finding more and more that in my own on-line studies I actually spend very little time in the Institute's Moodle, but I am getting reasonable grades and positive feedback. I'm not present and the few times I have been able to attend the Institute, I find few others do either.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle newbie getting started on 3.5.2 - Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, new to Moodle in general and had a few questions on the best direction to go.  Thanks very much for any time reading/pro Thanks so much for any info here, and please point me to a betters pot if I've missed it.  I have Moodle set up on PHP7.2/ MySQL and have looked at a lot of the links under documentation, but if the items below are something I should have been able to pull from a video please let me know! I'd love to have some pointers from more experienced users that have set up courses.  I'm building out a course from an existing workbook.  There are 9 "lessons" that are 10-20 pages each.  At the end of each lesson , there are questions that are more essay-type than something I could quiz. Questions: How would you organize the lessons in Moodle?  My current understanding is that I should create a topic for each, then add a Lesson activity under each one.  And that will let me create multiple content pages.  Is this a good understanding? For student feedback on the essay-type questions...would it make sense to have that as a forum or an assignment document people need to submit? How do multiple groups of people work?  Can I have multiple classes going at the same time?  Can enrolled students see forum results from prior students?  etc. Thanks in advance for any direction!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle newbie getting started on 3.5.2 - Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: You will get many ideas from folks here, because Moodle is a very flexible product.  Here are my ideas. 1) Yes, I would put each "lesson" into its own topic in Moodle.  Then, I would build Resources and Activites within each topic, including quizzes and discussions.  I use the Collapsed Topics add-in that provides a bit more flexibility for topics to be opened or closed. 2) If you want students and yourself to easily share observations, then I would use a forum.  Feedback to a student's essay question goes only to that student.  But you can use both, if you wish. 3) Yes, Moodle provides flexibility with groups.  I tend to use groups for breaking a larger class into smaller chunks for discussions.  I have also used Moodle to delivery the very same items to multiple courses (same course, same semester) and then separated these courses, for discussions, into their appropriate sections .  You can set Moodle to not show different groups each other discussions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle newbie getting started on 3.5.2 - Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Erm... there is so many things you could do with courses, so many tools you could use but consider this, form follows function. What are your learning themes? Two learning themes may be similar, so that may be a single course, but more likely not. The is all sorts of varieties and flavours here, so it's pretty much your own choice. Your workbook has chapters so it might be one chapter dictates the content of one course. Say a Maths book has a chapters on trigonometry, Pythagoras and Algebra, and while similar in many ways, you won't create one course for all three chapters, well I wouldn't gets too messy. A course can have lots of learning outcomes, but it should only have one theme. You have a work book, with chapters each with their own assessment items. If you were to copy that book precisely, then you might be opening yourself to copyright breaches, so be very careful. Cease and desist orders can be very expensive. We all face these issues and how we respond to them is an individual choice. Some foolishly, blithely ignore the issue, others, like me, just love reinventing the wheel so might use ideas from a number of different sources, but we create our own resources and activities . I learned long ago that it is OK to leave behind a body of work for others to use, even if they are people whom you are leaving them with are erm... not very likeable, shall we say. Pick your own level, something you are comfortable with and try not to plagiarize too much. Look for resources that have a Creative Commons seal on them, modify them for your own use, don't just use them as they may not suit your cohort of users, or may be about the mark but not precisely target your learning objectives. It's a lot of work, but it becomes easier to maintain that than it is to create it. The Moodle Docs are a good place to start, Managing a Course has good information. Adding activities has another set of pages. You can't have Activities without Resources . Understanding the differences between each type of activity and resource will help you figure out what you want to use in your course. Initially, remember the KISS principle, it's all about building your confidence with an unfamiliar tool. If you are confident in your work, then your students will be a lot more relaxed about this brand new tool. They will still push back, but if you sound like you know what you want, and keep a consistent message about using Moodle, they will come around. Some of the questions you are asking already are a lot further down the track than your knowledge of the tool will allow for easy understanding. Groups are simple, once you understand how Roles work, Yes, you can use one course for as many different classes at the same time without an administrative nightmare, using Groups, or, my favourite, Course meta-links .  But don't rush it, Moodle is a big and can be subtle tool and will trip you up if you try too hard. Aghh enough.... Good luck...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Running Moodle in XAMPP
ResponsesInList.Text: Ho Broto. Why is it throwing a memory error? It shouldn't...mmmm interesting. First, reboot your computer, that should clear memory issues. When restarted, check the Xampp Control Panel, see if Xampp is actually loading at start up first. The Apache , My SQL at least should be showing green. If it isn't, click Start on whatever options you installed. When green, go to the config button for the server and open the httpd.conf file. Scroll down until you see a line that says something like: Define SRVROOT "C:/xampp/apache" ServerRoot "C:/xampp/apache" Check that this is where the installation really is, it supposed to be here, not anywhere else. Xampp doesn't like it being somewhere else, loses itself too easily. Then look for the line: listen 80 Check to see if it is looking at the right port. Then scroll down some more and look for the line: ServerName localhost:80 If that is what it is reading then try addressing it as localhost/moodle/ in your browser. The 80 is the port number that Apache uses to listen for HTTP web based requests and localhost is the name given your Apache server. If you want to set it to the ip address of your local machine/server, then change the line to: listen 192.168.237.134:80 This assumes that the above address is static, in which case you might want to address it as 192.168.237.254:80, it cannot be dynamically assigned by the router. Obviously, you will have to reset your machine's network settings and instruct the router to not assign this address. HowToGeek.com can help you there if you are not sure how to do this. You can, if you have access to VMWare or similar, set up a virtual machine of, say, 60GB, and install Xampp there, giving that VM a static IP. Do not put anything else on it, just the Xampp, the Moodle, the WordPress, the Mahara , or anything else using PHP and MySQL, and your own web pages, of course. Also, I have found that the Apache Friends distro of Xampp is a little more stable, but if you want to do anything fancy in Apache, like virtual servers, then you're going to have a problem if you don't edit the httpd.conf and other configuration files through the Xampp Control Panel. One tiny edit can bring the whole thing down. I have been required to reinstall is for another project I have to work on, but my recommendation is to avoid Xampp at any cost. Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Title: Enrol all users in numerous courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Moodle 3.2.9 We are looking at implementing a number of courses which all users must take.  We are using a custom enrollment plugin based on external database enrollment. The situation: All active users at our university are required to take a particular course based on their role in the university Faculty members - Course A Staff - Course B or Course A (decision not yet taken) Students - Course C The users will be forced to retake at least once a year. Our current enrollment plugin only creates active users who are either enrolled or teaching at least 1 course.  Also, courses are created automatically by the plugin and maintained via cron daily.  Each semester we create new courses and associated enrollments. The problem is basically the staff users or any users not associated with a moodle course as they will not be in moodle as the Enrollment / User creation is supplied by our Student Info System (SIS). In a best case scenario, our SIS will create the necessary course and handle the enrollments including the staff users or for that matter and new users not yet associated with any courses. I was thinking Flat file enrollment but the users need to exist in moodle in order to be enrolled. Suggestions??? Eric

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrol all users in numerous courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Use a csv file. have a look at this documen t... You can use the same csv file for a lot of different things. Create a new file add in the users, as per instructions, then enroll them using the course short name. For example: username,password,firstname,lastname,email,course1,group,cohort1 And you might have details like: jane.doe,password,jane,doe,jane.doe@college.org,facultyA,faculty,, bill.smith,password,bill,smith,bill.smith@college.org,studentC,students,sophomore and so on. This way, you can add in whatever they want. Just set it so that when it is uploaded, the file doesn't create new users, or duplicate existing users if the user already exists. And course1 value = course short name. If you want more courses, then course2 and so on. Warning: I'm not sure what you are getting at when you mention your SIS, I have always thought that the SIS or LDAP or whatever would supply users authentication, but the users are still entered into the Moodle database. Never bothered to look myself. Check your dbase with a third party tool and see if that is so, or try a small file with a test group, which you should have one anyway. Or on your test Moodle to see if it works.  I have always had a test group of staff/faculty and students, two of each group to test these things with and i have no idea how many times I have wrecked my test Moodle before trying something on my production sites.. .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course completion not working for Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Howard, I am facing the same issue. I tried for activity completion but it is not working. Please suggest me some solutions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course completion not working for Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you sure you set the course completion criteria?  Just turning it on for the course and setting activity completion settings is not enough.  You have to tell it what constitutes completed. Also, check your activity completion report--does it show your activity (ies) as complete? Check your activity reports--it looks like you are requiring complete.  Does your scorm report complete?  I can publish something that looks like a scorm but doesn't actually report complete/incomplete if I don't tell it what I want.  If your scorm doesn't generate a final grade, you might want to use Learning objects for the activity grade (0=incomplete; 1=complete).  And some scorms report incomplete/passed/failed rather than incomplete/complete.  If you have a scorm that does have scores, you could set a required grade rather than passed/completed.  The authoring tool you use can really impact how your course reacts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Controlling concurrent Users
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have a business requirement, where I need a limited number of users only to access the course at a particular point in time. This is mostly in the case of a cohort group. Any suggestions on how we can achieve this? Thanks, Ramya

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Controlling concurrent Users
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm wary of saying that you can't do that.... but it would be very, very tricky. Moodle doesn't "know" how many people are logged in - even less who is accessing a particular course. The only thing you can do is to check who has accessed something in a course within the last 'n' minutes. I'm not sure how that would help you to achieve your requirement. I don't think it would.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Controlling concurrent Users
ResponsesInList.Text: One idea is to put your students into "groups," and then set up your activities to be restricted by time, thereby spreading out the load. For example, a quiz.  Duplicate the quiz, divide your students into two groups, make one quiz available to group1 from 12-4PM, and the other quiz available to group2 from 4-8PM. I am not exactly sure what you are trying to accomplish, however.  In general, most courses have to worry about quizzes, forums, and assignments.  Of these, I think it is only quizzing where you can run into loading problems (If 500 students are told, begin the quiz right now.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Controlling concurrent Users

ResponsesInList.Title: Backup Temp Dir error message
ResponsesInList.Text: 3.5 user, AWS servers:  When I & my teachers try to duplicate assignments & some other things, we get the error message error/cannot_empty_backup_temp_dir.  When I researched this in Moodle Docs & Help, I was told to make sure I had permission .  How do I do this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup Temp Dir error message
ResponsesInList.Text: Don't host on AWS but if it's a Linux, ownerships/permissions normally set in Linux via ssh session to server . Since Linux's use pretty much the same basic 'chown' and 'chmod' commands those are the commands one would use on /path/to/moodledata To check ownerships/permissions on moodledata directory, first list it: ls -ld moodledata That will show **something** like: drwxrwxr-x. 14 apache apache 4096 Sep 17 05:58 moodle35data Do the same for moodledata/temp/ [root@sos moodle35data]# ls -ld temp drwxrwxr-x. 7 apache apache 4096 Sep 16 06:50 temp The d is a directory.   The rwx is read/write/execute The 3 rwx's ... owner first set of 3, group is the second set of rwx, and the last set of rwx is 'others' ... that's all users in the globe. **EXAMPLE for moodledata/temp/ cd /path/to/moodledata/ chmod ug+rwx temp -R give user,group read/write/execute on directory temp and all directories files in temp (the -R is recursive). While in the ssh shell, you should have an online manual for commands (called 'man').  To see all the options and technical explanations for the 'chmod' command, use the following command: man chmod 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup Temp Dir error message
ResponsesInList.Text: On thinking about this some more .... and Oogling ... question: Is your moodledata in an S3 Bucket or some sort of bucket on Amazon?   Different beast from 'typical' moodledata on attached drive or a partiton on Linux server - which is what my previous response may have mistakendly 'assumed'.   Sorry 'bout that! So .... https://www.google.com/search?q=AWS+set+ownership+permissions and this https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Installation_Guide_for_Installing_on_Amazon_EC2 Please share how you are setup.   Surely there is someone in these forums that host on Amazon. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

viewing documentation for Moodle 3.1. Up-to-date documentation for the
latest stable version of Moodle is probably available here: error/moodle/cannot empty backup temp dir . This results from a file permissions error in the moodledata directory. Ensure file ownership and permissions are correct." Does anyone know if there's a doc that tells how to do this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: is there any way to salvage lost outgoing e-mails?
ResponsesInList.Text: You mean Moodle delivers mail to localhost which relays mail to the actual mail server? And the problem was in the actual mail server? Then I guess Moodle and the localhost have done their job. You can confirm by going through the mail logs of the localhost. Or, the mails are still spooled in localhost. Tell it to resend. (Typically "# sendmail -q")

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: is there any way to salvage lost outgoing e-mails?
ResponsesInList.Text:
```text
I got this info from our mail server admins:

The question is not, how we could resend from our mail-server, the
question is, how moodle can resend.
Our setup are one moodle-server (on alice), a mail-server (on alice,
too), a mail-server (on ben).  moodle -> localhost -> ben.
The mail-server on alice did not get any mail, because it was not
reachable.
How we can resend the mail, moodle failed to send?  «moodle-mail -q»?

If not, how we can configure moodle to use sendmail instead of smtp, to
prevent lost mails in future?

For your information, if not possible:  smtp never does promise to
accept a mail.  Also if server is running on localhost.  A restart of
the mail-server would be enough to lost mails.  So it is a stupid idea
to use smtp for sending mails, if moodle has no possible way to resend
mails.  It has to have a Queue.  If you say "mail-server should run on
localhost to prevent most issues", than you should not support smtp and
use sendmail.  (But we did not found an option in moodle to do that and
google sais no.)
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: is there any way to salvage lost outgoing e-mails?
ResponsesInList.Text: there is no easy way to get Moodle to resend all emails that have previously failed. But if you remove the smtphosts config setting in admin > Server >Email > Outgoing mail configuration (and leave it blank) then as per the description under that setting "If you leave this field blank, Moodle will use the PHP default method of sending mail." - which will likely pass it to sendmail on your local server. (as long as PHP is configured this way - it should be, it's the default method.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: is there any way to salvage lost outgoing e-mails?
ResponsesInList.Text: thanks, that will help us to avoid such problems in the future

ResponsesInList.Text: Welcome to the world wide web! That IP is scanning your server. ﻿ looking for a compromised server that might have had php scripts installed remotely. ***None of the php scripts you see in the logs are part of Moodle.*** The IP address: Do a whois on the ip and one will see that specific IP is from: inetnum:        132.232.0.0 - 132.232.255.255 netname:        TENCENT-CN While you could attempt at communicating to the netadmins of TENCENT asking them to investigate, prevent, block, etc. good luck with that! It's annoying ... and if you don't want to see them, block the range of IP addresses that would come from that network 132.232.0.0/16 If CentOS 7, there is a zone for 'reject' ... any access by an IP address in the class B block of IP's could be set to autoreject. firewall-cmd --zone=drop --add-source=132.232.0.0/16 would do it - does do it ... know for a fact as I have already blocked that net. If CentOS 6, one could use the route command to route all traffic from that class b block of IP's off into la-la-land. Now before some gets critical about blocking entire ranges of iP's and networks ... in case you haven't noticed, WWW3 - the cyberwar has already begun.   And, my clients are not from CN ... not that am prejudice, etc. ... it's a network thang ... nothing personal. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does Moodle have some sort of coin or token system?
ResponsesInList.Text: Doug, your concept is interesting, and I am not discouraging you from exploring it, it might be a creative way to teach, and I would not want to be the one to discourage creativity. In general, this seems to be the opposite of "normal" education: students learn something and "gain" knowledge.  The goal is typically to be rewarded for gaining knowledge.  Students start with zero percent knowledge, and they typically work up to 100 percent knowledge.  This is most often referred to as the "course grade." So your idea makes me wonder about the advantage of starting with 100 "coins" and using them up.  And I do not see the advantage of stopping a student from accessing learning activities because they have run out of "coins." Well, just my thoughts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does Moodle have some sort of coin or token system?
ResponsesInList.Text: Two plug ins that come to mind are these two blocks: Level up : a block where users earn XP by doing things in the course (teachers can set up what the kids do) - you can have multiple levels and set up a required amount of points to earn per level. Points can be earned on a course by course basis, or all points can add cumulatively for all courses. You can’t “trade in” these points but you can restrict acces to things based on a users current level. Stash Block : a block that houses a student’s “stash” - things they’ve earned. You can place “tokens” anywhere in a course for students to collect. They can even “trade in” objects in their stash for some other object. Hopefully these can at least help get you close to what you’re looking to do?

ResponsesInList.Title: User email addresses
ResponsesInList.Text: We use Moodle 3.5 on an AWS server ; we are using it with our Jr. & Sr. High school kids at present.  Here's the issue:  our younger students (grades 6 - 8) are still under their parents' guardianship, & some have siblings.  The parents want the emails to all be sent to one address, but Moodle won't allow an email address to be used for more than one person.   We are considering using Moodle school-wide (K - 12), but this would be a problem for over half our families!  Is there a workaround for this?  I know there are other schools out there using Moodle - how do they get around this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User email addresses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jonathan, There is a tick box that can enable multiple users to have the same email ID. Login as admin and Go to Dashboard > Site administration > Plugins > Authentication > Manage authentication. There is a tick box that says "Allow accounts with same email" , tick it and save. Now multiple users can have same email ID.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User email addresses
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks - finding the tick boxes if one doesn't know they're there is sometimes a challenge.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User email addresses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jonathan, it's there since 3.0 ( MDL-49280 ): https://docs.moodle.org/30/en/Managing_authentication#Allow_accounts_with_same_email . I'd not use it: use email aliasing hopefully supported by parent accounts. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User email addresses
ResponsesInList.Text: Another option is to use a 'trick' with a gmail account. Have the family create a gmail account if they do not have one. For this example, suppose the email account is jones@gmail.com When you create accounts in Moodle for the children (Sally, Bill, Ann) use the email addresses jones+sally@gmail.com, jones+bill@gmail.com, and jones+ann@gmail.com.  Moodle will recognize those as distinct email addresses.  However, when the email is sent, Gmail ignores the '+xxxxx' part of the address and sends all the emails to jones@gmail.com.  The neat part is that the email recipient can still see the '+xxxxx' part of the address, so the parents can identify to which student the email refers. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: backing up theme in moodle 3.1.6

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backing up theme in moodle 3.1.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Not sure what one means by: "my themed front page and subsequent pages I have created" If you backup course ID 1 ... which is the front page ... then whatever was on the front page is backed up.   But, there is a catch 22 there ... cannot restore the backup to the front page. Are these 'pages' to which you refer outside of Moodle, or are they moodle content ... you filled out some sort of resource in Moodle ... like a link to a Page?  Did you change the banner to the theme inside some sort of box for modifying the theme in Moodle? IF it's moodle content, the data is in the DB so making a full site backup would backup everything ... full site backup is an archive of the code directory, an SQL dump of the DB for the Moodle, and an archive of moodledata IF your addition/pages, images are outside of Moodle but contained in the code directory somehow then a backup of the moodle code has those additons/pages. Does that help? 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backing up theme in moodle 3.1.6
ResponsesInList.Text: HI Ken Where do I find course ID 1  ( file path ? ) , please ? My "front" page is where users see the site, and then click on the login button ( a hosting company has themed it for me ) . The other pages are ones that I created , php files  that contain site information etc What I wanted to do was to be able to back up all the text pages and theming (  as well as the courses which I've been able to do ), in the event of the hosting company going out of business/failing etc so that I don't have to start from scratch again, hope that makes sense ? Cheers Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backing up theme in moodle 3.1.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle is an application (dynamic) consisting of a bunch of php scripts which talk to your database (whose records from various tables contain the data) to render/display what one sees in browser.   Thus, there is no 'path' to the front page (in Moodle-ese, course ID 1) .   Unlike 'static' (not dynamic) web sites that have an index.html file containing HTML references to images and links to files.   All content on the page is actually in the index.html file - not in a database table. To backup the site in case servers go down or the provider goes out of business, etc.. one has to do a full site backup which consist of an archive of the code directory, an archive of the moodledata directory (where all uploaded files are stored), and a dump of the database (a .sql file). There is no built in link/admin tool to do a full site backup.  It must be performed outside of Moodle.  If you have ssh access a full site backup typically done through the use of an operating system utility called 'tar' (command line) - for moodle code and moodledata.  The .sql dump typicially created either through another mysql utility (command line) called 'mysqldump' or phpmyadmin if that's installed. Please see: https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Site_backup or https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Site_Backup_for_Low-tech_Users A full site backup will include the front page ... course ID 1. It is **very wise** to backup, from the Moodle course administration menu, **each course** on a regular basis (especially after adding a lot of content, or students have submitted major work, etc.).  And since you've sort of expressed a concern in where you host , download the course backups to store locally on your workstation.   Take the time to do that, and you will NOT regret it should something happen to server . Your site appears to be hosted with synergy-learning.com suggest contacting support there and ask about what other tools they might have to backup your site. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backing up theme in moodle 3.1.6
ResponsesInList.Text: A follow up ... synergy-learning.com is a moodle partner.   As such, if you have used any of their custom code/extensions (like a custom theme - ie, the front page, course ID 1, is under that custom theme, etc.) you might not have ssh nor the ability to backup and download the moodle code.   Just like no one can get the themes that moodle.org uses. Have never hosted with an MP, but don't think Synergy-Learning will go away any time soon ... they've been a Moodle Partner since mid 2000's ... MP's usually have redundancy and robust networks/servers and backups, even if you can't backup code yourself. So maybe the only backups one should concern themselves with are course backups. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assistant Help
ResponsesInList.Text: To see what plugins you have, go to Site Admin, Plugins, Plugins Overview.  You will see many because a normal Moodle comes with many plugins already there.  But in the Notes column, you will see "Additional" for those that you have added.  In MoodleCloud, you shouldn't see any Additional plugins because of the restriction to not allow plugins. To find which plugins are available, go to Moodle.org, in the Extend Moodle area, click on Moodle plugins directory.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assistant Help
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, Nancy, what Rick says, and yes, it is really frustrating beginning with Moodle and it is far more sophisticated now than it was when I started using it...mumbledy, mumbledy years ago. I am handicapped by being male though.. so read the instruction second last and ask for help only when all other options are secondary to suicide. A lot of what you need is actually right there, but it is often couched in terms or presented in ways not familiar to us, so we get it wrong too often. Ask yourself, "What do I absolutely need first?" A general repository of materials you already have perhaps? So how do I get those things onto the Moodle first? Once comfortable with that, "What do I want next?" Do it one step at a time, starting with the most simple things then getting more and more sophisticated as you get more confident. The issue is not the Moodle, it is just a tool, it is our approach to it that really counts. The more we rush it, the more frustrated we become. In another post, one of our long term developers, and I think really imaginative and one of the best, Chris Kenniberg, made the comment that it takes years to get really comfortable with something like Moodle. So be patient and do what you are comfortable with, build your skills don't try and do it all at once. After all, even the Triangle player needs a lot of practice and experience before joining the orchestra.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error Setting up of database session failed.
ResponsesInList.Text: Version of Moodle is very (very) old ... 2.0. Back then the thought was to use the database for recording user sessions ... newer versions now use files for sessions as opposed to DB. Don't re-call if 2.0 will take this addition to the config.php file or not, but try it: Add to config.php file the following: $CFG->dbsessions='0'; Just to make sure in your moodledata directory, create a directory called 'sessions' and make sure it has the same ownerships/permissions as other directories in your moodledata. No need to restart any service or server.   Just try your site again ... config.php file is read almost on every access to your site so if the above works for your old version, it's in affect right away on next client access. PS - you need to upgrade ... period! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: JPG vs. JPEG
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mitchell, By the way, getting Unoconv to also handle a .jpeg file can be done by making two modifications to the unoconv file to add the file type in the Graphics and Presentation section of recognized file formats. On my Centos server the Unoconv file is located at /usr/bin/unoconv and all I did was search for jpg. There are two format instances, one in the Graphics section and one in the Presentation section. I duplicated the two lines of code and changed each occurrence of jpg to jpeg, saved the file, and then restarted the service. If a student submits either .jpg or .jpeg files, they are correctly converted to PDF's. If a student submits a LO Impress or MS PowerPoint file with jpg or jpeg pictures on a slide, the whole file is correctly converted to a multiple page PDF with the pictures correctly rendered. Since the modification is done to the unoconv file, it will be applied to conversions for all sites and versions of Moodle on the server.
