ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how do you guys update course content? moodle 3.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes and no. If you delete the attempt, you delete the grade. The work around is to record the grades on paper, delete the attempts, and then manually enter a grade in the grade book. This will preserve the grade data in a manner, but you'll lose any data in the attempt (like how many incorrect, which questions seemed to be problematic, etc.). It will allow you, however, to edit the Quiz activity by adding/removing/rearranging questions as you would like. So in a sense, for a Quiz, the attempt is also an automatic grade, while a manual grade is not an attempt by proxy. Does this make sense? For example, we have almost all of our tests that are done on paper also programmed in Moodle via the Quiz activity. For most of these, it is teacher-preference to use either the Moodle or paper version as we meet 5 days per week face-to-face. I'd much prefer the electronic version as the benefits for time-savings outweigh any particular cons in from my perspective, but this is teacher choice at the end of the day. Grades for the paper version are entered in the grade book using a manual entry for that particular Quiz activity if completed on paper. I'll also add that once you have completed attempts, Moodle does not like it when you adjust answer keys for correct or additional answers while a test is in progress. I don't know the underlying logic myself but I'm sure it is perfectly legitimate and sound. This will throw errors at students taking the test when they submit it. As a result, they'll have a number of incomplete items to do over again (learned this the hard way but couldn't quite figure out that it was my fault for a while, thinking I was being proactive in improving the answer keys while tests were going on). This was for the Cloze question type in particular, but also if you are trying to change other question types like drop downs or drag-n-drop. For the Cloze qtype, you can add any number of additional wrong-but-partial credit responses to the answer key when the test is going on. So, if you need to change part of an answer key for additional correct answers with the Cloze type in particular (I've made plenty of mistakes and typos that students are gracious enough to point out), best to wait until after all attempts are submitted to adjust it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how do you guys update course content? moodle 3.0
ResponsesInList.Text: For me, Billy, the issue is not necessarily the content, it is the timing of updates. Maths and Science courses don't significantly change, replaced, yes, but not often changed. Typos and minor errors are easily corrected, any time, but when replacing whole documents, experiments, assignments, quizzes and that, they are done after a course is completed. This is in preparation for the next group of students who will be using it. Break times, tend to be a bit busier than I would like sometimes but that is how it is. I don't use text books in classes, but I will use the materials from them in my course, as a Book resource, a scanned page, a Page emulating a solution, so that eventually, the Moodle becomes the complete reference. I also have a number of text books for each subject and each grade level so I can diversify the materials a little. Text books can be mistaken as dogma, particularly text books that do not get changed for year after year, which discourages critical thinking, so why limit students? I do not keep the same courses going year after year, how boring, but always revitalise the materials to suit changing trends, sometimes changing curriculum ideas, but mainly to suit the cohort. No two year's cohorts are the same, and what worked last year is going to bore this year's crop because it's too easy or too difficult. I'm finding the basic information remains the same, but the approach needs to be adaptable. Your question seems like it is looking for a perfect solution, and I have to tell you, there isn't one.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how do you guys update course content? moodle 3.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Colin, This is a fair point since you are maintaining your own content. Timing is definitely important. Timing for upgrades/changes can be tricky so as to minimize expected and unexpected issues. We have 6 quarters per year (I know that doesn't quite make sense, but as a quarter system, so too are summer and winter sessions run on 8 week segments in addition to the 2 in the fall/spring) which makes large scale changes tricky as there is rarely much down time save for our winter break which is the longest at two weeks. I often end up having to phase changes in 'quietly' from one group or level live each quarter versus everything at once. But I also have a much smaller population to support which makes that much more amenable. I'd be much more hard pressed to work this way in a larger university department or university at large unless they gave me free reign and would tolerate the resistance and backlash I would no doubt face . What is your strategy for updating the content for your classes? I'm lucky(?), or our faculty are lucky(?) in that it is my job to assist and facilitate them in making those changes. They are free to do them, but often it goes into a request list into a Kanban system where they set what they want to be done with some specifications/guidelines, and then I go and do it! They get to review and edit after that before it is considered complete. I'm also lucky (?) in that most of the current faculty really do not care about doing the changes themselves-all they really want is for Moodle and their courses to work. I know if I were one of the faculty members and knew how to do all of this, I would probably get far more involved then they do-but just a quirk of how our organization is at the moment.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how do you guys update course content? moodle 3.0
ResponsesInList.Text: William, we use a four term system for our K-12 education's academic year. This is usually with T1 and 2 being Semester 1 and T3 and 4 for semester 2 for Year (or Grade) 7-Year 12. Each term has a division of 14 days between them and five or six weeks (on the calendar) over the early summer, end of academic year in December to beginning new academic year at the end of January. I am at the mercy of my employer with regard to the schools Moodles I have used, but I admin a small "not-for-profit" Moodle for a social support charity in my spare time. I do it all for my classes, and help other teachers who are interesting in using Moodle by providing them with materials or access to my courses, seems to work. The school Moodles are usually simple, the Australian Curriculum varies little from year to year and with the emphasis on content, so changing them often becomes a response to what the Students start off with. I am starting to flip my classes, so it's all changing again, but the essential ideas won't change that much initially. I have videos that students will be using and from there, they will get sets of exercises to suit the requirements, in Maths. There is not a lot I can do to change it, except use a variety of worksheets. For the better cohorts, a lot of problem solving, for the not so good, more fluency drills. That is basically about it for Maths. Science is different though. We have far more scope to take a more varied approach even with the content driven approach of the AC. I try to mix it up irrespective of learning abilities. Fewer worksheets and more research work. I have been using wikis for collaborative writing, but I have considered using Peer Instruction with it as well. Going to give it a try with senior students in the near future I think. Fewer quizzes and a range of research questions inside a topic is another idea. For resources, differentiation doesn't work for practicals (labs), so prac reports are assessed on the perceived abilities of the students in the prac group, which is actually quite difficult. (Any ideas or other strategies for using assessment as a differentiation tool would be most welcome.) Most of this kind of thing already exists, so I don't have to worry about writing it up, just make sure the students know they can download materials from the Moodle prior to coming to class. Something I have been thinking about is "This class is Science 1102, this semester we are investigating these areas. Pick a topic from this list of areas, (areas we are supposed to cover from the AC), that interests you. Investigate it and present your findings on it at semester's end." They have to do their own research, write their own essays, provide models, videos, podcasts, presentations, or anything that they are comfortable with that demonstrates their learning. This can represent a chunk of their semester grade, and they get lesson time to work on it. With this, they only have to use the Moodle to get basic information, then they are on their own. There won't be any resources apart from links to specific skills needed for something, whatever the students ask for, but will need a forum or other activities to ensure they are heading in the right direction. This means it could be set up and running in a day or two. The not-for-profit is different. I have to be more careful as government, both State and Federal, will change the rules around welfare services or child protection or even road rules and that site needs more accurate information. That can be changed any time, as there is someone in the local office who's job it is to track any change then bring it to social workers and counsellors attention, and mine too. When I get confirmation of a change, I just go in and rewrite that section. So far, it works and it is not a big drain on my time so I am happy to do it. Phew... long winded, sorry about that, but I hope it answers your questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to delete the queue of outgoing (notification) mails

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to delete the queue of outgoing (notification) mails
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle isn't a mail server .  It does 'package up' ... ie, builds information into EMail formats to be sent and attempts to send ... but it doesn't really have a 'que' of mail that hasn't been delivered for one reason or another.   That's the job of the mail server to which Moodle is pointed via SMTP or if one is NOT using an SMTP relay then it could be the local Exim/PostFix/Sendmail ques on the server itself. So to clear mailques, one has to check the ques of whatever is setup to handle the mail. Hope that helps in where to look! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to delete the queue of outgoing (notification) mails
ResponsesInList.Text:
The main cron job actually consist of a series of 'scheduled task' in 3.5.   The task can be executed by themselves. Go to: https://yoursite/admin/tool/task/scheduledtasks.php Find related task  ... there is a 'run now' link.  You won't find one for 'clear mail ques' cause Moodle isn't a mail server! There is one for "Check for updates
\core\task\check_for_updates_task" and one for Forum mailings and maintenance jobs
\mod_forum\task\cron_task Those are both part of the main cron job but when running the task, limited to only that part/piece of the main cron job. If linux, suggest having a ssh terminal window open where you can watch server logs in realtime.  I install a thing called multitail and then configure it to show me realtime logs ... access log, error logs of apache, messages log, and if you are running Exim/PostFix/Sendmail then their log file. Or 'poor mans monitor' ... tail -f /var/log/maillog 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Copying sections between courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Once again I find myself struggling with copying between courses. One of the key things about Moodle is how you are going to set up your courses... If you have a lot of educational content, which topics are separate courses and which topics can be in one course but separate topics... I'm sure you are all struggling with this. Do I make one course called 'English' and inside that course I have topics called 'Grammar' and 'Vocab'... or do I make two separate courses for this. Now it happens quite often that over the years come new insights. Topics become courses or... courses become topics within a course. I find it really difficult to merge courses in Moodle. Importing just overwrites all topics. Inserting empty topics at the start of a course and then importing works sometimes, but still you often end up with moving imported resources/ activities around. There's a plugin called 'Sharing Cart' which helps as well. Or the 'mass action block'. Yet I feel there's basic Moodle functionality missing here. What if... when importing from a course... you have one step between. A screen that actually asks you where in the course you want the imported content to show up? You import from course X section 1 does not always mean that you want it imported in course Y section 1. Might be section 2 where you need it. Can someone relate to what I'm saying here? Sharing content between courses should be a lot more easy than the current 'import' option?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable remove course from database when press delete button
ResponsesInList.Text:
Debug gives you the info needed to solve: Debug info: MySQL server has gone away The database server couldn't keep up with the data it was processing or getting from the Moodle. To start, need to add one line to the config file for MySQL if you can: 
```text
max_allowed_packet  = 32M
```
 The value of 32M is a guess here.  The default for max_allowed_packet in MySQL 5.5 to 5.7 is 16M. After adding the line to my.cnf, must restart MySQL for the changes to take effect. That might get you by.   You might have to make other/more tweaks to DB server config. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Professional membership in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. Cohorts would probably work.  I personally love cohorts.  But it isn't clear if all of them will have the same courses assigned.  That said, you could have a variety of cohorts (I used to have>50 at a time). 2.  The short answer is yes.  The longer one is really...it all depends on how you want to award hours. Do you just want hours on a certificate?  That's easy if you use the Custom Certificate plugin.  Do you use Configurable Reports (plugin) to do some sort of student transcript and track how many hours  students get with SQL reports?  Well...yes, but quite a bit might go into that (including custom course fields and such). 3.  Don't know what you mean by this?  You want them to get a certificate at the end of a course?  Easy to do.  A Badge?  Easy to do.  A Badge after completing a series of courses?  Easy to do.  Some other thing?  Might be more complicated (Competencies?). 4.  Not sure what you mean by have access to create...Admins can pretty much do anything.  You want to upload a document for only those students?  You can do that; just add restriction for membership in the cohort(s) you add them to.  If you use Configurable Reports, you could probably build a report that pulls particular courses and is only visible for particular cohorts as well.  But that is a bit more complicated. 5.  If you use the Custom Certificate, you can have it email students a certificate when they complete the course (but course completion restriction is also a plug-in, but a super useful one).

Per
your message, if Teacher is to be able to send messages then so can any
authenticated user including students which vitiates achieving my goal.
Looks like it is quite a common goal. Is my understanding correct? Thanks Mary was just trying to get messaging to work.  She didn't care if students messaged other students like you and I do. The main issue with the sendmessage permission is that it is all or nothing.  If you deactivate it, then student's can't send teacher's messages as well.  So to prevent them from messaging students, you have to ALSO prevent them from messaging teachers. What most people want is to enable teacher-to-student messaging only.  Unfortunately, moodle messaging doesn't support this, and you have to hack moodle code to make it work. For 3.4 and 3.5, if you are willing to add a few lines of code, it makes it happen: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=360307

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cannot setup email
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunately, setting up email at the server level just isn't simple. It's not Moodle's fault. There's a load of different ways a mail server can be configured. I assume you mean that Moodle is not able to send emails at all? Is this the case? Essentially, you need to find an SMTP server that you have access to. Ask your hosting company or your server admin depending on how Moodle is hosted. You then need the hostname of that server and the authentication details if you need them. You then go to Site administration > Server >Email > Outgoing mail configuration, and stick the details in the boxes and save. If you're lucky it'll all work. It shouldn't be any more complicated than that. Sometimes it is, but it's usually because the mail server or a firewall is not set up correctly. What you can't expect is to send email without identifying a 'friendly' mail server. These days you'll just be blocked. Spam prevention. However, if it was working and it stopped, what changed? Moodle doesn't just stop sending mail.

ResponsesInList.Text: Mohamed, I can not speak about other LMSs. But in Moodle's case, it is set up to charge for courses, not membership. So the payment plugins are really enrolment plugins which require payment. If you want to charge for membership to the Moodle site, there is no plugin type that I am aware of for that. But its fairly easy to use the Moodle webservices (or API directly) to code responses to events from the payments processor (eg create user, change user password, etc). While that will work, personally I think it makes more sense to alter the business model to fit Moodle, than Moodle to fit the business model.  So I suggest that you let people have free membership to the site, and I guess offer some free trial courses, and then have some courses backed by a paypal/stripe enrolment plugin.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Open  tag in Additional HTML rendered whole site useless
ResponsesInList.Text: So you can't go directly to: http://yoursite/admin/settings.php?section=additionalhtml If that fails, add the following line to config.php depending upon if header, body, or footer: $CFG->additionalhtmlhead=''; $CFG->additionalhtmlfooter=''; $CFG->additionalhtmltopofbody=''; No need to restart anything, just log back in and get the area via the menus. Make your edits in the correct box using the closing tag this time ... or just remove what have. Save. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: unoconv not converting documents
ResponsesInList.Text: While not absolutely true... the files get put in Moodle's file system which is as good as impossible to find. The name is hashed and it's put in a numeric directory structure. Basically, you need to find it in mdl_files and then work out where the file is. Good luck! For your second question, Moodle *would* realise it was a different document. Files are identified based on their contents, not their name. So even one character different would make the file different in the underlying file system. The "real" name is only stored in the database table.

In the last 15 years that setup has had issues only once ... easily fixed ... directions were sent via EMail. One of the other things I do now is change the 'standard' port 22 for ssh to something else.  In less than 2 minutes today new servers get their first pokes and probes at the ssh port - not that they can guess a secure password easily ... they never stop ... annoying ... sooooo take away Then one can acquire Moodle via git (install git first) so that installations can be done via command line ... no issues with infinite loops.   And it can, from that time forward, be easily updated or upgraded.  Zero day flaws .. fixed/patched in a matter of minutes ... as soon as Moodle HQ releases them. Then there's the additional handy stuff ... mysqlTuner, OS tools dns-utils, iptraf, alpine, zip and unzip etc. and as one needs/discovers one needs, install other. Not long ago, there was a sys admin ... new, just taken over, etc..  Had Scientific Linux.   Couldn't allow remote assitance .. so http://sos.tcea.org/moodle32/ CentOS 7 with Apache Solr search working, Annotation working ... and a course for Installing Moodle Solr SLinux 6 or CentOS 6 or CentOS 7 - self-enrol ...   patterened after what was done with a BC, CA user running Ubutnu 16.04 ... that had Moodle Partner backups to restore but assistance to do so, didn't finish, etc.   Was truely an old-time course by 'correpondence course' via EMail with txt file attachments that had 'copy and paste' commands. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: unoconv not converting documents
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been trying to work out our issue with unoconv on a Jessie install (Moodle 3.2+, Apache2.4, PHP 5.6) as well. I have had positive results with a few different options. Place an environment change in the /usr/bin/unoconv script around line #1206: ### Main entrance os.environ['HOME'] = '/tmp'                <------- Added this line if __name__ == '__main__': Changing the HOME variable to /tmp from the default of /root works for us but maybe changing that fariable in the unoconv script is not a best practice since the script will undergo an update at some point and scrub the change. Another option: Place a line in /etc/apache2/envvars about line #5 or so (then restart Apache) # this won't be correct after changing uid unset HOME export HOME=/tmp                     <------- Added this line Adding the envvars line changes the HOME variable for the Apache user I believe while still keeping the system HOME as /root. I do not know if this is a wise thing to do (simply because I am not an Apache expert, barely a novice). Last option which may be a good one: add a putenv("HOME=/tmp"); in the Moodle config.php file. In our case each of these has resulted in the unoconv tool working properly. I get the feeling that setting the HOME variable in the config fill will provide the safest results as it would then limit the effects to just the Moodle application. As it turns out, changing the owner of /var/www to the www-data user also works.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Clamav unix domain socket not working
ResponsesInList.Text:
/tmp got sticky bit by default, /tmp permissions should never be modified without need, it may lead to a various system issues! In this particular case, I think user clamav is not able to access /tmp/phpKv1QbL which is owned by www-data:www-data, Kieu need to check if clamav is really a member of www-data group, e.g.: 
```text
kabalin@web0:~$ id clamav


uid=37998(clamav) gid=110(clamav) groups=110(clamav),33(www-data)
```
 If that is the case, make sure that clamav daemon has been restarted, so that group membership change has been applied to daemon.

ResponsesInList.Title: Students see all submissions in the assignment of their group
ResponsesInList.Text: I recently upgraded to version 3.4. In this version I noticed that the students see the submissions of other students in the same group. In the previous version (3.1) the students did not see the submission to the other students, only yours by default. How to fix this? Thank´s

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students see all submissions in the assignment of their group
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello. Can you confirm you are using the assignment activity and have you checked "Students submit in groups"? Is that what you intended to do? If you select students submit in groups then they are basically working together on an assignment so are expected to see each other's work. If you merely want them to submit their own individual assignments you don't select this option.  They might be in different teaching groups anyway, but they should still submit individually if that is what you prefer.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Visual statistics for single user.
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, it really depends.  The data is all there, you just need to figure out how to make it visual. For example, your #1 question might not need anything visual.  One can simply look at the student's grade book for grades.  Or look at the quiz results (for times and grades.)  Or take this data into Excel. For #2, you will never know what people watch.  You can see if they clicked on a video link, but that's about it. But let me probe a little.  Can you give us an example of what you would really like to have?  Maybe sketch out an example, scan it, and upload it? This week I will be giving a presentation at MoodleMoot Spain titled "Using Tableau with Moodle for Visual Analytics."  Might you be attending?  We could meet and talk more about your needs.  (After my presentation, I will be posting a link to more information that supports my presentation.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Visual statistics for single user.
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Rick, this is what I'd like to see in moodle. 1. a graph that visually reports what/when a single student has done and with what outcome; something like this 2. a general report that shows what a student has completed and how, and what not has completed yet; something like this These examples are picked from khan academy. It's just to give an idea of course. Is your presentation available? I'm interested in testing visuals for analyzing learning outcomes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Visual statistics for single user.
ResponsesInList.Text: It could certainly be done. It would even be an interesting project. ...but you're going to have to find/pay someone to write the thing.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Visual statistics for single user.

Your first diagram, since it tries to capture "time" can't be done.  "Time" is unknown for most activities .  Video time is meaningless for a student. However, number of clicks might be interesting to look at (as in your "energy" idea.)  Also, I am not sure if the "by date" is meaningful.  But your general idea makes some sense to measure energy along with a final activity grade.  Well, just my thoughts. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrading Moodle 2.9+
ResponsesInList.Text: Can't hyperjump from 2.9+ to 3.5. In moodle it's called a 'migration'.   May not be like any 'migration' you've ever done. https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Moodle_migration If the 2.9+ site is still up, login and go to server -> environment.   Update the component.   Then use the drop down pick list for versons from current to 3.5 ... which will be getting a point release this week or very soon to 3.5.1. There will be changes to the DB you will need to make as well as PHP version. Best to test migration/upgrades like this on a sandbox setup server. You might want to start at: https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Releases#Moodle_2.9 and work your way through all the versions above noting the changes at each version to work out a plan for the 'march' ... 2.9.x to the highest 2.9.x -> 3.0.highest -> might be able to go to 3.4.highest, then to 3.5. Easier if on Linux and using Git - IMHO ! ;) 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Text: Not sure how often Moodle checks, but it should be able to access accounts.google.com which really could be different in DNS resolution depending upon your location and proximity to a Google center of some sort. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating Alias shortcut files
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Mr Clay, thanks for your query. Firstly it is worth recapping, especially for anyone reading this who is grappling with this, that from what I can see the key to using Alias files and updating them is that the main original filename must stay the same, so you need to upload a new file with the same name as the existing file then choose overwrite. This can be a pain if you want to replace e.g. ADVICE_SPRING18 with ADVICE_SUMMER18, however you can rename the link name if that helps. Once you realise this then it is possible to update these files in their original location. However there does seem to be a delay. This may actually be a browser cache issue rather than cron. Try this work around to force the update - it worked for me: 1. Upload replacement file with exactly same name and choose OVERWRITE in the main file location. 2. Download or open this file in this same original main file area 3. ResponsesInList.Text: While Colin and Howard have already responded to the original request and provided solution, thought I'd throw in 2 cents for leaving the moodle in /moodle/ Why? The https certificate is probably not a global but for a host ... what ever is at Apache server (ssl config) document root.   So if one changes CA's or whatever, there would no longer be anything to mess with in regards to apps that have restrictions/protections for the URL to the site. Leaving Moodle in it's own code directory allows one to use something in /var/www/html/  To begin, maybe a blank (no content) autoforwarding index.php or index.html file to /moodle/ This allows (if there is enough space on server and DB server can handle a little more) for the cloning of the production site (the code in /moodle/) to a /dev/ instance for the purpose of 'testing' .... all sorts of things moodle ... new theme, new plugins, etc. ... and one doesn't have to be concerned about wrecking the production site. Matter of fact, one will find all over the community forums the recommendation of a sandbox/dev site for testing and trying things there before doing the same things on production - especially an upgrade. Having a /dev/ on same server means same environment .... apache config/ mysql /php with extensions etc. No need to spin up another server ... no need to install a local host version (Windows or Mac or Linux or Virtualbox, etc.) setup. One also doesn't have to add/change DNS .... production code in /moodle/ 'tinker site' in dev ... still under one FQDN and the /dev can be restricted multple ways -  allowing on those who should be tinkering. Yes, there are some catch 22's ... version of PHP + My SQL /MariaDB version/config are two (but that has only bitten some who have had older moodles ... waited too long to upgrade the moodle).  Got 3.5?  That's long term support. Ok, my 2 cents. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Office 365 - School Data Sync Moodle 3.5
ResponsesInList.Text: I was just wondering if anyone has used the School Data Sync option in the Office 365 plugin. Currently it says it is in Preview Mode. Does it work? Can it create Moodle Courses and synchronise the enrolment of Students based on their membership to Office 365 Class Groups on Azure?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Office 365 - School Data Sync Moodle 3.5
ResponsesInList.Text: ermmmm complicated method. More complicated a method is, the greater chance of error. Best bet, Use Moodle as your LMS and use Office365 as a tool kit to produce documents.  Don't try anything fancy, it never works; keeping things simple makes it easier for everyone, particularly time-strapped teachers. I would suggest here that Office365 is not always the best option to be producing documents.

ResponsesInList.Title: Resources with non latin file names error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Everybody! This a new Moodle 3.4 installation on IIS web server with English and Greek language packs installed. ( http://e-learning.okana.gr ) Whenever someone tries to download a file or folder with a greek file name, no matter the browser used, gets a "file not found" error. Greek texts and greek resource names are working fine. The corresponding php database , conserning the file name field,  is configured with UTF. Attached a test file with a greek file name if someone could give it a try! Thank you in advance,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Resources with non latin file names error
ResponsesInList.Text: Works fine when I view in a course or when I download the file from a course. My environment is very different though. Centos 7.3, Moodle 3.4.3+ Build 20180621, mysql 5.6.40, php 7.2.2, and utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Off topic: I just the other day created a Greek keyboard layout for MooTyper that will be in the next release. ResponsesInList.Title: Cohort, Groupings and Groups
ResponsesInList.Text: So I have spent more than a day trying to find a solution to my situation - which I think involves Cohorts, Groupings and Groups. Unfortunately I cannot find anything that deals with my specific situation and I cannot think of a work-around. I am using Moodle 3.4.2+. I have a course (digital literacy) which is delivered from 10 different sites by 10 different facilitators. Each course runs for 2 weeks and each site accommodates 15 participants. Assessment of the assignments submitted by each participant is done centrally by one individual (the assessor). Assignments submitted by the participants include both individual assignments and group assignments. The assignment groups groups are site based, each consisting of 3 participants, i.e. 5 assignment groups per site. The individual doing the assessment (the assessor) needs to assess participants per site and assesses both individual and group work. My challenge is that I see no way of grouping participants per site, who themselves then need to be grouped into group-assignment groups in such a way that the assessor can go to the Gradebook and assess all the site participants from that site. As I see it, Gradebook only  accommodates one way of selecting participants to grade and I, therefore could not, for example, create Groupings (or a Cohort) to separate participants per site and then create Groups within these Groupings for group assignment submission, since the assessor would not be able to assess per Grouping in Gradebook. The alternative would be to create one course per site per course cohort, which would mean 10 sites x 2 (two groups per month) x 12 (months of the year) which would be 240 separate courses - which I think would be unmanageable. Unless, of course, I have missed something - and I am hoping some clever and experienced Moodler can point me in the right direction. Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cohort, Groupings and Groups
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andy, When you say 'site', in Moodle terms is this a group which is made up of people based in the same location? Or are you talking about different Moodle sites? I think you mean the former, so I'll go with that assumption for this reply. A few things to be aware of: Groupings are groups of groups. Users can be members of several groups. Groups can be members of several groupings. So I think this is how you set it up: 1 Grouping called Locations. This Grouping contains the groups called Belfast, Paris, Prague. Students are added to these groups. Then you have a Grouping called Belfast. This grouping contains the groups Belfast A, Belfast B, Belfast C, Belfast D, Belfast E. Students are added to these groups accordingly. Similarly, create groupings called Prague and Paris, put their respective groups in them, and put the students in to the groups. Now create your last Grouping. This Grouping is called Assignments. Put all of your Belfast A-E, Prague A-E, Paris A-E groups in to this grouping. Use the Assignments grouping for the group assignment.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User Tour Questions

If you're unable to upgrade to 3.5, there's a work around, where you basically add the course id to the target of the tour and then duplicate the tour for new courses. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Notification issues: your advice is welcome
ResponsesInList.Text: Users can alter their own preferences for recieving notfications about assignments. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Installing plug-in in test environment
ResponsesInList.Text: You can install plugins via ftp if you are sure they are packaged properly and you are putting them in the right folder within the Moodle codebase. I am not sure what the error with the certificate you mention could be, but I think validation is something different, i.e. checks on the plugin itself rather than anything to do with the certificate. It would help if you could post a screen shot.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Installing plug-in in test environment
ResponsesInList.Text: Sounds like your cloned site was running under a valid (acquired from a CA) certificate (not to be confused with certificates in Moodle) where the site URL is https:// and there is a green icon indicating the cert for the server FQDN is valid. The clone is still set to run https but the server it resides upon does't have. a valid (acquired from a CA) certificate setup, thus you see in FireFox the warning about site not be valid and an option to override (or accept self-signed cert). For installing plugins in the clone, please see: https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/Installing_plugins IF you attempt to use 'install from Moodle.org' that might fail as the plugins server at Moodle may not be able to see and talk to your test clone using https ... which is what it would prefer to do. Thus suggest installing via zip file might be best in this case.   That means, however, that you, the OP , have downloaded the zip that is compatible with your version of Moodle. Having said that however, please see: https://docs.moodle.org/35/en/SSL_certificate_for_moodle.org for a way to 'borrow' a cert to use with your cloned site that could possibly help in using 'install from Moodle.org' option. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 回复: Re: My HTML editor not start in Moodle 1.9.5
ResponsesInList.Text: There are just too many changes for any upgrade to be workable. I would suggest backup all your existing courses, unzip them, strip the code out of the text parts and then in v3.5, paste the remaining text into new courses. Upload images individually. This takes time, but unless you have thousands of users, and hundreds of courses, you are going to be bored as opposed to being frustrated and seriously stressed. Go to you site, place it into Maintenance Mode, delete the editing folder, replacing it with the newly unzipped editor. Take your site out of Maintenance Mode and test it, see if that works. The connectionless state of code in web apps allows you to do this without compromising other parts of your app.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need Help with User Tours
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a late reply, but I am not encountering this same need and I've found a solution that works for us. I'm hoping this helps others who might find this thread. While Moodle 3.3 will strip the iframe tags, it seems to not mind some other basic HTML tags, such as the <video> tag.  I was able to successfully embed a video into a User Tour by using this tag.  So you need to post your video to a publicly reachable location that will allow your video to be accessed and then you can use this code: <video width="###" height="###" controls> <source src="http://path/to/your/video.mp4" type="video/mp4" /> </video> Replace the ## signs with the dimensions of your video. More about how to use this tag can be found here: https://www.w3schools.com/tags/tag_video.asp I hope this helps someone!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle LMS Username and Password Verification 504 Gateway Time-out
ResponsesInList.Text: DNS doesn't "verifies the password and username" but 504 Gateway errors do/could involve DNS. There isn't a single fix ... must be investigated. Google Search: https://www.google.com/search?q=504+Gateway+error One can see several links. Please see from the above Google search, this page (many are just like it): https://bobcares.com/blog/how-to-fix-504-gateway-timeout-error-in-your-websites/ While the next is about WordPress, what one does is almost the same for Moodle: https://www.000webhost.com/blog/504-gateway-timeout Where one is hosted, how hosted, in control of DNS or not, etc. makes a difference in more specific information. Suggest contacting help desk of hosting provider for some assistance. If using a Mac client/Linux client (can even run from your own server if Linux) ... try some curl test to your server. Like: curl -vvv -I https://FQDNofYourMoodleSite/ include the /moodle/ directory if that's how you access your Moodle. Do a 'dig' for your server: dig fqdnofmoodleserver Do a reverse lookup on the IP address seen in the output of above: dig -x IPADDRESS Other things to check .... php max execution time, time zone correct? Your web service errors logs. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MS Office Skills Test - Word, Excel, PowerPoint
ResponsesInList.Text: This sort of skill testing has always been difficult to authenticate in an online environment. The question is whether the person logging in, is the same person who is enrolled. Without the usually expensive and often tempramental software, it is hard to ensure the candidate is the right person. What is the targeted environment? Business, College, Training school, University, Secondary School? Or is it all online, a remote learning situation? Each situation has some benefits that can lend themselves to a partial solution, and that is all it is, a partial solution, because nothing is guaranteed. All I have usually relied upon is the honesty of the candidate, which is easy to ensure if I am the Invigilator. I have used email to provide a code to access an activity, but not in Moodle, (don't know if that one would even fly in Moodle). With online things, it is even more difficult. In these things, there is likely no right answer,  I don't think I have one, someone else may have something. However, having said that, mostly remote students use laptops, with webcams. The testing software could include a photo if the Candidate, taken at the time of testing. Things like keystroke loggers and that are not just an intrusion on people, they are an outright threat and I would never suggest they be used at any time. I expect that anything that does that will be outlawed in the EU soon anyway, if not already, so I wouldn't go there. Other countries will follow suit, I expect.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MS Office Skills Test - Word, Excel, PowerPoint
ResponsesInList.Text: I used to teach office applications and never bothered to try and automate document evaluations via quizzes the way you mention. I did use multiple choice question based quizzes for making sure they knew office applications vocabulary, tools, locations of items on menus, etc. But, when I wanted to see a student, " format the title of a document ," I had them create a whole document and submit it in an assignment. The built in capability of Moodle to convert files to PDF's was very handy and allowed me to mark up their submissions, just as I would if they had submitted the assignment as hard copy on paper. When I bought myself a tablet with pen, it just got even easier to grade. ResponsesInList.Title: Q&A Forum Subscriptions
ResponsesInList.Text: The Q&A forum is a great way to make sure students post their responses before reading other replies. However there seems to be an issue with the subscriptions for those forums. When a student submits his/her answer to the instructor's question, that complete post is emailed to all subscribers, which defeats the purpose of making students post first if they can read it in an email. Yes, subscriptions could be disabled, but that also defeats the purpose of student interaction in the forum whenever the question is answered. Is there an option for Q&A forums to only have a notification email that a post was created with only the subject and none of the content?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Q&A Forum Subscriptions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bryce, I think that's not one of the possibilities. There are 4 subscription modes for forum activities : Optional > Users have to opt in Initial > Users have to opt out Forced > Everybody gets the updates, no opt out Disabled > No updates are sent, no opt in You could switch subscription mode to Optional, so your users can choose for themselves which discussions they wish to follow.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Q&A Forum Subscriptions
ResponsesInList.Text: Joost, Thank you for your reply. You're right, the students could opt out, but the instructor needs the ability for students to be notified of new posts because of the collaborative nature of the class. Could this be a possible feature request for the forum activity to allow only the subject of the post in the forum notifications? Otherwise, the whole point of the Q&A forum is circumvented by the notification emails (forcing students to post first before they can see other posts).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: One Moodle site for several organisations
ResponsesInList.Text: ".... expect any problem of sharing the same Moodle within different organisations. " Will give just one example without a lot of detail ... Company A doesn't want  to see blogs, wikis, chat modules in the pick list when they start to create an activity/resource.   So you, as an admin, hide those mods. Company B, however, does want 'chat'. The hiding of those is system wide ... no alternatives to choose for Company A no and  Company B yes.   That's a stock Moodle. There is a  multitenacy fork of Moodle that supposedly allows ... and one could find the repo for it and install ... but support for that is usually not a topic in these community forums. While it sounds like more admin it's not that much ... virtual apaches ... company A has companya.site domain , company B has companyb.domain ... they are separate instances ... own users, own modules, own addons, etc. IF those are installed via git ... it's realatively easy to update / upgrade all sites or just the companies that want latest/greatest as opposed to company that is more 'conservative' and prefers to be near 'leading edge', but NOT on 'bleeding edge'. My experience with such setups?  1 ISD, 2 high schools, 4 junior highs, 8 or so elementary schools. 1 beefy server . all sites on same box ... spartans.tld, warriors.tld - example of the 2 HS's.  Each campus could do as they liked ... without having to worry about how what they were doing affected the JHS or Elementary campuses.   Each campus used LDAP for authentication restricted to campus OU's. Updates to Moodles ... for all 14 instances took about 1 hours time ... and that was with backups to code, DB, and minimal data backups. Am certain others might add their two cents. ;) 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: One Moodle site for several organisations
ResponsesInList.Text: Javier, I run a Moodle site that functions in the manner you described. There are about 5 different organizations using the site. Each organization has its own Moodle category and theme. Managers are assigned to a particular category. Courses are contained within a category. All users are directed to their Dashboard page after logging in. At that point they see courses for which they are enrolled. There are some limitations with this type of organization. All users must login through the same interface. Managers are not able to add new users to the system, unless they are granted full Admin access or you modify the Manager role capability. Users are global to the system. So it is possible to enroll a particular user to a course in any organization. In order to seal off courses and structures from users, you must strategically hide menu blocks or add CSS code to hide links. To answer your questions: Managers can have a cap for the number of enrolled students - I'm don't fully understand what you mean. There is no way to limit the number of students a Manager can enroll in a course. Courses are not visible for students and managers of different organisations - This takes a bit of work to accomplish - see note #4 in the above list of limitations. Managers have a common course where we can share common content. This course should be hidden for the students . - You should be able to do this by course enrollment. There is multi-tenant version of Moodle you might consider, IOMAD . I've just started working with it, but at this time recommend it with some reservation. It will do most of what you want, but requires a lot of configuration.  Documentation is essentially non-existent, and it lacks a large user support forum. It is basically a layer on top of Moodle that can be used to structure the underlying Moodle courses and users. Moodle is not aware of IOMAD (very few changes were made to Moodle core), so you need to manage users and courses through the IOMAD interface. What IOMAD does well, is fully isolate managers and users from other organizations on the site. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Stay logged in?
ResponsesInList.Text: This is definitely NOT a good idea. You will sooner or later, run into invalidsesskey issues, which with a session timeout that long.... you're creating a lot of work for yourself. Try setting the value to a school day, say $CFG-->sessiontimeout = 28,800; That is eight hours, and it forces a login every day. Also, don't forget the timeout is set to begin at the last action or keystroke of an activity. So you can realistically login at 8:00am, do a bit of work before noon, then do nothing until, say 6:00pm then at 1:00am do something else, and still not be logged out at 8:00am that morning. As Ken said, it can be done by hacking core, but there is the possibility of getting it wrong and creating more problems than you solve. Using the config.php file is safer.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Koen, from https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_33_STABLE/lib/grade/grade_grade.php#L1080 and https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_33_STABLE/lib/classes/event/grade_deleted.php#L70 , it looks like grade_item is not an object, null or probably false (DB table, grade_grades ). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error on deleting users
ResponsesInList.Text:
Thank you for your response Matteo. It seems like I'm not the only one. In the mean time I found https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-51694 https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=335075 I used 
```text
select * from mdl_grade_grades where itemid not in (select id from mdl_grade_items)
```
 from the tracker issue and found 2084 records on a total of 707849. I deleted them with 
```text
DELETE from mdl_grade_grades where itemid not in (select id from mdl_grade_items)
```
 which was mentioned in the bug. After running the delete query all was working fine again and I managed to delete the 400 users. I think your suggested code change would have worked too, but I preferred in this case to clean up the database - it might prevent future problems.

ResponsesInList.Text: I can't vouch for other's experience with Xampp, e.g. Rick has maintained that it has generally been a positive experience, and more luck to him. All I know is that it became a nightmare so I dumped everything. I didn't know enough to save anything at that time, but I did have a set of backups of all the courses I had developed in my Xampp Moodle so restored them when I got everything working. There weren't any issues I recall, but I think that was due more to the Moodle backup/restore process and good luck rather than Xampp's use of PHP. I suggest that Xampp's limitations are not worth the effort of pursuing Xampp so would recommend installing Apache, MySQL, PHP, phpMyAdmin and Moodle. If you want, you can then install apps like Mahara , Wordpress, MediaWiki, a Podcast generator, a chat board and lots of other things, if you are interested. Also, please note: I used the WAMP for about four or five years with a minimum of fuss, used it pretty ruthlessly and broke Moodle a number of times testing stuff with code hacks mainly, but IANAD , so it was easy to make a mess of it. I then purchased a NAS, and while it hasn't been entirely trouble free motoring, I can do a lot more than I used to by using the server setup in the NAS. One of these days I might get around to transferring my web site to it, and set it up with external access, but not in any great hurry to do that. I couldn't do that with Xampp. BTW : I understand that the Xampp/Moodle was designed for the technically illiterate, like teachers , to easily install on their computers to have an accessible development tool. In this it easily fulfils that role. If you want to do nothing with your Moodle, just make courses, then it is probably the tool for you. If you want to learn to admin your Moodle... mmm probably not.  Good luck with whatever you decide.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: pointing moodle site to a new host server
ResponsesInList.Text: I am sure that Howard and others will give you more guidance. No, there is nothing stopping you from hosting your own moodle, except the knowledge to do this.  My post above provides an example of the kinds of questions that you need to address.  For example, when you say "I suppose ..." well, this is not good enough.  You must know, not suppose. The beauty of Moodle is that you can experiment and learn as much as you want. There are many ways to host your own moodle.  Begin by probing your own needs.  For example, are you talking about providing 2 courses a year, or 500?  50 students, or 1,000,000?  Look at your own needs first, then some folks here on moodle.org can continue providing guidance to you. It is also good to let us know a little about your background and abilities to host moodle yourself.  For example, if you were to say "I know nothing about computers and don't want to learn," we would probably direct you to use a Moodle provider.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: pointing moodle site to a new host server
ResponsesInList.Text: Rule of thumb, if you have lots of users, it is going to cost no matter where you put it. So is that cost higher than the cost of hosting your site on your own servers, providing your own storage, your own technical expertise? Could there be a reason to ensure you either take advantage of the existing expertise within your organization, or to develop your own expertise? Or would your organization be happier with a purchased MoodleCloud site? It's always entirely up to you, but make sure you know what it is you want, what your capabilities already are, what limitations may be placed upon your Moodle in any scenario. The important thing is to work out beforehand exactly how you want to get where you want to go, then just do it. Oh, if you already have a self-hosted web site, then Moodle will fit there nicely - if not, and the limitations of a purchased MoodleCloud site would be seriously restrictive, then I would suggest a Moodle Partner. You may, or may not, have to pay a little more than for a shared server, but you will always get the essential support you need to keep your site up and running. <initial suggestion>Learn Moodle with MoodleCloud, unless you have to provide a seriously wider site. OK, there are limitations, but while you are learning, you won't go too far wrong. You can practice some things on your desktop without damaging your MoodleCloud site, if you can install Apache , MySQL or MariaDB , php v7, then Moodle.</end>

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Safely Shutdown and then Restart Moodle 3.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Well.. after taking all your backups and copying them and all that. Step 1: Turn your computer off, using the normal shutdown processes for your server, that shuts down everything. Moodle itself is connectionless, or stateless, so if there is no user accessing the Moodle, that effectively shuts it down. As long as the server is shut down properly there is no risk to your data. What do you mean "We won't need to do any migration steps since it is just a VM relocation." Moving Moodle anywhere is a migration, but if you are referring to the network ip address of a different server then all you need do is copy the files, all the files, to the new location, make sure your wwwroot and dataroot paths are correct and it should all work.

Does make a slight difference on the command to use to gracefully shutdown apache/my sql d if doing so from the Guest OS itself. If for example, one had VMWare, Ubuntu/CentOS and other Linuxes have VMWare tools installed ... those tools talk to the hosting service in restarts and reboots of the Guest OS and they also shutdown (gracefully) the web service (apache?) and the DB server (MySQL?). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscription based homepage - Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: There are a few worries here... I'm not sure I can answer your questions entirely helpfully. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscription based homepage - Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan Pham, You need to have two installations - WordPress and Moodle. They can be on the same web server , but in separate folders. Your WordPress site will not take up much bandwidth, so it can easily coexist with Moodle. In order to have paid subscriptions you need to have e-commerce software installed on your WordPress site. WooCommerce is a good reliable choice. Edwiser Bridge synchonizes Moodle course names with WordPress/WooCommerce. When I use Edwiser Bridge, I also use their Single Sign-on product which then automatically creates a Moodle user and enrolls the purchaser in the Moodle course. The course content resides in Moodle - it does not reside in WordPress. When a person clicks on the link to a purchased course, that person is then taken to the Moodle course. You might also investigate LearnDash , which is a an online course plugin for WordPress. It is more limited than Moodle, but if your courses are mainly SCORM modules, it should meet your requirements.  Also, everything (web site and course content) would then be in WordPress. The main constraint on a web server (for WordPress, Moodle or LearnDash) is the number of concurrent (at the same time) users.  You can have thousands of registered users, but if they are not active on the system at the same time then the load on the server is minimal.  Moodle requires a lot of database activity. My experience has been that general hosting services (e.g. shared server space on places like BlueHost, GoDaddy, HostMonster, HostGator, etc.) are not the best for Moodle.  I have Moodle installed on one of those hosts for testing purposes only, but it gets very, very slow if more than 6 or so users are on the system at the same time.  I recommend talking with a Moodle Partner - they are very experienced with Moodle and can provide server at a level that meets your needs. I don't know how much load LearnDash places on a server. I expect it will be less than Moodle requires. A lot will depend on your SCORM package content - whether it is static text or has a lot of streamed videos. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscription based homepage - Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan, This addresses your Option 1:  There are two payment options which I use in Moodle, 1) PayPal, which is built in to Moodle core, and 2) Stripe, which has a plugin available.  Each of those payment methods has an enrollment duration setting. So a person could make a payment directly from Moodle and be enrolled in a course for a specified number of days. The issue to work around is that enrollment is course-based, not site-based.  You cannot grant access to all courses in a site based on one payment. However, there are ways to get around this limitation. The following solutions are listed in my order of preference. 1. Enable "Course Meta Link" as an enrollment method on your site. Create a Moodle course that you will use for payment purposes and enrollment. In all your other actual courses, add "Course Meta Link" as an enrollment method and select the payment/enrollment course as the Link Course.  What happens in this case is that enrollments in the payment/enrollment course are passed to the other linked courses. So when the payment/enrollment course enrollment expires, enrollment in all the other linked courses expires.  Moodle uses the terms 'meta course' and 'child course'.  Read the meta course documentation . 2. Place all of your "courses" into one Moodle course. For semantic purposes, let's call your individual "courses", "modules". You then create one Moodle course and each of your modules is placed in a Moodle course section /topic (e.g. as a SCORM package or other activities ), or embedded in a Moodle Book or Lesson activity. Students will enroll in this one Moodle course and then have access to all your modules. 3. Use the Moodle Flexpage set of plugins so you can create tabbed pages in a Moodle course. Each page can then contain any Moodle activity or resource. Regards, Floyd

ResponsesInList.Text: I think Adam is dropping the files in: https://docs.moodle.org/en/File_system_repository and then using the top option in this post: https://danmarsden.com/blog/2013/09/24/managing-scorm-content-in-moodle-2-6/ But I suspect he didn't choose "alias" when selecting the file, and selected "make a copy of the file" when setting up the SCORM package, so instead of maintaining the link to the file system repository it copies the scorm zip into the standard filedir in Moodle so when you replace the file in the file system repository it doesn't update the SCORM package. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New to Moodle - Common Mistakes
ResponsesInList.Text: The first thing to keep in mind - all technology should be a  solution to a problem, not something to do because it looks modern.  You must decide what Moodle can do for you that you can not do now, can only do with a great deal of effort, or want to do in the future. Everyone is different so everyone will make different mistakes. Mistakes I made in the first run: Shared hosting and a canned install. Predictably course backups started to fail but I was lucky not to lose my students work. Underestimating time required to produce good quality material. Assuming all students could quickly use a rather complex site. My advice: Start with a VPS and a clean "standard install" you do yourself - ie LAMP stack. This is the main highway so any pitfalls are well worked out. Unless your students can access your local install, you will need to set this up later anyway. Use a development server . Check you can back up and restore and any upgrades or changes check first on the development server. If you can't or won't do this, start practicing or go with Moodlecloud or a Moodle host. That is just setting up Moodle. Then you have to create interactive activities with your students. Start small, week by week, and aim for quality.

So I installed localhost on an external drive. It is slow, but it works. https://download.moodle.org/windows/ Tinker with a generic course. You can grab a generic course from many places. Hint: there is very little that Moodle won't do. Think out of the box. Ask often. I started with Moodle 1.8, and all I've seen is the possibilities growing. Have fun!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New to Moodle - Common Mistakes
ResponsesInList.Text: The best bit of advice I can give.... If you are going to run Moodle yourself then you need to understand that it is a large, server application and that comes with some challenges. Moodle itself is - in the great scheme of things - pretty simple to deploy. An order of magnitude than, say, an email server. However... if you are going to run a server then you have just become a server admin and with that comes responsibilities. You now have to worry about security, updates, email, DNS, LDAP , database admin and so on. None of this is rocket science and you can learn it but you *will* have to. You can go and buy an Linux VPS off Amazon or whoever and install Moodle blindly from instructions and it will work but you'll probably come unstuck if you don't have a basic understanding. So... if you're running a server allocate some time to learning about file ownership and permissions. How your web server is configured, where its log files are, how DNS works, how email works. Learn to use Google! You don't need massive depth but you do need an overview. Even running on hosting doesn't get you out of much of this. If you don't have the time, are scared or are just not interested then call a Moodle Partner and let somebody else worry about it. And one last thing that others have mentioned... do NOT use one of the "one click" style installers (Softaculous, Bitnami , linux distro packages). It may seem compelling but you'll regret it. When you want to upgrade and/or you find a problem you will almost certainly be on your own. ResponsesInList.Text: I will add a little more to what Howard has said about a VPS. Yes, I know of these VPSs where all you get is a "shell" login and command line.  I can't handle these myself (yet.) But there are also VPSs that come with much more.  The ones that I have experienced is where you get a pre-configured (sometimes quite well configured) web server.  You also get some kind of "control panel" that give you a pretty good set of utilities that help you manage and configure your server a bit further, and you get a graphic interface to your server's file system.  With most VPSs, you do have the ability to interact with a command shell, FTP , or other means.  So for example, when I installed Moodle on my VPS, I didn't have to do much of anything for Moodle's email system to work.  And my VPS came with a firewall and some good (but not all) security features, including a SSL certificate. That being said, one still needs to learn what is going on with their VPS.  Sure, you decide if it is easier to learn a utility or easier to learn to use the command line, you often have both options.  I find myself first using a utility, but then learning how to do things with the command line.  I think most people would say that using the command line is the most powerful way to manage your server, and I would agree.  But I still find myself using utilities, such as phpMyAdmin , to take care of some database admin things. I too would agree to not use any one-click utility to install Moodle, even on a VPS.  Learning how to install Moodle from scratch will provide you many more benefits in the long run.  Oh, for simple and quick experimenting, sure, go ahead with the one-click.  Then a little later, one can typically "reprovision" their VPS to its beginning state, and do the moodle install from scratch.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New to Moodle - Common Mistakes
ResponsesInList.Text: Most common mistake #1: Not thinking you can do it yourself - all you have to do is practice stuff before you do it. You gotta learn to be a quarterback. Most common mistake #2: Being afraid of making mistakes and then not learning from them. Most common mistake #3: Not explaining things to other people properly, assuming they understand because they have experiences similar to yours. They might be similar, but they are not the same, so don't assume an expertise. Most common mistake #4: Doing something and thinking you know it, you understand it, then finding out months later you can't remember how you did it. Keep a change log of what you have done. Sometimes this is a quick, simple note, other times it can be a tedious boring chore, but always keep a record. Most common mistake #5: Not reading the Moodle Docs . But the Docs can be an issue too. Don't understand something, go back to the bit you do understand then try to work out what you don't understand, then re-read the Moodle Doc, if it still doesn't make sense, don't be afraid of editing it using different language. Sometimes they read like a help file from Adobe or Microsoft, clearly written by experts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New to Moodle - Common Mistakes
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mike, Like all good questions, the answer is "it depends". Since you didn't give any information on your level of computer literacy or software experience it's difficult to know where to start. There has been a lot of good discussion / advice with a wide range of opinions so I'll add mine. I consider myself a competent computer person but being primarily self-taught I have learned by doing (sometimes rather painfully). Not for everyone but it's the way that works for me. For my first Moodle install, I used the Softaculous installer in  the cPanel control center supplied by hosting service in their shared server package. (I can hear the keyboards clacking already with all the reasons NOT to go this route but I'll ignore them for now) because: It got a working installation of Moodle in about 2 minutes I was able to start exploring Moodle immediately rather than worrying about all the technical stuff If it blew up I could easily install another copy. So began my Moodle journey 3 years ago. Since then I've learned that: Using a shared server works ok for a while but you'll soon outgrow it if you have more than a couple of dozens users. Slow response times, poor backup performance and limited tweaking/customization options to name a few. The standard Softaculous install, while workable, needs to be tweaked via the command shell that is not available in the shared server packages. So I upgraded to the lowest Virtual Private Server (VPS) package and it's been working great. Always have at least 2 Moodle installs; one for production and 1 or 2 for testing updates/plugins/themes/etc. That way you can play with the testing systems and if they break, no big deal. In fact, that's what got me learning and using the command shell to fix what I'd broken. By reading the excellent Moodle forum posts here, you can learn alot and I find people's responses to be timely and very helpful. Reading some of the ebooks available for Moodle and watching the numerous Moodle YouTube videos BEFORE doing stuff, helps you understand how to use the system much better than just forging ahead on your own. One other thing about the documentation being out of date is that the development of Moodle occurs at a fairly rapid pace and major new features and best practices are implemented with each new release. I'm very impressed at how much it has improved since I started using it at version 2.7. While the official docs may not be up-to-date, the answer to most questions can be found by searching the forums, and if you can't find it there just ask. In answer to your original question of Common Mistakes, I say: Not reading the documentation (RTFM). Despite internet rumours, it will not affect your manliness! Not asking questions (after searching the forums of course - don't be lazy!!) No matter what you do, there will always be mistakes of some sort (omission, miscommunication, ignorance, etc) Trying to create a whole lot of content without understanding the ramifications first. Start small with a single course, and don't try to do everything at once. Not learning the various activities and how they work. The available activity blocks are amazing and each one has a number of features that take time to learn. Not diving in and making some mistakes yourself (i.e. fail forward). Hard to learn if eveything is always smooth sailing. Not taking advantage of some of the great FREE downloadable courses like Moodle Features Demo found at moodle.net . Download and install them to see how good courses are put together. Not creating test users with different roles so you can test what other users experience. While Moodle does offer the "switch role to" option for System Administrators it is not quite the same as logging in as a user with a different role. Not setting up users with different email address domains. For example, I found out that our corporate email system was blocking any company email address so the "forgot password" option at the login screen didn't appear to be working for our users, while in fact it worked fine for other domains. Hope this helps. cheers, Derek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New to Moodle - Common Mistakes
ResponsesInList.Text: Ben, you have emphasized this point about "switch role" versus "fake people," which is especially on target of why Moodle is such a great product.  In the four LMSs that I have used (BCDM) they all offer this "switch role" ability.  However, they all suffer from not showing you exactly, meaning "exactly" what the student sees.  When I began using my own Moodle ten years ago, I discovered that Moodle was much more powerful than the other LMSs in this category. First, switching roles tends to primarily show what items are hidden versus not hidden.  This is useful, but not the whole story.  When a student says "I don't see it..." we have to ask, "Why not?"  Moodle provides the ability to "log in as" which is the best way that I verify exactly what the student is seeing. Wow, what a feature.  The other LMSs didn't allow me to do this! With my schools selected LMS, Canvas, apparently there is this ability, but my Canvas administrators have decided that they provide this feature only to their Canvas support staff.  When I want to see what a student sees, I have to phone the support group, they do it, and I have to believe what they tell me they see (or ask for a screenshot.)  The power of Moodle is that I can do this immediately, which solve problems immediately! As you and Derek have said, the added ability to create experimental (fake) uses is also extremely important as one learns how to use an LMS.  I learned that I could do this almost day-one after installing my first moodle.  This ability is the absolute best way to see exactly how your Moodle behaves. When my university was considering switching from D2L to Canvas, I was one of about a dozen faculty helping evaluate Canvas.  Of course, I wanted to be both the teacher and a student, so I asked if I could have a fake student login.  My administrators were surprised that anyone would want this, but they did give me one.  I was the only instructor who asked for this fake student login!  I was able to discover problems that no one else could.  Well, to be fair to the other instructors, they had not ever used an LMS (Moodle) that provided this ability, so one often does not know what to ask for because they have never seen this ability. At my previous school that used Blackboard, again, I was the only instructor who had asked for some fake students.  Again, I was able to learn more about Blackboard than any other instructor, and even the administrators! So I just wanted to emphasize how important the ability to create fake students to try things is when learning a new LMS.  With my moodle, I don't have to beg administrators to do this, I just do it myself.  Sure, there might be administrators who would turn-off this ability (for instructors) at their schools, but teachers can always install their own personal moodle on their own computer and experiment on their own (or with MoodleCloud) which is another nice feature of Moodle.

What should i do how to fix this? thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: DDL SQL execution
ResponsesInList.Text: Moving to the General help forum...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: DDL SQL execution
ResponsesInList.Text: First, make a backup of the database ... an sql dump.   Even if it's a little putzed, having something that's a backup is better than no backup at all. You must be attempting this in prep to upgrade to 3.5 of Moodle (that's a guess).   Is that right? See it's on Win-7?   What is mysql version? Did you recently upgrade the MySQL server to a higher version in order to convert character set/collation of the DB for Moodle? Someone else had similar issue/error dealing with indexes. Yours: Duplicate entry '2465-Win7-139522' for key 'mdl_wikipage_subtituse_uix Do you have a recent backup of the database?  a mysqldump?   If so, one could simply create a new database for the moodle with character set/collation set on creation of the db. mysql> create database moodlenew character set utf8mb4 collate utf8mb4_unicode_ci; Quit the mysql client. \q then import the mysqldump (might be named moodlebackup.sql - whatever you named it). mysql -u root -p moodlenew < moodlebackup.sql That will import to the new database and regenerate those indexes on the fly. Then, edit config.php file and point to the newer database. OR ... if you recently upgraded mysql, then run: mysql_upgrade -u root -p That will check all databases/indexes and fix them on the fly ... upgrading. 'spirit of sharing', Ken
