ResponsesInList.Title: Make User Notification Preferences for a Block Plugin Available Only to Selected Users or Roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I developed a site feedback block plugin for 3.4.2+ (20180502) which allows all users to send notifications to specified recipient users from the dashboard .  I would like to configure things so that only the recipient users see the notification online/offline preferences for this plugin (screen shot attached); I don't want to clutter up notification preferences for general users with settings for a plugin from which they will never receive notifications.  Is it possible?  If not, can the display of these preferences be limited by role?  Thank you!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Make User Notification Preferences for a Block Plugin Available Only to Selected Users or Roles
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm  a bit confused... what do you mean by 'recipient users'? Is this a specific class of user (e.g. teachers)? If so, you are confused about roles - you do not check if a user has a role; you check if they have a capability. However, in order not to have got loads of warnings when you created your block you must have created the basic 'view' capability. Why not just give that capability to the roles that need it? I think I might be misunderstanding your question though.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Make User Notification Preferences for a Block Plugin Available Only to Selected Users or Roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the quick reply!  My mistake, it does sound like I was talking about a class of users or a role, but that's not the case.  The plugin simply delivers the feedback message to a site admin-supplied list of users, which was the only reason that I called them recipients.  The plugin doesn't care about the roles of the specified users to which it delivers. Interestingly I didn't get any warnings or errors while installing it!  I don't have a db/access.php, only a db/messages.php with an empty capabilities array; my theory was that would allow anyone to submit feedback, which is working.  But I would like only the list of users/recipients to have "site feedback" in their notification preferences.  General users that can only send feedback might be confused to see preferences for something they'll never receive. I think you're saying that I need to define a capability for viewing the notification preferences, which I could assign to and remove from users as the list changes.  Does the notification preferences page look for capabilities when determining what to display?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Make User Notification Preferences for a Block Plugin Available Only to Selected Users or Roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok I misread your original post. If you're doing development you need to have debugging switched right up to Developer. Check this - https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Blocks#db.2Faccess.php - you'll get warnings without those capabilities. The documentation here - https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Message_API#How_to_register_as_a_message_producer ...tells you how those capabilities work. They are checked in the 'site' context (as the notification settings is a site-wide thing). I wonder what caps you have in your messages file now? I think you'll end up having to create new roles with these new capabilities and assign them site-wide, which I think is probably far too much bother.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Make User Notification Preferences for a Block Plugin Available Only to Selected Users or Roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Think I got it!  Thanks for pointing me in the right direction.  I did have to use a role, it's not per user, but I'll give up on that and just tack a capability onto an existing role.  With the setup below, general users can submit feedback to the users in the recipient list, but only those users with the role assigned (and with the capability allowed in the role) are seeing the notification preferences. db/access.php: $capabilities = array("block/site_feedback:notification_preferences" => array("captype" => "read", "contextlevel" => CONTEXT_SYSTEM)); db/messages.php: $messageproviders = array("submit" => array("capability" => "block/site_feedback:notification_preferences")); lang/en/block_site_feedback.php: $string["pluginname"] = "Site Feedback"; $string["messageprovider:submit"] = "Site feedback notifications"; $string["site_feedback:notification_preferences"] = "Manage site feedback notification preferences";

 It seems to be related to some type of
cache/file permission error, specifically related to the .pdf document
conversion stuff (unoconvd & libreoffice). We have not had this
problem so widespread until somewhat recently, after offloading the
unoconvd process to a separate server (we still had this issue when
unoconvd was running locally, though it was less frequent). This error occurs for every single student within an assignment a
single time. After the error has occurred for that one student, if you
go back and try to grade their assignment you won't get an error. If you
try to switch to grading a different student that you haven't graded
yet, this error pops up and you can't do anything unless you reload the
page. Here is the line of code that errors, https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/21f89c034c5a56a64b12f3256b0f503d7f584911/lib/filestorage/file_storage.php#L390 After playing with the document conversion code in /lib/filestorage/file_storage.php, I can watch the temporary files being created by the offloaded unoconv/libreoffice service. I have tried to get unoconvd to run the libreoffice/openoffice conversion process as user "apache" but it doesn't seem there is a way to get that to work properly.  There's also a --preserve option for unoconv that I've tried using in listener mode but it doesn't preserve the owner of the file, only rwx permissions as far as I can tell. Previous versions of file_storage.php used a different method than touch () to check/remove the temporary files created by unoconv that didn't rely on file ownership--I'm not sure why this was changed except for maybe slight performance gains? Has anyone else run into this issue? How can I run the unoconv/libreoffice document conversion as the apache user on my offload server?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: File permission issue casuing json error; unoconvd document conversion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tony, aplogies, I got your post out of my radar. Did you already solved it? It's a permission issue which breaks the JSON syntax of the AJAX call, probably due by the conversion tool not running with the same user/permissions of the user your Moodle instance is running on. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: File permission issue casuing json error; unoconvd document conversion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Matteo, Thanks for responding. I have not fixed this yet.  Aside from granting root permissions apache, I don't see any way to fix it. It seems there may need to be some changes made to Moodle core re: the document conversion process , and how it saves these temporary files to disk or how it checks that a file exists (in file_storage.php). Note that this only happens when the unoconvd/openoffice conversion process is offloaded to a separate server. We had to do that due to performance issues when it ran on the webservers themselves. As I mentioned in my original post, there is no way to run the document conversion process as a user of your choosing or to have the document conversion process retain the original file permissions. (there actually is documentation in unoconvd for a flag that is supposed to retain the original file permissions but it doesn't seem to work) So, when the document conversion does its thing--saves a file owned by root:root-- and apache/Moodle attempts to overwrite the file using touch(), it can't. The official Moodle documentation highlights the ability to run the document conversion on a separate server (and I don't see how this wouldn't be necessary for large Moodle sites) so I would expect this to work properly. That documentation was likely written before file_storage.php was modified to use touch() . touch() has inherent permissions issues. It's likely the offloading of the document conversion process used to work but it doesn't any longer. Thanks, Tony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Use Chart.js in a Tab Page
ResponsesInList.Text:
In the code I use four arrays  to get the data I want to use for the chart. The program is looping through the database to get all the results and put the data into the appropriate array: 
```text
            $labels[] = $fcol;  // This gets the exercise number.


            $serieshitsperminute[] = format_float($gr->hitsperminute); // Get the hits per minute value.


            $seriesprecision[] = format_float($gr->precisionfield);  // Get the precision percentage value.


            $serieswpm[] = $gr->wpm; // Get the corrected words per minute rate.
```
 Then it is just a matter of passing the data to the chart api: ﻿ ﻿ 
```text
echo $htmlout;    // Output the normal grade table of results.


if ($grds != false) {  // If there are NOT any grades, DON'T draw the chart.


    // Create the info the api needs passed to it for each series I want to chart.


    $serie1 = new core\chart_series(get_string('hitsperminute', 'mootyper'), $serieshitsperminute);


    $serie2 = new core\chart_series(get_string('precision', 'mootyper'), $seriesprecision);


    $serie3 = new core\chart_series(get_string('wpm', 'mootyper'), $serieswpm);




    $chart = new core\chart_bar();  // Tell the api I want a bar chart.


    $chart->set_horizontal(true); // Calling set_horizontal() passing true as parameter will display horizontal bar charts.


    $chart->set_title(get_string('charttitlemyowngrades', 'mootyper')); // Tell the api what I want for a the chart title.


    $chart->add_series($serie1);  // Pass the hits per minute data to the api.


    $chart->add_series($serie2);  // Pass the precision data to the api.


    $chart->add_series($serie3);  // Pass the words per minute data to the api.


    $chart->set_labels($labels);  // Pass the exercise number data to the api.


    $chart->get_xaxis(0, true)->set_label("Range");  // Pass a label to add to the x-axis.


    $chart->get_yaxis(0, true)->set_label(get_string('fexercise', 'mootyper')); // Pass the label to add to the y-axis.


    echo $OUTPUT->render($chart); // Draw the chart on the output page.


}


echo $OUTPUT->footer();   // This line prints the normal Moodle footer
```
 This is the result showing my normal grade table for a single user.  The link at the bottom, Show chart data, is optional. If I select one of my headings to reorder the grade table, the chart is automatically redrawn to reflect the new view. : Using essentially the same code a teacher gets a chart depending on what they select which will also include student names.

ResponsesInList.Title: SMTP server configuration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi We have a Moodle version 3.4 installation. Moodle is configured with Debian 9.4, PHP 7 and Nginx. we have an anonymous SMTP server (Windows 2012 R2). When we try to register new users they do not get a confirmation on their E-mail address. I have tested the connection to the SMTP server wtih telnet on port 25 and from that connection it is possible to send an E-mail. On the SMTP configuration site I have configured a SMTP host address (full qualified domain name) and SMTP-security is set to none. smtpauthtype is set to login (none is not an option) and username and password is set to blank (default). I have checked the lib/phpmailer/moodle_phpmailer.php file and SMTP AutoTLS is set to false. There are no errors in the logs and when You try to register on a course You get no errors and also no E-mail. Has anyone encountered this problem? Best Regards Steen Pedersen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SMTP server configuration
ResponsesInList.Text: You can dig further as documented in https://docs.moodle.org/en/Debugging#Debug_email_sending .

ResponsesInList.Title: Ang: Re: SMTP server configuration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Visnanath Thank you for your answer. I have investigated the problem further, and the problem is the confirmation E-mail that Moodle sends when a new user is registered. The confirmation E-mail is considered High Threat Phishing in our external spamfilter and therefore the mail is stopped and in quarantine. The problem is that the link embedded in the mail is considered as suspect. I have whitelisted the sender address in our spamfilter so our immediate problem is solved. But we could encounter the problem again if a user registers and uses an external mail account (a mail account that uses a DNS that does not point to our external spamfilter) in the registration process. Then there is the possibility that another spamfilter stops the mail. Best Regards Steen Pedersen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ang: Re: SMTP server configuration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steen So the culprit not something technical - like the sender, envelope sender, from which SMTP server, what SPF allows, etc. but the _content_, the hyperlink in your case. In other cases it is the "noreply" in the sender address, HTML mail, etc. As you said, these problems are never solved for ever, they are continuously under construction.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SMTP server configuration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steen, you could even install https://moodle.org/plugins/local_mailtest: it will help you in finding what the SMTP server replies w/o the need to enable the SMTP debugging which applies to the whole site. You'll probably discover that you need an authenticated SMTP relay in Moodle and you can configure it in your IIS SMTP server e.g. https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=199598 . HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Ang: Re: SMTP server configuration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Matteo Thank you for your answer. I have given an answer to our problem in the previous post. Best Regards Steen Pedersen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  How can I change the video player that Moodle uses?
ResponsesInList.Text: AFAIK , the native video player is usable in every browser by default. However, if you go to Site Admin > Plugins > Media Players > Manage Media Players, which I think is available in your version, that should allow you to select the video player you want. To upgrade is simple, once you have done it, before that however, mmmmmmm: Download the next version you need to upgrade to. Seriously suggest you use this path to upgrade, starting with v2.8, then v2.9 then v3.1, v3.3 then later v3.5. You can do this one step at a time, but do not skip any step. If you jump from v2.6.x to 3.5 you are in for a nasty shock. Check what third party plugins you are using and if they are still available, download versions that suit your Moodle download . Step 1: Backup everything, prepare it for restoration if something goes wrong. Step 2: Copy your config.php file so that it won't be overwritten or deleted by accident, save it to another folder, external to Moodle, but accessible. This is a safety measure do NOT skip it. Step 3: Place the site into Maintenance Mode, Site Admin > Server > Maintenance Mode Step 4: Go to the Moodle root directory, and delete all the code. Step 5: Unzip or untar the downloaded version, then copy and paste into the Moodle root directory. You could unzip/untar directly, but I prefer to copy and paste. Step 6: Copy the existing config.php file back to the Moodle root directory. Step 7: Run the Moodle - you should be back online. Any third party plugins you use that are no longer workable or not replaced will show up as "Not on disk" in the Manage Plugins page, To fix this, uninstall them before upgrading. Include the plugins you have located and install them. To make sure this works, or to find any unexpected little "undocumented features" do this to your test Moodle first. If you have no test Moodle, then I suggest you build one, quickly. Keep it current to your production Moodle and try things there before doing them to your site. I have always done this and believe me, it minimizes a lot of potential problems by allowing you to make mistakes without them affecting your production site. Do it several times, as many as you like, just to make sure and gain confidence. Simple, once you have done it once or twice. Also, someone else may have something to add, or perhaps they do it differently, but this works for me, so unless I missed something, it should work. Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  How can I change the video player that Moodle uses?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Colin, Thank you for your reply. Sadly, I think I don't hace that "Site Admin > Plugins > Media Players", I have "Video File" which gives me some default configs to work with (if the video is responsive, how many pixels, etc). But won't let me pick video players.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  How can I change the video player that Moodle uses?
ResponsesInList.Text: Apparently then it would be a later feature. So there would likely not be an easy solution. You will have to think back to how you did things to set up the player in the first place and replicate that. Sorry, there is no short answer here, so please read on. The problem is that as you fall further behind the current release, the skills built around older releases are forgotten. This came up recently with a question that was asked about a v1.9. It had no easy answer, it took a while to get even a direction to work towards fixing it; but I am sure one would have been available at the time v1.9 was the current release. Like the product, the skills base evolves, and older solutions to problems are lost, unless they can be hunted down in the archives of the hundreds of thousands of questions already asked. I suggest as a matter of urgency, that you think about these ideas: Create a test Moodle to do things to. It can be anywhere, a desktop, a laptop, just not the server where your site is. In doing so, you have to create a server environment, Apache , PHP, MySQL , phpMyAdmin and Moodle. Add to the Moodle your Users, your courses, you don't need everything but just a good sampling. Change all their passwords to a generic password, pick a couple and use them as your main test students. Test out everything. Learn what can go wrong as you add a plugin, remove a plugin, add a new User, delete a User, suspend an account, reactivate an account, everything, See what happens when you delete, or unenrol a student and then when you re-enrol. Back up a course and turn the power off to your computer before the backup is complete, see what happens. I know this is not recommended practice, but your home made server is really there to be destroyed, so don't be afraid of destroying it. Another thing you can do is to recognize that you will not always be an admin of that particular Moodle. You might get another job, have a car accident and be off work for six months, win the lotto and decide a 100mill  is enough to live the high life.. Who knows? The point being that you have, it seems, not left any notes for yourself or anyone else as to how you have modified your Moodle. Create a change log and insist that anyone who admins your Moodle creates an entry, every time they modify anything. This allows you to review any change and either undo that change or replicate it if something goes wrong. Someone else acting as an admin should be able to open that change log and know exactly what you have done. That is good admin and really only takes a few seconds to enter the changes made. I have done this ever since I found myself in exactly the same position as you, but not with video players. It works. If you really want to get detailed, describe all the steps to what you did, everything, and for some things, this should actually be a requirement. Use your test Moodle as the basis for learning how to upgrade your site, follow the steps in my previous post. Do it several times, get the confidence, and once you have done it a couple of times, you will be wondering why you didn't upgrade before this. Just don't forget to be careful, and check everything as you do it, it will become less of a challenge and more of a routine chore. That is really what you want, the sense of routine. When you do upgrade your production site, it will be routine and no great challenge. I still do this on my test site, and the Moodles I admin are still working smoothly. The people who actually own the Moodles think I am really good, sure got them fooled...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CSV format when uploading to cohort
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I came across this with a colleague recently and I'm guessing you're doing the same thing. You need to upload this file at 'Upload Users' and not 'Upload Cohorts' i.e. [yourmoodlesite]/admin/tool/uploaduser/index.php Catherine

ResponsesInList.Text: Catherine, The users are already in the system so by going to 'Upload Users' I would be creating duplicates.  I need to upload existing users to a cohort. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CSV format when uploading to cohort
ResponsesInList.Text: The users are already in the system so by going to ' Upload Users' I would be creating duplicates. - No you won't. Moodle doesn't allow you to create 'duplicate' users by default. You can use the 'upload users' feature to update existing users (and put them in to these cohorts) https://docs.moodle.org/33/en/Upload_users#Cohort_membership_assignment The adding cohorts by csv upload feature is for creating cohorts (not putting users in to them)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CSV format when uploading to cohort
ResponsesInList.Text: Ah!  You're trying to upload to the cohort upload area!  That is a problem.  I second C Behan's remarks. If you accidentally choose upload new users, it will tell you there is an error because those accounts already exist--it doesn't allow duplicate user names. You'll want to not only choose the Update existing but also Override with file or Override with file and defaults (this is a problem some people have--they leave it No changes and nothing happens, which is what they told it to do). I'd also recommend making sure that the auth field (ldap,manual, etc) is also on your csv because if it isn't, Moodle might reassign authentication (It's happened to me a couple times), which can cause some trouble.

However, there are two ways ... but you'd have to get cooperation of Teachers ... Option 1: In the title of whatever, at the tail end, ask Teacher to put their lastname in ()'s.  Howard's suggestion. OR, Option 2: in the description of the whatever, just their last name and set the description to be displayed ... which does add a little to the course scroll of death and wouldn't be displayed if using Collapsed Topics (in which case option 1). Another depending upon if course sequence is important or not ... each teacher has a section assigned to only them.  Other teachers cannot add activities /mods, etc.   Set up of that not automatic so one is looking at more setup time as an Admin. All in all - as is traditional in Moodle, look for a 'work-around' ... but whatever direction you explore/go, try to keep it simple. 2 cent opinion .... 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: where do i start
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Elsie. In addition to what Davo says, are you a developer or an educator wishing to set up a Moodle site? Because if so then one easy way to do this without coding skills is to sign up for a MoodleCloud site where the site is made for you - and you can concentrate on the training. MoodleCloud is a hosting package run by Moodle HQ and requires no prior technical skills. Apologies if this is not what you meant, and you meant that you want to develop a customised site yourself.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: where do i start
ResponsesInList.Text: And I would interpret your question as saying  "How can I brand my site to look like my own?" I am covering a number of possibilities here too. You haven't said what you current position actually is, so I am assuming that you are planning this to be opening soon. Use a theme you can easily modify. Well, most themes are easily modified now, you can change colours, change banners, change the appearance by changing the settings of the theme. Depending on how far you want to go, you might want to start with one of the basic themes, and modify that to something approximating what you want. Documentation for doing that starts here . Later, as you become more confident with what you are doing, you may want to switch your theme to something more sophisticated, like the Fordson Theme, there are lots of them. There is a couple of other things you  may want to think about first though. As Mary suggested, use the MoodleCloud to become familiar with using Moodle, that is an excellent place to start. Understand though, MoodleCloud is, of necessity, somewhat limited and it may very well be that you will outgrow it fairly quickly. I would suggest you use your desktop or laptop to set up a Moodle for yourself. This is your test site, no-one else has access. You will need Apache , MySQL or MariaDB or PostGreSQL , and PHP, (preferred v7). Also, include phpMyAdmin or phpPGAdmin to manage your database externally. Obviously we don't know what your tech skills are, but if you have good skills you should be able to do this all yourself, or likely you will know some whiz-kid who could help you set it all up. Or you could download and install the XAMPP Moodle, but don't expect it will last too long, it is inflexible and when it starts to go wrong, it is better to delete the whole lot and start again. Test everything here before you introduce any change on your production site, it will save you a lot of heartache if it goes wrong. You may, eventually, need to have your own domain with your own Moodle, in which case, you may require a good service provider. There are lots of them, all over the world, just realise you may be facing some unknown issues with regard to usage if you are using someone like GoDaddy or similar. You may want to use a Moodle Partner, they will help you a great deal. This is your production site and should never be used to test stuff, that is what your private Moodle is for. Moodle is useful in a whole range of areas, and I would suggest you go to this post and read it carefully . There is a lot of really good ideas here about Moodle, what can be done, what is achievable. It is aimed at a school district setting, but the attitudes behind the post are what you may want to look at in some depth. Welcome to the rabbit hole, Elsie, enjoy the ride..

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error code: invalidsesskey
ResponsesInList.Text: Straight from the Moodle Docs on this error... The most likely reason for obtaining an "Invalid Sesskey" message is because your session has timed out i.e. you were inactive for an extended period. Please log in again. Other possible reasons are: Your site doesn't have the PHP setting "session.auto_start=0" (see Installing Moodle - software ) You logged out at some time between opening the form and submitting it. You have followed a bad link to a form script. Your database has an incorrect value for sessioncookiepath in the mdl_config table. You edited the code in a file on the server while logged in to your moodle website. If any of these are the cause of your problem, then perhaps some re-education is required.... If this is a frequent occurrence, I'd start with checking the sessioncookiepath.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Urgent: Upgraded to moodle 3.5 and login with Google not Showing
ResponsesInList.Text: When your site was a 3.2 it was using an addon-plugin for Google Authentications.  3.5 now has Oauth2 (Google) built into core.   To get the 'red' button to show, you might have had to edit a file in the 3.2. You were using: https://moodle.org/plugins/auth_googleoauth2 Please read the first paragraph. At any rate, hope you made a backup of code and of the DB prior to upgrading.   Your best option at this point is to restore the site to the 3.2. You will then have to research what one has to do to convert all users that used Google in the 3.2 to the Oauth2 in 3.5 *before* you attempt an upgrade to 3.5 and drop the addon-plugin + setup the new.   ** mdl_user ** table will have to be manipulated to get users changed from the old to the new. There is no utility to make mass conversions other than CSV uploads and those now restrict what fields one can change in the mdl_user table. Once your 3.2 site is restored, make full site backups ... code, DB, and data directory ... and restore them to a clone server to work through the process of converting users accounts. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SAML2 Mapping
ResponsesInList.Text: There are two things that would need to be in place: The external account stores the encrypted password value in a format Moodle understands. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SQL For resource/file count
ResponsesInList.Text: nevermind, find my the way. anyone can use this sql if need to get uploaded file single teacher in a courses SELECT c.id "CourseID" ,c.shortname AS "KOD KURSUS" , COUNT(*) "Course Files" , ROUND( SUM( f.filesize ) /1048576 ) AS file_size_MB FROM mdl_files AS f JOIN mdl_context AS context ON context.id = f.contextid JOIN mdl_course AS c ON c.id = ( SELECT instanceid FROM mdl_context WHERE id = SUBSTRING_INDEX( SUBSTRING_INDEX( context.path, '/' , -2 ) , '/', 1 ) ) WHERE filesize >0 AND f.userid='26783' GROUP BY c.id;

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can I teacher be assigned to a grouping?
ResponsesInList.Text: I thought this was a simple structural problem, but reading your question a second and third time, mmmm My first read was: 100 branches broken into three area groups. Each area group is managed by one person. That one person will be responsible for ensuring completion of the required course/courses in each area. The issue I see is grouping the areas so that one Manager is responsible for one area. You might want to look at this documentation on Groups and this on Groupings before going further. Perhaps a more sophisticated approach might be Cohorts, but I have never used one. Of course, if I am reading this wrong, it is all nonsense. My second read was: If you have 3 area managers to each area, that is a little more complicated. Create three groups in each area, assigning staff and a Manager, as a Teacher, adjusting permissions as you require. You might want to add the Manager as a Non-Editing Teacher, making sure they have the permission set to see, (and grade?) the work completed. Better to add functionality into a Role than to try and take it out. Using groups should resolve the problem. My Third read was: Make the course a meta course, creating different child courses to access the materials, assigning non-editing teachers to the child courses. You remain the Teacher for all meta and child courses, and ensure permissions are correct. The non-editing teachers can only see their own child courses. (This is likely the most simple actually - well for me it would be.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I put an advert on every page (of 1 course)?
ResponsesInList.Text: You can create blocks at any level and choose where they show.  If you create a block in a course, you could set it to display on every page of the course. When you create the block, go to the Configure block area and expand the Where this block appears area.  Choose Any course page (or maybe Any page). If you want different ads to show (rotation), you could create the ads in Glossary and use the Random Glossary block to randomly choose one from the list and display a different ad with each page refresh. Some activities might not display blocks normally, but there are probably settings for the activity to display blocks.  Just look at all the settings in the areas that you don't see what you want.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ideas for teacher resources
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Anthony and welcome to Moodle Before I make suggestions, why not sign up to our free (no strings attached) Moodle HQ-run Learn Moodle Basics MOOC course starting on June 18 which teaches the basics of teaching with Moodle You'll have a better idea of how it works for teachers then. If you need to add files and folders, your idea of having a course where all teachers are enrolled is a good one. They will have a one-stop shop for items they need. You can indeed set up a Database activity for them to share resources they have between each other, but if you are beginning with Moodle I would suggest it is not very intuitive to start with. ResponsesInList.Title: DG's tips - Plugins,Codes & links
ResponsesInList.Text: I am in a need of my own thread to try to give back to the community as it seems that I am taking a lot and being helped by a number of great people in the community. So instead of spamming other peoples I am going to drop a few things I have learn't over the last two years into here so that others may stumble over it. There's so much to learn in making a great Moodle site for your students and clients and we know that it has to be engaging otherwise this blended learning model is going to lose them. A static file repository is just that, they will turn up one or two times then once they have found it too difficult or not enough in there to keep them engaged, you have lost them. So I suppose this is my way of using the Moodle thread as a bit of blog to come back to and drop in what I pick up on my little journey, with the hope that it inspires others and saves a bit of time.. Unfortunately we know that we have a limited to editing time in these forums, so I find this a little hard in that there is a lot of double up of posts going on. But as this is the format we just have to work with it. I will work on this thread over coming weeks to pull in from other area's of what I have found useful via sometimes long winded conversations in other threads. But, with that in mind it is how we knuckle out these little quirks that come with Moodle. I also note, I come from old DOS days so not afraid to break things to see how they work. Thus some of the code I have picked up my or may not be the best for others to use. Hopefully this is ok with the Mods as some of you have seen me around the threads asking and asking..

ResponsesInList.Text:
This little how-to comes from moving to  a Mobile-first design cycle versus a desktop first. Like a lot of training organisations, there is always going to be the split between the Face to Face and online\hard copy resources. Thus still the use of Powerpoints and Pdf’s are at the forefront of getting this information into the inquiring minds that need it. Also the need to work on all 3 platforms, Microsoft\Apple\Android. So far the tools of choice for my type of delivery are: Gdrive for streaming of PPT’s\PDF’s H5P – Now streamed from a Wordpress site to the Moodle site for a better mobile experience. (I do note I have seen a few transferring PPT's to H5P lessons now, which is another way of doing this) This little how-to is a day’s work of working out a better way of presenting the PPT’s and Pdf’s to the mobile app. PPT’s. This is the code you are going to face when you got stock out of Gdrive. 
```text
<iframe src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/YOUR_FILE_CODE/embed?start=false&loop=false&delayms=3000" frameborder="0" width="960" height="749" allowfullscreen="true" mozallowfullscreen="true" webkitallowfullscreen="true"></iframe>
```
 This is the code that is working best for me. 
```text
<iframe class="embed-responsive-item" src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/YOUR_FILE_CODE/embed?start=false&loop=false&delayms=3000" width="660" height="349" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>
```
 This comes from a bit of research and trying to get a better responsive set of code to use. I did refer to this but I couldn’t get it to work as planned with the custom CSS commands so had to butcher it a bit to at least make the PPT’s to look and feel fine on the tablet and Mobile phones. https://benmarshall.me/responsive-iframes/ PDF’s While I do use the Flowpaper and love the ease it works for me. There is still the need for an alternative way of placing smaller pdfs at the reach of the students and or copies of the PPT’s for them to download and reference from. Plus the standard codes I have been using don’t allow for them to show up in the mobile app. Original codes – hosted on the Moodle site. https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=318224 A new way for now that works for the mobile app. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44164367/how-to-embed-google-drive-document-pdf-in-blogger-post/50366186#50366186 What we are interested in is this code string. 
```text
<iframe src="https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B3VnSl89GUNxaXI1NzNrLUZTYWs/preview" width="640" height="480"></iframe>
```
 Of note is “preview” Load your pdf to Gdrive. Share to “Public” (but this is not going to be left open) Grab your code.. 
```text
https://drive.google.com/file/d/YOUR_FILE_NAME/view?usp=sharing
```
 Once you have this, Go back to sharing and turn it to anyone with link only. This will bring it back in so the bots and google are not throwing your files up in search engines.. Now we want to to iframe this. 
```text
<iframe src="https://drive.google.com/file/d/YOUR_FILE/preview" width="640" height="480"></iframe>
```
 Now bring those two together.. 
```text
<iframe src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/YOUR_FILE_CODE/embed?start=false&loop=false&delayms=3000" frameborder="0" width="960" height="749" allowfullscreen="true" mozallowfullscreen="true" webkitallowfullscreen="true"></iframe>


<iframe src="https://drive.google.com/file/d/YOUR_FILE/preview" width="640" height="480"></iframe>
```
 Place it in to a Page activity. Head along to your mobile app and see how they look. Both can be expanded to full screen and Pdf can be downloaded if you have that setting set. All have touch ability on Android. I am yet to test it on iPhone.. If someone goes down that route let me know. I will have a few meetings over the coming week with clients on ipads and iPhones so will check it out and report back. The only thing I saw was a slight delay in Gdrive on the first render of the pdfs. Once they have been opened once and rendered it seems other times there are not problems. So be aware if you have like a 30-40 page pdf as Gdrive will have to do its magic on it. Also of note, I am wrapping this all in flexbox containers, which gives spacing and seems to work well with the mobile app.

However, if you have command line access, there is a command line only script to backup individual courses using whatever you had as default settings in backups. You'll need a real power supply, for example a 2.5 A one. @Marcus, I have a Pi 2 case which rejects Pi 3. Make sure that the case takes a Pi 3. @AL, I assume Pi itself consumes much less power than an Odroid. It runs happily taking 600-750 mA from the 5 V supply of a USB -> 3 to 4 W! ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Raspberry Pi, Linux and Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nicolas Thanks for the report on Model B+. Specifically the improvements: > 1) Better and faster Wi-Fi, and > 2) faster ethernet. In fact, the benchmarks confirm a moderately faster Wi-Fi and massively faster Ethernet. (But MoodleBox in off-line mode make no use of Ethernet.) Also CPU performance is confirmed to be higher in proportion to the increase in clock frequency from 1.2 GHz to 1.4 GHz. Only the SD read/write speeds remain the same, which is to be expected. @Rick Sorry, for making a fuss about the power consumption. The physics says the faster CPU clock and the next generation of network circuitry are going to need more power. That is why I was not surprised by the magazine report of a 3 W increase. Although I have not tested, I bet the B+ will run from a laptop's USB port. Assuming this 3 W increase is correct, it means the B+ will draw 3000 mW / 5 V = 600 mA more than the B. So B+ will draw 600 mAh more from the battery every hour. If the laptop battery has a capacity of 5000 mAh and it ran 5 h earlier now it will run 5000 / (1000+600) = 3 h 8 min. Whether that is a big deal, you have to decide. (Again, in theory.) The fact is that Nicolas has tested B+ and recommends it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Raspberry Pi, Linux and Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, From this official source from the Raspberry Pi Foundation, for optimal function the RPi 3B+ should run with a 3.5A power source (same requirement as the RPi 3B ). However, according to Wikipedia , no usual USB port from a computer can deliver so much power (2A max!). This does mean that even with the RPi 3B, using a computer USB port as power source can be unreliable. For the low power needs of the MoodleBox (if nothing is connected to the RPi's own ports), this is usually not a problem though and it works relatively well, at least with the 3B model. However, my experience with the RPi 3B+ is not as successful. I tried with several computers, and the pattern is not regular. Some observations: When powering from USB of my desktop computer (from 2011) and my laptop computer (from 2015), I get under voltage warnings in the log of the RPi 3B+. The power LED (red) of the RPi 3B+  is not continuously on. When powering from USB of my desktop computer, everything works normally though. When powering from USB of my laptop, I don't get Wi-Fi signal. In conclusion, just as the Raspberry Pi Foundation, I don't recommend to use RPi 3 in "real work" powered from a USB port of a computer, especially if you have some devices attached to the USB ports of the RPi.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Service Unavailable

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copy user (role) permissions from one course to another
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunately, that only seems to work at the system level rather than at a course level. So far the best solution I have found is to create a new system-level role, set the rights for that role, and then change the students' roles to that new role. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copy user (role) permissions from one course to another
ResponsesInList.Text: Sounds like your problem is external to Moodle. If using LDAP , for example, you should be able to set up the groups such that your users are enrolled with student role rather than the custom role you have set up. It may also be that you modified the student role rather than creating a new custom role for those instances where you need students to have more permissions. If that's the case, copy the student role, save it as a new role, then revert the original student role to defaults. The first suggestion I made above would solve the problem in bulk, but would require you to do that manual process for each new course.

They are already built to be part of a sequence, for example course 1 may be logging into the application, course 2 would be setting up your preferences, course 3 would be using a feature of the software. These all need to be part of a parent curriculum / learning plan? I'm trying to configure moodle in such a way that an employee (or group of employees) can be assigned to this curriculum and all the child courses will be assigned to the user and they are prompted to complete them in order. Is it possible to have a course with multiple SCORM packages that the user must complete in sequence? Would a Meta-Link course help with this? (Is it possible to have them complete courses in order and will the meta course report results for child items?) I've also tried assign courses to competencies and then assigning it to a learning plan, but i can't get the learning plan to show up for the users (Users login to my dashboard by default), any thoughts? My terminology may be off, we are moving from another LMS, apologies in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grouping Together Multiple SCORM Courses?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Don, I believe you can do what you want. We have multiple scorms within a course. This allows a modular progression as you described. Set the course to "Topics" or "Weeks" mode. (where you set Scorm single activity) Add scorm activities as desired. Set restrict access to force the sequence you want. Not sure about your Meta course proposal... we use the subcourse plugin to merge course grades as activities. Cheers Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grouping Together Multiple SCORM Courses?
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with Mark about putting multiple scorms into one course, assuming they are all related content.  There is a fantastic third party course format (Onetopic) which allows you to make each topic display as a tab.  Just like in Topics, you can hide each topic from the student until they complete the prerequisite content.  Onetopic is cool because when you hide topics until they complete, once they complete, the new topic opens up at the top.  I just tested this and it looks amazing!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grouping Together Multiple SCORM Courses?
ResponsesInList.Text: As described by Mark, that will work, but I am curious about your thinking around using Meta-courses. Meta courses are used where there is a lot of common content for a lot of users. Instead of having huge numbers of students in one course, you can break up the actual course enrollments but keep a single course full of content. Does this relate to what you were thinking, or your situation?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grouping Together Multiple SCORM Courses?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm going to echo the consensus here -  we use SCORM packages in separate sections of the same course to track progress across discrete competencies in a progression. You can use restrict access and activity completion together to set the user flow through these items. MetaCourses, in my experience, are best for linking multiple sections of the same course together (for example, in higher ed where you have multiple sections of, say, math 101 being populated by an external database like LDAP ). This is where all students are getting the same content but are enrolled in MA-101-A, MA-101-B, etc. Meta course can allow you to create a single course then put all students into that course in separate groups and have enrollments dynamically updated as students add and drop. IF you go the multiple single-activity course route as you describe, I would make a master course and use subcourse activity to record grades from all the separate courses. BUT it would probably be easier to just make a single course and load all your SCORMs in there.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to remove "You should set yourself a goal if you´re planning to succeed"
ResponsesInList.Text: I can't think of any theme that uses this text, so it might take a while to find what you want. Option 1: Go to Site admin/Language/Language Customization then select your language then Continue, then Load the Language Pack. Do a search for the string you're looking for, and delete it. Option 2: Have a look at Site Admin > Appearance > Additional HTML, you might get lucky and it has been placed there, but maybe not. I strongly suspect these will not work. I am thinking that some kind soul has hacked Core code and written this directly to the form that loads on the front page . I think the best bet is likely to do a grep in the Moodle root folder and looking for the string, then open those documents, php, js or html pages probably and delete it wherever you find it. You will also have to look at the database , as the images suggest a field has been included, probably a user defined field or possibly an additional table, which causes a lot of other problems. You are going to have to find all references to that table and delete them as well. Not an easy task. Of course, the best alternative is to update your Moodle to the latest version and redesign your theme. That gets rid of any additional code that has been hacked in. Of course, if this is just a personal thing, and you are not a Moodle Administrator, then I am afraid you are just going to have to wear it, but talk to someone who is an Admin, they might help. Of course, you could set you goal to something like, "I want to read Shakespeare in its original language and follow my Favourite Character, Dick the Butcher's, career advice."

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to remove "You should set yourself a goal if you´re planning to succeed"
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello.  There is nothing hard coded here.This is the description for  Choice activity that has been added to your front page.I don't know the theme you are using but the way to remove this wording (or even remove the choice activity) to turn on the editing on the front page, find the  Choice activity and click to edit it. If you don't find it in the centre of the front page as in my picture then locate the Main menu block and click to edit the Choice activity. When you open it up to edit it you will see there is a checkbox to tick if you want the description to display on the page. Remove the tick and that wording won't display. Alternatively, you can delete the whole choice if you no longer need it.If you don't see the Main menu block then you can add it and then do the above. See the documentation on removing an activity from Site pages.

ResponsesInList.Title: User Management - Bulk
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm very frustrated with the available options for bulk user management.  I am trying to remove users that have been inactive for more than a year, which currently seems impossible.  I can't seem to generate a list which does NOT include 'never' under last login.  Even if I could, there is no option to select multiple users to delete.  This leads me to the 'Bulk User Actions' function. Within Bulk user actions, I can export a list of users into a CSV, which is great!  I can use the CSV to delete users!   Here is the problem:  The CSV does not include last login information.  The generated list is filtered by last login date, to me this is the most important criteria other than student ID.  Why is it not included in the CSV output?   Is there a way to have it included? Currently, the CSV output includes users whom have 'never' accessed the site... even though I specified first and last access date range.  Is there a way to omit users whom have 'never' logged in?  I wish there was a filter option to NOT include users whom have never logged in. Does anyone have any recommendations on how to purge moodle accounts in bulk?  There must be something I can do.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User Management - Bulk
ResponsesInList.Text: If adding filters for 'last access' doesn't suit, I'd recommend that you try the ad-hoc reports plugin. Using it, you can make a customised report that is perfect for your purposes. Then, make the report exportable to CSV and voila. Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User Management - Bulk
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eric, This is a problem alright. Here's a workaround: Create a cohort called and id-ed e.g. 'old', and other called and id-ed 'oldwho never logged in' Use the bulk user actions to add the users that you filtered above to the 'old' cohort. Now go back to your your bulk user actions, clear the selection, and add the filter to include thow who have never accessed the site. Add the results to the 'old who never logged in' cohort. Then, again, clear your filters and selection, and in your bulk user actions, add the filter: Cohort ID is equal to old. Save and add another filter: Cohort ID doesn't contain 'old who never logged in' This will return users who last logged in over a year ago but exclude those who have never accessed the site. You can now delete them. Catherine

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User Management - Bulk
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eric, One possible solution to this could be in downloading the mdl_user table from the database (if you have PHD MyAdmin or Moodle Adminer available). In this table, you'll find columns for lastmodified, lastaccess, lastlogin etc., all with a date/time stamp in Epoch style. This can be easily converted to something more understandable. Then use this filtered table as a basis for your upload users CSV file. That way, you can delete or suspend users that haven't been online for a while.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: local testing on Windows for EXISTING moodle site on linux server
ResponsesInList.Text: First ... am certain you will get differing opinions and suggestions ... things like 'stick with what you know', etc. The key for this response was your reasoning ... server in production is 'linux' (but it would be a good idea to find out what distro) and your thought on environment (locally) being as close to production server as possible. So ... if production server was Linux Ubuntu (LTS) with native php, mysql , apache (that's another item for sharing ... what does production server actually run?... etc., etc.. Here's my 2 cents: VirtualBox https://www.virtualbox.org/ Install of Linux OS same flavor as production Example Ubuntu 16.04 but could be CentOS 7. https://www.google.com/search?q=installing+ubuntu+16.04+on+virtualbox Backup your production site ... db dump, tar ball of code, tar ball of moodledata, and restore that to your Ubuntu 16.04 instance in VB. You will to contend with FQDN ... but one can cheat with a host file edit (harder to do on Windows but from what I have read doable). After you get VB, Ubuntu (with apache/my sql /php whatever) running and right before you restore your Moodle by FQDN, edit the host file of your PC and give the private IP address on your home network (192.168.0.x) a mapping to your servers FQDN. You are fooling your PC into thinking mygreat.moodle.org is on your local laptop in VB/Ubuntu. No change to config.php file needed then. When done messing with the VB instance and you want to view the production server again, just comment out the line you added to the host file that pointed to your private IP. Have used the above 'trick' while presenting at a TCEA Moot (in Texas) and the venue didn't have a robust wireless network/coverage for attendees and presenters ... attendees couldn't get to internet without tethering their smart phones - whose connections were 3G at the time .... kinda like the 'world wide wait' of dialup days on 3600 baud. I was showing them http://somerealserver.org/moodle/ - a backup restored to laptop running virtual box and CentOS 5 at the time. There's my 2 'sense' (nope, spelled it right! ) 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: local testing on Windows for EXISTING moodle site on linux server
ResponsesInList.Text: +1 to James suggestion. Much depends upon how you are hosted.   The info provided about size of Moodle DB and moodledata and methods you have used (ftp) indicates to me, you are not hosted on a VPS ... if you are, you've not explored expansion of the VPS setup ... which one can do. I admin a few servers on Rackspace for another entity.  More than one of their servers grew larger - same things - DB and moodledata.   But due to the fact the RS boxens are what others would term 'VPS's', the servers could be expanded to handle increased usage ... at present, the need for 'space'. In RS, one can setup an additional storage device (volume) of desired size ... example below is VMWare but RS is really essentially the same. Filesystem            1K-blocks       Used Available Use% Mounted on /dev/mapper/vg_moodle4-lv_root 51475068   13964724  34888904  29% / / is the root and if moodledata were to be on that device it would have been in /var/www/moodledata But there isn't enough space ...  in the virtualized server config, a volume was added thus /dev/mapper/vg_moodle4-lv_home 2053461808 1142864368 806280924  59% /home In this case it was given /home ... but could have been /data and it actually houses the moodledata directory. In humanly understandable values: /dev/mapper/vg_moodle4-lv_home 2.0T  1.1T  769G  59% /home Translation: /home is 2 TeraBytes in size it's using 1.1TB and has 769G free space left. So where you host ... is it a VPS?   And does hosting provider allow customers to 'attach a device' to VPS's of whatever size you can afford (it ain't free)? Advantage in setup like this  .... same environment ... cloning the production site to another instance of Moodle would be tight ... but doable.  *** NO FTP required *** ... if VPS and space available one could 'clone' moodledata to moodle2data for the dev site with a cp -rp command ... those files never leave the server and are just copied to the moodle2data location.   There would also be a little crunch in getting the dev DB installed at first ... but one could cull some of the moodle tables not needed for a dev site ... like 'log' on mysqldump of production database and thus the resulting SQL file smaller ... thus, if follows, the DB for the dev server also smaller. Since dev site is really only for your purposes, users accounts could be removed ... courses reset ... which removes student submissions etc.  You have, basically, your own 'playground'. Expansion of space could be cheaper and a lot less hassle than leasing yet another server that would have to be fixed/patched, etc. ... ie, administered. Again ... 2 cents. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Video training for company
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd like to upload a corporate training video and set up a system so I know when my employees have watched the video. Is there a way to set up a course to do that? Thanks, Josh

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Video training for company
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Josh The simplest way to do this, is to use completion settings, http://docs.moodle.org/en/Course_completion_settings and then set the page with the video on it to "complete" when the page is viewed. This won't tell you if the user *really* watched the video though. Some 3rd party plugins can do a better job of checking if the video itself was played through. I have set this sort of thing up a few times. The general thinking however, is that its best to check that the learning in the video was imparted. So you have  questions on the video page or after it and then track that the questions were answered correctly. So here you would use a Moodle Quiz activity, or maybe a Lesson activity, with the video embedded inside (or possibly make the video page a separate activity.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a video module that students are required to watch.  How do I grade this module as 100% once they have viewed the video?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Todd, There is no way to determine whether or not someone watched an entire video.  It's possible to click the link and go out for a stroll or a latte.  So, I suggest the following: Add a separate quiz activity that has a few questions related to key aspects of the video. Successful completion of the quiz will serve as confirmation the video has been watched, or at least that students know key aspects of the video content. You could place the video and the quiz in a Moodle Lesson as one activity. The Lesson quiz will serve the same function as the quiz mentioned above. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Text: In reference to 2, I would stick with the regular quiz. That way I could make a few extra questions, then set the quiz to randomly pick from the available questions. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: List of trainees and assigned courses
ResponsesInList.Text: What plugin? Your first question was about seeing a list of courses for individuals. This question seems to be about uploading courses and maybe user data? User upload: You can use a .csv file upload to create and update user accounts.  You can enroll people in courses using the same upload by adding columns (course1, course2).  You can even add people to groups in courses, if you have already created the course groups and are really good when adding people to courses on an upload.  The same format will allow you to add people to cohorts (which enrolls them in courses, if the courses are set up properly).  Cohorts can be created in bulk through an upload, too--but it is a bit trickier.  Groups can be added to courses with a different .csv form. Bulk course creation: I've heard you can bulk create courses (I have never tried) using a .csv file upload.  I think it will just create a shell, which is why I never used it--when I had a bunch of courses that needed creating, I needed copies of existing, not empty shells that needed development.  It's all about what you need. Bulk category creation: I suppose it might be possible to bulk create categories but I've not seen anything about it or tried. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hide my courses listing in the navigation menu
ResponsesInList.Text: Hiding ‘Navigation’ drawer in Boost For hiding the drawer in boost theme, we need to follow 2 steps, first we need to hide the drawer section and then suppress the hamburger icon: The left sidebar is open by default, make it closed by - A slight code tweak is required in line 31-34 in theme/boost/layout/columns2.php, Change - if (isloggedin()) { $navdraweropen = (get_user_preferences('drawer-open-nav', 'true') == 'true'); } else { $navdraweropen = false; } To - if (isloggedin()) { $navdraweropen = false; } else { $navdraweropen = false; } Forum discussion link :- https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=346967 Now, suppress the ‘hamburger’ icon used for toggling the sidebar view - Add the following code in Site Admin -> Additional HTML -> Within HEAD <style> .navbar-nav [data-region="drawer-toggle"] button { display: none; } </style> Forum discussion link :- https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=355612 Note :- It suppresses the drawer section for everyone, even for admin and teachers.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I cant access Moodle Admin setings
ResponsesInList.Text: Error 500 is a generic response when a server detects an error but can't pinpoint it. Server logs may provide further information about this error.  Most often this is a server side error and outside the user's ability to control. Contacting the Server Admins may provide a positive result. Alternatively, try clearing the cache and cookies, this sometimes helps. Otherwise it could be a permissions error, or the "currently unable" would indicate a timeout error. If so, then it is likely to be a PHP timeout error which occurs with an improperly formed request, which is not likely to be your problem, but talking to your Server Admins could help. Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all I am very new to moodle, but I want to create a two pages connected to a database where includes the following first table UserID, includes users ID that I will give it to them second table TopicNames, includes certain topic name based on the user id, so each userid for example has specific topic so how to make a login screen that call the userid then after authorizing appear that userid topic name?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: login page attached to related custom message
ResponsesInList.Text: If you are new to Moodle this will involve a lot of clicking and figuring things out and installing a plugin, or writing some PHP. But you can do it. This project is about what the user should see after they first login, I think. In most sites this will be the user dashboard . You can also set it to other pages too. See here: https://docs.moodle.org/34/en/Dashboard#Default_home_page If you use the dashboard, you can customize the appearance by putting blocks on it. You can even put a block at the very top in the center. That sounds perfect. Well its a bit tricky because the "default dashboard" and the 'user dashboard" are different. Its easy to think you are customizing the default dashboard, when its really your personal one. But thats one of the learnings you will encounter in this journey. Now there are all sorts of blocks and you can even write your own if you know how to write PHP and like coffee and late nights. But a good one to start with is the HTML block. Because you can freely edit it with the HTML editor and add pictures and comic sans (my favorite font) and stuff. Now all we need to do is to get the data from the database into the HTML block at the top center of the dashboard. Enter the Generico filter (my plugin ...everyone groans ...). But really ... it will do the trick. And it will mean you do not need to write your own plugin. Its how I do this sort of thing for other people's sites. You can put a custom SQL query into a Generico template and it will fetch it and display it on the page.  The filter will look for crafty little Generico strings, that look like this: {GENERICO:type=essmatask,username=bobthebuilder}, and replace them with whatever your template says to. The docs for Generico are here: https://docs.moodle.org/34/en/filter_generico That at least is how I would approach this project.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Administration not working!
ResponsesInList.Text: Who changed what? That is the only way that this sort of error occurs, someone has deleted something from the server , or added an over-ride file somewhere. Find that, fix it and things should return to normal. Otherwise, keep your config.php file, delete all the other code, replace the lot with either a fresh download or another unzipped copy of your last download, then, after checking your current config.php file, making sure it is not the file that was changed in the first place, rename the new config.php to config.bak and copy your old config.php file back to the root folder and start it up. You can copy and paste the fresh code, start it up as normal and it should do a refresh, add in any plugins you are using. You can spend days looking for an error that you might not find. Where is your time best spent? If it still happens then there is a major issue in your server or PHP settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Adding Activities into Resources
ResponsesInList.Text: I proposed this new feature at the Glasgow Moot and it was voted third by participants. The addition of stealth mode for activities and resources recognises how often teachers want students to access an activity from within a book, or a page or in a label with say Tabs added to it. However this is not simple for teachers are not very familiar with Moodle. What is being requested is a simple way to do this, so that in a book, for example, the add activity is available. Practically this would be easiest to implement if it is seen as a way of automatically creating a stealth activity in the containing section for that book resources and placing a link to the activity into the book, along with the edit/delete functions. Does anyone have a suggestion of how this might be implemented? I would be keen to help take this forward if possible. I have created this as a new feature request in the tracker https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-61783 Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding Activities into Resources
ResponsesInList.Text: You did. I was there. It struck me at the time that what you might want is an 'Add an activity' button in the Atto editor. You can then embed an activity (really just a link to an activity) inside any bit of text. A bit of Javascript could be organised to make it editable to teachers. I think the talk of 'stealth activities' rather confused matters as that's really an implementation decision. I can see all sorts of problems. It's changing the way that Moodle organises itself completely. You would also need a feature to make it easier to find activities (especially for the poor support staff) as they could be anywhere?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding Activities into Resources
ResponsesInList.Text: I think restricting it to activities in the course is necessary for usability and for issues around enrollments and roles etc. Embedding other activities (rather than just linking to them) would be helpful too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding Activities into Resources
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for your responses. Certainly I agree with C Behan that it should be restricted to activities in the current course, or rather that any activity would be created within the current course and probably within the section that the resource was sitting in. That is what I meant by bringing in the issue of stealth mode - I was trying to work out how this could be implemented without a major change to the system of where activities sit within Moodle. Howard's suggestion makes a lot of sense. In this context a straightforward way of implementing this would be to add a button in the atto editor that would Bring up a list of activity types and allow one to be selected (in the same way as this happens in a course section) When the an activity is selected and the various fields are populated, the new activity is saved in the section that the resouces is in, but set to  "make available but not shown on course page" A link to that activity is created along with the standard edit buttons to allow that activity to be editted from within the resoucese. I suspect that it is the final part of 3 which would be most problematic and if neccessary it could be left that you go into the activity in order to edit it, but it would be best for less experienced users if it just looked the same. Problems with this would be moving, backing up resources that "contain" activities, but in a sense this is the same situtation that happens with activity autolinking - if you do not copy both the resource and the original activity it will not work, but it will be obvious why. Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Audio preloading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Robyn This sounds like a problem for your technical team to be honest. I would wait for them. I would first do my best to find out how to reproduce the problem reliably. Using video in courses is not new and there are a lot of other tools out there that will help. Unfortunately, what has been mentioned already, Camtasia, Adobe Articulate and even Poodll, all excellent tools, can also bear some costs that a lot of students may not be able to cover. The most successful tool I have used for screen casting has been Screencast-o-matic. This is an Open Source project that does bear the badge but is easy to use for newbies. A small fee, like $(US)15/pa I think it is, drops the badge and allows users to gain access to the editing tools, but the raw video produced is useful. All you need is a camera on your desktops or use the builtin camera on laptops. For videos that require a live action or demo sequence, (you mention patient care), a hand held cell-phone video is good, or even a tripod mounted taping can be very useful. In any circumstance, I have found the largest problem is sound, that is, the sound recording can be wrecked by background noise. Even the best video can be excruciating if the background noise detracts from the video. A lot of phones also do not have good sound pickup, if the action is occurring too far from the phone. Sadly, there are not too many decent dubbing tools but perhaps something like WavePad might be useful here. Adobe Audition is obviously the top of the range, but so is the price. Good luck...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Course : Add Topic/Section Permission
ResponsesInList.Text: Let us make sure we are using the same language, Aditya. This is very common problem so I am putting this in the context I am interpreting it, so I hope this makes sense for you. Fundamentals of Computers and Information Technology - I would think that is a single course which may have one or more Teachers. Same with every course listed here: Operating System (DOS, Windows and Linux) Computer in Office I (MS Word and MS Excel) Computer in Office II (MS Power Point, MS Access and MS Outlook) Communication Skills and Personality Development Introduction to Internet and Web Technology Introduction to Financial Accounting with Tally Programming with Visual Basic Dot Net Database Handling with Foxpro (????????????) Are all individual courses .  I suspect you are referring to these as "topics", but maybe not. Course : Diploma in Computer Application - I would use this as a Category in Moodle. To which one person is Manager, maybe 2, but no more than that. Usually there is a Convener for the course, one person who is responsible overall for the course, the course content and assessment practices. This Category is the actual learning path and successful completion of all courses in this learning path would give the student a Diploma. This line: 9 Teachers enrolled in course suggests that 1 course has 1 Teacher, that 1 Teacher is assigned per course . From the information you have provided, you seem to be  asking three main questions. How can I prevent Teachers from creating new courses? - Easy, do not make them Course Creators. How can I prevent Teachers from editing each other's courses? - Easy, make sure they are teachers only in one course. How can I make sure they can access a course to edit it so they can change or add new material, activities or questions? Again, easy, as they are the Teacher of their course, no-one else can edit that course.  They can do all the things that a Teacher can do inside the course they have the capabilities to do. To set this up, assign one Teacher to a course at the course level, NOT the Category level. The only person who has access to all aspects of each course is the Category Manager(s). If you want several teachers to access a single course , but refuse them editing rights, make it clear that they DO NOT have editing rights in anything but their own course . Assign these people as "Non-Editing Teachers" They have almost every right a Teacher has, but they cannot edit anything.  Additional capabilities can be granted, if they are needed, but it will mean that if a Non-editing Teacher wants a particular exercise in a course , then they will have to negotiate with the Teacher for it to be included. This line: "I do not want that Teacher can change any setting of Course and He/She can add Topic and Activity." actually doesn't make a lot of sense to me. You don't want them to change a course but you want them to change a course ? I doubt you can do this given the way that editing capabilities are set up in Moodle. If you mean you do not want them to be able to change the learning path , then they cannot as a Teacher of a course . I hope I am making sense, but please, let's continue this if you are unclear.

No offense, this is constructive criticism.  but have to ask ... are you a teacher?  A course designer? or the server administrator who is trying to 'organize' the content in the Moodle?   As an administrator of the server ... both OS and in Moodle, job is to facilitate instruction.   What tools would your teachers want to use to teach XYZ? 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Audience Response System
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Are there are plans for an Audience Response System in
Moodle?  I have seen several work-arounds (Choice, Quiz, etc.), but they
all strike me as Heath-Robinsons, and I was wondering if there
is a proper ARS in the pipe-line. Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Audience Response System
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't know and have not heard of anyone working on one. If you have all your question pre-planned, then yes you can sort of use Choice, Questionnaire, Quiz, or either the Real Time or Active quizzes for audience response. The Hot Question plugin may be a better option if you are wanting to pose, "spur of the moment" type questions during a lecture. The teacher can pose a question, let everyone respond, then start a New Round to pose other questions. The Hot Question setup allows settings to control visibility of responses to other students. If visible, then students can "Vote up" a response. There is also a setting that allows for anonymous responses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Audience Response System
ResponsesInList.Text: OK, thanks for the reply. My questions are all pre-prepared: I use them to check prior knowledge and then also intersperse them in my my teaching for various activities .  I've tried the work-arounds you suggest (except the Hot Question plugin, but that a logistical problem), but they all have their weaknesses. At the moment, I use Kahoot, and I'm really looking for something simple like Kahoot.  Kahoot is great, but is limited in question and answer length, and so scenario-type questions are tricky (again, work-arounds are required).  I also wrote my own app to do it, and it works well enough, but I write for Android only, so that excludes too many of my students. As I use Moodle in my lectures for other stuff, it just made sense to have a simple ARS running in there also. Thanks anyway. Regards

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Audience Response System
ResponsesInList.Text: Ken, I have used both TurningPoint and H-ITT clickers, and I have used both of these with Moodle quizzes.  But my solution is not as direct as you probably want.  Anyway, here is what I do. I create the quiz, typically multiple choice, in Moodle.  In the classroom I display each question.  At this same point in time, I have my clicker software turned on.  Students click on their response, and I click on the correct answer (students don't see my click.)  After the class is over, I export the grades from the clicker software to a CSV file (or Excel) and then import them into my Moodle grade book. Yes, you are looking for a feature to avoid this need to export/import.  Maybe so, but I have no problem with simple export/import techniques.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Player complains constantly - trying for an answer again
ResponsesInList.Text: I didn't see your first time round posts, so I am unlikely going to add too much to what you already know. I would say that as a general rule, when I was adminning 3 Moodles, (micro-Moodles) I updated each once a year, and always used the next to latest release, so they were all on the same release, not just version, actual release number. I also updated PHP when advised to do so. The point is that in doing this, I could avoid the sort of issue you are discussing. The next to latest version always had the major bug fixes done, there was a large skill base on these forums for support and there was no great step up for users, except from v1.9.xx to v2.x What I have found with SCORM though is that the packages worked for a while, then we had to replace them where we had downloaded them, sometimes re-editing them to suit, or update them where we made them which, again, avoided the sort of problem you are raising here, I now suspect. I know that one organization went exclusively self made SCORM after I shifted interstate for a while, no idea what the others were doing, but there doesn't seem to be any problems that I have heard of. (With legislative change though, they may not even be using SCORM any more, but again, I haven't heard.) The issue for me with SCORM has always been the same, you can't change the environment and expect packages to work without some updates. They work for a few changes, but they won't keep working. Can you recompile them? Rebuild them? Not using SCORM for a long time now, I am not sure what the latest tools are, Articulate, or Camtasia or some such, can you gain access to these tools and rebuild?
