ResponsesInList.Text: I use Lectora as well to publish scorm content--I've found sometimes they just want to be re-published (delete the entire scorm folder before publishing) and reloaded.  Don't know why.  Trivantis is really loving the anchoring items and seamless play stuff...but my experience is that anchored items cause a lot of problems on mobile devices and seamless play is not as seamless as they think.  I finally turned it off because it wasn't doing what they said it would--new pages were displaying poorly and it was pretty distracting. Your real problem though, is the internet connection message.  Typically, this means the internet connection is unstable and continued use of the module could result the module not saving progress.  Last year, we had a problem with this message a lot one month.  A bunch of research and testing resulted in adjusting a setting: Site administration -> Plugins ->Activity modules -> SCORM package-> Admin settings We unchecked "Enable SCORM 1.2 standard mode" and the problem disappeared.  I'm not entirely sure what this mode does or why unchecking it resolved the problem and we'd run our site for years without this being a problem...but this resolved it. The location may be slightly different for you, as my installation is much older than yours but it might be worth looking at.

ResponsesInList.Text: Been following of this some ... not a SCORM expert but do admin some Moodles that use SCORM (a lot).  And, in the past (older versions of Moodle) issues were present and explained ... supposedly fixed. But ... network comes before application in ISO model.   Moodle is the application - so it's really the end point. Earlier stated 'fiber optics' ... is that true from your location all the way to the server including your workstation's NIC and the server NIC's themselves? Assuming linux, what does ifconfig look like on your server?  Look at the RX packets, RX errors, TX packets, TX errors numbers. What network testing have you done from your location to your server? Traceroutes?  Constant pings? And from your server back to your location. Even with Fiber Optics there are other devices involved in a connection from Point A to Point B (Moodle server). On your server, doesn't SCORM do a check for a file ... checknet.txt ... search your web server logs for that check. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

Question 2 If that course (in calendar format) where the three groups is created, has teachers adding content to the content areas of each section - will that teachers content be invisible to other teachers and students-not-taught-by-that teacher? ie will separate and invisible groups of students-and-their-teachers be able to share the course and all its features (like HTML text areas, assignments etc) all separately? Either way I want three groups of totally separate students/teachers to be easily allocated access (by these closed "teacher-pupil" relationships ) so that each group has a (calendar format)  course their teacher can post and use without teachers or students work/posting/content being seen by other groups Any help appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.78 the smartest way to provide teacher-student group privacy between groups sharing courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dom, you're definitely on the right track with the idea of using meta courses. If your groups are confined to the Child course, they will not be able to see or share their work, each child course is completely independent of each other. The Teacher is assigned to the Child course and not the Meta course. A Manager can be assigned to the Meta Course(s) or a single Teacher can be assigned to each Meta course. That person alone will be responsible for content. If you have a Manager of that entire Category, the Manager will be able to view/edit/enroll/exclude/add/delete to any course in that Category. Any Role assignment at a course level, Manager, Teacher, Student applies ONLY to that course. And I would suggest that the Child-Meta course arrangement is the simplest and most elegant method available in any LMS of using mutually exclusive groupings. It cannot be over-ridden under any circumstance. That's the only way I can make sense of your question, Dom, even after reading it several times. It is seriously convoluted as to what you want to achieve. Someone else may have a different take on it that could provide a better answer...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best place to add a document for many courses
ResponsesInList.Text: My solution may not apply to you, but I will provide it. I would keep this file on my own web server (website), and then use a URL link to it in Moodle.  In other words, one file in one location, linked to by many courses.  When I make changes to this document, it will be correct in all courses.  If your school does not have a web server, you might want to get a personal one.  Of course, this method provides some separation between documents from your Moodle, but it works well.  Actually, I do this, i.e., use a personal repository for all of my course content webpages, and have never thought about doing it differently.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best place to add a document for many courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Site policy is the easiest way around this. IF they have no completed Site Policy agreement, they cannot access the site. At the end of each academic period, quarter, semester, term, year, course section, whatever, run a cron that resets the Policy Agreement field in the User table to 0. This means they have to redo the agreement once per academic period you define. As it currently stands, the choice activity is complicating things and I suggest is really not helpful. So unless you can incorporate the activity, or something similar, into the agreement, then it will remain an issue for you.

ResponsesInList.Text: Just adding to the great suggestions so far - If you have the rights to add plugins or can have them added for you, the Sharing Cart block is an additional plugin that makes it very easy to copy activities and resources from one course into another. ResponsesInList.Title: Error: Invalid permissions detected when trying to create a directory [solved]
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, I've found this problem elsewhere on the forums but not with a satisfactory solution or explanation. My server environment: VPS: Ubuntu 16.0 LTS latest versions of Apache MySQL (as of April 2018) PHP (7.2) with additional modules installed and enabled My SQL InnoDB format = Barracuda Moodle v 3.4.2 Environment passes all Moodle checks. Migrated data from another server, i.e.: mysqldump DB backup /var/www/moodledata/filedir /var/www/moodledata/geoip /var/www/moodledata/lang /var/www/moodledata/lock /var/www/moodledata/muc /var/www/moodledata/repository File permissions: /var/www/html: chown = root:root; chmod = directories 755; files 644. /var/www/moodledata: chown = www-data:www-data; chmod = 777 The whole site was up and running for ~1 week before I started getting the following error increasingly until the whole site stopped working: 
```text
Invalid permissions detected when trying to create a directory.
```
 I read here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=343116#p1386751 (2016-12-05) that it might be an opcache issue. Which I took to mean that opcache was unable to write files to: /var/www/moodledata/cache, /var/www/moodledata/localcache, /var/www/moodledata/sessions, /var/www/moodledata/temp, and/or /var/www/moodledata/trashdir I connected to the server via CLI and did the following: 
```text
$ chown www-data:www-data -R /var/www/moodledata


$ chmod 777 -R /var/www/moodledata
```
 And the issue immediately went away. Nobody else had accessed the server before the issue arose. So somehow, the file permissions got changed without any intervention from me or anyone else. Is this a known bug in Moodle? I couldn't find a similar one in the bug tracker. Thanks in advance, Matt

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM on Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text:
I'm having some problems with a SCORM 1.2 package in LMoodle. If users complete all the questions in one go, the module is

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM on Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Check the settings which you have done for SCORM. Also check out the grading method in SCORM FAQ and SCORM settings doc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM on Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: this is the main FAQ you should take a look at: https://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Handling_of_Multiple_Attempts It could be flagging the partial attempt as "completed" and then a re-entry is putting you in "review" mode (Review mode might appear in the top left of the SCORM player while viewing the scorm) - to avoid "review mode" you need to set "force new attempt" to "yes". Another thing that could be causing this is if your SCORM package  defines a "mastery score" - this states that if the user exits the scorm with a score lower than the score set it should set the SCORM as failed. More information on that is here: https://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Moodle_changes_cmi.core.lesson_status_from_.22completed.22_or_.22passed.22_to_.22failed.22 if none of that helps  you might need to modify your SCORM package in your authoring tool to change how it behaves when users attempt to resume a previous attempt.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Learning Administration Question
ResponsesInList.Text: Something that might help is to read about cohorts...this is like groups but at the site or category level.  You can enroll cohorts in a series (path) of courses and require course A completion for course B completion (but not course B starting)--though this would be VERY complex with that many courses.  I used to manage a site with (at the point I left the agency) more than 10000 courses and requiring prerequisite completion was practically impossible. Or you could enroll the cohort in course A and provide enrollment keys based on performance (or other criteria) for subsequent courses. Cohorts are awesome. I *think* you can probably set up something in account creation that would add them to a cohort, which would start them on the curriculum path you wanted. And as for completion/grading--you set grades for different items (like the AICC--which, in Moodle, you'll see a lot of SCORM references...it used to say SCORM/AICC, but it is my understanding the SCORM activity module will run AICC still--but I've never done AICC) and you tell the grade book how to look at grades and there is a grade report in each course.  Course completion allows you to say what is required and then triggers 'completion' when those conditions are met--if you set grade requirements in activities , completing the activity without reaching the required score will not trigger completion.  And you can set show if conditions on stuff--like if someone doesn't get a required score, it will display a message on the home screen, etc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Bulk upload: Update question
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm a Moodle site administrator for English language classes at my university department, and I'm using Moodle 2.8.10. I've bulk uploaded the student data for a lot of students that are taking the same course (Course A). Essentially, I now want to do the same thing for another course (Course B). Some of the students who are taking Course A are also taking Course B. The only Upload Type that seems to make sense is "Add new and update existing users". However, for the students who are taking both Course A and Course B, I'm concerned that this method will remove them from Course A (ie. update means "overwrite" rather than "append"). Am I right? And if this is the case, is there anyway around this problem? All help much appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk upload: Update question
ResponsesInList.Text:
Fill in missing from file and defaults adds data in the existing user account with data provided in the
uploaded file if the field is empty (does not already contain data) and
fills in the default values for existing user details when no data is
provided in the uploaded file. This would seem to  be the best way to add another course You should also be able to export your Group A users - in case they have updated their details. Put it in maintenance mode first, add your course B column and import.  Then add Group B only students ( as new users?) Check this with a test user and backup first of course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk upload: Update question
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you James and Catherine. Yes, that solution worked. I just changed the course name of the bulk upload file to Course B, and used "Fill in missing from file". Thank you so much!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk upload: Update question

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Face to face (Totara) events - previous sessions showing to students
ResponsesInList.Text: So, first issue: hidden from students...you say this is about F2F but it isn't--it is really about the interaction between course settings, section settings and activity settings, ultimately, I'd guess.  In course settings, you can choose if something hidden from students is actually invisible or just unavailable.  The section setting is what is making the item unavailable, which is okay but if you really want it to disappear, you should probably hide the activity as well. I'm not really sure what the second item is showing--but it does say the item is unavailable... Second issue: it doesn't look like these images were taken from student view.  I'm fairly confident this is true because the Manage courses button appears for you.  There is no real student view from the Admin perspective in categories.  Switching to student in a course applies to that course...not everything.   Switching to student can be helpful but sometimes you need to BE a student to see how it totally works.  Do you have a student account?  Or a test user account that only has authenticated user permissions?  Try enrolling the student account and logging with it to see what happens for the actual student.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Face to face (Totara) events - previous sessions showing to students

ResponsesInList.Title: Resetting a Course for One Student
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there a way to remove activity completion data for a single student within a course, without jeopardizing other students' activity completion reports? We're talking SCORM packages and certificate generation. In essence, is it possible to reset the course for one student--so that the student can start "from scratch" in the course--no activity completion records and no grades?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Resetting a Course for One Student
ResponsesInList.Text: There are two ways, one is to clone the course, remove all user data and enroll that student in the cloned course, or to give that student a new username and enroll them in that course. That is likely to be the simplest way. It seems from your comments that other students have all done, if so, you could archive the course, reset it and re-enroll that student another way to do it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.4 database got problem after uninstalling a plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: No recent backups ... shame on you! :\ That's interesting .... duplicate admin page registrationmoodleorg.   New one to me. Possible to reinstall ... well, one would have to attempt that manually. Download the plugin (it's a zip).   Then either upload the unzipped directory created by unzipping to the appropriate location in code or upload the zip via some other file browser tool and unzip. Check ownerships permissions on the newly created directories to match those attributes seen for other folders/files in moodle code. Now if those were in-compatible to begin with what issues were exhibited when first installed?  Could you get to admin areas?   If not, the manual reinstall has gained you nothing to fix. The other way .. never really recommended as a first option, but in this case ... First, make an sql dump of the database you have ... even if broken, a restore of that could prevent a major boo-boo. Moodle, as you know, is a stack ... code + db.  In the DB for Moodle there is a table called 'mdl_config_plugins' which has rows for all plugins ... core as well as addon.   There could be several rows for the plugins you installed. There is also another table for filters: mdl_filter_config Ditto for what it might contain. Use whatever graphical tool you have to work with the DB and call up those tables to view.  That graphical tool could be phpmyadmin or some other (you've not said yet what platform nor how hosted). Remove those rows. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Internet connection is unreliable or has been interrupted (  Nginx )
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi natapol, that SCORM message doesn't directly depend on your web server configuration but on the network quality in between the user and the (web) server. If it always appears regardless the user then you've roughly two options: serious bandwidth/load issues in your web server you're denying serving plain TXT files - which what is used by SCORM (Moodle) to check the network connection availability ( /lib/yui/build/moodle-core-checknet/assets/checknet.txt ); which turns out to be your case since you deny access to any TXT file but from an enlarged Class C ( allow 192.168.0.0/16; while usually a Class C would be /24 ) The only other notable thing in your nginx configuration is that you're still using url rewriting instead of a native PATH_INFO support but this is something unrelated. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Appearance Problems
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm using the current version of Moodle.  I have two appearance problems.  First, I've put in a Word document and have said I want the document to appear automatically.  But no matter what setting I put in appearance the system requires the student to download the document to see it.  The students I have are even more computer illiterate than I am and I don't think they will be able to realize they have to click on another link to see the document.  How can I set the settings so the document will come up with just a click to the document link? Second, I have a zipped Storyline Module that when you go through the whole process has the module on the far right of the screen and students have to scroll back and forth to see it.  I know that if you click the box to the right of the Module title it will click back to the center, but again I'd rather not have to have them go through several screens to see the module.  How do I change the settings to do this? I know there was a great article on this in the forum, but I'll be darned if I can find it again.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Appearance Problems
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Melanie, Two questions in one... and each with it's own answer. To answer your first question: there are no tools in Moodle that will automatically display your MS Word document without leaving the browser. This is the reason why the file will be downloaded, so the user can pick the application to view it in (MS Word, Office 365, Libre or OpenOffice, or Mac Pages). As for the SCORM package: you can set the SCORM activity up so it'll display in a pop-up of predefined height and width. You'd have to select New window in the SCORM activity settings page, in the section Appearance . This will allow you to also set up correct height and width, and various other relevant settings: You may hav eto experiment a bit before getting this right, but in the end, it'll look far better than before. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Appearance Problems
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to add to Joost's response ... If you want your users to be able to click and view the document rather than downloading a .doc file, consider putting the contents of your word file in to a Moodle Page or Book. Paste the document as plain text and format it in your Moodle text editor, or clean it up using a tool like https://html-cleaner.com/ and paste the HTML or use this plugin to assist you: https://moodle.org/plugins/atto_wordimport

ResponsesInList.Title: Subscription control using Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I would like to use Moodle as e-learning platform but I have specials needs. I wan to control the auto- singup of users based the domain name of a registered teacher and a reference number. Let's say for example that I have a teacher with a mail in "@toto.com" and a reference number of 50. I wan to allow the autosignup of 50 students for the "@toto.com" domain. My idea was to develop my own subscription page that perform the control and complete the registration using the API. Before begin I would like to have the feedback of the communauty , is this a good way to achieve my goal ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscription control using Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: No, I suggest not a good idea. Moodle is about individuation within the community. Each User has an individual email and is easily identifiable. Each User also has a Role in whatever context that the User is in. In one course, the User could be a Student, in another, a Teacher, in another Category, a Manager. If you are bulk, or generic, enrolling Users, that becomes seriously problematic, and you are going to have to be hacking a lot of core code, from enrollments to security, permissions, capabilities and even just simple activities to get it to work. There are two possibilities, break Moodle code down and use it as the basis for creating an entirely new LMS, which is a massive undertaking and likely not going to be a very rapid solution. Or, allow new Users to add themselves to the Moodle after meeting whatever criteria you require to be met, e.g. the email address. It would be a lot simpler to add an email check, and counter, to keep track of User enrollments than rebuilding core code. You could create a plugin for this, fairly easily, if you have the right coding skills. At a quick glance I would think that this ew module would do something like: 1. Admin adds email domain for new enrollments 2. Users then add their enrollment details, and onSave: Email domain is checked against acceptable domains If OK then Enroll student counter +1 else Error Message "Sorry, but your email address does not match known email addresses. Enrollment is cancelled" Step through form fieldname = " "; Return to http://your.domain/Error/invalid enrollment page. Clearly it won't be that simple, but in the end, I suspect it is going to end up looking something like that. A plugin you write rather than a revamp of the entire code is more practicable, I suggest. BTW , IANAD , and haven't done any serious coding for a long time now, so I would expect it has passed me by so don't take my word for any of this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to change activity completion checkbox icon to flag
ResponsesInList.Text: This icon is found in the pix folder, I would expect, and once you have the name, do a grep search for that name in the code. From there, you will have to change the image name in the code. This takes a long time and is not always guaranteed to work properly afterward. Be careful because unless things match exactly right, it can be a real pain. Names and sizes are important here, suggest you replace the image by renaming the original and your preferred image takes the same name as the image you are replacing. It must also be the same dimensions. As for changing the images from ret to green flags after completion, IANAD so don't know if this can be done easily. Changing images dynamically is relatively easy, but changing them on cue, that is the hard part.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle crashes after several students try to access or submit a questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Error 500's could be the result of many things.  The links you've provided in your research may have had 500 errors but in briefly reading through them ... the first is very old (which is why that thread is locked).   The second and third links provided had different problems although showing error 500's ... and different solutions. In your case, this is key: "Cannot find session record h25kg7hhk122f7d26rp45l40l6 for user 97, creating new session or similar. which indicates that you are using database for sessions, as opposed the recommended 'files. Login to moodle and in the site admin search box type: session. Find the setting for sessions to use database and change to files - ie, turn off using database for sessions. That might kick you out of your session as the next click on anything would check for a session file and there isn't one there yet for your access. Check your moodledata directory ... there should now be a 'sessions' directory and contained therein a file ... which is a session file for a user. Also, check how often your server is running the cron job/task ... recommendation now is every minute.  One of the task in the cron job is a check on sessions and to clean up stale session files found in moodledata/sessions (once you switch from DB to files).  If you don't change sessions to files and leave it for DB, that could be the problem ... task can't update the records fast enough or at all if DB server is struggling. As far as desire to have X number of users in system taking quiz/questionnaire at same time, that  relates to several factors in setup of server.   The major one being the number of connections allowed to the DB for the Moodle ... which is a mysql setting.   Not set in Moodle, but via whatever you have for My SQL in cPanel ... IF that is even there for you may not have a package with the hosting provider that allows you to tweak such settings ... if you are on a shared system. So a little more info about server is in order .. How are you hosted?  shared/VPS/other How much memory does your server have OR been allocated? Etc. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: please :::: You are not eligible to take this questionnaire.
ResponsesInList.Text: The problem with this is that if you start giving guests privileges, then you are likely to create problems for yourself further down the track. So, best bet, where is this questionnaire going to be? On the Front Page ? That is asking for trouble. Somewhere off the Front Page? Better, but risky. In a Category that contains nothing but information useful for a guest about your site? Best option. In that Guest Category, Guests can view everything, look at anything and participate in Questionnaires forums and perform tasks whatever you like, because they can't do it anywhere else.  In that Category, you look at the permissions of Guests and upgrade them to whatever you want them to do. Be careful though, don't go overboard or you may find that they can do far more than you thought they could and you end up having to spend a lot of time in repair work. In the Guest Category, go to Admin > Permissions and change them to suit your need. Test them before you offer to Guests. Also, test them outside the Guest Category, just to satisfy yourself you haven't done anything that is likely to spill over to somewhere else.

ResponsesInList.Text: The link to the Feedback Docs is here . Apart from anything Mary suggests, and that is viable if that is all you really want to do, you can also do this: 1. Plan exactly what you want Guests to be able to do. 2. Familiarize yourself with the usual Capabilities and Permissions of Guests. If you do not do this, then anything can happen. 3. Go to Site Admin > Courses > Manage Categories and Courses. Create a new Category, say GuestDocs. 4. a] Go to GuestDocs and go to Administration > Permissions and open the Permissions and Capabilities for Guest. Change those Capabilities you want them to have, this will only apply to Guests in this Category. Change those Capabilities  you want them to have. Those changes will only apply in that course. Note the distinction here. Moodle is very contextual, that is, thing happen where you want them to, but apply to everything that is dependent upon the place you start from. Start a Category level, changes apply to all courses in that Category. Start in a Course and changes ONLY apply for that Course. The key is what do you want them to be able to do? The trick is then going to be to get Guests to go into the Guest Category.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: After restoring moodle web file, need help
ResponsesInList.Text: Sounds like partial site restore included the databases a week old whose tables (mdl_files) no longer match what is in moodledata (fildir/trashdir) ... which was on another drive and didn't 'crash'. Restoring a week old backup of code directory usually isn't a problem unless plugins/changes to code files have taken place, but the DB for the site certainly has changed in a weeks time. Does your IT department have DB backups ( sql dumps) that match the dates of the code backups? Full site backups include: an archive of the code, a database dump (.sql), and an archive of moodledata (filedir by itself minimally). There is a command line utility called moosh (a php script on steroids) that does have some 'commands' to help ID orphaned/missing files but it cannot, of course, recreate those files and restore them to the sea of files in moodledata from the information contained in the DB. So, there is no 'easy' fix to this let alone a 'fix' that doesn't involve reuploading files missing. Once you do get this sorted, strongly advise a daily backup of the DB be made and archived OFF the server ... and a daily archive of moodledata/filedir also be made and archived OFF the server (since it's Windows dunno if one can do rsync's nor not but that would be the best way for archiving moodledata/filedir OFF the server. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student need to choose Language 2 times

You can have any number of Moodles as long as you have the disk space to carry it. In a NAS, there are two things you may need to know, one is how to make your own package files, This allows you to set up each Moodle using the NAS itself. Depending on your NAS manufacturer, there are a number of different options. I really don't know if you can just setup and use a PHP app like Moodle without installing it via a package. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student need to choose Language 2 times
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle has all kinds of switches to control its multilingual behaviour. Here is a plan _without_ really testing (what I would expect): 1. Language before the user logs in 1.a Language autodetect: OFF Moodle delivers in the Default language 1.b Language autodetect: ON Moodle will compare the available languages of the site with the language settings of the client's browser and delivers in the best match. If no matches, then in the Default language. 2. Language after the user logged in The language will be Users preferred language (in his profile) 3. Language once the user attends a course Follows the language settings of the course For more details, read the documentation in the Languages forum. @Colin, in a setting which I manage, separating the users to participate in different courses, not to mention in different sites, is not practicable. Because they work as a group! Here's the background: The participants are teachers, who will later teach in their local language, either Sinhala or Tamil. The subject matter is technical, engineering, so the common sources are in English. The participants *work together* in English, and in parallel create content in their own language. In short, the course happens in a mixed language mode!

You can time by logging their login time, but I doubt there is a logout time and still not get an accurate count of what they have done. Also, a person who is really bright, plays the school game really well can be in and out in 10 minutes with a completed task, but someone who struggles with their reading, their comprehension, may take an hour to complete the same task. How do you reward effort, and not the clever selection of parents and homelife? There is an built in counter for the number of contributions someone makes in a forum, go to their Forum posts from their User Profile, which I think might be a 3rd party plugin. Everything else you may need you should be able to generate it out of the database with a variety of standard reports, ad hoc reports or build your own reports via SQL . Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recurring courses in Moddle
ResponsesInList.Text: There are a couple of ways to do what you want. set up your course, "Secure Coding Practices." Use Groups labeled for the session: "Ben's Students - May, 2018" Into that group go all your May people. For the next session, use a group named "Joe's Students - June, 2018." When the group completes the course, change their status from student to guest (so they can see but not do anything more) or suspend them (which retains their data, but keeps them out of the course). The gradebook retains their grades, and it is downloadable to an excel spreadsheet, etc. This method, you don't need to remake the course for each session. Set up the course as a template. Use the template to make a new course for each session. the short course name is SCP-May.18 SCP-June.18 and so forth. Download grades from each course whenever you want. If you want to download assignments, that is doable in the assignment module as a teacher or higher role. The learning curve on Moodle can be steep, but note that steep means a lot of info in a short time. Spending that short time will introduce you to a very powerful LMS, used, i.e., by Open University, which is about as world class a university system as there is.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do I add partial Site Administration Permissions to a Teacher profile?
ResponsesInList.Text: There are likely to be a couple of ways of doing this, but in any case, be very careful and make sure you understand the full implications of what it is you are asking for and what you may do. The way I usually do this sort of thing is go to Site Admin > Users > Permissions > Define Roles and then select the cog on the right of the Teacher Role. Understand the permissions and capabilities that you are giving your Teachers here. Find the ones you are looking for and change them to Allow. Here is the problem.  The Teacher Role will only be useful inside a course the Teacher is assigned to. Outside that course these changes won't mean anything and have no impact. If you want to ensure that Teachers can access the things you want them to have access to, we come to the other way you can make changes that will work. Recognize that the Authenticated User is the Role everyone has when they log in. The Role stays with them, until they enter a category or course where they are a Teacher, or Manager, or Student or whatever. So, using the Authenticated User Role as a Template, create a new Role that reflects what you want them to do outside the course. OR Make everyone that needs it a Manager First technique won't be successful because it doesn't work outside a course. The third technique won't be successful because it is a nightmare to administer, The second technique won't work either because the Authenticated User Role inherits its capabilities from the next junior Role and add a few permissions. You could get it to work partially, but full workings as you describe them... no, sorry, not going to work. Best of all is to not make any such change. Some jobs just need get pushed up the chain so your chain could look something like Moodle Admin 1 Administrator/s 1-3 depending on the size of your Moodle but the fewer the better. Managers 1 or 2 or 3 PER Category, again, depending on size. This is important, the Managers can work at the Category level, and take a lot of work off the shoulders of the Admin/s. Course Creators no more than 2 per Category, don't need any more as they will be in high demand initially, but once settle, demand drops off exponentially. Teachers 1 per Course!!!!! If you want more than one Teacher to teach one course, then seriously suggest Meta Links Course, (best way out of that one - believe me.) Any number of Non-editing Teachers, if needed. Each Role is assigned by the one immediately above it, so a clear hierarchy of responsibility is established. Good luck...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site won't load without backslash - redirect error
ResponsesInList.Text:
```text

HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
```

ResponsesInList.Text: There's a block you can add to (for example) the home page - called 'Online users'. Note that it really only shows you how many people used the the system in the last 5 minutes. Moodle doesn't 'know' who is logged in. That's done by sessions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Get User logged in count query
ResponsesInList.Text: You can't... it works the other way around. Session cookies in the browser control logins. You can't detect that. That's why the block looks at users who have interacted with the site in the last few minutes. It's the best approximation you can get. You *could* check that users have logged in - that is the event of them logging in but it doesn't do you any good. There's no stateful data to say they are "logged in now". It's not really a sensible question when it comes to web applications unfortunately.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Single sign-on with office 365 account
ResponsesInList.Text: AFAIK , Office365 has no LTI connectivity, and it seems that Microsoft is just not interested in developing it, as Azure is another Microsoft product and they want people using Azure and not LTI. I suspect LTI would make SSO so much easier.... but having said that, why bother? I am not a big fan of putting things "in the cloud", perhaps because I am a little paranoid and I have no idea who, outside of the people who should have access to what is put there, is accessing my materials and details, my student's materials and details, my school's materials and details, especially when it comes to commercial companies like Microsoft or Google. These are natural targets, and can and will be hacked, no matter how hard they try to prevent it. There are sufficient number of alternatives to using cloud based apps that can be stored on your Moodle servers, but I do accept that while this is my preferred option, it is not always viable. The lesser of two evils for me would be Google Drive, which does use LTI... but that is me....

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Single sign-on with office 365 account
ResponsesInList.Text: The link to Office365 docs you provided says this: " Note: OAuth 2 authentication (enabling users to log in to Moodle with their Microsoft account) and the OneDrive repository are included in the standard Moodle, so require no additional plugins to be installed. " In the setup section of page, Configuraton ... of the page you've provided, the first item is 'Enable the OpenID Connection...' ...  which is Oauth2 ... now part of core. https://docs.moodle.org/34/en/OAuth_2_Microsoft_service Not sure what the connection is to LTI ... but SSO using Oauth2 core is, in my perception, sort of a mis-conception, me thinks ...  *true* SSO works only on a LAN/WAN (or virtualized LAN/WAN/VPN) when one logs onto the local/virtualized LAN/WAN/VPN ... other wise, when remote, it's really just another method of authentication and interconnectivity. Assuming Microsoft's Oauth2 works like Google's, once a user is logged onto a Moodle with Microsoft credentials any link to MS Office, etc. provided in the Moodle is under the login ... ie, a link to MS Office will show each user their MS Office. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Fatal Error: $CFG>Dataroot is not configured properly
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi. I've moved my Moodle from a localhost to a live server on One.Com. I've moved the Moodle folder, the Moodledata folder, and imported the database for Moodle. When I try accessing the Moodle page I recieve the following error: Fatal error: $CFG-> dataroot is not configured properly, directory does not exist or is not accessible! Exiting. The config.php shows that $CFG>dataroot is pointing towards the full path to the moodledata folder on the server. Do anyone have any tips or ideas for what could be wrong? Anything I can provide to give a better view of the situation? I'm new to Moodle so I don't know for sure what is of interest. I'm using Moodle 3.4.1.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Fatal Error: $CFG>Dataroot is not configured properly
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm assuming your One.Com server is Linux and runs Apache . Check that the user Apache is running as has access to the files in the Moodledata folder. If you have shell access you can change ownership with chown -R apache_user /path/to/moodledata . You'll have to work out what apache_user is, it's apache on some systems (e.g. CentOS), www-data on others (e.g. Ubuntu) or could be something else entirely. If this doesn't work you can try allowing all users access to this folder with chmod -R 777 /path/to/moodledata although this may be slightly less secure. The installation documentation may help point you in the right direction although obviously you're not creating the folder in this instance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Prevent attempts and grades after suspending users
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I am using Moodle 3.4 I want to disable users in bulk. What I know is, I can do this by adding a column suspended with value "1" and update users. I do not want to lose attempts and grades of suspended users that's why I afraid to do that. What happens if cron runs. How I can prevent cleaning of suspended users and their attempts and grades from cron. Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Prevent attempts and grades after suspending users
ResponsesInList.Text: Suspended users are not deleted, they are suspended, not terminated. However, let us make sure that we are using the same terms. Suspended is a student who, for whatever reason, is to be denied access to the Moodle for a period of time, not a student who has completed. Completed students are students who have completed the course work, and moved to the next course. For these, backup the course, then reset it. This empties the course, but does not remove them from the database , and your backup is kept safe for re-accessing if required. When students are no longer enrolled, they really should be deleted from the database, EXCEPT there is not way to actually do that. it seems. They are hidden but can be revived if required. This just adds clutter to the database, IMNSHO , Why can student records not be kept in a completely different module, or transferred to an adjunct database  kept especially for the purpose of reviving students records if they re-enroll after a period of time. This obviously means that records are kept, which may not sit well with the EU new data privacy laws. The cron has nothing to do with really, unless you actually delete users and then it only has a minor impact. The records are hidden, not really deleted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Prevent attempts and grades after suspending users
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Colin, Thanks for reply. What I understand by your kind answer is,"If I suspend users in bulk by csv who already attempted quizzes, their attempts did not washed out even cron runs" Right?? My scenario is: I have around 50000 students enrolled in different courses. I want that once time period finished for particular course I suspend that course's enrolled users so that they are not able to login and my server prevented from unnecessary load. Same time I want to keep all attempts of that course which belongs to suspended users.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Prevent attempts and grades after suspending users
ResponsesInList.Text: Ahh right, what you are talking about is removing students from the course they are finished with or have not completed in the required time frame. OK, that makes it easy. Use the cron to 1) Backup the course with full user data, uploads, images, quizzes, blogs, forum posts everything. 2) When backup complete, use the cron to reset the course. Resetting removes Users and User Data, a pristine course again. 3) You should have a csv file that uploads Teachers and assigns the right Teachers to empty courses. (That might be controlled by the cron too, but I am not sure about that.) If you set the csv file correctly, it will assign Roles properly. This Moodle Doc should help you build this file so it works every time it is run without duplicating Users or Role assignments. Careful planning of the Cron with regards to dates and times, and using your user upload file, that should, basically, automate the process. Essentially, the backup is your record of the course. If you do not want Users still seeing courses on their Dashboard , long after they have completed the course, you have to reset. You cannot archive a course to hide it, Moodle automatically assumes the enrollments are active, and will keep that course for the people enrolled in it.

I hear you say "but the site has all sorts of unknown custom code that we don't want to lose" Tough. Set up a new site, migrate your content and then post here about the features you have lost/things that are missing and people in the community will make suggestions to help you get those features back using newer supported plugins. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activity completion default settings
ResponsesInList.Text: You're probably right Brandon. Using phpMyAdmin , or similar, go into the [prefix]_courses table and add the SQL statement UPDATE `mdl_course` SET `enablecompletion`="1",`completionnotify`="1" Click the "Go" button and it should update the entire table. Obviously the statement is going to be very different if you don't have phpMyAdmin, or similar, and you have to update via the CLI. Just as obviously, if you cannot access your database , for whatever reason, then this becomes somewhat unlikely, but usually there is an administrator of some sort you can talk to to get what you want. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: teacher - manual activity completion
ResponsesInList.Text: I would create a grade book item for the outside activity, then grade it when the outside activity is completed.  You can choose the appropriate points for this item, relative to all of the other graded assignments. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: self-enrolled students can not access course if self-enrolment is disabled

You really have to think about what courses are going to be doing what, what is the need of that course, what is it purpose? Short courses with one or two or three small topics, that are hooks for longer courses can be set up like this. Sample courses, or small introductory courses can use self-enrollment. Courses you want to use and re-use, that have high enrollment turnovers, that are not critical to an assessment or certification process, or voluntary are usually set up with self-enrollment. Again, I don't know how good this app is, but at least two schools around me are using it for precisely the purpose you require. The beauty of these tools is they can save recordings as MP4s and as long as they are not too long, they are not overly large files with enormous file sizes. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MoodleCloud - user roles changes/ adding teachers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Alex. It is worth reading through the documentation Admin quick guide and particularly about roles, authentication and enrolment. The documentation on Assign roles might also have some pointers. Basically, apart from the admin, users tend to have student or teacher role within courses, and not for the whole site. They sign up or are created as "authenticated users" and you can give them different roles in different courses - if you wish. Additionally, teachers only work within courses, adding teaching materials and activities ; they don't "upload courses" if by that you mean actually create empty courses. There are other roles such as Course creators and managers which you can grant to people if you want them to play a greater part in creating courses from nothing - although you wouldn't make everyone that on  a site ( a bit like "too many cooks spoil the broth". Have a read of the documentation Standard roles as well and ask more questions. It is indeed possible to add empty courses with a CSV file and include users with the teacher role in those courses, so you quickly have, say ten courses, each with their own teacher, who can then edit the course and add the material they want. If that is all you need, then let us know and I can point you in the right direction.

ResponsesInList.Text: OK, have been working on this for a couple of days now and have been successful with installing apache-solr search in a fresh moodle 3.1 on CentOS 6. Here's what I did from notes ... might be brain dead so .... CentOS release 6.8 (Final) Linux site 2.6.32-642.1.1.el6.x86_64 #1 SMP Tue May 31 21:57:07 UTC 2016 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux As root user: PHP-SOLR ======== cd /root git clone https://github.com/ecaron/php-pecl-solr.git cd php-pecl-solr phpize ./configure make make install (compiling requires gcc and related libraries) ls /usr/lib64/php/modules/ should see a solr.so file in the above directory nano /etc/php.d/solr.ini add to the above file: extension=solr.so /sbin/service httpd restart php -m should show solr in the listing of php extensions php -m |grep solr should respond with solr APACHE SOLR - CentOS 6 ====================== This one is tricky ... and does require JRE at least version 1.8 Oracle pulled the 1.7 offline just the other day. As root user: java -version java version "1.8.0_40" Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.8.0_40-b25) Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.40-b25, mixed mode) I had to download the 1.8 to laptop and then scp it back up to server in /opt/ (just to keep things in the same place) http://download.oracle.com/otn-pub/java/jdk/8u91-b14/jdk-8u91-linux-x64.tar.gz in /opt as root where jdk-8u91-linux-x64.tar.gz resides tar xvf jdk-8u91-linux-x64.tar.gz then used alternatives to install /usr/sbin/alternatives --install /usr/bin/java java /opt/jdk1.8.0_91/bin/java 2 You'll get a screen asking which number to setup. Check version: java -version as above. Apache SOLR does require a user: solr /usr/sbin/useradd solr cd /opt/ wget http://www.us.apache.org/dist/lucene/solr/6.0.1/solr-6.0.1.tgz tar zxvf solr-6.0.1.tgz cd solr-6.0.1 solr bin/install_solr_service.sh /opt/solr-6.0.1.tgz -f bin/solr create -c moodle chown solr:solr * -R ****DO NOT remove /opt/solr-6.0.1 solr directory. Had to open access to port 8983 in iptables and did have to restart the server. Check to see if there is a solr file in /etc/init.d/ Should have been created upon install. ps aux |grep java should show solr running. You can start/stop with /sbin/service solr stop/start In Moodle config for solr Host: localhost Port: 8983 Index: moodle Played with it just a bit ... had a hidden System Admins category with a hidden SA course and only one URL in it .... ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle under HTTPS
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm trying to update my server so it runs exclusively under HTTPS. However when I implement this (in htaccess), the Moodle home page layout doesn't display correctly. Anyone know what needs to be done in Moodle to correct this? I'm running version 3.0.10. Thanks! Bob

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle under HTTPS
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bob, You probably have a mixed state of HTTP and HTTPS requests. If you are forcing the site use HTTPS, but some elements either can't load under HTTPS or they try to load under HTTP, then those elements get blocked and will not load. You can look at blocked elements in Chrome by opening the debugging console (Shift+Ctrl+J). Look for any errors. Additionally, go to the Network tab in the debugger and then press Ctrl+F5  to force the page to reload fully. You can see which elements did not load. Question : What is in your .htaccess file? My suggestion is to address this issue in the Apache vhost file to redirect any HTTP traffic to HTTPS. This way, any HTTP traffic automatically goes to HTTP regardless of any setting in Moodle or other places. In essence, all requests on the server will have to use HTTPS even if the HTTP resource is requested. Here is code Let's Encrypt puts in the <VirtualHost *:80> block (as an example for a specific domain ): RewriteCond %{SERVER_NAME} = www.example.com [OR] RewriteCond %{SERVER_NAME} =example.com RewriteRule ^ https://%{SERVER_NAME}%{REQUEST_URI} [END,NE,R=permanent] Or, in general: RewriteEngine On RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off RewriteRule ^ https://%{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} There are a number of guides online: https://www.namecheap.com/support/knowledgebase/article.aspx/9821/38/redirect-to-https-on-apache https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16200501/http-to-https-apache-redirection#16200545 You can test your HTTPS/SSL configurations at: https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest https://www.htbridge.com/ssl https://www.htbridge.com/websec/ Kind regards, Tony

Having just checked my site, the source code (not a rewrite by apache) lists the CSS references as HTTPS. I installed it using HTTPS and did not have to deal with the mixed content. I figure you can't rely on users to use HTTPS without forcing them to do so.
